# Bug register

> **The single register.** Not a file per bug, not scattered TODOs. **Any lane opens a row; QE reconciles the register at every promotion** (`CLAUDE.md` §20e). A lane edits only the `Status` of a bug it has fixed.
>
> **Why this file exists.** Open defects had no home. They were split between `39-product-review-findings.md` (a *dated record of reviews*, append-only, and not a feature lane's to edit) and `PROJECT_STATUS.md`'s known-limitations table. Neither can carry a row whose status changes, and a review finding is not the same thing as a defect with an owner and a fix. This file replaces that responsibility rather than adding one.

## Identifier blocks — per lane, from 2026-08-02

**Product owner's direction.** New rows use the opening lane's allocated block, so two lanes can no longer allocate the same number and QE no longer renumbers at merge (which is what [B-017](#b-017--a-lanes-merged-slice-disappeared-from-integration-and-the-backlog-reoffers-it)'s neighbourhood cost once already). Rows numbered below 100 predate the scheme and keep their identifiers permanently; **an id is never renumbered.**

> 🔴 **The allocation table is [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §20e, and it is not restated here** ([B-1001](#b-1001--this-register-carried-a-second-copy-of-the-identifier-allocation-table-and-it-had-been-wrong-for-thirteen-days)).
>
> ⛔ **This section used to carry its own copy** — one row, Lane B's, under the sentence *"Only Lane B's block has been stated to Lane B."* ⚠️ **That was true when written on 2026-08-02 and false by the end of that day**, when the product owner allocated every block at once. **Nothing connected the two events**, and the copy sat here for thirteen days telling a lane opening a row that its own range did not exist.
>
> ⚡ **Replacing it with a reference is the fix *and* the guard.** **A checker for *"does this copy match the registry?"* would itself be a third copy of the answer** — §2, *truth has exactly one authoritative representation; everything else derives from it.*


## How it works

**Any lane opens. The module's current assignee fixes. QE verifies and closes** — never the lane that fixed it.

**A defect belongs to a module, not to a lane.** The module is permanent; the lane assigned to it rotates (`CLAUDE.md` §20e). A row therefore names **the module**, and whoever is currently assigned it resolves the defect. A row whose module has no current assignee waits for one — which is not the same as being unowned.

**Reporting is every lane's duty, not only QE's.** Finding a defect outside your assignment is not permission to fix it — it is an obligation to record it, with every field below filled, before carrying on inside your Change Budget. **Only QE sets `VERIFIED`.**

> **No defect disappears because the lane that found it could not fix it.** That is the single failure this register exists to prevent, and it is the one a busy lane commits by accident — in a comment, in a commit message, in an intention to come back.

**Before starting any slice, a lane reads every `OPEN` and `FIXING` row** (`CLAUDE.md` §20e, *Startup*). Rows against the module it is assigned are fixed first, or deferred **with the reason stated in the commit message**. Silence reads as *nobody looked*.

> **Finding a bug never grants implementation ownership.** *Discovery* decides who reports it; **the affected module decides who fixes it.** They are rarely the same lane, and that is the point. Ownership moves only by explicit reassignment, never by having noticed.

**A defect is not a dependency.** If your work is blocked because another module has not yet built or agreed something, that is a coordination item — [`LANE_COORDINATION.md`](LANE_COORDINATION.md) — not a bug. A bug is something that behaves wrongly today.

### Defects in code that belongs to no module

`signora_platform/**` (frozen, §20a), `apps/` (the composition root) and the frontend foundation (§20c) are not modules, so no assignment reaches them. **QE cannot fix them either — it changes no production code.**

Such a row names the code, records **Current assignee: none — not assignable**, and **waits for the product owner**. It is never quietly adopted by whoever is nearest.

**This gap appeared on 2026-08-01** when the Integrator role was absorbed into QE. [B-007](#b-007--the-migration-runner-locks-one-database-and-migrates-another) is its first instance, and [C-010](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is the item that will resolve it — deciding how unassignable code gets assigned is an architectural decision, not a lane's to make.

**`integration` never fast-forwards to `main` with an open 🔴.** That is the one blocking rule; 🟠 and below are the product owner's call.

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 🔴 | Blocks a milestone |
| 🟠 | Wrong behaviour a customer would hit |
| 🟡 | Wrong but survivable |
| 🟢 | Cosmetic |

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `OPEN` | Reproduced, not started |
| `FIXING` | The current assignee is on it |
| `FIXED` | Lane says done, with a regression test |
| `VERIFIED` | QE reproduced the fix. **Only QE sets this** |
| `WONTFIX` | Deliberate, with the reason stated |

**Where the regression test goes:** the affected module's suite, written by the lane that fixes it — never this file. The rule requiring one is `CLAUDE.md` §11.

**Bug ids are `B-nnn`, allocated sequentially and never reused.** A finding from a product review keeps its `R-` id there and gets a `B-` row here only if it is a defect rather than an improvement.


## How the registers were reconciled, 2026-08-02

**Two lanes allocated `B-003`…`B-006` independently while the repository ran on two baselines.** The rows promoted to `main` keep their numbers; **QE renumbered the later set**, which is this file's stated rule for an id collision.

| Was, on `lane-qe` | Is now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `B-001` · `B-002` | — | The same two defects as the promoted rows. The duplicates were dropped, not renumbered |
| `B-003` the migration runner | **[B-007](#b-007--the-migration-runner-locks-one-database-and-migrates-another)** | Renumbered. It is the **code** half of promoted [B-003](#b-003--a-lane-following-runningmd-exactly-cannot-run-its-own-suites), which is the documentation half |
| `B-004` the truncation claim | **[B-008](#b-008--the-suite-says-it-truncates-every-table-and-truncates-five)** | Renumbered |
| `B-005` the documented API command | **[B-009](#b-009--the-documented-command-for-starting-the-api-cannot-start-the-api)** | Renumbered |
| `B-006` orphaned narrations | **[B-010](#b-010--re-seeding-the-playground-orphans-every-narration-silently)** | Renumbered |
| `B-007` `make` absent | **[B-011](#b-011--make-is-not-installed-on-this-workstation--not-a-repository-defect)** | Renumbered, and resolved on the workstation |

**No row was lost and none was silently merged.** An id, once promoted, is never reused for a different defect.

## Open

> ⚡ **A SECOND INSTANCE OF THIS CLASS ARRIVED WITHIN HOURS, from a different lane, in a different technology, and it is recorded here because [B-424](#b-424)'s conversation asked for exactly this evidence.**
>
> ⛔ **[B-231](#b-231)** — registering Better Auth's `twoFactor()` plugin broke account registration outright, and **the unit suite was green throughout at 2607 tests.** ⚡ **Lane A's own words: it *"asserted the plugin was imported and never touched Better Auth's database. That is a test of the configuration rather than of the capability."***
>
> 🔴 **Same defect, different surface.** **B-175 asserts a class string rather than the rendered result; B-231 asserted an import rather than the capability.** ⛔ **Both are tests of an INPUT to a framework, and both stayed green while the product was broken** — one on every authentication screen, the other on the first journey a customer takes.
>
> ⚠️ **Neither was caught by a gate, and in both cases the thing that found it was somebody using the product** — the product owner opening `/verify`, and a Playwright journey running against the real stack. ✅ **That is [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s sentence with two fresh instances rather than a restatement.**
>
> ⛔ **QE is not proposing a gate.** ⚡ **The two instances share a cause a gate cannot reach: a test that names an input can be written in any framework, and no check knows which assertions were meant to be about behaviour.** ✅ **What they do justify is a review question rather than a rule — *does this assertion fail if the product breaks?* — and that belongs to whoever next revises the testing guidance, not to a defect row.**

### B-1010 · 🟡 Two sibling gates ask *"is this built thing reachable?"* and an HTTP endpoint falls between them

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/reachability.py`](../infra/reachability.py) and [`infra/runtime-composition.py`](../infra/runtime-composition.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **nothing is broken and nothing unsafe ships.** ⚠️ **What is absent is coverage of a class this repository already decided was worth automating, in the one dimension neither sibling walks** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **recorded, not built.** ⚠️ **A third gate is a governance-weight decision and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s freeze says an observed problem is required; this row IS the observation, and one instance is not yet a pattern** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-17** by **Lane A**, who reported it as *"not a defect, so no `B-` row"* — ✅ **and was right about the endpoint and understating the gap** |
| **Commit found** | **`cbc71c12`** |

### 🔴 The gap, in the gates' own words

📁 **`reachability.py`'s docstring names the class and the pairing:**

> ⚡ ***"The sibling of `runtime-composition.py`, and deliberately the same shape: that one asks 'does the deployed worker consume what this module projects?', this asks 'does any screen lead to this route?'*** ⛔ ***Both answer the same class of question — something is built, correct, tested, and nothing reaches it."***
>
> 📁 ***"Timeline shipped complete and inert ([B-301](#b-301)) — the backend half of the same failure, which is why the two checks are siblings."***

| gate | the edge it walks |
|---|---|
| `reachability` | **route → screen** |
| `runtime-composition` | **module projection → worker** |
| ⛔ **nothing** | **HTTP endpoint → frontend consumer** |

### 📊 The instance

**`GET /workspaces/{id}/accounts/{id}/decision-package`** — ⛔ **no reference anywhere under `frontend/`.** ✅ **Measured, not inferred.** ⚡ **Built, per-account, and nothing calls it**: it is the account drawer's AI block *and* Account 360's, whenever either is built.

### ⚠️ The example moved within the hour, and the row is stronger for saying so

**Reported by Lane A, 2026-08-17, hours after filing**: **`decision-package` now HAS a consumer** — `useAccountDecisionPackage` in `lib/query/hooks.ts`, read by the Companies expanded row's AI panel.

✅ **Verified: the consumer is on their UNPUSHED branch only.** ⛔ **Absent from `origin/main`, `origin/integration` and both pushed lane refs** — **so this row was accurate when filed and remains accurate of every ref QE can certify.**

⚡ **But the instance is now a poor witness, and pretending otherwise would be the defect this register keeps finding.** 📁 **The class is unchanged: *nothing walks endpoint → frontend consumer*.** ⛔ **What changed is that this particular endpoint stopped being inert because a lane happened to build its consumer — not because anything detected it.**

🔴 **That is the argument FOR the row and AGAINST building the gate today, at the same time.** ⚠️ **An inert endpoint that resolves on its own within hours is weak evidence of a standing problem** — ✅ **and [B-301](#b-301) is the counter-example that keeps the class alive: Timeline shipped complete and inert and stayed that way, which is why the two sibling gates exist at all.**

📁 **So the row waits for a second instance that does NOT resolve itself.** ⛔ **If none arrives, that is the answer.**

### ✅ What this row is NOT

⛔ **Not a defect in the endpoint.** 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md) already names the cost of building ahead of a surface** — *"the pipeline ran nine stages ahead of any user-visible surface and that was a real cost"* — **so an endpoint waiting for its consumer is a known, accepted shape, and Lane A classified it correctly.**

⛔ **Not a criticism of either gate.** ✅ **Both docstrings claim exactly what they do.** ⚠️ **The gap is between them, not inside either.**

⛔ **Not a proposal to build a third gate today.** 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s governance freeze requires an *observed* execution problem, and this is the first observation.** ⚡ **If a second endpoint ships inert, that is the pattern and this row is the evidence for it.** ⚠️ **Building it now would be the speculative-abstraction move [§6](../CLAUDE.md) forbids, dressed as diligence.**

### B-1009 · 🟠 QE reported a slice as "never offered to QE" from a ref count, and its content was byte-identical on `main`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE process** — branch triage, and the standing instruction to resolve an *ahead* count by patch-id |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **nothing unsafe shipped and no gate was weakened.** 🔴 **What it cost was nearly concrete: the operative version of the belief makes a future slice WORK AROUND SOMETHING ALREADY BUILT**, and QE had told two lanes and written it into three promoted records |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`FIXING` — REOPENED 2026-08-16, same day, by its own stated condition.** ⛔ **It recurred in the very next poll: the patch-id resolution was RUN and BOUNDED with `--since=2026-08-10`, and `ba904596` is dated 2026-08-07.** ⚡ **The original diagnosis — *QE skipped the instruction* — is false as a general account, and the refusal to build a check is withdrawn** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-16** by **Lane A**, who ran one `cat-file` against a warning QE had given them; **verified independently by Lane C**, who had queued the same false claim for a product decision and withdrew it |
| **Commit found** | **`f6c12a43`** |

### 🔴 The claim, and the measurement that disproves it

**QE wrote, in `PROJECT_STATUS.md`, `SESSION_HANDOFF.md` and `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`:**

> ⛔ *"carrying `affiliation_reader.py` and **276 test lines** never offered to QE."*

```
origin/main:…/people/infrastructure/affiliation_reader.py       PRESENT
git log -1 origin/main -- …/affiliation_reader.py  → ba904596

blob on main    7fab4469c054e77dcde5bb22c59fc27ce5786457
blob on lane-b  7fab4469c054e77dcde5bb22c59fc27ce5786457      ← byte-identical
patch-id fd0f55cd  057beed982b2  → already on main as ba904596
```

⛔ **Only `2e3d33e0` — a claim commit — is genuinely unpromoted, and a claim alone is not a stranded slice.**

### ⛔ The mechanism, which is the whole row

**The measurement was `git rev-list --left-right --count`: `2` ahead, `1163` behind.** ✅ **Both true, and both facts about a REF.** 🔴 **QE converted them into a claim about CONTENT — *this work has never been offered* — and never checked the content.**

⚠️ **The standing instruction exists for exactly this and was skipped:**

> ⛔ **RESOLVE EVERY "ahead" COUNT BY PATCH-ID BEFORE BELIEVING IT.**

📁 **QE resolved the merge-base *(2026-08-07)* and the file list *(507 insertions)* and stopped there.** ⚡ **Both of those made the branch look MORE substantial, which is the direction that made the wrong conclusion feel better supported.**

### ⚡ It is the exact mirror of the same session's other finding, and the pair names the root

| | the ref | the content |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle 237 — orphaned board SHAs** | ⛔ **on no ref** | ✅ **promoted** |
| **This row** | ⛔ **1163 behind, cannot fast-forward** | ✅ **promoted** |

⛔ **In both, an instrument read the ref and a human reported the work.** ⚡ **`git show` succeeds on an unreachable commit and `rev-list --count` succeeds on a duplicated one — neither command is wrong, and neither answers the question that was asked.**

📁 **Same family as everything else this session: an instrument answering a checkable question adjacent to the real one.** 🔴 **The difference is that here the instrument was fine and QE supplied the wrong question.**

### ✅ What made it visible, and it was not a gate

**A lane declined to accept a warning and spent one command on it.** ⛔ **No check in this repository would have caught it** — nothing compares a stale branch's patch-ids against `main`, and `state-check` reports board and register consistency, not branch content.

⚠️ **QE told BOTH lanes the false version and it propagated**: Lane C queued it for a product decision, and D-240 ruled a relevance check on work that needed none. ⚡ **The ruling is not wasted — it is now the standing answer for the next genuinely stranded branch — but it was ruled on a false premise and that is recorded here rather than left tidy.**

### ⛔ What this row ORIGINALLY proposed, and why that was wrong within the hour

**It said: no check.** 📁 *"The instruction already exists and is explicit; adding a script to enforce an instruction QE skipped would be treating a discipline failure as a tooling gap."* ⚠️ **It also set the condition for its own reversal:** *"If it recurs, that reasoning is wrong and the row should be reopened with the second instance as evidence."*

### 🔴 REOPENED the same day — it recurred, in the poll immediately after this row was written

**Status changed to `FIXING`.** ⛔ **QE ran the patch-id resolution this time — and bounded it.**

```bash
git log origin/integration --format='%H' --since=2026-08-10   # ← the defect
```

**`ba904596` is dated 2026-08-07.** ⛔ **Outside the window.** ⚡ **So the scan reported `fd0f55cd` as `NEW` — the identical false conclusion this row was filed about, reached by a different route, roughly one hour later.**

**Unbounded, it is unambiguous:**

```
fd0f55cd  patch-id  057beed982b2
ba904596  patch-id  057beed982b2   ← match
```

### ⚠️ The reversal, stated plainly rather than quietly amended

⛔ **The first diagnosis was *QE skipped the instruction*. That was true of instance one and is FALSE as a general account.** ✅ **Instance two ran the instruction and still got the wrong answer**, because **a patch-id search is only as good as the set it searches, and nothing about `--since` announces that it has narrowed the question.**

🔴 **So this is an instrument defect after all, and the original refusal to build a check was wrong.** ⚡ **It is also, precisely, the family this whole session has been about** — *an instrument answering a checkable question adjacent to the one asked* — **and the adjacent question here was *"is this patch-id on integration SINCE A DATE I PICKED?"***

📁 **Lane C predicted this shape in its own words hours earlier**: *"knowing the mechanism did not stop me producing the instance, which is the uncomfortable version and the true one."* ⛔ **QE filed a row naming the mechanism and produced the next instance of it before the row was pushed.**

### ✅ What the fix must be, and what it must not be

| ✅ | ⛔ |
|---|---|
| **Never bound the search set** — the correct operand is every commit reachable from the target ref | A `--since` tuned to a "safe" window, which only moves the boundary |
| **Report the SET SIZE searched**, so a reader can see what was covered | A bare `NEW`/`DUP` verdict with no statement of scope |
| **Refuse rather than answer** when the search set is empty or truncated | Returning `NEW` on a set that could not have contained a match |

### ✅ RESOLVED — the check does not need writing, because git already is it

**`git cherry <upstream> <head>` is exactly this question**, computed by patch-id, natively:

```
$ git cherry origin/main origin/lane-b-commercial-profile
  + 2e3d33e0  Claim TASK-468 — Workspace Setup: replaced, not refined
  - fd0f55cd  M-I · who has held a role at a company, and who left     ← already upstream
```

⚡ **`-` means *the patch is already upstream*. `+` means *genuinely new*.** ⛔ **`fd0f55cd` reads `-`, which is the correct answer this row exists because QE did not have** — and **the remaining `+` is a claim commit, which is why the branch was never a stranded slice.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **QE's hand-rolled unbounded loop** | ⛔ **timed out at 2 minutes** over ~2000 commits — one `git show \| git patch-id` per commit |
| **`git cherry`** | ✅ **0.043s**, same answer, **and no window parameter exists to get wrong** |

🔴 **So the `--since` was not merely a careless bound — it was a workaround for a performance problem created by hand-rolling a comparison git already implements.** ⚡ **The bound existed BECAUSE the wrong tool was slow.** 📁 **That is the actual root, and it is one layer beneath both earlier diagnoses:**

| attempt | diagnosis | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | *QE skipped the instruction* | **True of instance one only** |
| **②** | *A patch-id search is only as good as the set it searches* | **True, and still not the root** |
| **③** | ✅ **QE rebuilt a comparison git ships, and then bounded it to make its own reimplementation fast enough** | **The root** |

⛔ **No script is warranted after all** — ✅ **but the earlier refusal was still wrong, and for the wrong reason.** **It said *the instruction exists and QE skipped it*; the true statement is *the instruction exists, names no tool, and every hand-rolled implementation of it is slow enough to invite a bound.*** ⚡ **The correct repair is a sentence, not a program: the standing instruction should name `git cherry`.**

### ✅ The general account, and it is Lane C's rather than QE's

**QE proposed two framings and Lane C rejected both as unbuildable, correctly:**

> ⛔ **A bounded scan must state its bound in its own output, or the reader inherits a conclusion without its scope.**

⚡ **That is checkable and *"QE skipped it"* was not.** 📁 **Lane C's own instance of it, offered as the pair**: a `--grep` that matched **doc-comments** and released `TASK-1432` on a text match — *"the tool answered; it answered a smaller question than the one asked, and said nothing about the difference."*

### 🔴 It is the same rule as [B-1006](#b-1006), and filing them separately was the mistake

**B-1006's minimum fix, written hours earlier and in the same register:**

> ⚡ ***"The one that prints the note is the one that did not mislead anybody"*** — **the same diagnostic in all three entry points, positioned where truncation cannot remove it.**

⛔ **That is this rule, applied to a REF instead of to a DATE.** ⚡ **`--audit-main` narrows its operand to the working tree's manifest; a `--since` narrows its operand to a window; a `--grep` narrows its operand to a text match. All three answer confidently and none announces the narrowing.**

✅ **So the repository has one rule with four instances and had it filed as three unrelated rows plus a lane's aside.** 📁 **Recorded here rather than merged into a new row**, because **B-1006 and B-1009 have different owners' evidence in them and collapsing them would lose the measurements** — ⚠️ **but they should be ruled together, and that is stated so the product owner is not asked the same question twice.**

⚠️ **That sentence is not QE's to write** — the instruction is the product owner's. **Filed, with the measurement, rather than edited.**

📁 **Fire-tested before being recorded**: `git cherry origin/integration origin/lane-a-product-surface` returns four `+` and no `-`, which matches an independent read of that branch's history — **so the tool is not simply answering `-` to everything.**

### B-1008 · 🟠 The dashboard published a Security Invariant count from the cycle before last, four cycles after a footnote was added warning against exactly that

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE process** — Repository Closeout activity 5, [`PROJECT_STATUS.md`](../PROJECT_STATUS.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **no gate is weakened and nothing unsafe ships.** ⚠️ **What it costs is the dashboard's one claim about itself**: *"every figure is read from the promoted commit, never carried forward"* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-16, cycle 237.** ⛔ **QE wrote the fix, so it stays `FIXED`** (§20e) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-16**, cycle 237's Closeout, by declining to copy either the dashboard's figure or the certification log's and reading `certification/manifest.json` for all three runs instead |
| **Commit found** | **`2e7f5da6`** |

### 🔴 The measurement

| cycle | commit | record says | dashboard published |
|---|---|---|---|
| 235 | `251f7183` | **458 invariants** | — |
| 236 | `9879f715` | **632 invariants** | ⛔ **`458+`** |
| 237 | `2e7f5da6` | **632 invariants** | ✅ **632** |

⛔ **Cycle 236 published cycle 235's figure**, and the certification record it was closing out said `632` in the same file it was reading the commit hash from.

### ⚠️ The `+` is the part worth naming

**It read `458+`, not `458`.** ⚡ **A hedge makes a stale figure unfalsifiable rather than accurate** — `458+` is *true* of `632`, and of `6320`, and it answers nothing. ⛔ **A reader cannot tell a hedged measurement from a measured one, so the `+` converts a detectable error into an undetectable one.**

📁 **Same shape as the week's dominant family**: the figure was correct for a question nobody asked — *"is it at least 458?"* — while the question was *"how many are there?"*

### 🔴 It is a RECURRENCE, and that is the reason for the row

**The footnote directly beneath the line says so, dated cycle 232:**

> *"Every figure on this line was stale, and by a wide margin… The table above it had been re-measured each cycle; this line had not, and nothing connected the two."*

⛔ **A correction was made, a warning was written, and the class recurred four cycles later in the same file.** ⚡ **So the 232 repair fixed the instance and not the mechanism** — **nothing derives these figures, and Closeout activity 5 is performed by a human reading a log and typing into a table.**

### ✅ Fixed here, and three more found by the same method

**Re-derived rather than re-read:** **DR invariants `443` → `632`** · **frontend `3254/184` → deleted, because the record now carries it** · **reversibility head `0054` → `0057`** · **smoke `217s` → `165s`**.

⚠️ **And two figures were MISLABELLED rather than stale, which is a different defect:** *"60 ADRs"* counted `README.md`; *"148 numbered architecture documents"* counted two unnumbered files. ✅ **59 and 146.** ⛔ **Those numbers were never wrong — the words above them were**, and no re-measurement would have caught it because the count matched the command that produced it.

### ⛔ What this row does NOT do

**Propose deriving the dashboard.** 📁 **That is [B-1001](#b-1001)'s question — whether a copy earns its place — and the answer there was *delete it*, while the answer for a health line a human reads at a glance is probably *check it*, as [B-1003](#b-1003) settled for the allocation table.** ⚡ **`backend/tests/test_runbook_allocation_table.py` is the shape that would work here.** ⛔ **Not built in this cycle, because a check written during the Closeout it is auditing is a check nobody has fire-tested.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE process** — Repository Closeout, branch sequencing |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **nothing executable reached `main`.** **All three are `docs/coordination/*.toml`, and they fail the Closeout test on the SUFFIX alone.** ⚠️ **But `--audit-main` refuses, and the guarantee it states is the repository's central release claim** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-16, cycle 237.** ⛔ **`main` was never rewritten.** ⚡ **The sequencing was corrected and the refusal discharged itself, exactly as this row predicted below** — **measured after promoting `2e7f5da6`: `1996 commit(s)` · `214 certified` · `1782 inside a certified snapshot` · **`0` outside one**.** 📁 **The three named commits became ancestors of a certified commit and were reclassified without anybody touching them.** ⛔ **Stays `FIXED` rather than `VERIFIED`: QE wrote it** (§20e) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-16**, by `--audit-main` immediately after cycle 236's Closeout |
| **Commit found** | **`c0c3a5b7`** |

### 🔴 What I did

**I rebased `lane-qe` onto `origin/integration` — which had moved past the pinned snapshot — and then fast-forwarded `main` to `lane-qe`.** ⛔ **So `main` gained everything on `integration`, not just the Closeout.**

✅ **The correct sequence is to base the Closeout on the CERTIFIED commit**, so the only thing `main` gains after a promotion is the Closeout itself.

**Nine commits reached `main` beyond `9879f715`. Six are Closeout-legal. Three are not, and every one fails ONLY on `docs/coordination/*.toml`:**

```
a1e3841a  TASK-1482 — the legacy Attention rail entry
9a699382  I released a blocked row on a text match
9b159ea2  D-238 — eight rulings
```

⚡ **That is [B-1005](#b-1005) realised on `main` rather than in a cycle decision** — **the classifier does not know `.toml`, so a documentation-only planning commit cannot be absorbed as a Closeout.**

### ⚠️ It self-heals, and that is a reason to record it rather than to relax

📁 **All three are ancestors of `origin/integration`, so the NEXT certified commit makes them ancestors of a certified tip on `main` and the audit reclassifies them as in-snapshot.** ⛔ **The refusal will disappear without anybody fixing anything**, which is exactly why it needs a row: **a violation that heals silently is one nobody learns from.**

### ⛔ What I am not doing

**Rewriting `main`.** 📁 **Every commit on it is a record other sessions have read, and falsifying history to make an audit green is the failure `CLAUDE.md` §2 names in its own words** — *"a record of what was true then must not be rewritten to match now."* ⚡ **The audit is right that these three arrived outside a snapshot. The honest repair is the sequencing, not the history.**

### B-1006 · 🟠 `--audit-main` audits a REF using the manifest from whatever tree you are standing in, and refuses when they disagree

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py), `_audit_main` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it produces a FALSE REFUSAL, not a false pass**, so nothing unsafe is admitted. ⚠️ **But it fires at the exact moment it matters most — immediately after a promotion — and it names real commits as having *"reached `main` without a gate"***, which is the most alarming sentence the tool can print |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-16**, promoting cycle 235: the audit refused with 3 commits listed, and the same audit on the same `main` reported *the guarantee holds* from a different working tree |
| **Commit found** | **`251f7183`** |

### 🔴 The two operands

📁 **`rev-list RULE_RATIFIED_AT..main`** — **a REF.** 📁 **`_runs()` reads `certification/manifest.json`** — **from the WORKING TREE.**

⛔ **Those are different things and nothing makes them agree.** ⚡ **The bounded exception guarantees they will disagree**: *"a certification record cannot contain its own commit hash, so the commit that WRITES the record is always created after the run it records."* **So the record for the commit just promoted lives on `lane-qe` while `main`'s tree still holds the previous manifest.**

**Measured, both directions, same `main`:**

| standing on | verdict |
|---|---|
| `main` | 🔴 **REFUSED — 3 commit(s) reached `main` uncertified** |
| `lane-qe` *(has the record)* | ✅ **212 certified · 1750 in-snapshot · guarantee holds** |

### ⚠️ Why the three it named are not violations

**`b0048fea`** *(TASK-420)*, **`0309f75b`** and **`fb0cff64`** *(coordination projections)* **are all ancestors of `251f7183`, which IS certified.** ⛔ **They read as violations only because `certified_all` was empty of `251f7183` — the manifest in that tree had never heard of it.**

📁 **The two coordination commits are also [B-1005](#b-1005)'s classifier gap showing through**: `docs/coordination/*.toml` fails `CLOSEOUT_SUFFIXES`, so they cannot be absorbed as Closeouts either. ⚡ **Two defects producing one alarming message.**

### ⛔ The fix is not obviously "read the manifest from `main`"

**Reading it from `main` would make the audit unable to see a record that has not been promoted yet** — **which is every record, at the moment it matters.** ⚠️ **And reading it from the working tree is what lets QE audit before promoting.**

⚡ **The honest statement is that the tool answers a question about a ref using evidence from a tree, and the caller has to know which.** ✅ **A diagnostic naming both — *"audited `main` at X using the manifest in the working tree at Y"* — would have turned a two-minute alarm into a one-line read**, and that is the minimum. **Whether the predicate itself should change is a gate-meaning question and [B-131](#b-131)'s route.**

### 🔴 THREE entry points, and only one of them says so

⚡ **Found across three sessions in one day, on the same operand:**

| entry point | reads from | says so? |
|---|---|---|
| **`--next-cycle`** | this clone's `integration` | ⛔ **no** |
| **`--audit-claims`** | this clone's `integration` | ✅ **yes — prints the note as its FIRST line** |
| **`--audit-main`** | this clone's `main` | ⚠️ **prints `_scope_note()`, which a `tail` hides** |

📁 **Lane C could not verify QE's refusal because their local `main` is 575 commits behind `origin/main`** — ⛔ **and reported *"I could not verify"* rather than *"it passes here"*, which is the only honest reading available from a stale clone.**

⚡ **Their observation is the sharpest thing in this row:**

> ## **The one that prints the note is the one that did not mislead anybody.**

⛔ **`--audit-claims` said *"note — 3 commit(s) on `origin/integration` are not in this clone's `integration`"* as its first line, and QE read past it once and caught it the second time.** ✅ **`--next-cycle` says nothing at all.** ⚠️ **`--audit-main` says it, and puts it where a `tail -6` removes it — which is how QE published a verdict about a `main` three commits stale earlier the same day.**

📁 **So the minimum fix is not one diagnostic — it is the SAME diagnostic in all three, positioned where truncation cannot remove it.** ⚡ **A note that only survives an untruncated read is a note that works for careful readers and nobody else.**

### ⚡ It is one ruling with [B-1005](#b-1005), not two

**Two of the three commits this refusal named are `docs/coordination/*.toml` failing `CLOSEOUT_SUFFIXES`** — ⛔ **so they cannot be absorbed as Closeouts either.** ✅ **Raised by Lane C, who owns the other half:**

> ⚡ ***The classifier does not know `.toml`, and that shows up as noise in `--next-cycle` AND as a false refusal in the audit.***

📁 **So the product owner should see one question rather than two**: **a file extension two independent allowlists were both written before, costing a cycle per republication in one place and a false alarm in the other.** ⛔ **Splitting it into two rulings invites two partial fixes.**

### ⚠️ The distinction this cost me, stated so the two sentences do not read as contradictory

**QE broke the cycle-235 snapshot while this was being found**, and a reader comparing §20e with the Closeout will otherwise see a contradiction:

| | |
|---|---|
| 📁 §20e | ***"`integration` keeps moving during certification, deliberately"*** |
| ⛔ what QE did | **merged another lane's commit into `integration` twenty seconds into a run, and the gates measured a different commit than the pin named** |

⚡ **Both are true because they are about different things.** ✅ **§20e is about the REF: a lane merging while QE certifies is expected and must never block them.** ⛔ **What must not move is the WORKING TREE of the machine running the gates** — **`make certify` runs in place, so a checkout or a merge changes what every subsequent gate reads.**

📁 **Named by Lane C as worth making explicit, and they were right: the rule I wrote to them an hour before breaking it did not cover the case I broke.**

📁 **Same family as everything else this week: the reading was correct and the operand was not the one the consumer uses.** ⚡ **This time the consumer is the audit and the operand is the tree it happens to be standing in.**

### B-1005 · 🟠 Two independent classifiers are both blind to `.toml`, so 157 planning commits in a week were treated as executable

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py), `_is_closeout` and `IMPACT_RULES` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the bias is toward OVER-certifying, so nothing unsafe reaches `main`.** ⚠️ **What it costs is the rule itself**: *"documentation and planning accumulate until they accompany executable work"* **did not apply to 157 of 932 commits — 17%, concentrated entirely in planning** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-15** by **Lane C**, who noticed every queue regeneration plans as `platform`/16 gates and **declined to propose a classifier rule** — [B-131](#b-131)'s class, and QE's |
| **Commit found** | **`044fbf30`** |

### 🔴 Two classifiers, one blind spot, reached by different routes

| | asks | how `.toml` fails |
|---|---|---|
| **`_is_closeout`** — used by `--next-cycle` and `--audit-main` | *may this reach `main` outside a certified snapshot?* | **passes the PREFIX** (`docs/`) and **fails the SUFFIX** (`.md`, `.json`) |
| **`IMPACT_RULES`** — used by `--plan` | *which gates does this change select?* | **matches no rule**, and *"an unrecognised path is `platform`, never `none`"* |

⛔ **Neither knows `.toml` exists.** ⚡ **A single classifier being conservative is a fail-safe; two agreeing by coincidence is a gap that looks like corroboration** — **which is why this survived: every instrument agreed, and all of them were wrong in the same direction.**

### 📊 The cost, measured twice and reconciled

**`origin/main`, `--since=2026-08-08`, 932 commits. Predicate: ≥1 file matching `docs/coordination/**.toml`, AND every remaining file passes `_is_closeout()`.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Touching `docs/coordination/**.toml` | **187** |
| ⚡ **Disqualified SOLELY by the `.toml`** | 🔴 **157 — 17% of the week** |
| Of those, touching *only* those files | **45** *(Lane C's narrower question)* |

⚠️ **Both figures are correct and they answer different questions.** ⛔ **45 asks *"how many commits are nothing but a regenerated projection?"*; 157 asks *"how many would have been closeout-exempt but for the `.toml`?"*** — **and the second is the one the rule is about, because a commit touching `BACKLOG.md`, `LANE_COORDINATION.md` and `coordination.toml` is documentation in substance.**

📁 **At 45 this row reads *"a lane's regenerations are noisy."* At 157 it reads *"the accumulate rule has a 17% hole, concentrated in planning."* Same defect; only the second justifies the care the fix needs.**

### ⚠️ It puts two ratified rules in direct conflict, for exactly one lane

📁 **[D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *"a planning change that is not published has not been made."*** **So Product Office is REQUIRED to republish the projection whenever planning changes.**

📁 **§20e: *"documentation, claim commits, planning updates and execution-board maintenance accumulate until they accompany executable work — certifying them alone spends a full gate run proving a markdown table is still true, which is how a team learns to skip cycles."***

⛔ **Neither rule is wrong. The classifier is what makes them collide**, and it collides for the one lane whose output is mostly planning. ⚡ **Raised by Lane C, who is the lane it costs.**

### ⛔ The fix is NOT obviously "add `.toml`", and that is the whole difficulty

**`_is_closeout` is what stands between an uncertified commit and `main`.** 📁 **`infra/` is deliberately excluded from `CLOSEOUT_PATHS` precisely so that changing a gate cannot be waved through as a Closeout — [B-014](#b-014) is what that cost when it was not enforced.** ⛔ **Widening the suffix list is the same move in a different dimension.**

⚠️ **A `.toml` under `docs/coordination/` is generated and read only by `coordination.py` and by lanes polling.** ⚡ **But `CLOSEOUT_SUFFIXES` is not scoped to a directory, so admitting `.toml` admits it everywhere — including any future `.toml` that configures something.**

#### 🔴 Corrected 2026-08-16 — that sentence is false, and the counter-example is inside `docs/`

⛔ **`docs/coordination/modules.toml` is read by a GATE.** ✅ **Measured, not inferred — `infra/certification-guard.py:840`:**

```python
registry = tomllib.loads(_git("show", f"{commit}:docs/coordination/modules.toml"))
```

📁 **That is inside `--audit-claims`, which decides whether a claim commit was legal.** ⚡ **So there is a file under `docs/` that decides whether a gate passes — which is precisely the property `CLOSEOUT_PATHS` excludes `infra/` for.**

🔴 **This turns the caution above into a named failure mode.** **A suffix-based widening would make `modules.toml` Closeout-legal, so an ownership change could reach `main` outside a snapshot and silently alter what `--audit-claims` accepts.** ⛔ **[B-014](#b-014) is that exact failure, one directory over.**

✅ **The consequence for whoever rules on this: the fix must be PATH-based, never suffix-based.** ⚠️ **`coordination.toml` and `queues/*.toml` are projections; `modules.toml` is an operand of a gate. They share a directory and a file extension and nothing else that matters.**

#### ⚡ Both directions observed in one poll — 2026-08-16, cycle 237

**The row measures the cost as *157 commits treated as executable*, historically.** ✅ **It has now been watched deciding live, in both directions, from one repository state:**

| instrument | on | verdict | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`--next-cycle`** | `integration` | ⛔ **`da7d3d7f` is EXECUTABLE** → cycle available | `.toml` matches no `IMPACT_RULE` → `platform` |
| **`--audit-main`** | `main` | 🔴 **3 commits reached `main` uncertified** | the same `.toml` fails `CLOSEOUT_SUFFIXES` |

📁 **`da7d3d7f` is four planning files** — `BACKLOG.md`, `DECISION_REGISTER.md`, `coordination.toml`, `queues/lane-a.toml`. **Nothing it touches changes what the software does.**

⚡ **One blind spot, read as *too executable* by the warrant and *not documentary enough* by the audit, in the same minute.** ⛔ **A reader who saw only one of the two would conclude the classifier errs in one direction and could be tuned; seeing both makes it clear the classifier simply does not model the file.**

✅ **What this row does NOT do is propose the rule.** **It records the gap, the cost and the tension.** 📁 **The precedent is [B-122](#b-122): a change to what a gate MEANS went to the product owner with evidence and came back as a ruling.** **Same route.**

### ⚠️ The cost is narrower than first stated, and the remainder is QE's availability

**Observed 2026-08-15, hours after this row was filed.** ⛔ **Lane C released `TASK-1401` to clear Lane A's supply floor, and Lane A could not see it** — a released row lives on a Product Office branch until QE integrates it.

⚡ **QE integrated it WITHOUT certifying.** 📁 **Integration does not require certification; PROMOTION does** — so the row became visible on the ref every lane polls in one fast-forward, and it accumulates for `main` with the next executable work.

✅ **So the cost this row describes is narrower than *"every republication costs a cycle"*. It is *every republication costs a cycle AT PROMOTION TIME*** — **the difference between a lane waiting and a dashboard waiting**, and only the first is expensive.

⛔ **It does not dissolve the defect, and two things remain true.** **`--next-cycle` still calls a `.toml`-only range warranted**, so the repository still opens cycles for regenerated projections. ⚠️ **And a lane still cannot see a planning correction until QE integrates it** — 🔴 **which puts QE's AVAILABILITY on the critical path for a planning correction, rather than the gate.**

📁 **That last sentence is Lane C's and it is the part a cold reader would not predict:** **the mechanism this row is about turns out to cost less than it looked, and what is left is not a classifier problem at all.**

### 📁 How the evidence was gathered, because it failed once first

⛔ **QE published 159 and Lane C published 157. Neither disagreed with the other's data.** ⚡ **QE's FIRST script called `_is_closeout` and returned 157; a SECOND, written to split the count, re-expressed the condition as a prefix test and returned 159. QE ran both and published the later one.**

🔴 **That is [B-1002](#b-1002) reproduced in a throwaway script** — **a second implementation of a predicate, diverging from the authoritative one, invisible because both returned a plausible number.** ⛔ **The two commits are `99a0e8bb` and `c44a837f`, each carrying a `docs/design-snapshot/**.dc.html`: prefix passes, suffix fails.**

✅ **The practice recorded from it, and it is three-part:** ***a number needs its REF, its PREDICATE and its MAPPING.*** **2026-08-15 produced one failure of each — B-270's severity across four refs, this predicate, and `196 vs 198`'s mapping.**

> ⚡ **And the refinement that closes the gap *"state your predicate"* leaves open:**
>
> ## **If you compute a number twice, reconcile it before publishing either. If you computed it once, say which predicate — so somebody else can compute the second.**

### B-1003 · 🟠 The runbook hands every lane slot 0's port, and it had told QE so itself

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE documentation** — [`docs/RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md), seven `localhost:5432` sites |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **`:324` instructs a new lane to `CREATE DATABASE` on slot 0's server**, which is how `signora_lane_a`, `signora_lane_b`, `signora_lane_qe` and `signora_validate_lanea` came to sit on `5432` — ⚡ **exactly where [B-270](#b-270)'s destructive fixtures fall back to.** **The runbook does not merely mis-direct a lane at slot 0; it instructs them to create the decoy there** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-15, cycle 233.** ⛔ **`VERIFIED` is QE's to set and QE wrote the fix, so it stays `FIXED`** (§20e) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-15**, by QE citing the file to Lane A as a mitigation for B-270 **without opening it**. ⚡ **Caught by Lane C**, who had flagged the same lines and left them correctly |
| **Commit found** | **`9a01139c`** |

### 🔴 The part that is not a stale document

📁 **`RUNNING.md:64` is a note in QE's own file, addressed to QE:**

> *"The explicit `localhost:5432` examples further down this file are now correct only for slot 0. `make` targets derive the port and need no edit; **hand-run commands do. Left for QE**, whose file this is."*

⛔ **QE had a warning, in its own file, naming its own role, and cited the file to another lane without reading it.** ⚡ **The instance is *citing a file instead of using it*; the rule is *a peer's accuracy record is not evidence about a specific claim* — and here it was not even a peer's.**

⚠️ **A stale example a reader might notice is one thing; the same lines handed to a lane as the safe path around a data-destruction defect is another.** **The difference is entirely in the use, not in the text** — which is why `:64` is **kept** rather than deleted once discharged.

### ✅ The repair is derivation, and it is scoped by measurement

⛔ **Substituting `5732` for `5432` would trade one stale constant for four** and put the file back here the next time a lane is added or retired. 📁 **`signora_lane_b` is in there today naming a lane closed 2026-08-12 — that failure has already happened once.**

⚡ **And `:382` carries its own fix one row below itself:** the `SIGNORA_REDIS_URL` row already says *"index 0 is human review's. Substitute your environment's index"*, and the `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL` row directly above it does not. **A one-row inconsistency in a two-row table — the repair needs no new wording, only its neighbour's own pattern.**

⚠️ **Scope narrowed by Lane C's measurement:** an inline `VAR=x cmd` in a recipe **overrides an exported variable**, so a shell poisoned by the old runbook is still safe on the `make` targets. ⛔ **What the document must protect is hand-run commands and `:324`'s `CREATE DATABASE`** — **and `:324` is the one no guard can reach, because it runs before any test does.**

🔴 **The fix cannot state a database name.** [B-271](#b-271) proved the derivation and the compose file disagreed about it, so the runbook says **how to find out** — `psql … -c "select datname from pg_database"` — rather than what the answer is. ⚡ **`pg_database` is the only operand that cannot be stale.**

### ✅ What shipped, and one thing it found about QE itself

**The allocation table is now slot-based with PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO port columns, GENERATED from `infra/environments.py` rather than typed.** ⛔ **Six command sites derive; none quotes a port.** ✅ **`RUNNING.md:64` is KEPT and marked discharged** — it records a warning that sat there, addressed to QE, while QE cited the file without opening it.

⚡ **`backend/tests/test_runbook_allocation_table.py` — 11 cases — makes the table's drift a failing gate rather than a discovery.** 📁 **Deliberately a check and NOT a deletion, which is the opposite of [B-1001](#b-1001)'s repair**: there a reference carried everything the copy did; **here the table earns its place, because `--exports` answers only for the clone you are standing in and cannot show you that Lane A is slot 2.** ✅ **So the copy stays and stops being trusted.**

**Fire-tested five ways: drift one port → 1 red · delete the `Lane E` row → 3 red · put a `5432` command back inside a fence → 1 red · swap two columns on one row → 1 red · rename the header → GREEN**, ⚠️ **which is honest and is recorded: the parser is positional and does not read the header, so a rename is invisible to it while a reorder is not.**

⛔ **QE wrote the corrected table from inference and got it wrong** — **`lane-qe` recorded as slot 2 when it is slot 1, and `lane-e` omitted entirely** — **one minute after writing *"no lane types a port."* ⚡ Caught by generating the table from `environments.py` instead**, which is now how it is produced. **`test_every_environment_has_a_row` is the case that would have caught the omission.**

🔴 **And the repair surfaced QE's own environment.** **`backend/.env` read `localhost:5432/signora_lane_qe`** — ⛔ **slot 0's cluster, and QE was one of the four `signora_lane_*` databases it had cited as evidence for `:324` being their producer.** ✅ **QE's own stack is now up on `5632`, migrated to `0056`, `.env` repointed, Redis moved off human review's `6379`, and 446 Security Invariants pass against it.** ⚡ **QE had been running on slot 0's server the entire time, because nothing ever told it otherwise — which is the clearest possible argument for the table carrying port columns.**

### B-1002 · 🟠 The promotion guard's idea of CERTIFIED diverged from the certification package's, and the missing condition was the one the product owner had just changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py), `_satisfied` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a record that never executed a required gate was PROMOTABLE.** ⚡ **[B-122](#b-122)'s scenario exactly**: `frontend-suite` was absent from 228 runs, and **absence was never a failure here**, so the guard would have passed every one of them |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-15.** ⛔ **`VERIFIED` is QE's to set and QE wrote the fix, so it stays `FIXED`** (§20e) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-15**, by QE investigating **[B-435](#b-435)**, Lane C's row that `infra/` sits outside the type gate. ⚡ **The three `mypy` errors were the symptom; this is what was under them** |
| **Commit found** | **`c411aaa3`** |

> ⚠️ **Distinct from [B-435](#b-435), which stays open.** **B-435 is *`infra/` is not type-checked* — 15 of 25 files fail when checked directly, and widening the gate is a change to what a check *means* ([B-131](#b-131)) that belongs to whoever owns `infra/`.** ⚡ **This row is the defect B-435 exposed in one file, and only that file is repaired.** ⛔ **The other five `ruff` findings in it are pre-existing and deliberately untouched** — measured against `HEAD` before editing, 6 findings after and 5 before, and **the one that is mine is the one that went away.**

### 🔴 What it was

📁 `_satisfied()` was a **second implementation** of the certification predicate, and its docstring claimed a parity it did not have: *"Derived exactly as `CertificationRun.satisfied` derives it."*

| `Record.failures` | the guard |
|---|---|
| dirty tree | ✅ |
| any recorded gate failed | ✅ |
| any scenario failed | ✅ |
| coverage below the floor | ⚠️ **yes — against a hardcoded `95.0`** |
| 🔴 **a `REQUIRED_GATES` member did not run** | ⛔ **absent; the file never referenced `REQUIRED_GATES` at all** |

⛔ **Four of five, and the missing one is the one that changed on 2026-08-15.** 📁 **`for gate in run.get("gates") or []` meant a record with no `gates` key iterated zero times, produced zero failures, and read as satisfied** — the empty-array class `36-empty-array-checks.md` found in nine CHECK constraints, which `REQUIRED_GATES`' own comment already names: *"a run recording no gates at all would otherwise satisfy 'every gate passed' vacuously."* **The package defended against it. The guard did not.**

### ✅ The fix — two named predicates, because there were always two questions

| | asks | required-gate check |
|---|---|---|
| **`_satisfied`** | *did this run's recorded gates pass?* — **about the past** | ⛔ **no, deliberately** |
| **`_promotable`** | *may this be promoted **now**?* — **about today** | ✅ **yes** |

**Three call sites moved to `_promotable`: the promotion gate, `--guard-check`, and the certified-commits listing.** **`--audit-main` and the planning floor keep the historical one.** ✅ **`REQUIRED_GATES` and `MINIMUM_COVERAGE` are imported from `record.py`, never restated** — [B-1001](#b-1001)'s rule, applied the same day it was written.

**Verified live:** `ac622c24ad30`, a six-gate record, is **REFUSED** for promotion naming `eslint` and `frontend-suite`; `136f112bea79` reads `8 of 8 required`; **`--audit-main` is unchanged at 208 / 1679 / 5.**

### 🔴 QE's stated reason for the split was WRONG, and the fire test is what found it

⛔ **QE wrote that making `_satisfied` strict would make `--audit-main` refuse 209 commits on `main`.** ✅ **Fire-tested. It does not.** **The audit accepts *an ancestor of a certified commit that is itself on `main`*, and a certified commit near the tip vouches for everything behind it** — with the predicate made strict the audit still prints *the guarantee holds*.

⚠️ **The 209 was a real measurement of the wrong quantity** — commits the two predicates *disagree about*, which is not the quantity the audit consumes. 📁 **A number consumed without its mapping, produced while writing [B-1000](#b-1000) about exactly that.**

⚡ **The design survives on the argument the fire test found instead.** **`certified_all` is EMPTY whenever no stored record satisfies the current set — precisely the window between widening `REQUIRED_GATES` and the first run under it.** ⛔ **With nothing to be an ancestor of, every non-Closeout commit on `main` becomes a violation simultaneously.** **A historical audit whose verdict depends on a gate added this morning is not a historical audit.** ✅ **And independently, the product owner ruled it: *"the records remain historical records under the gate set that existed at the time."***

### ✅ 13 tests, fire-tested four ways

**Dropping the required-gate loop → 3 red · restoring `or []` → 1 red · making `_satisfied` strict → 2 red · re-hardcoding the coverage floor → 1 red.**

⚡ **The `or []` result is the useful one and it is recorded in the test.** **Only `no-scenarios-key-at-all` goes red** — the four `gates` cases are **double-protected** by `_promotable`'s required-gate check and do not isolate `_entries` at all. ⛔ **`scenarios` has no `REQUIRED_SCENARIOS` backstop, so it is the only case carrying that guarantee**, and it is the least obvious member of the list.

### B-1001 · 🟢 This register carried a second copy of the identifier allocation table, and it had been wrong for thirteen days

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE register** — [`docs/BUGS.md`](BUGS.md), *Identifier blocks* |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟢 — ⛔ **it caused no collision that can be traced to it.** ⚠️ **It could only ever mislead in one direction: a lane reading it would believe its block was unallocated**, and the reasonable response to that is to ask rather than to guess |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-15.** The copy is replaced by a reference to [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §20e |
| **Found** | **2026-08-15**, by QE recording its own newly allocated `B-1000`–`B-1099` range and noticing the register it was writing into disagreed with the constitution it had just edited |
| **Commit found** | **`6d4f9fca`** |

### 🔴 What it said

📁 A one-row table listing **Lane B only**, under: *"Only Lane B's block has been stated to Lane B. The blocks for Lane A, QE and the unclaimed lanes are the product owner's to allocate, and this table is deliberately incomplete rather than guessed."*

⚡ **The caution was exactly right when written.** ⚠️ **The product owner allocated every block later the same day** — `CLAUDE.md` §20e now carries seven actors, two of them with a second range each. **The copy was never edited to follow**, and there was no mechanism by which it would be.

> 📁 **Lane C's §5h names this class precisely:** *"the copy is never wrong when written; it is wrong the first time the registry grows, and nothing connects the two events."*

⛔ **This one is worse than the general case in one respect and better in another.** **Worse:** it stated its own incompleteness as a *deliberate* choice, so a reader had every reason to trust that the absence was current. **Better:** it advertised the absence rather than hiding it, which is why nothing was built on it.

### ✅ The fix is a deletion

**The table is replaced by a pointer to the one authoritative location.** ⛔ **No synchronisation, no checker** — **the guard against a copy drifting is not having the copy** (§2). ⚡ **The same act removes the defect and the mechanism that produced it**, which is the only repair of this class that does not leave a fourth thing to maintain.

### B-1000 · 🟡 A correct diagnostic is produced and the reading discards it — SEVEN instances, TWO lanes, and the row was scoped to one of them

> 🔴 **RESCOPED 2026-08-16.** **This row was filed as *"QE skipped a mandatory Closeout activity… because it read `state-check`'s exit code as a verdict"*, and its `Module` said **QE process**.** ⛔ **It now holds seven instances and the seventh is Lane C's.** ⚡ **A repository-wide class filed against one lane is invisible to the other lanes committing it** — **which is this row's own defect, applied to this row.**
>
> **The class, stated once:** ✅ **an instrument produced the correct answer and the consumer discarded it.** ⛔ **Never the instrument being wrong.** 📁 **Its mirror is [B-1009](#b-1009), where the instrument was fine and the QUESTION was wrong.**
>
> | # | who | the discard |
> |---|---|---|
> | ① ② ③ | QE | an **exit code** read as a verdict |
> | ④ | QE | **`tail`** removed the diagnostic |
> | ⑤ | QE | **`\|\|`** printed a finding the push was not gated on |
> | ⑥ | QE | **`\|\|`** ran a second command nobody authorised |
> | ⑦ | **Lane C** | **`>/dev/null 2>&1`** on the one command that reports a silent failure |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | ⚠️ **Repository-wide practice, not a lane's** — originally *"QE process"*, and see the rescope above |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **nothing uncertified reached `main`**; `--audit-main` is clean across 208 certified, 1679 ancestors and 1 Closeout. ⚠️ **The board asserted a state one cycle stale**, which is the §2 class: a record every lane reads, trusted precisely because nothing else contradicts it |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-15.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's to set and QE fixed it, so it stays `FIXED`** — ⛔ **QE never verifies its own work** (§20e) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-15, cycle 232 poll**, by QE re-reading `state-check`'s *findings* rather than its exit code — ⛔ **one cycle after the same output had already printed it** |
| **Commit found** | **`6d4f9fca`** |

### 🔴 What happened

📁 **Cycle 231's Closeout commit `6d4f9fca` touched `PROJECT_STATUS.md` and `SESSION_HANDOFF.md`.** ⛔ **Activity 3 of eleven — *reconcile the execution board* — did not run**, so the board stamped `ac622c24` (cycle 229) while the dashboard named `136f112bea79`. ⚠️ **Every prior cycle got this right**: `810b27d9`, `f5391c2e`, `41b5ce4b` and `8055afe5` each moved the stamp.

### 🔴 The real defect is the reading, not the omission

⚡ **QE ran `infra/state-check.py`, saw `exit=0`, and published *"state-check exit=0"* as evidence the cycle was clean.** ⛔ **The finding was in that same output**, four lines above the exit code.

> **`state-check` is advisory by construction and never fails** — *"each of these has more than one correct resolution, and choosing between them is a governance decision."* **A zero exit means the checker ran to completion. It has never meant the repository agrees with itself.**

📁 **This is the third time in one cycle QE read an exit code as a verdict** — the `git branch -f` refusal that printed a `PINNED` banner over a move that never happened, the rejected `integration` push whose code was printed rather than gated on, and this. ⚡ **The pattern is one thing: an instrument answering a narrower question than the one asked, and its cheerful answer being consumed as the answer to the wider one.**

### 🔴 A fourth instance, while this row was being written

⛔ **QE pushed the repair to `main`, ran `--audit-main | tail -6`, and read *"the guarantee holds."*** 📁 **`_audit_main` reads `rev-list RULE_RATIFIED_AT..main` — the LOCAL ref**, which was still at `6d4f9fca`. **The audit vouched for a `main` three commits older than the one just published.**

⚡ **The guard was not wrong and was not silent.** **Its first two lines were `note — 3 commit(s) on \`origin/main\` are not in this clone's \`main\`` and the same for `integration`** — `_behind_origin()` exists for precisely this, and its docstring says so: *"A fetch updates `origin/integration`; it does not move `integration`."* ⛔ **`tail -6` cut both notes off.**

> 📁 **This is Lane A's lesson from the same week, arriving at QE**: they tailed a gate run to four lines and discarded the diagnostic on a Security Invariant failure — *"the one output you cannot regenerate."* ⚠️ **Here the diagnostic was regenerable and QE still had to be told twice.**

### 🔴 A FIFTH instance, 2026-08-16 — the check printed the answer and the next command did not consume it

**QE ref-pushed `origin/lane-c-sync` to `integration` after running its own executable-path check.** ⛔ **The check found one, printed it, and the push ran anyway:**

```bash
git diff --name-only origin/integration..origin/lane-c-sync \
  | grep -E "^(backend|frontend|infra|apps)/" || echo "  no executable paths"
git push -q origin origin/lane-c-sync:refs/heads/integration      # ← not gated on the line above
```

**Output:** `infra/coordination.py` — **then `pushed`.**

⚠️ **`||` fires when grep finds NOTHING.** ⛔ **So the guard printed a hit and the `||` correctly did not fire, and the push was on the next line rather than in an `&&`.** ⚡ **The check was right, visible, and inert.**

### ⚠️ What this did and did not violate, stated precisely rather than comfortably

⛔ **It is NOT a certification breach.** 📁 §20e: *"Integration does not require certification; PROMOTION does."* **A ref push to `integration` is mechanically the same fast-forward QE performs anyway**, and `infra/coordination.py` will be certified before it can reach `main` — `--audit-main` guarantees that independently.

🔴 **What it breached is QE's own stated basis for the technique.** **The direct-ref-push shortcut was justified — in writing, to two lanes, twice — on the ground that the content was PLANNING-ONLY.** ⛔ **This push was not, and QE published the justification and then acted against its own evidence in the same command block.**

⚠️ **And `infra/` is the one directory §20e singles out**: *"`smoke.sh`, `disaster-recovery.sh`, `state-check.py` and the compose files decide whether a gate passes, so changing one changes what certification means."* 📁 **`state-check` invokes `infra/coordination.py --check`.** ✅ **The change itself is [B-437](#b-437)'s repair, is Lane C's under D-022, and is small and good** — ⛔ **which is exactly the condition under which a bypassed check costs nothing and teaches the wrong lesson.**

### ⚡ Why it belongs on THIS row and not a new one

**Same defect, fifth costume: an instrument produced the right answer and the reading discarded it.** 📁 **Instances one to three read an exit code as a verdict; the fourth let `tail` remove a diagnostic; this one let shell control flow remove one.** ⛔ **In every case the instrument was correct and QE's consumption of it was not** — **which is the mirror of [B-1009](#b-1009), where the instrument was fine and the QUESTION was wrong.**

✅ **The repair is the same one B-1009 arrived at from the other side: gate on the result, or do not print it.** **A check whose output does not change what happens next is Decorative Logic in a shell script.**

### 🔴 A SIXTH instance, twenty minutes after the fifth, and it is worse

**Building cycle 239's candidate:**

```bash
git merge --ff-only origin/lane-a-product-surface        # ok — integration → 9aa08c26
git merge --ff-only origin/lane-qe || git rebase -q origin/lane-qe   # ← the defect
```

⛔ **The `--ff-only` correctly failed. The `||` then rebased `integration` — sitting at LANE A'S TIP — onto `lane-qe`**, replaying their seven commits under new hashes. **Then QE pushed, before checking what the fallback had done.**

✅ **Verified after the fact and nothing was lost**: all seven present by subject, `git cherry e0d6443a HEAD` reports **0** duplicates, `e0d6443a` still an ancestor. ⛔ **The tree is correct. `9aa08c26` is no longer an ancestor of `integration`, so a lane checking for it gets a false negative** — 📁 **the same class as the orphaned board SHAs one cycle earlier.**

### ⚠️ Why this is worse than instances one to five

**Those were passive: an instrument produced a correct answer and the reading discarded it.** 🔴 **This one was ACTIVE — the fallback performed a different operation than the one that failed, and QE published the result before inspecting it.** ⚡ **A `||` is not a diagnostic being ignored; it is a second command nobody authorised.**

### 🔴 The deeper error, which is not about shell syntax at all

⛔ **QE put its own DOCUMENTATION-ONLY branch into a cycle carrying a lane's four slices.** ✅ **The lane's branch was fast-forwardable alone** — taking it by itself would have moved nothing of theirs, and `lane-qe` could have waited a cycle at zero cost.

📁 **Two cycles earlier QE argued to Product Office, in writing, that a planning batch which blocks nobody must not force a lane to rebase.** ⚡ **QE then did precisely that to a lane, with its own branch, and the branch in question was four bug-register rows.** ⛔ **The rule was applied to somebody else's convenience and not to QE's own.**

✅ **The operational cost was small and was stated to the lane immediately** — their work was already inside the running certification, so they reset rather than re-run. ⛔ **The cost that matters is that QE spent a lane's trust to save itself one cycle of waiting.**

### ⚠️ A TWELFTH — QE calls a branch *idle* on evidence that cannot show it, every cycle

**Closeout stage 6 fast-forwards *"every idle lane branch"* and never touches *"a lane in active development"* ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).** ⛔ **QE decides which is which with:**

```bash
git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/$b main    # → "has this ref anything main lacks?"
```

🔴 **That is not the question §20e asks.** ⚡ **It answers *has this branch PUSHED anything*, and QE has been reporting the answer as *idle*.**

**Reported by Lane A, 2026-08-16, about themselves:**

> ⛔ ***"`lane-a-product-surface` — ahead 22, behind 7. Twenty-two commits, none of them pushed. The branch was the most active thing in my session."***

### ✅ The action was safe, and NOT for the reason QE gave

**The ancestor gate is what made it safe**: `git push origin main:refs/heads/<branch>` only succeeds where the old value is already an ancestor of `main`, **so no pushed work can be destroyed and no unpushed local commit is reachable by it at all.** ⚡ **Verified: `origin/lane-a-product-surface` was an ancestor, so the push moved a ref whose content was already promoted.**

⛔ **But QE justified it as *"both your branches were idle"*, and that word is doing work the evidence does not support.** 📁 **Lane A's framing is the correct one:**

> ⚡ ***"A ref with no unpushed work and a ref whose work is invisible to you look identical from where you stand, and only one of them is idle."***
>
> ⛔ ***"It cost nothing here because a fast-forward cannot destroy unpushed local commits. It would have cost something under any operation that could — and 'idle' is the word that would have justified one."***

### 🔴 A THIRTEENTH, and it is this row's ORIGINAL failure repeating — a skipped Closeout activity

**Cycle 242's Closeout ran every activity except 9 — the release summary.** ⛔ **`PROJECT_STATUS.md` was updated for figures, `SESSION_HANDOFF.md` and `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` were refreshed, `RUNNING.md` gained three hazards — and no summary was published.**

⚠️ **It surfaced only because cycle 243's summary anchored on *"cycle 242"* and the assertion failed.** ⚡ **Had the anchor been looser, or had QE used `replace_all`, the omission would have been invisible and the record would simply have skipped a cycle.**

📁 **That is this row's FIRST instance repeating**: *"QE skipped a mandatory Closeout activity and reported the cycle clean."* ⛔ **Activity 3 then, activity 9 now.** ✅ **Written late and marked as written late — [§2](../CLAUDE.md): correct a claim about the present, date a record of the past.**

### ⚠️ What actually caught it, and it was not a checklist

**An `assert count == 1` on an anchored replacement.** ⚡ **The discipline of refusing to edit without asserting uniqueness is what turned a silent omission into a failing script** — 📁 **and it is the same technique that caught two stale figures at [B-1008](#b-1008).** ⛔ **`state-check` does not check that a cycle published a summary, and neither does anything else.**

### 🔴 It recurred within the hour, in the handover that acknowledged it

**QE briefed a fresh Lane C session with:**

> ⛔ ***"`lane-c-sync a93bfe0a` — fast-forwarded, clean."***

**Their reply, having verified rather than accepted:** *"`lane-c-sync` had two unpushed commits and the tree had two uncommitted files, so *fast-forwarded, clean* was true of neither."*

### ⚠️ The two halves are different and only one is QE's error

✅ **The SHA was accurate when measured.** 📁 **Their commits are timestamped `2026-08-17 03:03`–`03:09`; the Closeout that set `a93bfe0a` was `2026-08-16 20:15`.** ⛔ **`origin/lane-c-sync` genuinely was `a93bfe0a` when the briefing was written, and their new session pushed afterwards.** ⚡ **That is `integration` keeps moving, working as designed — not staleness.**

🔴 **`clean` is the error, and it is the same word-class as `idle` above.** **QE meant *the branch carries no held work*; it reads as *your working tree is clean*, which QE cannot see and did not check.** ⛔ **Twice in one hour, and the second time inside the message acknowledging the first.**

### ✅ What it cost, and what it nearly cost

**Nothing, because the lane verified.** ⚠️ **But `clean` is the word that would justify a `reset --hard`, and the tree held two uncommitted `infra/` files** — **one a `NameError` (`sys.stderr` with no `import sys`) in a file-not-found branch, so the module loads, every happy path works, and it waits for the one run that needed the diagnostic.** 📁 **The failure mode this repository keeps finding: the tool works right up to the moment it has something to tell you.**

### ✅ The repair is a word, not a check

**The check is correct and stays.** ⛔ **What changes is the claim QE publishes from it:** ✅ ***"no pushed work"*, never *"idle"***.

⚠️ **And where the stronger claim is genuinely needed — before anything that COULD destroy unpushed work — QE asks the lane**, because `git log origin/<branch>..<branch>` runs only on their machine. **QE cannot determine lane activity from remote refs and must stop implying that it can.**

📁 **Same family as the other eleven, and the most routine of them**: **an instrument answering correctly, a narrower question than the word attached to its answer** — **in a step QE runs every single cycle.**

### ⚠️ An EIGHTH, caught BEFORE it ran — and it is about fire-testing itself

**QE announced the mutation it would use to test a suspected Decorative Logic finding: collapse `None` into `[]` inside `_running_containers`.** ⛔ **Lane C stopped it, having already run it:**

```python
# backend/tests/test_lease_dead_pid_asks_the_stack.py
monkeypatch.setattr(lease, "_running_containers", lambda: containers)
```

⚡ **The tests replace the function wholesale, so mutating its body is never executed by them.** ✅ **Verified independently by QE from the source.** ⛔ **The mutation reports `6 passed`, and QE would have concluded the distinction WAS load-bearing — the opposite of the truth.**

> 🔴 **A mutation applied to a function the test replaces proves nothing about the test — and it fails GREEN, which is the direction that misleads.**

📁 **This matters more than the other seven because fire-testing is the technique this repository leans on hardest.** ⚠️ **A mutation that should kill a test and does not reads as *the test is weak*; a mutation that never executed produces identical output and means *nothing was measured*.** ⛔ **Two opposite conclusions from one green.**

✅ **The rule that follows: before trusting a surviving mutation, confirm the mutated code is on the path the test executes.** **The working mutation here was in `holder()`, not in the stubbed helper.**

### 🔴 A SEVENTH instance, and it is Lane C's — which is what rescoped this row

**Lane C reported a notice `WITHHELD` whole and said *"nothing told me."*** ⛔ **False, and they found it themselves by fire-testing rather than reading:**

```python
# infra/coordination.py:1577
for _lane, _spec in sorted(_notice_health(rows).items()):
    print(f"coordination: NOTICE WITHHELD for {_lane} — {_spec}")
```

**A bare `print()` — stdout.** ⛔ **And their own command, repeatedly:** `python3 infra/coordination.py >/dev/null 2>&1`.

⚡ **B-427's fix had been working the entire time, and its diagnostic was routed to `/dev/null` by the office that wrote it.** ✅ **Verified independently by QE: no `file=sys.stderr`, so `>/dev/null` alone silences it.**

> ⛔ **Their formulation, and it is sharper than the row's own:** ***"the one command whose stderr I silenced is the one command that reports a silent failure."***

### ⚠️ QE defended them against this and was wrong on the facts

**QE argued the recurrence *"reads as carelessness and I do not think it was"*, on the ground that B-427 predicted no such suppression.** ⛔ **Lane C declined half of that and produced the line number.** ✅ **The defence was generous and unfounded, and is recorded as wrong rather than quietly dropped** — 📁 **a peer inheriting an incorrect exoneration is the same failure as a peer inheriting an incorrect finding.**

### ⛔ And one claim in the original report does NOT reproduce, withdrawn by its author

**Lane C told QE and Lane A the suppression was caused by naming `TASK-495`.** ⛔ **Re-run against today's tree it produces no withheld line at all.** ✅ **They withdrew the mechanism rather than substituting a better guess** — ⚡ ***"something moved underneath it, which is this week's fourth instance of that shape and I will not add a fifth by inventing which."***

📁 **The authoring rule they wrote stands and is an improvement; the diagnosis attached to it does not, and is corrected in the file rather than left to be believed.**

✅ **Re-run against the synchronized ref: 1891 commits, 208 certified, 1679 in-snapshot, 4 Closeout, no violations.** ⚡ **The count that exposed it was `1 Closeout` — unchanged after adding three Closeout-class commits.** **A number that should have moved and did not is the cheapest signal in this class, and it is the one to look for**: a green verdict has no such tell.

### ⚠️ The checker named a cause that was not the cause

📁 It reported *"the board has gone backwards — the B-100 signature, where a rebase keeps a lane's side of a shared table."* ⛔ **Measured: the stamp is byte-identical on `main`, `integration`, `lane-qe` and `lane-a-2b`.** **Nothing was lost in a rebase — the edit was never made.**

⚡ **Worth more than the correction itself.** **A check that detects a symptom is not thereby a diagnosis**, and the guess is stated in the same prose as the observation. **Believing it would have sent QE searching rebase history for an omission.** ⛔ **Not filed against `state-check`**: the observation was correct and load-bearing, and softening its explanatory sentence would make it less useful, not more.

### ✅ The fix, and why it is not a checker

**The board is reconciled and the stamp corrected.** ⛔ **No new check is added.** A checker for *"did Closeout run all eleven activities?"* would be a fourth place recording what the eleven are, and **the copy is never wrong when written; it is wrong the first time the list grows.** ⚡ **What actually failed already had an instrument — `state-check` printed the finding.** **The repair is that QE reads findings, not exit codes**, and the evidence for whether it holds is the next cycle's board stamp rather than a green tick.

**Lane A reported building `Actor` with `person_id` and deliberately no display-name field, citing `C-024`.** ✅ **The DECISION is right**: [C-203](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is `DEFERRED` on a stated trigger ([TASK-429](BACKLOG.md), M-E) and [TASK-427](BACKLOG.md) forbids a person's name anywhere.
