### 📁 The family, and why the register alone cannot close it

**Third instance of one class in five days:** **[B-263](#b-263)** — `C-210` held by two lanes · **[B-259](#b-259)** — what a per-file replace costs · **this one**. ⚠️ **The common element is that an identifier moved and the things citing it did not**, and ⛔ **`infra/state-check.py` cannot see it: it checks for DUPLICATE allocations, and this is a duplicate MEANING under a unique id.**

✅ **A check that would catch it exists in outline** — *does any file outside the register cite a `C-` id whose row is `CLOSED`, in a comment that reads as an open question?* ⛔ **Not built here, and not proposed as a row: it is one heuristic away from noise, and three instances is not yet evidence of a fourth.**

### B-437 · 🟠 The one channel this office has to the lanes discards 92% of every notice, and keeps the oldest half

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Platform Foundation** — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py) `_notice`, and this office's authoring practice ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it silently deleted a briefing written to stop a cost that had already recurred three times, and nothing reported the deletion** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-16.** ⚠️ **Two halves and only one was code** |
| **Found** | ⚡ **A routine poll.** **The published `origin/coordination` ref was 172 commits and two days stale, and republishing it put the notice in front of me** |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```
$ python3 -c "import tomllib; n=tomllib.load(open('docs/coordination/notices.toml','rb'))['Lane A']['notice']; print(len(n))"
5022
```

📁 **`_NOTICE_MAX = 400`, and the cut is `text[:400]`.**

**Expected.** ⚡ **That a lane reads the notice this office most recently wrote.**

**Actual.** 🔴 **A lane reads the FIRST 400 characters — 8% of it — and appending a new block puts the new text past the cut.** ⛔ **So the newest notice is the one that never arrives.**

### 🔴 What was actually lost, which is the reason this is 🟠 and not 🟢

**Three blocks, separated by `||`. Only the first was ever delivered — and the notice itself describes that first block as retired.**

| Block | Delivered? | What it said |
|---|---|---|
| ⓐ **The Help Center reasoning** | ✅ **Yes** — ⛔ **and it is the one already marked superseded** | A correction this office had itself corrected |
| ⓑ **`REBASE BEFORE YOUR NEXT PUSH`** | ⛔ **NEVER** | 📁 ***"third cycle it has cost QE time rather than you"*** — **with the measurement, the conflict, and the one command** |
| ⓒ **B-424 retired** | ⛔ **NEVER** | Its own closing line: *"this office believed it had routed something it had not"* |

> ⚠️ **ⓑ is the sharp one.** **A briefing written because a cost had recurred three times was never delivered once — and the cost recurred again on 2026-08-16, when Lane A's branch needed a rebase before QE could take it.**
>
> ⛔ **The notice that would have prevented it had been sitting in the file, published, for days.**

### ✅ The fix, and the generator was NOT the wrong half

📁 **`_NOTICE_MAX`'s own docstring already says what this field is: *"One line, deliberately. A notice that grows into a message log becomes…"*** ⚡ **The generator was right and the authoring was wrong.**

⛔ **So the cap is NOT raised** — raising it would build exactly the message log [D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) forbids, and the projection is a pointer rather than a document.

✅ **What changed is that the deletion now announces its own size**, because *"TRUNCATED at 400 chars"* reads like a tidy ellipsis and **4,622 discarded characters are not an ellipsis**:

```
[…TRUNCATED — 4622 of 5022 characters (92%) WERE DISCARDED, and they are the
NEWEST: this field is one current line, REPLACED, never appended to. …]
```

✅ **And `notices.toml` now carries the rule at the top of the file, where the author is standing when they make the mistake.** **Lane A's notice is rewritten at 399 characters and survives whole.**

### ⚡ The general shape, and it is one this repository keeps finding

> **A limit that silently keeps the WRONG end is worse than one that refuses.** ⛔ **Both drop data; only one of them looks like it worked.**

📁 **The same class as [B-270](#b-270)'s `make -n`, which answered a smaller question than the one asked, and as QE's `--since` patch-id scan at [B-1009](#b-1009), which narrowed the set without saying so.** ⚡ **In all three the tool succeeded, returned a plausible answer, and said nothing about what it had left out.**

### B-436 · 🟠 The lease reclaims itself on a dead pid, which does automatically what QE correctly refused to do by hand

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Platform Foundation** — [`infra/environment-lease.py`](../infra/environment-lease.py) ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it destroys a run's environment, and the run is somebody else's** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-16.** ⚡ **The third behaviour this row said did not exist yet: a dead pid now ASKS THE STACK before reclaiming.** ⛔ **Neither *never reclaim* nor *always reclaim*** — **reclaim only where the stack is evidenced idle, and fall back to the previous behaviour only where there is no evidence either way.** ✅ **Strictly better, never worse**: where docker cannot be asked it does exactly what it did before, so a workstation without docker is unaffected rather than newly blocked. 🔴 **`None` and `[]` are deliberately not collapsed** — *docker answered, nothing running* against *nobody answered* — **and a test asserts the distinction, because every other test would still pass if they were merged.** **Was:** 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C, 2026-08-15** |
| ⚠️ **And it exposed a hidden input in the existing test** | 📁 `test_a_lease_held_by_a_dead_process_is_reclaimed` **passed on any workstation before this change, because nothing consulted docker.** ⛔ **Afterwards its result would depend on whichever containers happened to be running** — a hidden input ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)), and one that passes on a clean machine and fails on a developer's laptop with a stack up. ✅ **Pinned rather than left to the environment, and the half the class was missing — a dead pid must NOT reclaim a running stack — added beside it.** ⚡ **The guarantee the class is named for is unchanged: a killed run still does not block forever** |
| **Found** | ⚡ **Fire-testing the `BLOCKED` diagnostic after QE's near-miss.** **The test produced no output, which is how the auto-reclaim was found: there was no `BLOCKED` path to test** |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```python
# a lease record naming a pid that no longer exists
holder()          # → None, and the lease file is DELETED
acquire("x")      # → succeeds, takes the environment
```

**Expected.** ⚡ **What QE established the same day: *a dead pid is evidence about the record, not about the machine.***

**Actual.** 📁 **`holder()` reclaims silently, and its docstring states the reasoning:** *"A stale lease is reclaimed silently — it describes a process that no longer exists, and reporting it as a conflict would send the operator hunting for something that already died."*

⚡ **That reasoning is sound for the case it was written for — a crashed run leaving a lock nobody can clear.** 🔴 **It is wrong for the case QE hit: the recorded pid was dead AND another clone had a live run the record never knew about.** ⛔ **QE was contemplating `release --force`, judged that a dead pid did not prove the machine was free, and did not force. `holder()` would have done it for them, without the judgement and without the message.**

#### ⚠️ What is fixed here and what is NOT

✅ **The `BLOCKED` diagnostic now says what a dead pid does and does not prove**, and names two commands that check the machine rather than the record — `ss -ltn` for the ports, `pgrep -af` for runs in flight. 📁 **`OPERATING-MODE.md`: when a guard's output is advice, the advice is under test.**

⛔ **The auto-reclaim itself is NOT changed, deliberately.** ⚠️ **Removing it makes a crashed run a lock nobody can clear without `--force`, which is the failure its docstring was written against — and the two failure modes are opposites.** ⚡ **A correct fix probably checks the MACHINE before reclaiming (ports bound, processes matching) rather than trusting either the record or the pid, and that is a behaviour change to a gate every target depends on.**

> ⛔ **Not proposed here.** 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) and [B-131](#b-131)'s precedent: a bug row states the gap; changing what a guard decides is a decision.**

⚡ **QE's addition, and it is what makes it a ruling rather than a patch: the fix cannot be *"never reclaim"* and cannot be *"always reclaim"* — both failure modes are real and neither is hypothetical.** **It is a third behaviour that does not exist yet.**

#### 🔴 The near-miss reconstructed — QE, 2026-08-15, correcting their own account

**QE first reported this as *"I was entitled to `release --force` and chose not to."*** ⛔ **True of their intent, false about the mechanism: they would never have needed to force.**

| observed | what it means |
|---|---|
| `make dr` returned `Error 4` | ⚡ **so the recorded pid was ALIVE then** — a dead one is reclaimed silently and never blocks |
| `kill -0` on it a minute later | ⛔ **dead** |
| Lane A's own process | 🔴 **live throughout, and the record never knew about it** |

🔴 **So a simple RETRY of `make dr` — the obvious next move after a transient block — would have auto-reclaimed and run.** ⛔ **No force, no prompt, no `BLOCKED` message.**

> ### ⚠️ CORRECTED before this row reached `main` — QE, 2026-08-15, measuring their own worked example
>
> **QE's first account said the retry would have restarted *"PostgreSQL, Redis, the API, workers and the relay on another lane's live journey."*** ⛔ **It would not, and they measured it rather than defending it.**
>
> ```
> make dr    → docker-compose.prod.yml · signora-prod-postgres-1 · API 8100 · web 3100
> make e2e   → SIGNORA_APP_URL=http://localhost:3500   ← DERIVED; 3300 in Lane A's clone
> ```
>
> ✅ **Re-measured here before rewriting: different compose projects, different ports.** ⚡ **`make dr` restarts the PRODUCTION stack; Lane A's journey ran against Lane A's stack. The demonstrated damage is zero.**
>
> ⛔ **So the hazard class is real and this illustration of its cost was not.** **The true statement is narrower: a retry silently takes an environment the operator believes is held, with no message — and what that costs depends on what the two operations actually share, which the lease does not know and does not check.**

#### ⚡ Which raises the better question: what does the lease still guard?

📁 **Its own `BLOCKED` message says *"they share one production stack, one pair of review ports and one test database."*** ⛔ **After [B-271](#b-271) and the per-slot stride, two lanes share none of those.** **Measured across the eight leased targets:**

| | shares | |
|---|---|---|
| `smoke` · `dr` · `up` · `down` · ⚡ **`certify`** | 🔴 **the one production stack** (`docker-compose.prod.yml`, ports 3100/8100) | ✅ **serializing these is correct** |
| ⚠️ **`certify` also** | **slot 0's PostgreSQL cluster** — `database.py:79` pins `_HOST = "localhost:5432"` unconditionally | — |
| `test` · `e2e` · `product-demo` | ⚡ **nothing** — each resolves its own cluster and web port (`5932`/`3500` here, `5732`/`3300` in Lane A's) | ⚠️ **serialized anyway** |

⚡ **So the lease is workstation-wide over a set that partly stopped being shared**, and its message describes a world the migration removed for three of the eight. ⛔ **Not a second defect and not fixed here** — 📁 **it is the same ruling: what the lease protects and when it may reclaim are one question, and answering half of it is how the current halves came to disagree.**

⚡ **And the option space is narrower than *"a third behaviour that does not exist yet"* suggested.** ⛔ **The guard is not uniformly wrong: it is CORRECT for five targets and vestigial for three**, so *"stop guarding"* is the wrong ruling and **"guard what is actually shared"** is a per-target answer — **materially easier to rule on.**

> #### 🔴 `certify` was in the wrong column, and I put it there with the tool I had just warned about
>
> **This table first read *"`test` · `certify` · `e2e` · `product-demo` — shares nothing"*, measured with `make -n certify`, which shows `5932/signora` and nothing else.**
>
> ⛔ **`make -n` shows the RECIPE. It cannot show that `__main__.py:209` spawns `bash ./infra/smoke.sh`, which binds 3100 and 8100, nor that `database.py:71,79` creates the disposable database on `localhost:5432`.**
>
> ⚠️ **[B-270](#b-270) carries this sentence, written by this office earlier the same day: *"`make -n` shows what the parent sets; it cannot show what a child injects."*** 🔴 **I wrote the warning, in this file, and then measured a different property with the same tool and the same blind spot.**
>
> ✅ **Caught by QE, who checked it because it is the target they run every cycle.**

📁 **QE's own verdict on the near-miss stands and is the honest one: *"What saved it was not refusing to force. It was going to look at the machine instead of retrying the command"* — and they investigated because the record looked odd, not because they knew a retry was dangerous.**

#### ⚠️ Why this stays 🟠 and is not raised to 🔴

**The obvious argument for 🔴 is [B-270](#b-270)'s precedent — a documented command silently destroying another environment — and Lane A raised that one to 🔴 on exactly that ground.**

⛔ **It is not taken here, for a checkable reason.** 📁 **`infra/registers.py:34`: `blocks_promotion` is 🔴 **and** unresolved. **Raising this row would stop every lane's promotion** over a hazard that (a) leaves `main` correct, (b) now has its check written into the `BLOCKED` diagnostic, and (c) needs a ruling rather than a fix.

⚡ **And the correction above strengthens this rather than weakening it.** 📁 **[B-270](#b-270)'s 🔴 was a documented command destroying IRRECOVERABLE data with no mistake required.** ⛔ **B-436 is a silent acquisition whose demonstrated cost is currently zero, and no case producing damage can be written until somebody establishes what the lease still guards.** ⚠️ **QE's own note: had they not measured, they would have argued this row up to 🔴 on an example that does not hold.**

⚡ **Severity says how much it hurts; the blocking class says whether the repository can move.** ✅ **This hurts a lane's afternoon and does not stop the repository, and inflating it would spend the one signal that does.**

|---|---|

| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **nothing is failing today.** ⚠️ **But `infra/` decides whether a commit may be promoted, and no gate reads its types** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-17.** ⚡ **`make types-infra` gates the seven files that decide whether a commit may be promoted, and all seven are clean.** ⛔ **Fire-tested rather than declared**: reintroducing the exact `named` double-binding this row's sibling fixed makes the gate exit 1. **Was:** 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C, 2026-08-15** |
| 🔴 **This row's headline was already false when it was fixed** | ⛔ **It said *"the promotion guard is one of the files that does not type-check."*** ✅ **`certification-guard.py` types clean and so do `state-check.py` and `coordination.py`** — **cleared by earlier work, and nothing updated the row.** ⚡ **Recorded rather than quietly corrected: a bug row that overstates its own subject is read by whoever prioritises it** |
| ⚡ **What the gate caught on the day it was written** | ⛔ **None of it visible to any other gate, because `infra/` has no suite either — for these files `mypy` is not a supplementary check, it is the WHOLE net.** 🔴 **`decision-queue.py`: `sys.stderr` with no `import sys`, in the file-not-found branch** — the module loads, every happy path works, and the `NameError` waits for the one run that needed the diagnostic. 🔴 **`release-preflight.py`: `holders` bound TWICE in one function** — `list[Holder]` from `_listeners()` and `list[str]` from `_memory_pressure()` — **working only because the branch that rebinds it always returns `0`.** ⛔ **Move that block below the port checks and the preflight iterates strings looking for `.is_review_stack`, inside certification.** 🔴 **`environments.py`: `BY_NAME` bound THREE times** — an empty `Final` seventy lines up *(dead)*, the real comprehension, and a `.update()` with byte-identical contents *(a no-op)*. ✅ **`state-check.py`'s `named`, fixed the same day** |
| ⚠️ **Scoped to a named list, and why that is not a half-measure** | ⛔ **26 files carry 23 further errors.** **Gating `infra/` wholesale today means one unreviewable change or ignores that make the gate decorative.** ✅ **The list is what is clean AND load-bearing, so it can only grow** — **and a file joining it is a file somebody made pass.** 📁 **The remainder is not a task**: `implementation-status.py` 9 · `repository-dashboard.py` 5 · `unsaved.py` 2 · `review.py` 2 · `kpi.py` 2 · `coverage-debt.py` 2 · `project-history.py` 1 |
| **Found** | Running `mypy --strict` on a file I had just edited, and wondering whether the gate would have caught it |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
grep -n mypy Makefile        # → cd backend && uv run mypy .
python3 -m mypy --strict infra/certification-guard.py
```

**Expected.** ⚡ **The tooling that decides promotions is type-checked by the same gate as everything else.**

**Actual.** 📁 **The gate runs from `backend/`. `infra/` is at the repository root, so it is never in the checked tree.** 🔴 **Measured across all 25 files: 10 clean, 15 fail when checked directly.**

⚠️ **And the count is honest rather than alarming — some failures are artifacts of standalone checking.** 📁 `infra/validate.py`'s single error is `Skipping analyzing "tests.certification": missing library stubs`, which is a path problem and not a type problem.

🔴 **But not all of them are, and the worst is the one that matters most:**

```
infra/certification-guard.py:366  "object" has no attribute "__iter__" (not iterable)
infra/certification-guard.py:369  "object" has no attribute "__iter__" (not iterable)
infra/certification-guard.py:1421 Argument 1 to "len" has incompatible type "object"; expected "Sized"
```

⛔ **That is the file `infra/certification-guard.py --audit-main` runs from, and the one that refuses a promotion whose target is not certified.**

#### ⚠️ What this is NOT

⛔ **Not a claim that any of the 15 is a live defect**, and not a request to fix 15 files. ✅ **`coordination.py` and `registers.py` are clean, so the directory is not uniformly untyped** — which makes the absence of a gate the finding rather than the code.

⛔ **And explicitly not a proposal to widen the gate here.** 📁 **Changing what a gate covers is the [B-131](#b-131) class** — it is a change to what a check *means*, not one a bug row may make. **The row states the gap; ⛔ the remedy is a decision.**

#### 🔴 What is UNDER the type errors — QE, 2026-08-15, and it is why the row matters

**QE reproduced the three errors and then read the code they sit in. ⚡ The types are the symptom.**

📁 **`_satisfied()` in the promotion guard is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of the certification predicate, and its docstring claims a parity it does not have** — *"Derived exactly as `CertificationRun.satisfied` derives it."*

| `Record.failures` checks | the guard |
|---|---|
| dirty tree · a recorded gate failed · a scenario failed | ✅ |
| coverage below the floor | ⚠️ **yes, against a hardcoded `95.0`** |
| 🔴 **a `REQUIRED_GATES` member DID NOT RUN** | ⛔ **NO — the guard never imports or references `REQUIRED_GATES`** |

🔴 **Four of five, and the missing one is the check the product owner is being asked to change in [B-122](#b-122).**

⛔ **`for gate in run.get("gates") or []` means a record with no `gates` key yields zero failures and reads satisfied.** ⚡ **That is `36-empty-array-checks.md`'s defect in the promotion path, and `REQUIRED_GATES`' own comment names it**: *"a run recording no gates at all would otherwise satisfy 'every gate passed' vacuously."* **The package defends against it. The guard does not** — so B-122's 228 gateless-of-`frontend-suite` runs would all have read satisfied here.

✅ **The fix is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s: derive, do not reimplement.** `record.py` is stdlib-only, so the guard can import `REQUIRED_GATES` and `MINIMUM_COVERAGE` exactly as it already imports `bug_rows` from `registers`. ⚡ **The three type errors close in the same act** — narrowing `object` properly is what makes *"`gates` is not a list"* refusable instead of silently `[]`.

⚠️ **Split ownership, deliberately:** ✅ **the `certification-guard.py` half is QE's** — it is their instrument, and a Product Office edit to the thing that gates promotion is the wrong lane on the wrong file. ⛔ **This row stays `OPEN` for the other 12 unchecked files and for the gate-scope gap, which is Lane C's.**

##### ✅ FIXED by QE, 2026-08-15 — the guard half only

**`REQUIRED_GATES` and `MINIMUM_COVERAGE` are imported from `record.py` rather than restated, by PACKAGE path with `backend/` on `sys.path`** — ⚡ **the leaf form reproduced the very `missing library stub` artifact this row flagged for `validate.py`, so the argument was avoided by not producing it.** ✅ **`mypy --strict` on the file: 0 errors, from 3.**

**`_satisfied` split into two named predicates**: `_satisfied` asks *did this run's recorded gates pass?* (the past, no required-gate check, deliberately) and `_promotable` asks *may this be promoted now?* (with it). **Three call sites moved — the promotion gate, `--guard-check`, and the certified-commits listing.** ⛔ **`run.get("gates") or []` replaced by `_entries()`, which REFUSES a malformed record instead of reading it as empty.**

**Verified live: `ac622c24ad30` is now refused, naming `eslint` and `frontend-suite`; `136f112bea79` reads *8 of 8 required*; `--audit-main` byte-identical.**

> ⚡ **QE corrected its own prediction in the act of fixing it, and the correction is the better argument.** **They expected the strict predicate to refuse 209 commits on `main`; the fire test said it refuses none** — the audit accepts *an ancestor of a certified commit that is itself on `main`*, and a certified commit near the tip vouches for everything behind it. ⛔ ***"209 was a real measurement of the wrong quantity"*** — commits the two predicates disagree about, which is not what the audit consumes. **A number consumed without its mapping, while writing a row about that.**
>
> ✅ **The design survives on what the fire test found instead:** `certified_all` is **empty** in the window between widening `REQUIRED_GATES` and the first run under it, so with nothing to be an ancestor *of*, every non-Closeout commit on `main` becomes a violation at once. ⚡ ***A historical audit whose verdict depends on a gate added this morning is not a historical audit.***
>
> 📁 **And one finding worth keeping**: restoring `or []` turns **only** *no-scenarios-key-at-all* red. **The four `gates` cases are double-protected by `_promotable`'s required-gate check and isolate `_entries` not at all; `scenarios` has no `REQUIRED_SCENARIOS` backstop, so it is the only case carrying that guarantee** — and the least obvious one in the list.

### B-197 · 🟡 The promotion guard protects QE-written states in `BACKLOG.md` and reads `BUGS.md` not at all, so a `VERIFIED` bug can silently reopen

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py), `verified_regressions` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **it cannot promote an uncertified commit.** ⚠️ **It can promote one that reopens a defect somebody had closed**, and the promotion prints `PASS` while doing it |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13, cycle 221**, by QE reading two refs by hand after a cherry-pick conflict recurred — ⛔ **not by any gate.** ⚡ **Raised as a row by Lane A**, who said it should not stay a thing noticed twice by accident |
| **Commit found** | **`a5b3b8b1`** |

### 🔴 The scope, measured

📁 `_promote()` reads **`docs/BACKLOG.md` on both refs and nothing else** — ⛔ **`grep -c 'docs/BUGS.md"'` against the guard returns `0`.** 📁 `verified_regressions` checks `QE_TERMINAL_STATES` = **`VERIFIED` · `CERTIFIED` · `PROMOTED` · `DONE`**, which are **the four QE-written states of a TASK row.**

> ⛔ **The guard's subject is task lifecycle. The bug register is outside it entirely.**

### ⚠️ Two things it cannot see

**① A `FIXED` → `OPEN` regression — which happened.** 📁 Lane C's tip carried [B-253](#b-253) as `OPEN` while `integration` had Lane A's `FIXED`; **their revert was correct and its base was stale.** ✅ **Caught because a conflict recurred and QE read both refs. Nothing fired.**

**② A `VERIFIED` regression in `BUGS.md`** — ⚡ **worse, because [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) says *only QE sets `VERIFIED`* on a bug.** **The guard exists to stop QE's own judgements being undone by a rebase, and it protects that state in one register and not the other.**

### ✅ Worth building, on the test that declined [B-193](#b-193)

> ***If this check goes green, what will the reader stop asking?***

**A reader would stop asking whether a closed defect survived the rebase — and comparing `BUGS.md` states across the two refs genuinely answers that.** ⛔ **Unlike B-193 there is no ambiguity about what to compare**: 📁 `registers.py` already parses the rows and `verified_regressions` already implements the ordering. **The work is applying an existing function to a second register.**

⚠️ **Not built in the commit that files it**, so this is a claim about the present rather than an announcement of a fix.

### ⚠️ QE allocated two identifiers outside its own block, and its own instrument caught it

⛔ **These findings were first filed as `B-200` and `B-201`. Both collide with existing rows** — `B-201 · state-check reads the history table as a second claim` and `B-200 · Two colour tokens that do not exist`, **both on `main`, both Lane A's.**

✅ **`infra/state-check.py` reported it** — *"B- identifiers are allocated twice: B-200, B-201"* — **which is the check working; QE had simply not run it before pushing.**

🔴 **And QE's block is exhausted.** **97 of 100 used. The three gaps are `102`, `122` and `182`, and `102` and `182` are LIVE REFERENCES** — 14 and 3 mentions respectively. ⚡ **`122` was the only genuinely free identifier, so it carries the durable finding above and the cycle-229 coverage failure is recorded inside it rather than given an id QE does not have.**

⚠️ **This is the third block to exhaust** — Lane C's `400`–`499` and Lane A's `C-200`–`C-299` were both extended on the product owner's explicit instruction. ⛔ **QE will not grant itself a range.** **Raised for a ruling; until then QE has zero free identifiers.**

### 🔴 Cycle 229's certification failure, recorded here rather than in a row QE cannot number

⛔ **No prior certification is withdrawn or re-read.** **Each recorded truthfully what it ran**, and re-judging a past record against a gate set it never claimed is the defect [§2](../CLAUDE.md) forbids in the other direction.

⚠️ **Lane A declined to file this, reading it as *"B-131 in the concrete"*.** ⚡ **QE files it separately because the claims differ**: **B-131 is that planned gates are not recorded. This is that a defect reached `main` under a CERTIFIED stamp** — and the second is the one a reader of `PROJECT_STATUS.md` would want to know.

### B-199 · 🟢 The commit correcting a stale figure in `MANIFEST.md` left the row counting three different sets, and two per-file byte counts were never true of their files

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **None — `docs/design-snapshot/MANIFEST.md`**, the Design Snapshot ([D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |

| **Severity** | 🟢 · **Non-blocking.** ⛔ **All 36 content hashes are correct and were verified individually**, so no lane is misled about *content* and nothing is gated |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE, 2026-08-14, cycle 227.** ⚡ **Measured on `main`, never read from the fix's own description**: `screens/` holds **35 files · 2,769,237 bytes**, and **both figures are over the same set** — the three-denominator defect is gone. ✅ **`Authenticated Entry` reads 99,112 and `Reports` reads 48,965**, each matching the file it names, and **all 36 content hashes resolve.** ⛔ **Lane C's own framing is the better one and is recorded here**: *a stale total is wrong about the world and a reader catches it by measuring; three denominators is wrong about itself and no measurement catches it without knowing which set each quantity means.* **Was:** 🔵 `OPEN`, fix authored at `e39988aa` |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13, cycle 226**, during validation of the delivery that contains it |
| **Commit found** | **`3d7e2d9e`** — *"The snapshot manifest went stale again, in the row that documents its own staleness"* |

**Expected.** A summary row states quantities over one stated set, and a per-file byte figure equals the file it names.

**Actual.** Neither holds.

### ① The corrected header counts three different sets

`| **Contents** | ✅ **37 files · 2,769,237 bytes · 35 screen designs** |`

| Quantity | What it actually counts |
|---|---|
| **37 files** | **every file, including `MANIFEST.md` itself** |
| **2,769,237 bytes** | ⚡ **the 35 `.html` files ONLY** — exact to the byte |
| **35 screen designs** | the `.html` files |

**Measured at `3d7e2d9e`:** `.html` **35 files / 2,769,237 bytes** · `.css` **1 / 10,554** · `.md` **1 / 20,990**. Whole snapshot **2,800,781**; excluding `MANIFEST.md` **2,779,791**.

⛔ **And it disagrees with this same document twelve lines below**, which records **`snapshot files 31 → 36`** and **`Screen count 29 → 34`**. The screens difference is `Entry Coverage Review`, which **this document itself calls *"NOT a screen specification"*** — so **34 is the defensible count** and the header promotes an audit document to a screen.

⚠️ **The version replaced was internally consistent.** On 2026-08-10 the row read `31 files · 2,286,072 bytes` and **both excluded `MANIFEST.md`** — one denominator throughout, verified against that commit's tree.

> 🔴 **The correction was less consistent than the staleness it corrected.** **A stale total is wrong about the world, and a reader catches it by measuring.** **Three denominators is wrong about itself, and no measurement catches it without first knowing which set each quantity means.**

### ② Two per-file byte figures were never true

| Recorded | Actual | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `Authenticated Entry` — **98,921** | **99,112** | the 2026-08-08 refresh record |
| `Reports` — **48,859** | **48,965** | the byte-for-byte verification note |

⛔ **Neither is a dated record of an earlier version.** **Both files have exactly one commit** — `c44a837f` and `c1609215` — **and neither ever changed size**, so both figures were wrong when written. **Their hashes match the current files exactly**, which is what makes it provable: a hash that matches cannot describe bytes of a different length.

⚡ **`Reports` is the one that matters**, because its line is the document's *stated evidence* for byte-identity — *"compared byte-for-byte … identical"* — and **the number offered as proof is not the file's.** The conclusion still holds; the proof offered for it does not.

### 🔴 It narrows the lesson the same commit drew

**It concluded:** *"The per-file hashes did not go stale; only the hand-maintained total did."*

✅ **The first half is exactly right — all 36 hashes verified individually.** ⛔ **The second half is too kind to the document: two *per-file* byte figures are in the same hand-maintained class and were never right.** **The problem is not the total. It is every figure a human types beside a hash they computed** — which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *truth has exactly one authoritative representation*, applied to a file whose whole purpose is to be checkable rather than asserted.

⛔ **QE proposes no fix** — the snapshot is Lane C's. **Reported because the defect is in the tree promoted this cycle**, and because QE, not the fixing lane, sets `VERIFIED`.

### B-198 · 🟠 QE files bug rows on `lane-qe` and also resets `lane-qe` to `integration` to synchronize it, and the reset silently discards any row not yet integrated

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE's Closeout practice** — not a file |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a defect record was lost.** ⚡ **[B-196](#b-196) was filed, pushed, and gone from every ref within one cycle** — **and it is the one register whose whole purpose is that no defect disappears because somebody could not act on it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-13**, by recovering the row. ⚠️ **The PRACTICE is not fixed and that is what this row is about** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13, cycle 224**, when an anchored insert failed because the row it anchored on was absent |
| **Commit found** | **`fde954be`** |

### 🔴 The two habits, and they conflict

**①** QE files rows on `lane-qe`, because [`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md) is a document and a gate fix is a slice.
**②** QE runs `git reset --keep lane-qe → origin/integration` at every Closeout, to synchronize.

⛔ **`reset --keep` refuses to discard uncommitted changes and discards COMMITTED ones without comment.** ⚡ **So a row survives only if a candidate happens to pick it up before the next Closeout.**

📁 **Audited on `main`: B-190, B-191, B-192, B-193, B-194 and B-195 all survived. B-196 did not.** ⛔ **The difference is not care — it is whether a cycle ran in between.**

### ⚠️ The near-miss is what makes it 🟠 rather than 🟡

**QE noticed only because an anchored insert asserted `t.count(anchor) == 1` and threw.** ⛔ **A broad replacement would have written B-197 into the file and reported success**, and **B-196 would have stayed lost with nothing to notice.** 📁 **The product owner's instruction — *never perform broad replacements when an anchored replacement can assert uniqueness* — is what surfaced this.**

### ✅ Recovered, not rewritten

📁 `bca167b7` in the reflog. ⛔ **The cherry-pick conflicted in `certification/manifest.json`, a generated file QE does not hand-resolve**, so **only the B-196 section was extracted and reinserted** — 2487 characters, unchanged.

### ⛔ What the practice fix has to decide, and why it is not made here

**Either rows stop being filed on `lane-qe`, or the Closeout stops resetting it.** ⚠️ **Both have costs and neither is obviously right**: the reset is what keeps `lane-qe` from diverging, and filing elsewhere means a document commit on a branch that carries gate fixes. ✅ **Stated as the decision rather than taken inside the commit that discovered it.**

### B-195 · 🟡 The board-header check asks whether a named commit is REACHABLE, so a record two cycles stale passes green

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py), rule 5g |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **it cannot make a bad tree pass.** ⚠️ **It reports `ok` on exactly the condition it exists to catch**, which is worse than silence because a reader stops asking |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed here**, and the reason is below |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13**, by QE applying Lane C's own observation to itself after they found a 14-cycle-stale header in `CURRENT-STATE.md` |
| **Commit found** | **`a6dd1eee`** |

**Steps.** Leave `PROJECT_STATUS.md`, `SESSION_HANDOFF.md` and `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` naming an older promoted commit. Run `state-check`.

**Expected.** It says the records are stale.

**Actual.** ⛔ **`ok   ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md is dated at 'e158dd04', reachable from HEAD.`** — **measured, with the records two cycles behind.**

### 🔴 The check asks a weaker question than its purpose

📁 The predicate is `_is_ancestor(named, HEAD)`. ⚡ **Every previously promoted commit is an ancestor**, so the rule only fires on a record naming something **unreachable** — a commit that never merged. ⛔ **It cannot detect staleness at all**, which is the condition §20d cares about: *the dashboard must describe the promoted repository.*

⚠️ **The file's own comment already concedes half of this** — *"the header is a proxy, not a proof; a reverted row still passes"* — **but a reader takes `ok` as *the board is current*, and that is the sentence it cannot support.**

### ⛔ Why QE's own Closeout produced the instance

**Cycle 218's Closeout touched `docs/BACKLOG.md` and nothing else.** 📁 `git show --stat` on it: **one file.** **The three records were left naming cycle 217** and the advisory said `ok`.

> ⚡ **[B-190](#b-190) fixed the comparison in this same rule; this is the predicate.** **Same file, same neighbourhood, and the earlier fix is why the wrong answer was legible rather than noisy.**

### ⚠️ Not fixed here, deliberately

**The repair is small — compare against `main`'s tip rather than testing reachability.** ⛔ **QE has written three guards this week and abandoned two**, and Lane C's test applies: *if this check goes green, what will the reader stop asking?* ✅ **Here the answer is favourable — a reader should stop asking whether the board is current, and a tip comparison genuinely answers that.** **So this one is worth building; it is queued behind an executable delivery rather than declined.**

### B-273 · A resend countdown ticks in real time inside a fake-timer test, so certification fails under load

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`tests/components/verification.test.tsx`](../frontend/tests/components/verification.test.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a Blocking Quality Defect by [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s definition: a failing test prevents promotion.** ⚠️ **It cost a 16-minute certification run and would have cost another** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-16.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ⚡ **Found by QE during cycle 235, reported rather than fixed** — 📁 *"QE reports bugs; feature lanes fix them"* |
| **Found** | **2026-08-15, by QE**, under certification load — ⛔ **not reproducible by running the file** |
| **Commit found** | **`d3cbfa6e`** |

**Steps.** Run the frontend suite on a loaded machine — QE's measurement: ✅ **5 of 5 passes in isolation · 2 of 2 full-suite passes · one failure under certification load.**

**Expected.** *"The resend timer starts at 45s"* asserts `Resend in 0:45`.

**Actual.** `Resend in 0:43`.

### 🔴 The cause, and it is that one option was doing two jobs

📁 **The countdown is a pure tick counter** — `components/ui/resend-timer.tsx`:

```ts
setInterval(() => setRemaining((left) => Math.max(0, left - 1)), 1000)
```

⛔ **The file used `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })`, which advances the FAKE clock by REAL elapsed time.** ⚡ **So two real seconds between the click and the assertion turned `0:45` into `0:43`** — **and on an unloaded machine that never happens.**

⚠️ **The option was not careless: it was load-bearing.** ✅ **`findByRole` polls through `waitFor` on the real clock, so under frozen timers it never re-checks and the test times out.** 🔴 **`shouldAdvanceTime` was holding `findBy*` up, and it was doing that by making the countdown tick.** **One option, two jobs, and only one of them wanted.**

### ⛔ What did not work, recorded because each looked right

**① `vi.useFakeTimers()` with no options.** 🔴 **Nine tests TIMED OUT rather than failed** — **React's scheduler and `userEvent`'s internal waits run on `setTimeout`/`setImmediate`/`MessageChannel`, and a frozen clock nobody advances leaves every one pending.** ⚠️ **A worse signal than the flake it replaced.**

**② `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers })`.** ⛔ **`userEvent` calls that hook during its own waits, which ticks the countdown mid-click** — **the same defect one layer down.**

### ✅ The repair — freeze only what the countdown uses

```ts
vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setInterval', 'clearInterval'] });
```

⚡ **Everything React and `userEvent` need keeps a real clock; the countdown moves only where `advanceTimersByTime` says.** ✅ **And the two `findByRole` waits become an explicit microtask flush** — 📁 **the wait was for a resolved PROMISE, never for a timer**, so flushing is the honest wait and it moves no clock.

### 🔴 Fire-tested, and the flake reproduced deterministically

⛔ **A real 2-second stall inserted between the click and the assertion.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Against the shipped file** | ⛔ ***"Unable to find… `Resend in 0:45`. Name `Resend in 0:43`"*** — **QE's failure, on demand** |
| **Against the repair** | ✅ **passes** |

⚡ **9 passed, and the file dropped from 35s of timeouts to 654ms.**

> 🔴 **The rule this earns: a test that asserts an exact time must own every millisecond that reaches the assertion. If real elapsed time can get there, the machine is an input** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *hidden inputs are architecture defects*, and a loaded CPU is as hidden as an input gets.

### B-272 · The coverage gate systematically understates every file that touches the database

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | **`OPEN` — Lane A, 2026-08-15** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, **checking its own slice's coverage before handover** on QE's advice — ⚡ **found by disbelieving the number, not by reading the code** |
| **Module** | ⛔ **`platform_foundation`** — [`backend/pyproject.toml`](../backend/pyproject.toml) `[tool.coverage.run]` and [`infra/coverage-debt.py`](../infra/coverage-debt.py). **Lane C's under [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)**, and **not this lane's to fix** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **The gate passes, so nothing is less tested than believed** — ⛔ **but `coverage-debt` names the wrong files, and a lane acting on it writes tests for lines that are already covered** |

#### 🔴 The measurement, and it is decisive

**Same test file, same tests, one configuration line:**

| Configuration | `authorization_subject.py` |
|---|---|
| **As the repository is configured today** | ⛔ **64%** — missing `86-87, 90-96, 99` |
| **Plus `concurrency = thread,greenlet`** | ✅ **100%** — missing nothing |

```
pytest tests/integration/test_api_capability_roles.py --cov=…authorization_subject
  → 21 stmts, 5 missed, 64%

… --cov-config=<covrc with concurrency = thread,greenlet>
  → 21 stmts, 0 missed, 100%
```

⚡ **20 tests passed in both runs. No production code changed. No test changed.**

#### ⚠️ The tell was that the "missing" lines were impossible

📁 **`resolve_role` is eight straight-line statements.** ⛔ **Coverage reported line `85` executed and line `86` — the very next statement — not.**

```python
85  membership = await self._memberships.get_membership(…)   ✅ covered
86  if membership is None:                                    ⛔ "missing"
87      return None                                           ⛔ "missing"
89  assignment = await self._capabilities.assignment(…)       ✅ covered
90  if assignment is None or assignment.role_id is None:      ⛔ "missing"
96      return WorkspaceRole(membership.role).value           ⛔ "missing"
98  role = await self._capabilities.role(…)                   ✅ covered
99  return subject_for(…)                                     ⛔ "missing"
```

🔴 **Every `await` line is covered. Every line between them is not.** ⚡ **That is not a gap in a test suite; no suite can produce that shape.**

#### 📁 The cause

**SQLAlchemy's async layer runs every database `await` through `greenlet`** — `sqlalchemy/util/_concurrency_py3k.py`, `greenlet_spawn`. ⛔ **`coverage.py` defaults to `concurrency = thread` and loses line events for frames resumed inside a greenlet it is not tracing**, so only the lines where control returns to the traced frame are recorded.

⚠️ **`[tool.coverage.run]` sets `source`, `branch` and `omit`, and does not set `concurrency`.** ⚡ **`greenlet 3.5.4` and `coverage 7.15.2` are both installed; the option is available and unused.**

#### ⛔ Why it matters even though the gate passes

✅ **Nothing is less covered than the repository believes** — the true figure is **higher**, so 95.01% is a floor rather than a ceiling.

🔴 **But [`coverage-debt.py`](../infra/coverage-debt.py) is the instrument [§19](../CLAUDE.md) tells every lane to run before handover**, and it currently names the database-touching files as the worst in the repository:

```
  MISSED   COVER  FILE
      96     61%  modules/workspace_tenancy/interface/router.py
      50     62%  modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/repositories.py
      15     53%  modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/query_service.py
      11     70%  modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/capability_repository.py
```

⚠️ **Every one of those is an async SQLAlchemy file.** ⛔ **A lane reading that list writes tests for lines that already run** — which is what this lane was about to do.

⚡ **It is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s standing pattern: an instrument answering a narrower question than the one asked.** **The question is *"which lines does the suite execute?"*; the answer given is *"which lines does the suite execute in the traced greenlet?"***

#### ✅ What is NOT proposed

⛔ **This lane did not change the configuration.** 📁 A one-line edit to `[tool.coverage.run]` **moves what the 95% gate means for every file in the repository at once**, and the measured figure would rise — **which is a change to a gate's meaning, and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) says that is a slice with an owner, not a convenience.**

⚠️ **The repository-wide magnitude is unmeasured here.** ✅ **One file moved 36 points**; the honest statement is that the true figure is higher by an unknown amount, and **whoever changes the configuration should re-cut `fail_under` from the new measurement rather than leaving a baseline that was set against the old instrument.**

### B-271 · `environments.py --exports` derives a database the compose file never creates

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | **`OPEN` — Lane A, 2026-08-15** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, **checking QE's proposed mitigation for [B-270](#b-270) before using it** — ⚡ **found by running the instruction, not by reading it** |
| **Module** | ⛔ **`platform_foundation`** — [`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) and [`infra/docker-compose.yml`](../infra/docker-compose.yml). **Lane C's under [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)**, and **not this lane's to fix** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **It is about to become the documented mitigation for a 🔴 data-destruction defect**, and two of the three variables it produces are wrong on a per-lane compose stack |

#### 🔴 The two files disagree about the database name

📁 **[`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py), on `lane-a-2b`:**

```
SIGNORA_POSTGRES_PORT=5732        ✅ correct
SIGNORA_DATABASE=signora_lane_a   ⛔ no such database on this clone
```

📁 **[`infra/docker-compose.yml`](../infra/docker-compose.yml)`:29–33`, which is what actually creates it:**

```yaml
POSTGRES_USER: signora
POSTGRES_DB:   signora
ports: [ "${SIGNORA_POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}:5432" ]
```

⚡ **The PORT comes from the same variable in both, so it agrees.** ⛔ **The DATABASE does not: the compose file hardcodes `signora`, and the derivation computes `signora_lane_<letter>`.**

**Measured on this clone:** `docker exec signora-lane-a-postgres-1 psql -U signora -d postgres -tAc "select datname from pg_database"` → **`postgres · signora · template0 · template1`.** ⛔ **No `signora_lane_a`.**

#### ⚠️ Two models, and each half of the answer comes from a different one

| | Assumes | Gets right |
|---|---|---|
| **[`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane)** — *"One Postgres, one Redis, many databases"* | **One shared server on 5432**, database per lane | **the database name** |
| **[`infra/docker-compose.yml`](../infra/docker-compose.yml)** — a compose project per lane | **A server per lane on its own port**, database always `signora` | **the port** |

⛔ **`environments.py` renders the first model's database onto the second model's port**, so the pair it emits describes **no environment that exists.**

#### 🔴 Why this is urgent rather than cosmetic

**QE is shipping this as the mitigation for [B-270](#b-270) in cycle 233:**

```bash
eval "$(python3 infra/environments.py --exports)"
export SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL="postgresql+asyncpg://…@localhost:${SIGNORA_POSTGRES_PORT}/${SIGNORA_DATABASE}"
```

⛔ **On a per-lane compose stack that resolves to `5732/signora_lane_a`, which does not exist.** ✅ **It fails loudly** — the [B-268](#b-268) class, and the good outcome — ⚠️ **but a lane following the documented workaround for a data-destruction defect gets an error, and the next thing anybody does with an error is work around it.**

⛔ **And `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL` is the one that bites**: 📁 `migrations/env.py` reads it from `os.environ` directly, so **pointing it at a different database locks one and migrates the other** ([B-007](#b-007), open).

#### ✅ What this lane is doing meanwhile, stated rather than implied

**Exporting all three at `localhost:5732/signora`** — ⚡ **this clone's own compose stack, derived from `backend/.env` and confirmed against `pg_database`** — **which is what every gate this lane has run was measured on.**

⛔ **Not proposed as the fix.** ✅ **The fix is that one representation decides both halves** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *truth has exactly one authoritative representation*: **either the compose file takes its database name from the derivation, or the derivation reads the compose file.** ⚠️ **Today each is authoritative for one half of a pair that is only ever used together.**

✅ **The repair makes the two inseparable rather than adding a check.** **`DESTRUCTIVE_DB_ENV` is one definition taking a database name, and every recipe that consents to truncation now gets the consent *from* it** — so a future target cannot acquire the flag without naming a database. 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): one representation, and `E2E_ENV` derives from it rather than restating the URLs.**

⛔ **`make -n e2e` verified byte-equivalent in effect** — same four variables, same values, order only.

#### 🔴 Same file as [B-265](#b-265), and that is the finding under the finding

**Both defects are `backend/tests/conftest.py` deciding which database everything talks to**, and they are the two halves of one gap:

| | |
|---|---|
| **[B-265](#b-265)** | A database **behind the migration head** fails 26 tests and never says so — ⚡ **loud, and misattributed** |
| **B-270** | A seeder points at **another environment's** database and reports success — ⛔ **silent** |

⚠️ **`DEFAULT_APP_DATABASE_URL` is the repository's implicit environment selector** — the test suite's, the seeder's, and anything else that imports it — **and nothing validates that the database it names is the one the caller meant.** ⚡ **Two variables (`SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL`, `SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL`) express one fact**, which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md), and **[`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) already computes the correct answer per slot.**

#### ⚠️ QE should know, because it is their stack

**Human review's Playground was deleted and re-seeded by this lane at 2026-08-15T03:5x.** ✅ **Nothing outside the Playground workspace was touched** — the delete is scoped by workspace name — **but the demo data a reviewer would have been looking at is this lane's, not the one that was there.**

#### 🔴 Escalated the same day — **it is not only the seeder. It is `pytest` itself, and it TRUNCATES**

**Severity raised 🟠 → 🔴 by Lane A, 2026-08-15**, on evidence found by doing it.

⛔ **A lane running bare `pytest` — with no variable set, which is what a fresh shell is — points the whole integration suite at `localhost:5432/signora`.** ⚡ **That is human review's, by the same `DEFAULT_APP_DATABASE_URL` default this row already names**, and 🔴 **`clean_database` truncates every table after every test.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **What the seeder does** | `DELETE FROM workspace WHERE id = :id` — ✅ **one workspace, by name** |
| **What the suite does** | ⛔ **`TRUNCATE` every table, after every test** |

**What this lane actually did, stated rather than summarised.** Resuming after a context compaction, in a shell that no longer carried the exports [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane) requires, it ran:

```
SIGNORA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TESTS=1 pytest tests/integration/test_api_capability_roles.py
```

**16 of 17 tests failed with `relation "capability_assignment" does not exist`** — ⚡ **the tell that it was on a database at `0054` rather than this lane's `0057`, and the only reason the mistake was visible at all.** ⛔ **The truncation runs in teardown regardless of whether the test passed.**

**Measured immediately afterwards, at `5432/signora`:** `workspace` **0** · `membership` **0** · `outbox_event` **0** · `alembic_version` **`0054`** · 69 tables.

#### 🔴 And it is not only a bare `pytest` — it is `make test`

⛔ **[`Makefile`](../Makefile)`:106`, the repository's own documented gate**, *"suite + coverage gate"*:

```make
test:
	@python3 infra/environment-lease.py run test -- sh -c 'cd backend && SIGNORA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TESTS=1 uv run pytest --cov'
```

🔴 **It sets `SIGNORA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TESTS=1` and no database variable at all.** ⚡ **`environment-lease.py run` adds only its own lease variable** — `run()` builds `{**os.environ, LEASE_VARIABLE: identifier}` — **so the database is whatever the caller's shell already had**, and a fresh shell has none.

⚠️ **`E2E_ENV` sets all three, eleven lines further down, for `make e2e`.** ⛔ **`make test` sets none**, and it is the more destructive of the two.

📁 **[`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane) does document the three exports** — ⚠️ **under *"this is only needed for a lane added later"*, in the section for **creating** a lane. **A lane that already exists reads that as done.**

⛔ **So the failure mode needs no mistake**: open a new shell, run the gate the Makefile documents, and the suite truncates human review's database. **That is what happened here.**

⚠️ **Stated exactly: this lane cannot prove what was there beforehand.** 📁 **By this row's own record the last thing written there was this lane's Playground seed**, so the balance of evidence is that what was destroyed was that seed rather than the product owner's original data — ⛔ **but that is an inference, and the honest report is that the environment was emptied and nobody can now say by which of the two events.**

#### ⚡ Why this changes the fix rather than only the severity

⛔ **The guard that exists is the wrong guard.** `require_explicit_consent_to_truncate` asks *"do you consent to truncation?"* — ⚡ **and the answer was yes, correctly: this lane's own database is disposable.** 🔴 **The question it does not ask is *which database*, which is the only question that was wrong** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *an instrument answering a narrower question than the one asked.*

✅ **A guard that would have caught it, and it needs no discipline:** **refuse to run destructive fixtures against slot 0.** [`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) already computes `"signora" if self.slot == 0`, so the check is *"is the resolved database human review's?"* → **fail with the reason.** ⛔ **A default that silently selects the one environment [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) reserves for the product owner is the defect; consent is not the missing half.**

⚠️ **And the default itself is wrong in the other direction too** — ⛔ **a test suite with no environment configured should refuse to run, not pick one.** 📁 That is the same shape as [B-268](#b-268) failing loudly, which this row already calls the better behaviour.

### B-269 · Three nullable JSONB columns document a `NULL` that no SQL predicate can see

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-14**, all three, with a test that asks the database rather than the ORM. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-14, building [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) ⓶b — ⚡ **found by a conditional write that matched zero rows**, not by review |
| **Module** | `commercial_profile` — **Lane A's** in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Latent.** ⛔ **Nothing read it wrongly and nothing shipped broken** — the defect is in what the repository ASSERTS about itself |

#### 🔴 What is actually stored

**SQLAlchemy's default for a JSON column serialises Python `None` as the JSON value `null`, not as SQL `NULL`.** ⚡ **The ORM decodes it straight back to `None`**, so every read is correct and always was.

⛔ **`WHERE moved IS NULL` matches nothing. Ever.**

| Column | Migration | Shipped in |
|---|---|---|
| `account_tag_batch.changed` | `0052` | ⛔ **[TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) — on `main`** |
| `account_assignment_batch.moved` | `0054` | [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) ⓶a — pinned at `f2ad4b68` |
| `account_segment_batch.added` | `0056` | [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) ⓶b — **where it was found** |

🔴 **Three of three.** ⚠️ **Every nullable JSONB column in the module carried it**, and the sweep now finds none.

#### ⛔ The false claim is in the migrations, and that is what makes it a defect

📁 **`0052`**: *"`NULL` until the batch applies, which is a different fact from an empty list."*
📁 **`0054`**: *"Collapsing `NULL` and `[]` would make *never approved* and *approved and changed nothing* the same row."*

⚡ **Which is precisely what the column does to any SQL predicate.** ⛔ **A partial index, a report, or a later guard written against those docstrings would be wrong** — and **a lane arriving cold reads the migration, not the ORM** ([§12](../CLAUDE.md)).

> 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): the repository must not assert something untrue of itself.** **The columns behave; the documents do not describe them.**

#### 🔴 The repository already carried this lesson, in a comment written for exactly this reason

📁 **`modules/observation_engine/infrastructure/models.py:43`**, verified rather than cited:

> ***"`none_as_null` matters: without it SQLAlchemy writes JSON `null` into the column rather than SQL NULL, and the constraint distinguishing an occurrence from a change would never see the absence it tests for."***

⛔ **So this was not a subtlety nobody had met.** ⚡ **It is a documented trap, in this repository, with a comment naming the precise failure mode — and three columns walked into it.** ⚠️ **That makes it an [L-1](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md) reuse finding as much as a correctness one**: the audit asks what already exists, and the answer was a comment written by somebody who had already paid for it. **Found by QE, on a sweep this lane had not run.**

#### ⚡ How it surfaced, and why no earlier test could have

**⓶b's `SqlSegmentBatchStore.record_application` is a compare-and-set** — `UPDATE … WHERE added IS NULL` — **so a second application cannot overwrite the record a reversal depends on.** ⛔ **It matched zero rows against a row written moments earlier**, and the first application of every segment batch was silently refused.

🔴 **The seam pattern, fifth instance**: **the ORM read path and the SQL predicate path disagreed about one column, and only the path nobody had written yet was wrong.** ⚠️ **A round trip through Python cannot tell SQL `NULL` from JSON `null`** — which is exactly why it survived every passing test in two shipped slices.

#### ✅ Fixed

**`JSONB(none_as_null=True)` on all three.** ⛔ **No migration and no backfill**: every row written so far still decodes to `None`, and nothing has ever queried these columns in SQL.

**The regression test asks the database** — `SELECT added IS NULL FROM account_segment_batch` — **rather than reading the value back through Python**, because the round trip is the instrument that could not see it.
