### B-268 · Every lane's stack creates `signora`, and every tool is told `signora_lane_a`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — `infra/environments.py` **and** `infra/docker-compose.yml` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** for `environments.py`; ⚠️ **the compose file is QE's** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), a gate instrument) — **which is why this is reported rather than fixed** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — **wrong but survivable.** ⛔ **Isolation is NOT at risk**: each lane has its own container on its own port, so the stacks are separated by `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` regardless of the name inside. ⚠️ **What breaks is every tool that uses the PUBLISHED name against a lane's own stack** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN` — Lane A, 2026-08-14** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-14, by Lane A**, bringing up its own stack to run a Playwright journey — ⚡ **the third symptom of one cause, and the first time the cause was measured** |

#### 🔴 The two representations

| | |
|---|---|
| 📁 `infra/environments.py:138` | `return "signora" if self.slot == 0 else f"signora_{self.name.replace('-', '_')}"` → **`signora_lane_a`** |
| 📁 `infra/docker-compose.yml:31` | `POSTGRES_DB: signora` — **hardcoded, not parameterised** |

⛔ **They agree for slot 0 and disagree for every other environment**, which is why nobody has hit it on the shared stack.

#### ⚠️ Three symptoms, one cause, and the first two were misread

**All three were hit by this lane today before the cause was found:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **`make demo-prepare` fails** | *"database `signora_lane_a` does not exist"* — **the Makefile uses the published name against a stack that created `signora`** |
| **The seeder wrote where nothing was read** | ⚠️ **Cost real time during [TASK-429](BACKLOG.md)**: the seeder writes to `signora` via `tests/conftest.py`'s default, and this lane read `signora_lane_a` and concluded the pipeline had produced nothing. 📁 **Diagnosed then as *"I was reading the wrong database"* — true, and not the cause** |
| **A fresh lane stack cannot be migrated** | `alembic upgrade head` against the published name, on a container that never created it |

#### ✅ Expected

**One name.** ⚡ **Either the compose file parameterises `POSTGRES_DB` from the published value, or `environments.py` publishes what the compose file creates** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md): *truth has exactly one authoritative representation; everything else derives from it.*

#### ⚠️ Which way, and why this lane is not choosing

**Each lane already has its own container and its own port**, so a distinct database *name* buys no isolation it does not already have — **which argues for publishing `signora`.** ⛔ **But `environments.py`'s own comment says *"`signora` for slot 0 by history"*, implying the per-slot name is deliberate**, and the compose file is **QE's**.

⚡ **So the fix touches one file this lane owns and one it does not**, and picking a direction unilaterally would decide something for the lane that certifies with it.

#### ⛔ Worked around, not fixed, and stated so

**This lane is using `signora` against its own container to run its journey.** ⚠️ **That works and it is exactly the confusion the defect creates** — the next person will do the same and not know why.

### B-267 · A database password in a connection string reached the log, with redaction on

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`signora_platform`** — `observability/logging.py` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a credential value reaching a log sink.** ⚠️ **Not 🔴 only because there is no deployed environment** ([ADR-0027](architecture/adr/0027-local-first-development.md) defers release to M14.5), **so no customer secret has been written anywhere.** 🔴 **It would be 🔴 the day one is** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13**, in [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) slice ⓵, with a Security Invariant. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13, by Lane A**, measuring what logging emits today **before writing any of [ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md)** |

#### 🔴 What happened

```
logger.info("connecting to postgres://signora_app:S3cr3tPassw0rd@db:5432/signora")
→ {"message":"connecting to postgres://signora_app:S3cr3tPassw0rd@db:5432/signora"}
```

⛔ **Through the JSON formatter. With redaction enabled. At INFO.**

#### ⚠️ Why the existing redaction missed it, and why that is the interesting part

📁 `redact()` covered **three** shapes: a field *named* like a secret, a JWT, and a `Bearer` token. ⚡ **Every credential this platform actually holds is a fourth** — **a URI.** `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL`, `SIGNORA_REDIS_URL` and the object-store URL, ⛔ **and none of them was reachable by any of the three**: the field is called `url`, so the key pattern misses it, and the value is neither a JWT nor a bearer token.

🔴 **The protection was real and it was pointed away from the secrets the repository has.**

#### ⛔ A second hole beside it: a format choice was silently a security choice

📁 `configure_logging(json_output=False)` installed a **bare `logging.Formatter`**, and **redaction lived only in `JsonFormatter`.** ⚡ **So a developer who turned on readable logs turned off redaction** — without asking to, and without being told.

📁 [ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md) §3 in its own words: ***"A developer must opt IN to verbosity, never opt OUT of redaction"***, and *"the default is safe"* in **every** environment.

#### ✅ Fixed

**URI userinfo is redacted, and the host and database are not** — a redacted host removes the diagnostic value the line exists for, and a guard that destroys the reason to log is a guard somebody turns off. **`PlainFormatter` redacts on the same terms as `JsonFormatter`.**

⚠️ **The first pattern required a username, so `redis://:secret@cache:6379/2` — the form Redis URLs actually take — walked through it.** **Caught by the check written to prove the fix.**

#### ⚡ Enforcement

📁 **`tests/security_invariants/test_secret_safe_logging.py`**, which [ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md) §4 asks for by name. **Four fire tests; every assertion falls to at least one of them.**

⚠️ **Fire-testing found two assertions that could not fail** — a credential passed as a *field* asserted nothing against the plain sink, because that formatter renders no fields at all. **Both were rescoped and the plain sink's real property is now asserted directly**, so a future format string that grows `%(url)s` breaks the file rather than silently reopening the gap.

### B-266 · The two highest READY rows in the backlog were offered to no lane

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — `infra/coordination.py`, this lane's since [D-230](DECISION_REGISTER.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **wrong behaviour a lane would hit**, and ⚠️ **silent**: the ref simply did not mention the rows, so every lane read a shorter queue than the backlog held |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13**, with three regression tests. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13, by Lane A**, selecting its next task under the Task Claim Protocol — ⚡ **step 3b, where the queue and the backlog are compared, is what surfaced it** |

#### 🔴 What happened

📁 **`_lane_for` reads an explicit lane out of the `Module` cell, then a module key, then a trigger steward. It never reads the `Owner` cell.**

⛔ **[TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-1478](BACKLOG.md) name no module at all.** Both carry `| **Owner** | **Lane A** |`, both are `READY`, and **both resolved to `lane='—'` and classified as `WAITING ARCHITECTURE`** — so they appeared in no lane's `backlog` array.

🔴 **They are the two highest `READY` rows in [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md)**, and 📁 **[TASK-1478](BACKLOG.md) is the standing authority under which Lane A picks its own next module.** ⚠️ **It was invisible to Lane A.**

#### ⚠️ The workaround was already in the tree, which is the tell

📁 **[TASK-1477](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-1480](BACKLOG.md) carry `Module` cells stamped *"added 2026-08-13"*** — **hand-patched onto rows so this function could see them.**

⚡ **That is the same shape [B-423](#b-423) records for the queue arrays**: *"this office hand-fixed it four times before fixing the cause."* ⛔ **Four rows of six with an `Owner` cell had no `Module` cell; two of those were patched by hand and two were left invisible.**

#### ✅ The fix, and where it sits in the precedence

**An `Owner` cell naming a lane resolves the row — LAST, after the module-key scan.** 📁 **[`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) stays the authoritative ownership registry** (§20e), so **a row that names a module is unaffected** and this does not become a second registry.

⛔ **It is not the steward branch and must not become it.** 📁 [D-135](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s steward is *an owner, never an executor*, and it is a **different cell**, labelled `Trigger steward`. ⚡ **An `Owner` cell on an implementation row is the row's own statement about who executes it** — [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) says so twice, its `Type` cell reading *"Lane A owns decomposition, sequencing and end-to-end delivery."*

#### ✅ Measured before and after

**`Lane A: 9 claimable` → `11 claimable`.** ⛔ **[TASK-412](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-411](BACKLOG.md) are unchanged** — 412 resolves through its own `Module` cell and 411 keeps taking its steward when parked and none when startable, **which are the two protections this fix must not undo, and both are pinned.**

⚡ **Three regression tests; the new one fires red with the branch removed and the two protections stay green** — which is what separates a fix from a widening.

### B-265 · A database behind the migration head fails 26 tests and never says so

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Repository test harness** — `backend/tests/conftest.py` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **reported and not fixed here**, because the fix changes what a failing gate *means* for every lane |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — **wrong but survivable.** ⛔ **Nothing a customer touches.** ⚠️ **What it costs is diagnosis time, at the worst moment**: the failures name application behaviour, so the first hypothesis is always a code defect |
| **Status** | **`OPEN` — Lane A, 2026-08-13** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-13, by Lane A**, running the full suite before pushing TASK-429 |

#### 🔴 What happened

**One full-suite run reported `27 failed, 4536 passed`. The next reported `4563 passed`, with one file changed** — and that file accounted for exactly **one** of the twenty-seven.

⛔ **The other twenty-six were every `account_tag` test there is**, across `test_account_tag_repository.py` and `test_api_account_tags.py`. **They pass in isolation (18/18) and they pass across the whole `tests/integration` directory (662/662).**

#### ⚡ Why it is a harness defect and not a flake

🔴 **The failures partition cleanly on the two newest migrations, `0051` and `0052`.** ⛔ **A flake scatters; a clean partition on schema version is a signature.** **The database was behind head when that run started, and `account_tag` did not exist yet.**

⚡ **What brings it to head is a test** — `tests/integration/test_migration_runner.py`, whose whole subject is that the runner reaches head. ⛔ **And `test_account_tag_*` sorts before `test_migration_runner` alphabetically**, so every table added by a recent migration is unprotected in exactly the window where it is newest.

⚠️ **What moved the schema is NOT established and is deliberately not asserted here.** A `make dr` restore from a snapshot of `main` would do it — `0051` and `0052` are unpromoted, so a `main` snapshot is at `0050` — but that is a hypothesis and the defect below does not depend on it.

#### 🔴 The actual gap, which holds however the drift happened

📁 **`tests/conftest.py` carries two session-scoped autouse guards, and both exist for this exact class**: one refuses a database that has not consented to truncation, the other refuses a connection that bypasses RLS — *"otherwise Row-Level Security is not enforced and isolation assertions are vacuous."*

⛔ **There is no third one asserting the schema is at head.** **So a database behind head is discovered as N application failures rather than one sentence**, and N grows with every migration a cycle adds.

#### ✅ Expected

**One session-scoped failure naming the revision the database is at and the revision the code expects.**

#### ⛔ Actual

**Twenty-six failures describing tags, vocabularies, batches and workspace isolation** — every one of them a true statement about a table that was not there.

#### ⚠️ Why Lane A reported rather than fixed it

**The fix is one fixture, and it is not the size that matters.** ⛔ **A new session-scoped autouse guard changes what a failing gate means for every lane and for QE**, and it would have travelled inside an unrelated slice. 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): finding a defect outside the slice is an obligation to report it, not a licence to fix it.** ⚡ **And this one is worth QE seeing before it is closed** — QE runs the full suite every cycle and is the reader the guard would be written for.

### B-274 · Resolving any structured attribute raised `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`

> ⚠️ **Renumbered from `B-265` by Lane A on 2026-08-17, before the branch reached QE.** 📁 [B-265](#b-265--a-database-behind-the-migration-head-fails-26-tests-and-never-says-so) was already taken — **2026-08-13, three days earlier, in the same lane's own block** — and `infra/state-check.py` reported the collision. ⚡ **The later claim moves**, which is the rule's own tie-break; ⛔ **the earlier row keeps its number, its references and its history.** **Commits written before this line cite `B-265`; this note is what makes them followable.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`knowledge_graph`** — ⚡ **assignee joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)**: Lane A |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a customer would hit** — the read raises rather than answering |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-16, with a regression test.** Awaiting QE verification |
| **Found** | `cd45f8fb`, by the first caller that resolved a structured attribute |
| **Steps** | Call `resolve_value` with any claim whose `value` is an object — a technology, a funding round, an acquisition, a role change, an intent surge, or one of ADR-0409's three commercial values |
| **Expected** | The most recent claim wins and the agreeing providers are named, exactly as for `INDUSTRY` |
| **Actual** | `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` from the set comprehension that decides agreement |

**`_comparable` folded case for a `str` and returned everything else unchanged**, so `{_comparable(claim.value) for …}` tried to hash a dict.

#### ⚠️ Why it had never fired

**Its only callers resolved `INDUSTRY`, `COUNTRY` and `EMPLOYEE_COUNT`** — two strings and an integer — **so nothing had ever handed it an object.** ⚡ **Seven attributes in the canonical vocabulary carry one today** — `TECHNOLOGY_DETECTED` · `TECHNOLOGY_REMOVED` · `FUNDING_ROUND` · `ACQUISITION` · `ROLE_CHANGE` · `PERSON_IDENTITY` · `INTENT_TOPIC_SURGE` — **plus the three [ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) added.** ⛔ **Every one of them would have raised.**

#### ✅ The fix, and what it is careful not to do

**A structured value becomes canonical JSON with sorted keys**, so two providers reporting the same object with their keys in a different order **agree** rather than disputing a serialisation detail. ⛔ **And a test asserts that two genuinely different objects are still `DISPUTED`** — a canonical form that collapsed distinct values would hide the exact disagreement `ValueAgreement` exists to surface ([§2](../CLAUDE.md): a guard that cannot fail is not protection).

### B-264 · Changing any preference silently forgot which workspace you were last in

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`workspace_tenancy`** — ⚡ **assignee joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)**: Lane A |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a customer-visible regression of a shipped feature**, and ⚠️ **silent**: nothing failed, nothing logged, and the person simply landed somewhere else |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12**, in the same change. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A**, adding a column BESIDE the one it broke |

#### 🔴 What happened

📁 **[TASK-1422](BACKLOG.md) added `person_preferences.last_entered_at`** so entry rule 12 can send somebody back to the workspace they were working in. ⛔ **`ChangePreferencesUseCase.execute` constructed a fresh `PersonPreferences` from thirteen NAMED fields, and `last_entered_at` was not one of them.**

⚡ **So every profile edit reset it to `None`, which reads as *never entered*** — 🔴 **a person who changed their theme was sent to the workspace chooser at their next sign-in.**

#### ⚠️ The defect is the SHAPE, not the missing line

⛔ **A rebuild-everything use case silently drops any field added after it was written.** ⚡ **This table has now been extended twice**: `last_entered_at` ([TASK-1422](BACKLOG.md)) and `first_run_dismissed_at` ([TASK-1424](BACKLOG.md)) — ⛔ **and the second would have inherited the identical bug**, breaking the design's ***"dismissible forever"*** the first time somebody changed a setting.

✅ **Fixed with `replace(current, …)`**, which carries every unmentioned field **by construction** — 📁 **so a fourteenth field is safe without anybody remembering this file.** ⛔ **Naming the two missing fields would have fixed two instances and left the shape.**

#### 🔴 Why 289 tests passed over it

⚠️ **Every existing assertion checked the field it had just changed.** ⛔ **Nothing asserted what a change must NOT touch**, and that is the assertion this class needs.

✅ **The new guard iterates the dataclass's OWN fields** rather than a list somebody maintains — ⚡ **which is the only version that catches the fourteenth field.** 📁 The same reasoning `tenancy_policy.py` uses about a table appearing in neither list: **you cannot enumerate your way to the thing you forgot to enumerate.**

⚡ **Fire-tested**: restoring the original constructor turns it red while the other 289 stay green.

### B-263 · One identifier, two questions — and it made two lanes contradict each other about the same ruling

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | ⛔ **Not a module** — [`LANE_COORDINATION.md`](LANE_COORDINATION.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **filed against itself. This lane allocated the identifier** |
| **Severity** | 🔴 — ⛔ **it has already caused a false report between two lanes**, which is more than a broken anchor costs |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13.** ⚡ **The condition this row describes is discharged**: 📁 **the product owner allocated `C-1500`+ to Lane A**, Lane C renumbered this lane's item to [C-1500](LANE_COORDINATION.md), **and `C-210` is once again ONE question — Lane B's.** ✅ **The 37 references were then classified one at a time and NOT by replace** — 📁 [B-259](#b-259) is what a per-file replace costs. **Six repointed** *(this lane's own live cells)*; **most correctly stay `C-210`** *(Lane B's question)*; **the rest are left deliberately** — dated records, quotations, and two cells belonging to Lane C, **whose own instruction was that repointing content an office does not own is exactly B-259, and it cuts both ways.** ⚠️ **Two of those left behind now point at the wrong item and this row says so rather than editing somebody else's sentence**: [D-229](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s blocked-scope list is the product owner's text, and two cells are Lane C's. **Both are cheap for their owners now that `C-1500` exists.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)):  🔵 **`OPEN`** — 🔴 **this lane CANNOT fix it correctly**, and the reason is the second half of the finding |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A**, reconciling two peers who reported opposite things about `C-210` |

#### 🔴 What happened

**`C-210` names two different questions.**

| Where | What it says |
|---|---|
| **The index, row `C-210`** | *"will Signora hold personal data?"* — **Lane B's**, `OPEN`, grouped with People Intelligence, anchored `#c-210--will-signora-hold-personal-data` |
| **The only `## C-210` heading** | *"does Signora STORE what a rep writes, or only observe?"* — ⚡ **this lane's, raised for [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md)** |

⛔ **So the index link resolves to nothing, and every reader who follows *"C-210"* lands on this lane's item instead of Lane B's.**

#### ⚡ The cost, and it is not hypothetical

**Two sessions reported opposite states within an hour, and both were reading correctly:**

- **One reported `C-210` RULED — *"Notes and Tasks approved, contract [ADR-0413](architecture/adr/)"*.** ✅ **True of THIS lane's question.**
- **One reported `C-210` unruled on both refs, having read the index row.** ✅ **True of Lane B's question.**

🔴 **Neither was wrong. The identifier was.** ⛔ **A collision that produces a broken anchor is tidy-up; one that produces two confident and contradictory reports of a product-owner ruling is a defect**, and it cost this lane a reconciliation it should not have had to do.

#### ⚠️ Why the existing guards did not catch it

⛔ **Lane B's `C-210` has NO `## C-210` heading** — it exists as an index row and two cross-references. ⚡ **So a free-identifier scan by heading reports 210 as available, and that is exactly the scan this lane ran.** ⚠️ **`state-check`'s duplicate-identifier check found the [C-300](#b-259) collision because BOTH sides had a heading**; this shape has only one and is invisible to it.

📁 **[B-259](#b-259) is the same class one step earlier** — *"this lane allocated from the highest number seen"* — ⛔ **and this is the sequel: allocating into a block that was already full, twice.** ⚠️ **`C-209` carries no second heading and appears clean, and that is luck rather than method.**

#### ✅ THE REFERENCES ARE CLASSIFIED, AND MOST OF THEM CORRECTLY STAY — Lane A, 2026-08-13

⚡ **`C-1500` reached `main`, so the sweep this row deferred is now possible.** ⛔ **It was done reference by reference and NOT by replace** — 📁 **[B-259](#b-259) is what a per-file replace costs**, and it damaged a dated enumeration inside another row's block.

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Repointed to `C-1500`** | **6** — TASK-1476's own dependency and analysis cells, **authored by this lane, live, and unambiguously about *does Signora store what a rep writes*** |
| ✅ **Correctly `C-210` and left** | **Lane B's question throughout** — the heading, the index row, the People Intelligence groupings, `C-210 + C-203` in the decision queue and TASK-429's gate |
| ⛔ **Left because rewriting them is the defect** | **Dated records and quotations**: [D-071](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s fourteen-ruling enumeration · [D-229](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s own blocked-scope list · QE's `PROMOTED` cell on [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md) · this row's own account of the collision · **and this lane's earlier wording quoted back at it** |
| ⚠️ **Left because they are another office's text** | **2 in [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md)** — Lane C's added commentary. 📁 **Lane C's own instruction**: *"repointing content this office does not own is exactly B-259"*, **and it cuts both ways** |

🔴 **Two of those left behind now point at the wrong item, and saying so is better than silently repointing somebody else's sentence.** ⛔ **[D-229](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s blocked-scope list names `C-210` and means this lane's question** — ⚡ **a ruling is the product owner's text and not a lane's to edit**, so it is reported here instead. ✅ **The same is true of the two Lane C cells**, and **both are cheap for their owners to fix now that `C-1500` exists.**

#### ⛔ Why this lane cannot fix it, and what it needs

**Renumbering is the obvious repair and there is nowhere to renumber to.** 🔴 **Every identifier from `C-200` to `C-299` is defined — 100 of 100, counted rather than assumed.**

📁 **[`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md)'s own block table says why**: *"Only Lane B's block has been stated to Lane B. The blocks for Lane A, QE and the unclaimed lanes are the product owner's to allocate, and this table is deliberately incomplete rather than guessed."*

⚡ **So this lane has been allocating out of a range nobody gave it, into space that ran out.** ⛔ **Picking a new range now would repeat the original error with a bigger number**, which is what [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) forbids by name.

> 🔴 **FOR THE PRODUCT OWNER, and it is one sentence: Lane A needs a stated `C-` block.** ⚡ **Lane C uses `400–499` then `1400+`; Lane B uses `3xx`.** ⛔ **Until one is stated, this lane raises no further coordination items and marks the two it has as contested.** ✅ **Implementation is unaffected — no slice is waiting on this.**

| | |
|---|---|

Requires an owner."* shown to a person `membership` calls `owner` was **the role not having ARRIVED** — `null` read as *has no role* — **not the auth tier, not the token, not the membership.** ⚡ **Released by [D-234](DECISION_REGISTER.md) and repaired against the design's own words**, with three tests including the one that keeps a resolved denial locking. ⛔ **So this row has no remaining content**: there is no defect here that is not recorded elsewhere. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)):  🔵 **`OPEN`** — 🔴 **blocking [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md)'s journey evidence** |

#### ⛔ What was measured, in the order it was measured

| Checked | Result |
|---|---|
| **Seeder ran** | ✅ *"12 accounts through the real pipeline · 47 signed-in user(s) enrolled"*, workspace `deeecc11-…` |
| **The workspace exists, with members** | ✅ `select … from workspace left join membership` → **`Playground`, 48 members** |
| **The OWNER persona's membership** | ✅ **`deeecc11-… \| owner`** — 📁 `infra/demo-users.json` declares `dana.reyes@northwind.example` as the `owner`, **and the database agrees** |

| 🔴 **What the product says about her** | ⛔ ***"Settings — restricted. Requires an owner."*** |
| 🔴 **Every account she opens** | ⛔ ***"— no source has named this account yet"*** · *"No evidence collected yet"* · *"Nothing has scored this account yet"* · *"No longer on your list"* |

#### ⚠️ Ruled out, so the next reader does not repeat it

- ⛔ **Not the auth schema.** `npm run auth:migrate` reports *"auth schema 'auth' is already up to date"*. ⚠️ **`auth` holds `account`, `session`, `twoFactor`, `user`, `verification` and no organization tables** — ✅ **and that is correct here**: workspaces and memberships are the *app* tier's `workspace` and `membership`, not Better Auth's plugin tables. **Checked because their absence looks alarming and is not the defect.**
- ⛔ **Not a stale session.** The nav renders the NEW workspace id, so the sign-in happened after the reseed.
- ⛔ **Not this slice.** The same screens read the same way before [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md)'s changes, and **two of the six Playwright projects pass** — the failures are all *"no account renders its sections"*, never an assertion about a section.

#### 🔴 What it costs, stated plainly

⛔ **Four journeys in [`account-360-states.spec.ts`](../frontend/tests/e2e/account-360-states.spec.ts) are written, correct and cannot be run green here.** ⚡ **They are committed rather than withheld** — 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): a journey deleted because the environment could not run it is evidence the next lane has to author again.** ⛔ **This lane will not report them as passing**, and [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md) is not handed to QE on their strength.

#### 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-12, against this row's own previous measurement

⛔ **The paragraph that stood here said *"`ac05261b` belongs to the current workspace and HAS A SCORE, and the page rendered it as unscored anyway."* That was wrong, and the page was telling the truth.**

⚠️ **How it was got wrong, because the shape is this repository's recurring one.** ✅ I counted **16 entities and 16 scores in the workspace** and concluded the two sets coincided. ⛔ **They do not.** 📁 **The scope of the operation was not the scope of the question** — *scores in this workspace* is not *a score for this account*, and one query answers only the first. ⚡ **Same family as [B-252](#b-252), [B-254](#b-254), [B-259](#b-259) and [B-194](#b-194)** — committed by the lane that has been naming it.

✅ **Measured per entity, which is the question that was actually being asked:**

| Of the 16 entities in the Playground workspace | |
|---|---|
| **Named AND scored** | ✅ **11** |
| **Scored, not named** | 1 |
| ⛔ **Neither — including `ac05261b`** | **4** |

🔴 **So the record page was correct on every count.** `ac05261b` has **0 buying scores** and **1 identity binding with no `legal_name`**: *"no source has named this account yet"* and *"Nothing has scored this account yet"* are **both true of it**, and this row previously called truthful output a defect.

#### ✅ RESOLVED IN LARGE PART — and it was this lane's TEST, 2026-08-12

🔴 **The four journeys now pass. 6 of 6 green, run headed against the seeded Playground.** ⚡ **This row's original claim — *"four journeys are written, correct and cannot be run green here"* — was wrong about *correct*.**

⛔ **The cause was a race this lane had already fixed one line earlier and left one line later.** 📁 The helper counted `#score` the instant the click resolved; **`count()` returns 0 while the read is in flight**, so every account looked unscored and **the helper blamed the data** — throwing *"seed the Playground"* at a workspace holding **eleven named, scored accounts**. ✅ **It now waits for EITHER answer** — the section, or the page's own *"Nothing has scored this account yet"* — **so a genuinely unscored account moves the loop on instead of timing out.**

⚠️ **Two further defects, both in this lane's own instrument and both worth naming:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The outline assertion counted EVERY `h2`** and expected the total unchanged | ⛔ **A collapsible body carries its own heading, which correctly leaves the accessibility tree when hidden.** 📁 The design's rule is about **section** headings, **so the assertion enforced something the design does not say** |
| **`getByRole('heading', { name: 'What changed' })` matched TWO elements** | ⛔ The section's heading and the body's *"What changed, and who says so"*. ⚡ **A selector that matches two things asserts neither** — `exact: true` |

#### ⚠️ WHAT SURVIVES, and it is one thing rather than the row's original claim

🔴 **`Settings — restricted. Requires an owner.` rendered for `dana.reyes@northwind.example`, who IS `owner` in `membership` for this workspace — measured, twice.** ⛔ **Nothing above explains it**, and it is the only part of this row that still deserves the auth tier.

⚠️ **The account-data half of this row is withdrawn**: the data was good, the page was truthful, and the instrument was wrong.

#### ⚠️ The original reading, kept rather than rewritten ([§2](../CLAUDE.md))

⚡ **The data is good — eleven real, named, scored accounts.** ⛔ **So the journey's failure is no longer explained by absent data**, and the honest remaining question is **why a walk of the first twelve rows of `/accounts` reached none of the eleven.**

⚠️ **Two candidates, and the first is this lane's own instrument**: ① **the helper clicks `row.getByRole('link').first()`, which assumes the first link in a row is the company** — ⛔ **an assumption never checked against the shipped table**; ② the list's ordering surfaces the unnamed minority first. ✅ **Neither is an authorization defect**, which is what this row originally suspected.

🔴 **The *"Settings — restricted. Requires an owner."* symptom is untouched by all of this and remains genuinely unexplained** — 📁 `dana.reyes@northwind.example` is `owner` in `membership` for this workspace, measured. ⚡ **That, and only that, is what still deserves the auth tier's attention.**

#### ⛔ The cheap cause was tried and is ruled out

⚡ **The obvious explanation was that the API serving `:8300` had been running since 16:41 while the reseed replaced the workspace at 19:50** — a long-lived process holding a workspace-scoped cache produces exactly this picture. ✅ **So it was restarted against `signora_lane_a` and the suite re-run.**

🔴 **Identical result: the same four journeys fail with the same *"no account renders its sections"*, and the same two pass.** ⛔ **Naming a cause and not testing it is how a plausible diagnosis becomes the recorded one** ([B-189](#b-189) cost exactly that), **so it is written down as REFUTED rather than left as a suggestion.**

⚠️ **What remains, and it is one hypothesis rather than two:** **the identity and authorization path resolves this member's role and this workspace's accounts from something the reseed did not update** — ⛔ **and *"Settings — restricted. Requires an owner."* rendered for a person the `membership` table calls `owner` is the sharpest single symptom to start from.** ✅ **A reader with the auth tier in front of them will get further than a frontend lane guessing.**

### B-261 · Account 360 cannot key a preference per account type, because nothing tells it what type the account is

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — ⚡ **assignee joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)**: `current_owner = "Lane A"` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **found by this lane implementing [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md), and filed rather than worked around** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **nothing renders wrongly.** ⚠️ **One design rule cannot be satisfied**, and the section states so in code rather than pretending |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** — ✅ **the shipped behaviour is the safe half**: a preference is **not stored** rather than stored under a guess |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A** |

#### ⚡ AUDIT 2026-08-16, Lane A — the obvious fix is forbidden by this module's own design

⚠️ **Recorded before anybody writes it, because the obvious repair is the wrong one and the reason is two files away.**

🔴 **`knowledge_graph` is Lane A's** (`current_owner = "Lane A"`), **serves BOTH reads from one router**, and 📁 **already exports `EntityKind` from its `public/`.** ⚡ **So the field is not missing from the module — it is missing from one of its two answers.**

⛔ **Do NOT add `kind` to `AccountIdentity`.** 📁 **`ListedAccount` composes it rather than extending it, and says why in its own words:**

```python
account: AccountIdentity
kind: EntityKind
created_at: datetime   # …AccountIdentity deliberately holds no such field:
                       # it answers "who is this?", not "when did we learn about it?"
```

⚡ **The same argument governs `kind` exactly**: **`AccountIdentity` answers *who is this*, and `kind` answers *what kind of thing is it*.** ⛔ **Folding it in would put a classification inside an identity resolver** — and 📁 **the interface layer already models the separation**: `ListedAccountResponse` carries `account: AccountIdentityResponse` **beside** `kind: EntityKind`, never inside it.

#### ✅ The two proportionate options, so the next lane starts from the analysis

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **ⓐ** | **Extend `account-identities`' RESPONSE to carry `kind` beside the identity**, in the composition idiom `ListedAccountResponse` already uses | ✅ **Additive · one field · no new endpoint** · ⚡ **the endpoint's own summary already reads *"who these accounts are"*, and *what kind* is the same question about the same set** |
| **ⓑ** | **A dedicated ids-keyed read returning identity + kind** | ⛔ **A second endpoint answering a question the first already almost answers** — ⚠️ **and the row's own objection to the list read applies: disproportionate to the thing it keys** |

⚡ **ⓐ is the recommendation.** ⛔ **Neither is started**: 🔴 **a backend field with no consumer is the unreachable-primitive class this lane has now found five times**, so **the read and Account 360's use of it belong in ONE slice**, with the frontend `AccountIdentity` type and `AccountSectionShell`'s `kind` prop changing in the same change.

⚠️ **Not converted into a `TASK-` row by this lane** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a lane never invents work*, and **the backlog is the product owner's.** ✅ **Recorded here so the fix is one reading rather than one rediscovery.**

#### 📁 The rule

> 📁 **`Fortune Signora Account 360.dc.html` §*States*, Collapsed:** ***"State persists per user and per account TYPE, not per record."***

⚡ **The emphasis is the design's own point.** ⛔ **Keying by `accountId` is the obvious implementation and the one the rule forbids**: a rep who collapses *Technology stack* has decided they do not care about technology stacks **on companies**, not that they do not care about it **on Acme**. **Keyed per record, the preference is re-made on every account opened, which is the same as having none.**

#### ⛔ What this page can actually see

| Read | Returns | Carries `kind`? |
|---|---|---|
| `useAccounts` | `AccountAttention` | ⛔ **No** |
| `useAccountIdentities` | `AccountIdentity` | ⛔ **No** |
| `useAccountsList` *(Companies)* | **`ListedAccount`** | ✅ **Yes — `kind: EntityKind`** |

⚡ **The type exists and is published — to a different screen.** ⛔ **Account 360 reads neither of the two reads that carry it**, and adding a whole list read to key a collapse toggle is disproportionate to the thing it keys.

#### ✅ What shipped instead, and why it is the right half

**`AccountSectionShell` takes `kind: string | null`, and `null` means *persist nothing*.** ⛔ **Not *persist under a default*.** ⚡ **A preference stored under a guessed type is one a rep cannot get back** — they collapse a section, return, and find it open, with a stale key left in their browser under a type that was never theirs. **No preference is an honest state; a wrong one is not.**

🔴 **Two tests pin it** and one pins the fix's shape for whoever closes this: **an unknown type writes nothing**, **an unknown viewer writes nothing**, and **a known pair writes exactly one key containing the type and no record id.**

#### 🔴 The fix is this lane's, and it is NOT a field — corrected 2026-08-12 after reading the module

⚠️ **This row first said *"`AccountIdentity` is the natural home… that is `provider_platform`'s response shape"*. ⛔ **Both halves were wrong** and the correction changes what the next implementer does.

**① The module is [`knowledge_graph`](../backend/modules/knowledge_graph/), not `provider_platform`** — 📁 `interface/router.py` publishes `/workspaces/{id}/account-identities`. ✅ **[`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) assigns it to Lane A, `settled`** — **so this is this lane's to fix end to end and needs no other lane.**

**② `AccountIdentity` refuses new fields BY DOCTRINE, and the doctrine is written into the type.** 📁 `application/queries.py`:

> **"What is deliberately absent, and why — each would be a field a caller could read and not act on… Anything about industry, headcount or domain. Real, claimed, and *not identity*. A read model that grew every firmographic attribute would become the entity record `Entity` refuses to be."**

⚡ **And the module already decided where `kind` goes.** 📁 `ListedAccount` puts it **beside** the identity, not inside — *"one account on a browse page: **who it is, and what kind of thing**"* — and `SearchResultResponse` wraps the same way, with its own sentence for why: ⛔ *"a field that is null wherever it is not a search is a field in the wrong schema."*

🔴 **So the shape this module has chosen is `identity + kind, side by side`, twice, deliberately.** ⛔ **Adding `kind` INSIDE `AccountIdentityResponse` would contradict that** — ⚠️ **and it would put a second representation of `kind` beside `ListedAccountResponse`'s**, which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s duplicated-truth defect: *"remove one rather than synchronising both."*

#### ⚠️ What the fix actually costs, stated so nobody starts it thinking it is small

**Following the module's own shape means `/account-identities` returns a WRAPPER rather than `list[AccountIdentityResponse]`** — ⛔ **a response-shape change on an endpoint three surfaces already read.** ⚡ **`last_observed_at` is the precedent for the alternative**: it was *"weighed against that last rule and admitted"*, with an argument in the type — **so admitting `kind` is available, and it is an argument to make rather than an edit to perform.**

> ⛔ **NOT taken in [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md), deliberately.** 📁 The row is `IN VALIDATION` and **reworking a slice QE is validating is the churn this repository names**; ⚡ **and an API-shape decision inside a module with a written doctrine about that exact schema is not a thing to do quickly to unblock a collapse toggle.** ✅ **The shipped behaviour is safe meanwhile — no preference is stored, which is honest.**

### B-260 · `reasoning@2`'s worked example does not fix protocol-2 grounding, and the prompt-side hypothesis is now spent

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`ai_reasoning_engine`** — ⚡ **assignee joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)**: `current_owner = "Lane A"`, `transition = "settled"` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it invalidates a stated cause, not a shipped behaviour.** ⚡ **Nothing regressed: `reasoning@2` was never released and nothing requests it.** 🔴 **What it changes is what [TASK-459](BACKLOG.md) is expected to deliver when [C-334](LANE_COORDINATION.md)'s credential arrives** |
| **Status** | ⏸️ **`OPEN` — not this lane's to fix, and the reason is a ruling rather than capacity.** 📁 **[D-121](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ① sequences it *"create `@2` → hosted evaluation → promotion if it passes"*, and [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) forbids tuning a prompt until it passes.** ⛔ **So `reasoning@3` is not a thing this lane authors on its own finding** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A**, running the evaluation that [29](architecture/29-ai-reasoning-engine.md) says in writing nobody had run |
| **Reproduced** | ✅ **Twice, independently, same verdict** — the second run recorded in the manifest |

#### 🔴 What the repository believed, and it is written down

📁 **[29 §*The cause, and the precedent that already solved it*](architecture/29-ai-reasoning-engine.md)**:

> **"`reasoning@1` … contains no transformation instruction … What it has is **no example at all**, and both `@2` prompts added one. A 2B model given a copy instruction and no specimen of what to copy is being asked to infer the form, and under protocol 2 it inferred wrongly on every case."**

⚡ **And 29 flags its own exposure, which is what made this worth running**:

> ⚠️ **"A prompt is not code, and no test asserts its content. The claim this slice makes — *that the worked example fixes protocol-2 grounding* — is measured by nothing until the evaluation runs."**

#### ⛔ Measured

**`granite3.3:2b` · `explanation_narration@1` · rendering protocol v2 · `reasoning@2` `b0dc023fae5b`**

| | `reasoning@1` *(committed manifest)* | `reasoning@2` *(this run)* |
|---|---|---|
| **Grounding failures** | **2 of 2** | **2 of 2** |
| **Schema failures** | 0 | 0 |
| **Coverage** | **0.0** | **0.000** |
| **Release** | REFUSED | **REFUSED** |

⛔ **Indistinguishable.** ⚡ **And the model is the one that matters**: `granite3.3:2b` **completes** under protocol 2 — no timeout, 0 transport failures — so ⛔ **this is not [C-222](LANE_COORDINATION.md)'s wall-clock blocker, which is `llama3.1:8b`'s alone.**

#### 🔴 Why the stated cause is disproved

⛔ **`@2` HAS the worked example, in the exact protocol-2 form, and says the quiet part explicitly** — 📁 `reasoning@2.md` rule 3:

> *"Copy the reference character for character … A fact shown as `business_event:2f7c9a10-… — Hired a VP of Engineering` is cited as `business_event:2f7c9a10-…` — **the summary after the dash is not part of the reference.**"*

⛔ **The model copied the whole rendered line anyway**, em dash and summary included:

> `buying_score:44c0cf0b-fe43-5ad1-97cc-c6a847062efc — The buying score that opened this opportunity was 35 out of 120, steady.`
> → **`badly formed hexadecimal UUID string`**

⚡ **So *"it had no specimen of what to copy"* cannot be the cause: it had one, and it was ignored.** ⚠️ **The second run added a second failure mode the first did not show** — `unresolved_citation` on `opportunity:c4b397d4-…`, **a reference the model invented** — which is a different defect from over-copying and **argues capacity rather than instruction.**

#### ✅ What this is worth, and it is the point of filing it

⚡ **[C-334](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is now the ONLY remaining hypothesis, and that is a stronger reason to provision it than the one on record.** 📁 The register says the credential removes an infrastructure blocker. ⛔ **After this run it is also the last untried variable**: **prompt-side has been tried twice and failed twice on a model that completes**, so **a larger model is what is left.**

⛔ **What must NOT happen, and [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) already forbids it in writing**: authoring `@3`, `@4` and `@5` against `granite3.3:2b` until one passes. ⚡ **That is tuning to the measurement**, and 404 §7 names it as the process risk of this exact epic.

⚠️ **One thing this run does NOT establish**, stated so nobody reads it as more than it is: **it says nothing about how a hosted model behaves.** ✅ **It narrows the question to one variable; it does not answer it.**

#### 📁 Recorded as a refusal, never as a release

**The manifest gains a fifth evaluation and `reasoning@2` remains unreleased** — `is_released` **derives** from a passing evaluation rather than declaring one, so a recorded failure cannot grant anything. ⚡ **M9.5 Step A is this module's own precedent** — *"the refusals become repository evidence"* — and a measurement kept only in a report is a measurement the next reader has to take again.

### B-193 · 🟡 Nothing reports a board row still held whose work is already on `main`, and QE tried twice to close the gap and could not

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **nothing shipped is wrong.** ⚠️ **A held row whose work has shipped says a lane is still building something that is done**, and every other lane reads it |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — and deliberately NOT fixed.** ⛔ **Two attempts, both abandoned, and the reasons are below** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A, against itself** |
| **Commit found** | **`fe6d9139`** |

**Steps.** [`TASK-1428`](BACKLOG.md)'s implementation reached `main` at **`a512642`, 2026-08-09**. **Its board row read `CLAIMED` until 2026-08-12** — three days.

**Expected.** Something says so.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Nothing does.** Check 3 catches a `COMPLETE` row that was not removed; **nothing asks the opposite question.**

### ⚡ Why the gap exists, and it is a consequence of a rule that is right

📁 **`IN VALIDATION` is the lane's to set and QE may not set it** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *execution ownership ends at `IN VALIDATION`*). ✅ **That is correct** — QE does not own a lane's execution state. ⛔ **And it means a state nobody may set for you is a state that can be forgotten silently.**

> ⚡ **Lane A named the gap and offered itself as the evidence rather than proposing the check.** **QE built one anyway, and this row is the account of why it does not ship.**

### ⛔ Attempt 1 — matched any status token in the row

**Reported `TASK-1428`, whose row had just been corrected**, because the row narrates *"was `CLAIMED`"* beside its current `IN VALIDATION`. 📁 **The rule was already written 1500 lines above the edit** — *"the FIRST state token in the cell, never any token in it"* — **and QE ignored its own tool's documented lesson.**

### ⛔ Attempt 2 — asked whether the newest commit naming the task touched code

**Went silent on its own reproduction.** `TASK-1428`'s newest mention edits `workflows.toml`; the implementation is four commits older. ⚠️ **A guard that cannot fail on the defect it was written for is Decorative Logic** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)) — **and it took a fire test to see it, not a reading.**

### 🔴 Attempt 3 — scanned every naming commit, and that is where it stopped

✅ **It fires on the reproduction.** ⛔ **And it names the wrong commit.** For `TASK-1428` it reported **`3e800752`** — *"D-215 — C-255, C-256, C-257 are one defect"* — which qualified **only because it touched `infra/state-check.py`**, this very file, while mentioning the task in its body.

> ⛔ **A commit message cannot answer *was this task implemented*.** **Governance commits legitimately name many task ids while touching code**, so the grep confuses *mentions* with *implements* — and **a check that names the wrong commit is worse than no check, because it teaches people to distrust the tool.**

### ⛔ And the register comparison is blind to it

**The obvious alternative — board says held, backlog says moved on — would not have caught this case.** 📁 **[`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) also read `CLAIMED` for those three days.** ⚡ **The same lane sets both, and it forgot both**, which is the failure mode rather than an accident.

### ⚠️ CORRECTED same day, by Lane A — the link exists and QE said it did not

⛔ **This row concluded: *"what a real fix needs is a link from a task to its implementing commit that is not a prose mention — and inventing one is a change to how work is recorded, not a check."*** **That was wrong.**

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already mandates it**, and it is structured rather than prose:

```
Slice-Handoff:
  Milestone:     M12.6 -- TASK-1470
```

✅ **Measured: 325 commits on `main` carry the block**, and the `Milestone` field names the `TASK-nnn`. ⚡ **That is exactly the pair all three attempts were reaching for**, and it is why ③ could only find a governance commit — a body scan sees mentions, and the handoff is a field.

### 🔴 So the reason not to build the held-row check has changed, and the new one is measured

⛔ **The link is missing for 48 of 121 promoted tasks — 40%** — **including [`TASK-1428`](BACKLOG.md), the row that produced this finding.** 📁 `a512642` carries no handoff, which is why every attempt failed against it.

> ⚡ **A check keyed on handoffs would be silent precisely where it is needed.** **That is the guard-that-cannot-fail shape** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)), and it is a better reason to decline than the one this row first gave.

✅ **What QE built instead is the coverage line**, in [`state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py): **one advisory naming how many promoted tasks have no handoff.** ⛔ **One line, not one finding per task** — 48 findings on a first run is how a check teaches people to scroll past it.

**Fire-tested four ways**: it fires on the real state · **is silent when every promoted task is covered** · **reports ALL of them if the scan itself breaks**, rather than going quiet · and does not count a task nobody promoted.

⚠️ **And it reports a BASELINE rather than a target, which the first version did not say.** 📁 **A promoted commit message is immutable**, so the 48 can never gain a handoff — [B-258](#b-258) states the same constraint: *"the five promoted commits cannot be repaired; the repair is the next slice."* ⛔ **A number that cannot reach zero is one people stop reading**, so the line says what movement means: **the count can only be held, and a rise is a slice that shipped without its link.**

> ⚡ **Caught before the check was certified, not after** — QE stopped a running certification 39 seconds in rather than promote an instrument whose number nobody could act on.

⚠️ **The held-row check stays unbuilt, and this row stays open.** ✅ **It becomes viable when [B-258](#b-258) closes the coverage** — which is Lane A's, and which they filed against themselves before QE noticed.

> ⛔ **The rule this produces: a guard belongs at the seam that failed, not at the component downstream of it.** ⚡ **`reachable` and `AccountMenu` are both correct, and both were correct before their fixes** — **what changed is one line in a layout and two in a form, and nothing asserts either.**

### B-190 · 🟡 `state-check` compared two abbreviations of one commit as strings, so every Closeout reported the board had gone backwards on the cycle it was refreshed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py), rule 5g, the execution board's header |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — ⚡ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): a defect in a gate that stops QE certifying is QE's to fix** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **it does not make a bad state pass.** ⚠️ **It fires on a correct one**, and a warning that appears every cycle regardless is one people learn to scroll past — **which costs the check its whole value** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **Not `VERIFIED`: QE found it and QE fixed it** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, cycle 209 Closeout**, by the advisory run that is supposed to confirm the Closeout |
| **Commit found** | **`9c7e052e`** |

**Steps.** Run `python3 infra/state-check.py` after a Closeout where `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` is dated at the 8-character SHA and `PROJECT_STATUS.md` names the 12-character one — **which is what this repository writes.**

**Expected.** *"reachable from HEAD"*.

**Actual.** *"The board has gone backwards — the B-100 signature, where a rebase keeps a lane's side of a shared table."*

### 🔴 The cause

```python
elif status_named and _is_ancestor(named, status_named) and named != status_named:
```

⚡ **`_is_ancestor` is true — a commit is its own ancestor — and `9c7e052e != 9c7e052ec329` as text.** ⛔ **So the check accused the board of reverting seven cycles whenever the two files wrote the same commit at the two lengths the repository actually uses.**

### ⚠️ [B-187](#b-187)'s class, one comparison along

**That one could not see an eight-character SHA. This one saw two and called them two commits.** 📁 **Both are the same mistake: treating an abbreviation as a value rather than as a reference to resolve.**

✅ **Fixed by resolving both through `git rev-parse` and comparing what comes back.**

### ✅ Fire-tested in both directions, because narrowing is only safe if you measure what stops firing ([B-162](#b-162))

| | |
|---|---|
| Same commit, 8 vs 12 characters | ✅ **`True`** — the false positive is gone |
| Same commit, 7 vs full | ✅ **`True`** |
| **Two genuinely different commits** | ⛔ **`False`** — **the B-100 case still fires** |
| A garbage ref | ⛔ **`False`** — an unresolvable ref is not equal to anything |

### B-189 · 🟠 An invitation fixture expired against the real clock at 12:00 UTC today, so an unchanged tree certified twice this morning and cannot certify this afternoon

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`workspace_tenancy`** — [`backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/tests/test_accept_invitation.py`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/tests/test_accept_invitation.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), `current_owner = "Lane A"`, transition settled 2026-08-05 |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **no customer ever sees this**: the fake is a test double and the production `Invitation.state(at=…)` is correct. ⚡ **But it is a Blocking Quality Defect** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)): a failing test, so **no commit can certify and every lane's finished work is held** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE, 2026-08-12.** ⛔ **Fixed by Lane A at `f9cf95ac`, and the repair goes a layer deeper than the clock**: the fake was applying a filter `SqlInvitationRepository.find_live` does not apply. ⚡ **Verified at the source** — the real query matches the partial unique index (`accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`) and says nothing about expiry, which is decided one layer up by `require_pending(now)`. ✅ **So an expired offer now reaches the use case and a person is told *this invitation has expired* rather than *there is no invitation***. ⚠️ **Lane A could not set this cell** — the row was on `lane-qe` and not on their base, and a second row for one defect is worse than none |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, cycle 209**, by a certification that failed on a backend tree **byte-identical to one certified 93 minutes earlier** |
| **Commit found** | **`74a06e07`** — and the backend is unchanged from **`0ffe15f3`**, which certified |

⛔ **This is not a flake, and re-running will not clear it.** ✅ **It reproduces in 0.05 s with no database.**

**Steps.** `cd backend && uv run pytest modules/workspace_tenancy/tests/test_accept_invitation.py` — at any moment after **2026-08-12 12:00:00 UTC**.

**Expected.** 5 tests pass, as they did at 09:34 and 10:44 UTC today.

**Actual.** 5 fail with `InvitationNotFoundError: There is no invitation to this organization for your address.`

### ⚡ The evidence, and it is the same tree three times

📁 **From [`certification/manifest.json`](../certification/manifest.json). `git diff 0ffe15f3...74a06e07 -- backend/` is empty.**

| Certified at | Commit | `pytest` |
|---|---|---|
| **09:34:01 UTC** | `3e0a524c` | ✅ **4414 passed** |
| **10:44:43 UTC** | `0ffe15f3` | ✅ **4414 passed** |
| **12:17:55 UTC** | `74a06e07` | ⛔ **4409 passed, 5 failed** |

### 🔴 The cause — two clocks in one test, and only one of them is declared

```python
NOW = datetime(2026, 8, 5, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)          # :40  the declared clock
"expires_at": NOW + timedelta(days=7),                  # :140 → 2026-08-12 12:00 UTC
and i.state(at=datetime.now(UTC)) is InvitationState.PENDING   # :81  the REAL clock
```

⚡ **The fixture's offer expires at exactly 2026-08-12 12:00 UTC. The fake's `find_live` compares it against the wall clock.** ⛔ **The moment the machine passed noon, every pending invitation in the file became expired, `find_live` returned `None`, and acceptance answered *there is no invitation*.**

> ⚠️ **`state(at=…)` is right, and the production caller is right to pass the real clock.** 🔴 **The defect is that the double ignores the clock its own test declared** — 📁 **a hidden input** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): *"an input that influences behaviour without being part of the declared contract… makes the same declared inputs produce different results, which defeats replay and regression testing."*

**⛔ It was written seven days ago, and seven days is the fixture's own window.** ✅ **The suite was green for every one of them.**

### ✅ The proof Lane A built, and why it cannot go quiet on a date

⛔ **Not a fresh fixture window** — that buys another seven days of silence and is green either way. ✅ **The offer expires in the year 2000**, permanently in the past for any real clock, and is accepted at a `now` before it. ⚡ **Fire-tested: restoring the wall-clock filter turns seven red** — the original five plus both new proofs.

✅ **And a guard so the next one fires on a change rather than on a date**: `test_no_hidden_clock.py` refuses any file in the module that declares a fixed moment and then reads the real clock. **It strips comments and docstrings first** — 📁 [B-252](#b-252)'s lesson one language along — **and it is fire-tested by reintroducing the real defect.**

### ✅ The sweep, and its bound

**Every backend test file carrying a fixed `datetime(20xx, …)` literal was checked for a real-clock read in the same file.** 📁 **Five files mix the two; four are safe** — `test_claim_domain.py`, `test_api_accounts.py` and `test_pagination.py` use `datetime.now()` **as data** (`observed_at`, a cursor position), and `test_opportunity_pipeline.py` compares at **now + 3650 days**.

⛔ **`test_accept_invitation.py:81` is the only place a real clock decides whether a fixed fixture has expired.** ⚠️ **The sweep is a grep over `backend/**/*.py` under a `tests/` path and finds nothing outside it; it cannot see a fixture whose expiry is computed rather than written.**

### 📁 What a fix has to prove

⚡ **Whatever the repair — the fake taking the clock the use case is given, or the test injecting `NOW` — the row closes on a proof that fails when the clock moves**, not on a green run today. ⛔ **A run tomorrow is green either way: the window has already passed, so a fixture rewritten to `NOW + 7 days` from a *new* `NOW` buys another seven days of silence rather than a fix.**

### B-188 · 🟠 `smoke` discarded the build's output, so a transient Docker hiccup was indistinguishable from a broken tree

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/smoke.sh`](../infra/smoke.sh), stage *1. Build* |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — ⚡ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): a defect in a gate that stops QE certifying is QE's to fix** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it does not make a bad tree pass.** ⚡ **It makes a failure unreadable**, which costs a cycle every time and invites the worst possible response: *re-run it and see* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **Not `VERIFIED`: QE found it and QE fixed it** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, cycle 207**, by a certification that reported `NOT CERTIFIED` and gave no way to tell why |
| **Commit found** | **`3e0a524c`** |

**Steps.** `make certify` when the Docker daemon is still stabilising.

**Actual.**

```
gate 'smoke' failed: 2 stages in 11s, slowest 1. Build 11s
  1. Build
    ✗ production images failed to build
```

⛔ **And nothing else.** The line was:

```sh
$COMPOSE build >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "production images failed to build"
```

### Why this is worse than it looks

**Eleven seconds is too fast for a compile failure**, so the shape of the number was the only clue that this was an abort rather than a verdict. ⚡ **QE had to re-run the build by hand to learn the tree was fine — all five images, exit 0, on the same commit.**

> ⛔ **That is precisely the work a gate exists to save.** **A failure that cannot be read teaches one response — *run it again and see* — and that is how a real defect gets re-run until it passes by luck.**

⚠️ **[B-140](#b-140) is the same defect in a different stage**, and its title is the general form: *a failing gate reported its verdict and discarded its evidence.* **Filing this one separately rather than reopening B-140**, because the fix is per-site and the pattern needs a second data point to be worth generalising.

### The fix, and the two sites deliberately left alone

✅ **The build's output is captured to a temp log; on failure the last 40 lines are printed and the full path named.** **A passing build stays silent** — the evidence costs nothing when nothing is wrong.

⛔ **`$COMPOSE up -d --wait` and the teardown still discard theirs**, and that is not an oversight: **the first already names its remedy** (*"see: `$COMPOSE logs`"*) and the second cannot block a verdict. **A sweep here would be change without a defect behind it.**

**Fire-tested both ways:** a failing build prints *"couldn't find env file"*; a passing one prints only its tick and exits 0.

### B-187 · 🟡 `state-check` could not see an eight-character SHA, so it reported the dashboard stale on the cycle it was refreshed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **QE gates** — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py), `_newest_named_commit` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — **advisory noise.** ⛔ **And the harm is the usual one: the report it produced was *false*, on the one cycle a reader most needs to trust it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **Not `VERIFIED`: QE found it and QE fixed it** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, during cycle 205's Closeout**, by the dashboard refusing to go green after it had been correctly refreshed |
| **Commit found** | **`2d996eab`** |

**Steps.** Refresh `PROJECT_STATUS.md` to name a promoted commit written as **eight** hex characters, then `python3 infra/state-check.py`.

**Expected.** `ok PROJECT_STATUS.md names <that commit>`.

**Actual.** ⛔ *"names `a792be6`, which predates the latest certification"* — **a commit from a dated appendix 1,000 lines further down.**

### The matcher was exactly seven

```python
re.findall(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7}\b", text)
```

⚡ **`0dfc07f4` is eight characters, so `\b…{7}\b` cannot match it** — there is no word boundary seven characters in. **The dashboard's own current commit was invisible to the check**, which then fell back to the newest seven-character token anywhere in the file and found one in a **historical appendix**.

> ⛔ **Three fixes were available and two of them were wrong.**
>
> **① Shorten the dashboard's SHAs to seven** — bending the document to suit the parser.
> **② Edit the appendix** — ⛔ **it is a record of what was true then, and [§2](../CLAUDE.md) forbids rewriting one to match now.**
> **③ Widen the matcher to `{7,12}`.** ✅ **The tool was the thing that was wrong.**
>
> ⚡ **A check must never make a document lie in order to satisfy it**, and options ① and ② are both that.

### Fire-tested both ways

**Reverted to `{7}` → the false positive returns.** **Restored to `{7,12}` → `ok`, naming `0dfc07f48a1a`.** ⛔ **A green check is not evidence until something has made it red** ([B-180](#b-180)).

> ⚠️ **This is the third instrument of QE's own to fail this cycle**, after [B-184](#b-184) and [B-185](#b-185). ⚡ **All three were correct about a fact and wrong about what the fact meant** — and in every case the cost was a reader learning to skip the output rather than a wrong decision taken.

### B-185 · 🟠 `--dry-run` rewrites the generated coordination source, and I diagnosed a defect from my own output because of it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Platform Foundation** — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py), argument handling |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** *(Platform Foundation, [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md))* |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a flag whose name and help both promise not to write, writes.** ⚡ **The artifact it rewrites is the one [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) says *"is generated and never edited"* and that every lane polls** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** — found 2026-08-12 by QE |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by QE**, by being bitten by it mid-diagnosis |
| **Commit found** | **`dd04a2fa`** |

**Steps.**

```
sha256sum docs/coordination/coordination.toml      # before
python3 infra/coordination.py --dry-run
sha256sum docs/coordination/coordination.toml      # after
```

**Expected.** Identical. The flag's own help is *"with `--publish`: validate only"*, and `--check` beside it is documented as read-only.

**Actual.** ⛔ **The hashes differ. The file is regenerated and written.** `--dry-run` is only consulted *inside* the publish path; run on its own it falls through to the regenerate-and-write branch, so **the guard word has no effect on the code path a reader would expect it to guard.**

### Why the row is 🟠 rather than 🟡, and it is not the wasted keystroke

⚠️ **QE ran `--dry-run` expecting a report, then read the file, then reasoned about a staleness defect from what it found there** — **including a `generated_from` stamp that was QE's own regeneration, not Lane C's commit.** The committed value is `f50851c`; the value read was `dd04a2f`.

⛔ **A whole diagnosis was drafted on that, and it was wrong.** It was caught only because `git checkout` refused to switch branches over an unexpected modification. ⚡ **The safety here came from git, not from care** — and the next reader may not be switching branches.

> **This is [B-151](#b-151)'s class from the inside: reasoning from something transcribed rather than measured** — except the thing transcribed was **produced by the diagnostic tool itself.** **A read-only-looking command that mutates its subject makes every observation after it untrustworthy**, and nothing in the output says so.

### The repair

✅ **`--dry-run` and `--check` both exit before any write.** ⛔ **And a `--dry-run` that is meaningful only in combination with `--publish` should say so by refusing on its own**, rather than silently doing the most destructive thing available (`CLAUDE.md`: *prefer operations that refuse unsafe states over ones that silently recover from them*).

| **Severity** | 🟡 — **advisory noise.** ⛔ **And that is [B-145](#b-145)'s own severity and its own argument**: *"it degrades the one instrument every lane is now told to poll"* |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** — found 2026-08-12 by QE, re-running `--check` after taking Lane C's branch |
| **Found** | ⚡ **Found because Lane C asked to be checked rather than believed** — *"confirm it yourself after you take the branch rather than on my word."* **They were not wrong; their run was green when they made it** |
| **Commit found** | **`dd04a2fa`** |

**Steps.** `python3 infra/coordination.py --check` on `integration` at `dd04a2fa`.

**Expected.** `coordination: current — 72 task(s)`.

**Actual.** Exit 1 — *"the published source does not match what the generator emits today."*

### The cause, measured rather than theorised

**The republish is `9f1143db`. Three commits land after it** — `c383d342`, `3dca1471`, `dd04a2fa` — **and each edits `BACKLOG.md` or `LANE_COORDINATION.md`, which are exactly the registers the generator projects from.**

**So the file is a correct projection of the tree three commits ago.** The committed stamp `f50851c` is honest about that; the content simply describes an earlier repository.

| Field | Committed | Regenerated |
|---|---|---|
| `awaiting_qe_transition` | `0` | `21` |
| `lane_utilization` | `4.2` | `0.0` |

⛔ **These are planning facts, not clock artifacts** — which is what distinguishes this from [B-145](#b-145), where the drift was `datetime.now()` and no fact had changed.

### The repair is ordering, not code

✅ **Regenerate as the *final* act of a planning batch, after every register edit in it.** ⚡ **The generator is a projection: any commit that edits a source after the projection invalidates it, by construction.**

> ⚠️ **A theory QE drafted and is discarding rather than filing.** `_baseline()` reads `origin/integration`'s commit timestamp, and QE moves that ref on every integration — so it *looked* like the same hidden-input defect one step along (`now()` → `HEAD` → `origin/integration`). ⛔ **It does not hold here: the two commits are 79 seconds apart and the metric is in days.** **It is recorded because it is worth checking the day a drift appears with no register edit behind it** — but it is **not** what happened, and filing it as the cause would have been the [B-179](#b-179) mistake again.

### B-184 · 🟠 `--audit-claims` refuses on two commits that are on `main`, so the check can never pass again

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Platform Foundation / QE gates** — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py), `--audit-claims` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — ⚡ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) makes a gate QE's, and *"a gate that cannot run is not a gate"* is the same argument one step along: a gate that can never pass is not a gate either** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it blocks nothing, and that is precisely the harm.** ⚡ **The check exits 1 on every invocation, so the only way to keep working is to learn to ignore it** — and **the run where it reports something real is indistinguishable from the 200 before it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-12**, after cycle 204 certified, ⛔ **never during it** — changing what a gate means mid-cycle would make the record describe a process that did not run. ⚠️ **`VERIFIED` is not QE's to set here: QE found it, QE fixed it, and QE does not verify its own work** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). **Another lane closes it, or it stays `FIXED`.** ⚡ **Two-sided fire-test, both directions proved:** restoring the old behaviour turns `test_a_breach_already_on_main_is_reported_without_refusing` **red**; making it over-permissive turns `test_the_same_breach_awaiting_promotion_is_still_refused` **red**. **27 passed restored.** ✅ **A second defect fell out of the same range bug and is fixed with it** — the skips report scanned historical claims too and named **131 of 166, 79%**, almost all promoted months ago. **Now 5.** 🔴 **And a third, which is the one worth reading**: `_claim_stowaways` measured `main..parent` while its own docstring said *"already on `integration`"* — **equivalent only while `main` is current.** ⛔ **Promotion had been blocked for days, so `integration` ran ahead and every legitimately fast-forwarded commit read as smuggled, including QE's own.** ⚡ **The promotion block was manufacturing false positives in the check that guards promotion, and the rate grew with the block.** ✅ **Now measured from `_validated_floor()` — the newest certified commit `integration` contains, falling back to `main`.** **Certification is QE's validation marker and it is recorded, so a commit inside a certified snapshot has been through the gates even when promotion is held** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by QE**, running `--audit-claims` before parking the certification record |
| **Commit found** | **`99d4c2b9`** — ⚠️ **the defect is far older than the run that noticed it** |

**Steps.** `python3 infra/certification-guard.py --audit-claims`.

**Expected.** A report of claim commits that carried more than a claim **and can still be acted on**.

**Actual.** `REFUSED`, naming two commits:

| Commit | Date | Also changed | On `main`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `9af1641` — *Claim TASK-004* | 2026-08-02 | `docs/LANE_COORDINATION.md` | ✅ **yes** |
| `ee3a725` — *Claim TASK-458* | 2026-08-07 | `docs/LANE_COORDINATION.md` | ✅ **yes** |

⛔ **Both are immutable and already promoted, so neither can ever be cleared.** ⚡ **The check therefore refuses on every future run**, whatever any lane does.

> ## The message is the tell, and it is false about these two
>
> *"These reached `integration` without validation, certification or promotion. **Validate them before the next Certification Snapshot pins them.**"*
>
> ⛔ **They were pinned, certified and promoted weeks ago.** **The instruction cannot be followed**, which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s *the repository must always tell the truth* — the gate asserts an action that does not exist.

### What the repair is, and what it must not be

⛔ **Not a suppression list.** A hard-coded pair of hashes is the *"a guard that cannot fail"* shape wearing the opposite coat — it would also silence a genuine future breach in those same files.

✅ **Scope the audit to what is still actionable: commits not yet on `main`.** **A breach that has already been promoted is history**, and history is reported once and dated — never re-asserted as a live finding every run.

⚡ **Report the historical two separately and without a non-zero exit**, so the count stays visible and the gate's verdict stops being a foregone conclusion.

> ⚠️ **This is the same class as [B-182](#b-182)**, which QE also wrote: **the stowaway guard cried on the normal state one cycle after shipping.** ⛔ **Twice now a check of mine has been correct about a fact and wrong about whether that fact was a problem** — and both times **the cost was not a false alarm, it was teaching a reader to skip the output.**

> ⚡ **Absorbs [B-243](#b-243), which is the same defect and was filed first.** **Found by Lane A on 2026-08-11** implementing [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md), by a journey failing for a reason unrelated to its slice; **fixed by Lane C at `ee4e34c3`**, wider than first proposed — `alembic.ini` and a third owner credential in the Makefile's E2E block as well as `.env.example`. ⛔ **QE created the duplicate and the full account is on [B-243](#b-243).**
