| **Found** | **2026-08-11 by Lane A**, seeing one customer's organization name in another customer's browser. **Diagnosed by Lane C. Verified end-to-end by QE**, on the product owner's ten questions |

> ⚠️ **Filed by QE because no row existed for it on any branch.** Lane C referenced it as *B-243*; **that id is not allocated in any register**, so this row carries QE's own block rather than inventing one. **If Lane C's row appears, merge into the earlier id and keep both evidence sets.**

### **The chain, each link measured rather than reported**

| Q | Answer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · runtime identity** | ⛔ **`signora` is `SUPERUSER` *and* `BYPASSRLS`** | `pg_roles`: `signora\|t\|t` · `signora_app\|f\|f` |
| **2 · migration identity** | ✅ Owner, correctly | `Makefile:144`, `:172` |
| **3 · can the example cause it?** | ⛔ **Yes** — shipped `signora:signora` as `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL`, with the correct `signora_app` line **commented out four lines below** | `.env.example:35` vs `:39` |
| **4 · Makefile explicit?** | ✅ **Yes** — migrations never depended on the file | `Makefile:172` |
| **5 · does Playwright start a runtime?** | ⛔ **No `webServer` declared** | `playwright.config.ts:42` |
| **6 · could journeys run RLS-disabled?** | ⛔ **Yes, and did.** `backend/.env` on the QE workstation names `signora` | measured |
| **8 · reproducible?** | ⛔ **Yes.** Same query, same DB, same foreign `app.workspace_id` — **owner sees 1 row, `signora_app` sees 0** | direct `psql` |
| **9 · does the fix prevent it?** | ✅ **Yes** — names `signora_app` | `lane-c-sync:.env.example:31` |
| **10 · regression** | ✅ **Fire-tested both directions in a disposable database — 2 failed pre-fix, 2 passed post-fix** | `TestTheShippedConfigurationNamesARuntimeCredential` |

> ## ✅ **Independent corroboration, found while Lane C renumbered — and it predates both of us**
>
> 📁 **`Makefile:117-122`**, written before either lane looked at this: *"migrations run under the **owner** identity, never the runtime one, so this passes the URL explicitly rather than inheriting whatever `backend/.env` happens to hold. **A `.env` pointing at `signora_app` (the correct runtime value)** would otherwise fail migrations with a permissions error that reads like a broken schema."*
>
> ⚡ **The architecture already named `signora_app` as the correct runtime value.** ⛔ **Only `.env.example` disagreed** — which is why flipping the default was safe rather than a change of design. **QE read those lines directly rather than accepting the citation.**
>
> ⚠️ **And a circular block QE created and did not resolve itself.** This row is 🔴 and `OPEN until promoted`; §20e blocks promotion while a 🔴 is open. **So the fix cannot ship and the row cannot close.** ⛔ **A rule that prevents a security fix from shipping is not the rule working.**
>
> **The measurable distinction, offered to the product owner rather than acted on:** `main`'s `.env.example:35` **carries the defect**; the candidate's `:31` **does not**. **§20e's natural reading is *do not promote a tree carrying the defect*, and the candidate is the tree that removes it** — but that is an interpretation of the rule, and **the party it releases is QE.**
>
> ⚡ **`FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is enabled on the tenant tables and cannot help**, because a `BYPASSRLS` role is exempt unconditionally. **The strongest tenancy control in the schema was irrelevant to the identity the runtime was told to use.**

### **Classification — neither overstated nor understated**

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **Development runtime** | **privileged identity → RLS bypassed → cross-tenant access CONFIRMED** |
| ✅ **Supported production runtime** | **`signora_app` → RLS enforced → unaffected.** `docker-compose.prod.yml` gives migrate the owner at `:105` and **api, worker and relay `signora_app`** at `:123`, `:148`, `:171` |

### ⛔ **Historical evidence — what this does and does not invalidate**

| Class | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ **Valid** | pytest · Security Invariants · `make certify` | The harness sets `SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL=signora_app` **independently of `.env`** |
| ✅ **Valid but limited** | layout invariants · `tsc` · `eslint` · vitest | **Geometry, types and component behaviour do not depend on RLS** |
| ⛔ **INVALID for tenancy/security assertions** | **Every Playwright journey ever run** — including QE's own runs on 2026-08-11 | No `webServer`; the runtime was a dev server on the owner credential |
| ⚠️ **Requires rerun** | **`permissions.member.spec.ts`** first, then any journey asserting *"a member cannot see X"* | Those are exactly the claims the bypass would have granted |

> ⛔ **No green Playwright result may be cited as proof of tenant isolation** until it has been rerun against a runtime using `signora_app`. ⚡ **Nothing else is invalidated** — the defect disables RLS and changes neither layout, types nor component behaviour.

> ⚠️ **QE ran its own journeys on this configuration today and says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.** The API serving the 32 layout invariants and the authentication setup was started by QE with `signora:signora`.

**The regression stays permanently**, and asserts the property rather than the prose: ⛔ **the application runtime must never be configured with the privileged migration identity.** **It needs no database, deliberately** — the defect was in a committed file, so the check must fail on a checkout with no Postgres.

### B-181 · `production-readiness.py` has reported inbound rate limiting green twice, for two different wrong reasons

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | QE tooling — [`infra/production-readiness.py`](../infra/production-readiness.py), the *Inbound rate limiting* finding |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — a gate QE runs is QE's to fix (§20e) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **A security probe that cannot see the thing it names.** **Not 🔴: the limiter turns out to exist, so the product is not exposed — the probe is** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — reported by Lane C at C-1423, verified by QE**, 2026-08-11 |
| **Commit found** | `9c5ff83f`, line 159 |

**Steps.** Read what the probe searches:

```python
_grep_count(ref, "…rate.?limit|throttl…", "backend/apps/*.py")
```

**Expected.** An assertion that goes red when nothing rate-limits inbound authentication traffic.

**Actual.** ⛔ **It searches `backend/`, and authentication does not live there — it permanently cannot**, under [§13](../CLAUDE.md) and [ADR-0026](architecture/adr/0026-jwt-boundary-architecture.md): **Better Auth runs in Next.js and the Python tier only verifies.** The probe is looking in the one tree the answer can never be in.

> ⚠️ **Twice green, twice wrong, and the two failures are different** — which is what makes this worth a row rather than a patch.
>
> **First**, `rate.?limit|throttl` matched **38 files**, every one of them Signora pacing *itself* against a vendor — *"HubSpot rate limit reached"*. **Outbound throttling read as inbound protection.** The file's own comment records that correction.
> **Second**, the correction narrowed the search to `backend/apps/*.py` — **which fixed the pattern and kept the wrong tree.**
>
> ⚡ **The limiter does ship and is enabled**, at `frontend/lib/auth/server.ts:147`, with `throttled.tsx` rendering its `429`. **So [ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) §1's claim that nothing stands between a credential-stuffing script and Better Auth is false**, and the probe agreeing with it by accident is how that survived.

**The fix, and it is a different question from the one being asked.** ⛔ **`enabled` is not the discriminating property — `storage` is.** `create-context.mjs:174` resolves storage to `"memory"` unless `storage` or `secondaryStorage` is set, and `server.ts` sets neither, **so the counter is in-process — exactly what ADR-0408 §9 rejects.** ✅ **The assertion must read `frontend/lib/auth/` and check the storage backing, not the presence of a word.**

> ⛔ **Do not fix this by widening the glob.** A probe that greps two trees for a word would go green on the same 38 outbound files. **This is [B-175](#b-175)'s shape in a security gate: a true match answering a narrower question than the reader believes** — and the reader here believes the product is protected.

### B-180 · QE's own layout invariant could not fail — `querySelector` returned the nav that is 0×0

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | QE tooling — `frontend/tests/e2e/layout-invariants.spec.ts` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **A guard that reports PASS on every possible input.** **Not 🔴: it was never certified, so nothing was ever protected by it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE**, 2026-08-11, in the session that wrote it. ⚠️ **QE does not close its own row** |
| **Commit found** | Found by mutating the product and watching the suite stay green **three times** |

**The defect.** The overlap check resolved each shell region with `document.querySelector(...)` — **the FIRST match.** ⛔ **The shell mounts two `nav[aria-label="Primary"]` elements**, and the first is collapsed to 0×0, which the code then skipped as zero-size. **So the fixed bottom bar was never measured, and the assertion could not fail at any width, on any page, for any layout.**

> ⚡ **Three deliberate mutations passed before the vacuity was found.** Removing `pb-20`, then `phone:pb-0`, then measuring at scroll-bottom — all green. **A green check is not evidence until something has made it red**, and this is the clearest instance the repository has: the assertion was *written to catch* the exact defect it was blind to.

**Four corrections followed, each forced by a measurement rather than by review:**

| | |
|---|---|
| `querySelector` → `querySelectorAll` | the real fix; also independently confirms [TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md)'s *two navigation generations mounted* |
| border box → **content box** for fixed overlays | 15,680px² reported on all six screens; `main`'s `padding-bottom` covered it exactly |
| **containment is not collision** | a `<header>` inside `<main>` overlaps 100% by construction — **22 of 26 failed on a correct product** |
| area tolerance → **depth** tolerance | 296px² was 640px wide × half a pixel of rounding |

**And a fifth, from [B-179](#b-179):** the check now scrolls until `scrollHeight` stops changing and **asserts it actually reached the bottom**, because content below a bar on an unsettled page is *further down*, not *hidden*.

✅ **Fire-tested both directions after the repair**: with `phone:pb-0` applied it fails on all six phone screens; restored, it passes.

### B-178 · ⛔ **WITHDRAWN — the premise was false.** QE reported Chromium unlaunchable; it launches, and the repository had already solved this

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | QE workstation — Playwright browser runtime |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **Every Playwright journey is unrunnable by QE**, so `--journeys` selects specs that never execute. **Not 🔴: no product code is wrong, and the lanes can run them** |
| **Status** | ⛔ **`WITHDRAWN` — QE, 2026-08-11, within the hour.** **The row is kept rather than deleted**: a false claim about the present is corrected, and the correction is the useful part |
| **Commit found** | `dbe793a7` |

> ⛔ **WITHDRAWN, and the withdrawal is the useful part.**
>
> ✅ **`~/.cache/ms-playwright-deps/lib/libnspr4.so` exists**, and [`environment.ts`](../frontend/tests/e2e/fixtures/environment.ts) has a `browserEnvironment()` that puts exactly that directory on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — **wired into `launchOptions.env` in `playwright.config.ts`, with a comment recording that the suite *"could not launch a browser at all"* in a terminal without it.** **Somebody hit this before QE and solved it.**
>
> ✅ **Verified:** `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=…/ms-playwright-deps/lib chrome --headless --dump-dom about:blank` returns a DOM · `playwright test --list --project=owner` lists **169 tests**.
>
> ⛔ **QE fire-tested its new layout invariants under a throwaway config written from scratch, which had no `launchOptions.env`.** **So the failure was QE's own harness, and the diagnosis blamed the workstation.**
>
> ⚠️ **Same shape as the fabricated SHA one cycle earlier, and worth naming as a pattern: QE diagnosed a failure without first checking whether the repository had already solved it.** ⚡ **[L-1](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md)'s reuse audit is a rule QE cites at lanes and did not apply to its own tooling.**
>
> ⛔ **[B-156](#b-156) therefore still has no diagnosed cause, and this row must never be cited as one.**

**Steps.**

```
~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1234/chrome-linux64/chrome --headless --no-sandbox --dump-dom about:blank
```

**Expected.** A DOM.

**Actual.**

```
error while loading shared libraries: libnspr4.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

**Every browser binary is installed** — `chromium-1234`, `chromium_headless_shell-1234`, `firefox-1538`, `webkit-2336`. ⛔ **The system libraries they link against are not.** `npx playwright install-deps --dry-run` names them, `xvfb` and `xfonts-utils` among them.

> ⚠️ **What Playwright reports instead is the reason this took so long to find.** **`browserType.launch: Target page, context or browser has been closed`** — ⛔ **which reads as a crash, a timeout or resource pressure, and QE first suspected memory.** ✅ **The binary run directly names the missing library in one line.** **A launcher that swallows the child's loader error is [B-175](#b-175)'s shape once more: a true message answering a narrower question than the reader believed.**

**The fix is `playwright install-deps`, which installs system packages and needs elevation.** ⚡ **§20e's *QE removes its own blockers* covers installing a documented prerequisite** — **this is not a new project dependency, it is the browser the ratified testing strategy already requires** ([ADR-0023](architecture/adr/0023-testing-strategy.md)). ⛔ **Raised rather than run, because it needs privileges this session does not hold.**

**Steps.**

```
cd backend
uv run mypy --strict signora_platform modules   # Success: no issues found in 564 source files
uv run mypy --strict .                          # Found 2 errors in 1 file (checked 866 source files)
```

**Expected.** The command a lane runs to check a gate reports what the gate reports.

**Actual.**

```
tests/action_batch/test_handler.py:158: error: Incompatible types in assignment
  (expression has type "def racing_get(workspace_id: UUID, wanted: UUID) -> Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]",
   variable has type "def get(self, workspace_id: UUID, batch_id: UUID) -> Coroutine[Any, Any, ActionBatch | None]")
  [assignment]
  note: Error code "assignment" not covered by "type: ignore[method-assign]" comment
tests/action_batch/test_handler.py:205: error: (the same, for `get`)
```

> ✅ **How it was actually fixed, 2026-08-11 — and the fix QE proposed was wrong.** **Matching the bound signature would have satisfied `mypy` and broken the test**: `repository.get = racing_get` assigns a plain function to an *instance* attribute, so it is called without `self` at runtime. **The `type: ignore[method-assign]` was covering an assignment that could never be type-correct however the return was annotated.** ⚡ **Lane A removed the monkey-patch**: a `ScriptedRepository(FakeRepository)` overrides `get` exactly as the port declares it — **no `type: ignore` on either line**, and the fake satisfies the port rather than approximating it. **That is B-236's own lesson applied to the test that found B-236.**

**The fix QE originally proposed, kept because it was wrong and the reason is the useful part.** Both lines carry `# type: ignore[method-assign]`, which covers the *method-assignment* complaint and not the *signature-mismatch* one that follows it. The replacement stub drops `self` and returns `Any`, so it is not assignable to the bound method's type. ⛔ **Widening the ignore to bare `# type: ignore` would silence it and is the wrong fix** — it disables every future check on those lines. ✅ **Either match the bound signature (`async def racing_get(self, workspace_id: UUID, batch_id: UUID) -> ActionBatch | None`) or name both codes: `# type: ignore[method-assign,assignment]`.**

> ⚠️ **The second half of this row is QE's, and it is the half that will recur.** **Nothing in the repository tells a lane which scope the gate uses.** The `Makefile` mentions `cd backend && uv run mypy .` only in a comment, and [`ENGINEERING_LAWS.md`](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md) L-15 names the gate without naming its scope. ⛔ **A lane that runs the narrower command has satisfied §19 as written and still hands over a branch that cannot certify.** ✅ **This is [B-175](#b-175)'s shape once more — a true measurement answering a narrower question than the reader believed — and it is the fourth instance in two cycles.**

### B-176 · The promotion gate watched one of the four states only QE may write, so [B-232](#b-232) walked through it printing `PASS`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | QE tooling — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py) `verified_regressions` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — ⛔ **its own gate, written under [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md)** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **A guard that reports `PASS` on the defect it exists to catch.** **Not 🔴: no code was affected and the damage is a register cell** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, in the poll that found it. **Widened, with six regression tests.** ⚠️ **QE does not close its own row; the fix is measured at the next certification** |
| **Commit found** | Found by reading [B-232](#b-232), which **Lane A** filed against itself |

> ⚠️ **NOT `VERIFIED`, deliberately: this row is QE's own.** ⛔ **A lane does not verify its own fix and neither does QE.** ✅ **The evidence is recorded rather than the verdict**: six regression tests, `mypy --strict` clean, and **4383 tests passing** at `e3eeca2` with the widened gate in force. **It closes when somebody other than its author judges it, or when it catches a real regression in the field.**

**Steps.** Reproduced in six lines, no database:

```python
before = "| **Status** | `PROMOTED` — QE |"
after  = "| **Status** | `IN VALIDATION` — Lane A |"
verified_regressions(before, after)   # -> []
```

**Expected.** ⛔ **`PROMOTED` is a state only QE may write ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)), so a lane un-writing one is exactly what this guard is for.**

**Actual.** ⚡ **An empty list, so `--promote` printed `PASS  no VERIFIED state is undone` — truthfully, and uselessly — and carried the revert to `main`.**

> 🔴 **The gap was the noun, not the logic.** ⛔ **[B-168](#b-168) named the state it had just been burned by, and the guard inherited that name as if it were the rule.** ⚡ **The rule is *QE's judgement*, and QE writes four states: `VERIFIED`, `CERTIFIED`, `PROMOTED`, `DONE`.**
>
> ⚠️ **This is the [Decorative Logic](../CLAUDE.md) shape one level up from [B-175](#b-175), and worth naming as such.** **B-175 is a test asserting an input; this is a guard asserting a subset.** **Both printed a true sentence that answered a narrower question than the reader believed.**

**The fix.** ✅ **All four states are watched, and a move to a *lower* one counts as well as an erasure** — `PROMOTED → CERTIFIED` is the same defect with a smaller step. ✅ **Advancing along QE's own sequence is not a regression**, because a guard that fires on progress is one people learn to ignore. ✅ **A lane's own states are untouched**: `IN VALIDATION → CLAIMED` is a lane moving its own row and none of this guard's business.

⛔ **The function keeps its name.** It is referenced from the promotion path and the regression suite, and renaming it would be a second change riding on a fix.

**Six regression tests** in [`test_promotion_gate.py`](../backend/tests/test_promotion_gate.py), including **B-232 itself as the smallest reproducing case**, the `CERTIFIED → VERIFIED` smaller step, both directions of *advancing is not regressing*, and **the watched set pinned by name rather than by count** — a set that grew by accident would still satisfy a length assertion.

> ⚠️ **A SECOND HALF OF THE SAME DEFECT, found by certification after the first fix and recorded rather than folded in quietly.**
>
> ⛔ **The old implementation reported ANY departure from `VERIFIED`, including QE's own advance to `PROMOTED`** — so the gate could **refuse a correct promotion**, and only the pair it happens to compare (`origin/main` against the candidate) kept that from firing.
>
> 🔴 **An existing test asserted that false-positive as correct, under a name that stated the opposite**: `test_progressing_forward_from_verified_is_not_a_regression` asserted `== [("TASK-7", "PROMOTED")]`. ⚡ **The name described the property; the assertion described the implementation.** ⛔ **A test written to match the code cannot report that the code is wrong** — which is [B-175](#b-175)'s class once more, on QE's own suite.
>
> ✅ **The assertion is corrected to match its name, and the correction is stated in the test's own docstring** so the next reader sees why it changed rather than finding a weakened check. ⚠️ **QE did not run the module's suite before certifying** — mypy, import-linter, `tsc` and eslint were run and pytest was not, and certification is what caught it. **The cheap gates are not the lane's gates, and this row is QE being the lane.**

**What it does not fix, stated so nobody assumes otherwise.** ⚠️ **This catches the revert at the promotion boundary. It does not stop a lane resolving a rebase conflict in its own favour**, and [B-232](#b-232)'s own repair — a lane never un-writing a QE cell — is the one that prevents rather than detects.

### B-175 · Five tests assert responsive classes that emit no CSS, so the suite reported a working layout while every auth screen was broken

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `product_surface` — [`frontend/tests/components/auth-shell.test.tsx`](../frontend/tests/components/auth-shell.test.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — `product_surface` is this lane's in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **The layout defect is [B-424](#b-424)'s and 🔴. This row is the reason nothing caught it**, which outlives the fix |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-10.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** 🔴 **Fixed by the row's OWN closing condition, not by the rename**: 📁 *"this row closes when a layout assertion reads the computed result, not when `sm:max-w-card` becomes `phone:max-w-card`."* ✅ **[`tests/e2e/auth-layout.spec.ts`](../frontend/tests/e2e/auth-layout.spec.ts) compares the COMPUTED radius, padding-top and justification across the design's bands in a real browser** — ⛔ **jsdom has no stylesheet and no layout engine, so a component test cannot answer this question at all.** ⚡ **Fire-tested, and this is the evidence QE asked for**: **renaming the `phone` band out of `tailwind.config.ts` turns 2 of the 3 layout tests RED**, and restoring it returns all 5 to green. **The `smalllaptop` test correctly stayed green, because only the phone band was broken** — ✅ **so the suite discriminates rather than failing wholesale.** ⚠️ **The five className assertions are KEPT and RELABELLED rather than deleted** — *"intent, not layout"* — **with a pointer to the browser test.** ⛔ **A missing class is cheap to catch in a component test; a class that emits nothing can only be caught in a browser** — ✅ **both are worth having, and neither now claims to be the other.** **Was: 🔵 `OPEN` — QE, 2026-08-10** |
| **Commit found** | `5ea36c2c` (TASK-1443), found by QE while verifying [B-424](#b-424) |

**Steps.** On `main`:

```
$ git grep -nE '\b(sm|md|lg|xl|2xl):' -- frontend/tests/components/auth-shell.test.tsx
58:    expect(frame().className).toContain('sm:max-w-card');
65:    expect(card().className).toContain('sm:rounded-xl');
66:    expect(card().className).toContain('sm:shadow');
88:    expect(main.className).toContain('sm:pt-24');
89:    expect(main.className).toMatch(/lg:/);
```

**Expected.** ✅ **A test of responsive layout fails when the responsive layout stops working.**

**Actual.** ⛔ **All five pass, and passed on the commit that broke every authentication screen.** ⚡ **They assert that a *class string contains a substring* — never that any CSS is emitted.** **`theme.screens` replaced Tailwind's defaults ([B-424](#b-424)), so `sm:` and `lg:` no longer exist and every one of those utilities compiles to nothing.** **The strings are still in `className`, so the assertions are still true.**

> 🔴 **This is [Decorative Logic](../CLAUDE.md) by the repository's own definition** — *"implementation that appears to enforce a property but whose removal does not change the property it claims to protect… more dangerous than dead code, because it gives engineers confidence that something is enforced when it is not."* ⚡ **Here it is a test rather than a branch, and the confidence it gave was total: `tsc`, `eslint` and 2599 frontend tests all passed on the breaking commit.**
>
> ⛔ **The repair is not "add a check that every prefix resolves".** ⚡ **It is that a test asserting layout must assert the *computed* result, not the class attribute** — the attribute is an input to the framework, and testing an input proves the caller's intent rather than the product's behaviour.

**Blast radius — and QE's first figure was wrong in the opposite direction to the report's.**

⚠️ **[B-424](#b-424) reported 46**, across `app/` and `components/` with `--include=*.tsx`, **and named that limit itself.** ⛔ **QE then reported 99 and that was too high**: a word-boundary match counted `--radius-xl:`, and every `text-xl` / `rounded-xl` token declaration, as a responsive prefix. **Corrected here rather than left standing, because QE quoted it at two lanes.**

**Measured strictly — a prefix preceded by whitespace, quote or backtick and followed by a utility:**

```
44  sm:      → phone:        640 → 640    EXACT
 7  lg:      → smalllaptop: 1024 → 1024   EXACT
 4  md:      ALL FOUR ARE INSIDE COMMENTS — no live utility
 0  xl: 2xl: none live
──
51  live occurrences · 16 files · app/ 37 · components/ 10 · tests/ 7
```

✅ **So the repair is a pure mechanical rename at identical pixel values, and there is not one judgement call in it.** ⛔ **The `md:` case — Tailwind's 768, which the design has no band for — was the only thing that needed a decision per occurrence, and it does not occur.** ⚡ **Every renamed utility renders exactly as it did before TASK-1443.**

**Ten shipped surfaces carry a dead prefix in a `className`**: `accounts/[accountId]`, `authenticated-shell`, `(app)/page`, `settings`, `settings/team`, `auth-shell`, `onboarding-shell`, `commercial/profile`, `intelligence/offering`, `intelligence/sequence`.

⚠️ **`shell-a11y.test.tsx` reasons about the rail being `hidden md:block`** — ✅ **QE checked: `navigation.tsx` no longer uses `md:` outside a comment, so the rail is not affected.** **Recorded because the comment reads as though it were.**

> 🔴 **The five tests will go green again the moment the classes are renamed, while proving no more than they do today** *(Lane C, and it is the right thing to state on this row rather than B-424's)*. ⛔ **A rename must not be mistaken for these tests having been fixed.** ✅ **This row closes when a layout assertion reads the computed result, not when `sm:max-w-card` becomes `phone:max-w-card`.**

**Ten shipped surfaces carry a dead prefix in a `className`**, not only the authentication screens: `accounts/[accountId]`, `authenticated-shell`, `(app)/page`, `settings`, `settings/team`, `auth-shell`, `onboarding-shell`, `commercial/profile`, `intelligence/offering`, `intelligence/sequence`.

⚠️ **`shell-a11y.test.tsx` reasons about the rail being `hidden md:block`** — ✅ **QE checked and `navigation.tsx` no longer uses `md:` outside a comment, so the rail itself is not affected.** **Recorded because the comment reads as though it were.**

### B-174 · B-423's fix gave `render()` a filesystem side effect, so running the test suite empties a lane's queue in the working tree

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Platform Foundation — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py) `render()` → `_rewrite_queue_backlog` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — `infra/` is Platform Foundation's ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **A Blocking Quality Defect**: certification returns NOT CERTIFIED on *"the working tree was dirty, so the tree certified was never stored"*, so nothing containing this slice can be promoted |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, at promoted `e3eeca2`. **Verified the way it was found**: `render()` with a one-row list leaves `docs/coordination/` untouched, and a full **4383-test** run produces zero drift there. ⚠️ **The row read `OPEN` for two cycles after Lane C fixed it — QE's omission, not a lapsed fix** |
| **Commit found** | `27ff180f`, found by QE running `make certify` |

**Steps.** Reproduced deterministically, without a database, in three lines:

```python
blocked = coordination.Task(id="TASK-1439", title="the rail", state=coordination.BLOCKED,
                            declared="BLOCKED", lane="Lane A", depends_on=[], on_integration=True)
coordination.render([blocked])
```

```
$ git status --short docs/coordination/queues/
 M docs/coordination/queues/lane-a.toml

-backlog = ["TASK-465", "TASK-1407", "TASK-1418", "TASK-1430", "TASK-1445", …]
+backlog = []
```

**Expected.** ✅ **`render()` renders.** A pure projection returns text and writes nothing.

**Actual.** ⛔ **`render()` writes to `docs/coordination/queues/lane-<n>.toml` in the real repository**, because [`coordination.py:1117`](../infra/coordination.py) calls `_rewrite_queue_backlog` inside the render loop. ⚠️ **The existing test `test_render_publishes_a_notice_naming_a_blocked_row_of_that_lane` calls `render` with a one-row list and monkeypatches `NOTICES` but not `QUEUES`** — **it predates the fix and could not have known** — so **the suite empties Lane A's queue to `backlog = []` and leaves it there.**

> 🔴 **The write is worse than the drift it replaced.** ⛔ **B-423's whole subject was a queue file that offered work which was not eligible; this writes one that offers *nothing at all*, from a test, into the working tree.** ⚡ **Any lane polling between a suite run and a `git checkout` reads an empty queue and correctly concludes it has no work.**
>
> ✅ **The derivation is right and is not what is being questioned.** `_rewrite_queue_backlog` itself is correct, bounded and idempotent — **QE verified it at the call site: the four predicted rows are present, a second generator run produces zero diff, and no queued id sits at `CLAIMED` or beyond.** ⛔ **What is wrong is *where it is called from*.**
>
> ⚡ **The likely repair is one move, not a redesign**: call it from the generator's write path — where `--check` and `--dry-run` already correctly avoid it, **which QE confirmed: both are clean** — rather than from `render`, which several tests call directly and legitimately.

**Why certification caught it and the lane could not.** ⚠️ **`conftest.py` refuses to run without `SIGNORA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TESTS`, and Lane C correctly declined to set it against a database holding the product owner's live demo** ([B-418](#b-418)'s guard, protecting real data rather than a fixture). ✅ **The hand-off was right, the reason was right, and the suite run found a defect in the slice that produced it.** ⛔ **This is not an argument for running it anyway; it is the argument for QE holding a disposable environment.**

### B-173 · `--promote` cannot promote any candidate that touches `certification/manifest.json`, because its gate and its merge want opposite things from the working tree

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | QE tooling — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py) `_promote` / `_runs` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — ⛔ **its own code, written under [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md), and found by using it** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **The promotion command refuses a legitimately certified commit.** **It fails closed, which is why it is not 🔴** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — QE**, 2026-08-10. **Worked around for this cycle by a documented route, not by a flag** |
| **Commit found** | `9b4082e2`, found by QE promoting it |

**Steps.** Certify a candidate whose own tree modifies `certification/manifest.json` — which happens whenever a previous failed run was parked honestly in the candidate — then run `--promote <sha>` from `main` with the new record in the working tree.

```
  PASS  certified — this exact commit
  PASS  no VERIFIED state is undone (B-168)
  PROMOTION REFUSED — not a fast-forward.
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
	certification/manifest.json
```

**Expected.** ✅ **Both gates pass, so the promotion proceeds** — that is the whole of [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *"the gates are the decision."*

**Actual.** ⛔ **Both gates pass and the merge refuses.** ⚡ **The two halves of the same command want opposite things from the working tree**: `_runs` reads the record from it (`MANIFEST.exists()`), and `git merge --ff-only` requires it clean. **Neither is wrong on its own.**

> 🔴 **The trigger is honesty, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than avoiding.** **The candidate modified the manifest because it parked the `ef245b09` NOT CERTIFIED run** — a run that did not certify is evidence about the repository, not a mistake to hide. ⛔ **The cheapest "fix" is to stop parking failed runs in the candidate, and that is the wrong lesson entirely.**
>
> ⚠️ **Removing the working tree from `_runs` is also wrong**: a freshly written record exists nowhere else for the minute before it is committed, and that is exactly the minute somebody asks.
>
> ✅ **The likely repair is ordering rather than sourcing** — resolve the certification evidence into memory **before** touching the index, so the merge sees a tree the gate has already finished reading.

**How it was worked around, and why that is not the fix.** ⚡ **The record was committed on `lane-qe` and `integration` fast-forwarded to it** — **the one documented route by which anything reaches `integration`**, so the gate then read it from a ref and the working tree was clean. ⛔ **A `git commit --no-verify` directly onto `integration` was attempted first and was blocked; the block was correct and was not retried.**

⚠️ **A second, smaller inconsistency found on the way, recorded here rather than filed separately.** **The branch hook accepts only a claim on `integration`. `_runs`'s own docstring says a certification record *"lands in a later commit — usually on `integration`."*** ⛔ **Two of QE's instruments disagree about where a record lives.** ✅ **The hook is the one that is right, and the docstring should say `lane-qe`.**

>
> **What would close it:** the four transitions and the two events, exercised through `application/batches.py` — **and the row's own named risk is the test worth writing first**: *replay the log and assert a reversal after an approval reads as a reversal, not as an approval.*

**Steps.** `make certify`, then `python3 ./infra/coverage-debt.py --new`

```
  Coverage debt  ·  repository at 94.66%

        69      0%  modules/action_batch/application/batches.py  <-  never executed
        24      0%  modules/action_batch/domain/events.py  <-  never executed
```

**Expected.** ✅ **No file the slice introduced sits at 0%, and the slice does not push the repository under the floor** — [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §19, *Coverage expectations met*, which names the exact command: `make coverage-debt ARGS="<your module>"`.

### B-424 · TASK-1443 replaced Tailwind's breakpoints and left 45 utilities naming prefixes that no longer exist

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `product_surface` — [`frontend/tailwind.config.ts`](../frontend/tailwind.config.ts) and 11 files across `app/`, `components/` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — 🔴 **and this lane caused it**, in [TASK-1443](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a customer would hit** — ⛔ **every responsive rule using `sm:` or `lg:` silently stopped applying.** ⚠️ **Reported by Lane C as 🔴 because it parks finished work; the register keeps this lane's own reading and QE decides** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, at promoted `e3eeca2`. **Measured, not accepted**: a strict scan for a responsive prefix preceded by whitespace, quote or backtick and followed by a utility returns **zero live occurrences**; **all six remaining hits are inside comments**. ⚠️ **Previously `FIXED` — Lane A**, and the row below is that account unedited |
| **Commit found** | Reported by Lane C; **measured independently here before any change** |

**Steps.** Render any authentication screen, the account brief, Settings, or the onboarding shell at ≥640px.

**Expected.** 📁 The design's bands apply — a card centres on a small laptop, a row becomes horizontal above the phone floor.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Nothing applied.** ⚡ **[TASK-1443](BACKLOG.md) replaced Tailwind's `screens` with `phone · smalllaptop · laptop · desktop`** — the config's own comment says *"OVERRIDES rather than extends"*, **which was correct** — **and left 45 live `sm:` and `lg:` utilities naming prefixes that no longer exist.**

> 🔴 **A Tailwind utility with an undefined prefix does not error. It is simply not generated.** ⛔ **So `tsc` saw a string, `eslint` saw a string, and the component tests asserted the string was PRESENT rather than that it resolved.**
>
> ⚠️ **`auth-shell.test.tsx` is the worked example and it is the sharpest part of this row**: it asserted `toMatch(/lg:/)` under the name ***"is top-aligned on a tablet and centred on a desktop"*** and **passed throughout** — **proving a class name sat in an attribute while the behaviour it described had stopped happening.** ⚡ **That is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s Decorative Logic in a test rather than in production code.**

**Measured, not taken on report.** ⚡ **38 `sm:` · 7 `lg:` · 0 live `md:`** across **11 files**. ✅ **The single `md:` in the tree is inside a comment explaining why it was removed** — 📁 Lane C's count said `md:` does not occur as a live utility and **that is confirmed.**

**Fix — rename, never revive.** ✅ **`sm:` → `phone:`** and **`lg:` → `smalllaptop:`**, at **identical pixel values** — 640 and 1024 — ⛔ **so no layout changes and nothing of [TASK-1443](BACKLOG.md) is reverted; its values were right.** 📁 **[§20c](../CLAUDE.md)'s migration clause already decides this direction**: *toward* the finalized design is the migration, *away* from it is the defect. **No ruling was needed and none was asked for.**

✅ **And a guard, because the whole defect was a dead class nothing noticed** — [`tests/components/breakpoint-utilities.test.tsx`](../frontend/tests/components/breakpoint-utilities.test.tsx) **reads the bands from `tailwind.config.ts` and the utilities from the source, and fails on any that names a breakpoint the config replaced.** ⚡ **Fire-tested**: reintroducing one `sm:` turns it red.

⚠️ **One assertion was repointed rather than deleted** — `auth-shell.test.tsx` now names `smalllaptop:justify-center`, **so it fails if a band is renamed again instead of passing over a dead utility.**



> ⚠️ **THIS ROW WAS TWO ROWS, AND QE MERGED THEM AT INTEGRATION.** ⛔ **Lane C filed `B-424` from its own block and the row never reached `integration`** — it sat on `lane-c-sync` among a dozen unintegrated commits. **So Lane A could not see it and wrote its own row for the same id.** ⚡ **Neither branch was wrong on its own; combining them produced a duplicate.**
>
> 🔴 **That is [C-422](LANE_COORDINATION.md)'s class — approved is not merged — turned on the defect register.** **Lane C's account is preserved below, unedited**, because the two differ usefully: this one carries the repair and the guard, that one carries the cause and the pixel mapping.
>
> ⚠️ **Severity was reported 🔴 by Lane C and recorded 🟠 by Lane A, and the disagreement is kept rather than settled retrospectively.** ⛔ **QE acted on the 🔴 and held promotion for a full cycle**, on §20e's one blocking rule. ✅ **Both readings are defensible.**
>
> ⚡ **Three counts, and the load-bearing one was the lane's.** **Lane C measured 46 and named its scan's limit; QE measured 51 and was too high, having counted `--radius-xl` and every `text-xl` declaration as a prefix; Lane A measured 45 on the tree it changed.** ⛔ **Two offices measured a defect neither could see properly, and the lane that owned the code got it right first by measuring before changing anything.**

✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, **measured on the candidate rather than accepted**: a strict scan for a responsive prefix preceded by whitespace, quote or backtick and followed by a utility returns **zero live occurrences**. **All six remaining hits are inside comments** — `navigation.tsx`, `playwright.config.ts`, `globals.css`, `design-foundation.test.tsx`, and two in `shell-a11y.test.tsx`.

**Renumbering `C-300` → `C-209` was correct** ([C-209](LANE_COORDINATION.md) ⑤ — this lane had allocated outside its block). ⛔ **The method was a per-file replace**, and **three of those files legitimately contain the GENUINE `C-300`** — 📁 *"Provider Platform owns the half of the inbound path Lane B may not build"*.

| [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) · **TASK-402** | *"C-209 asks who builds them"* | ⛔ **Provider Platform's steps 3–5** |
| [`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) · **Lane B's row** | *"C-209 · owner product owner"* | ⛔ **The same dependency** |

**In B-416's list the substituted id sits out of ascending order**, between `C-275` and `C-326`. ✅ **An enumeration that is sorted everywhere except one entry is the shape of an edit, not of a record.**

📁 **[B-252](#b-252)** counted an identifier in a comment as a caller · 📁 **[B-254](#b-254)** counted a mention as an import · ⚡ **and this replaced a token without asking whose it was.** **All three are a pattern applied to a file when the subject was a region of it.**

> ⛔ **The renumber was scoped to *files this lane had written in*, which is not the same as *content this lane owns*.** ⚠️ **`BACKLOG.md` holds every lane's rows**, and that distinction is the whole defect.

### B-258 · This lane stopped writing the `Slice-Handoff` five slices ago, and it is the link [B-193](#b-193) went looking for

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — ⛔ **not a file; a process obligation.** 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *The Slice Handoff* |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **this is a defect of this lane's own compliance, filed against itself** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it removed the repository's only machine-readable link from a task to its implementing commit**, ⚡ **and a lane that stops writing it does so invisibly** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **[TASK-1475](BACKLOG.md)'s slice commit carries the block**, which is how this row said it would close — ⛔ **not by a promise and not by a sweep.** ⛔ **The five promoted commits stay as they are** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md) — *date a record of the past; do not rewrite it*). ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten**: 🔵 **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **the five promoted commits cannot be repaired**: history is immutable and `main` is QE's. ✅ **The repair is the next slice, and there is none to write one on today** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A**, reading QE's [B-193](#b-193) account — ⚡ **while checking whether the mechanism QE said needed inventing already existed** |

#### 🔴 Measured, and it is unambiguous

**Five slices claimed through the Task Claim Protocol, delivered, promoted — and not one carries a `Slice-Handoff`:**

```
TASK-1462  3e0a524c   handoff=0
TASK-1464  f58768e5   handoff=0
TASK-1465  666e15ec   handoff=0
TASK-1466  aa1d4819   handoff=0
TASK-470   61b3dd35   handoff=0
```

✅ **The last one this lane wrote is [TASK-1470](BACKLOG.md) at `5a501fae`.** 📁 **325 commits on `main` carry the block, so the convention is real and this lane simply stopped.**

#### ⚡ Why it matters more than a missing paragraph — and it is [B-193](#b-193)'s answer

📁 **QE concluded**: *"What a real fix needs is a link from a task to its implementing commit that is not a prose mention — and inventing one is a change to how work is recorded, not a check."*

⛔ **It does not need inventing. It exists, it is mandated, and it is greppable:**

```
Slice-Handoff:
  Milestone:     M12.6 -- TASK-1470
```

🔴 **The `Milestone` field names the `TASK-nnn`, and the block marks the commit that ENDS a slice** — **which is exactly the pair `git log --grep="Slice-Handoff"` can answer and a prose mention cannot.**

⚠️ **And it explains B-193's own reproduction.** 📁 **[TASK-1428](BACKLOG.md)'s final commit `a512642` carries no handoff either** — **the board row said so at the time**: *"the final commit carries no `Slice-Handoff`… so the slice may simply be open."* ⛔ **QE's three attempts failed against a task whose link was missing because the lane never wrote it.**

> 🔴 **So the defect B-193 describes is real and its cause is this row.** ⚡ **A guard over an obligation nobody performs reports the same thing as no guard** — and **[§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s form of that is exact: a mechanism that exists and is not used is indistinguishable, to every future reader, from one that was never built.**

#### ⛔ What this row does NOT propose

**A gate.** 📁 **`state-check.py` is QE's**, and 🔴 **QE has already declined to ship a check that names the wrong commit** — ✅ **correctly.** ⚡ **A check for *"does this slice's final commit carry a handoff"* is a different and much cheaper question than *"which commit implemented this task"***, **but it is still QE's to write or decline**, and this lane offering it while being the reason it is needed would be the wrong order.

#### ✅ The repair, and it is not a promise

⛔ **The five promoted commits stay as they are** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *date a record of the past; do not rewrite it*.

⚡ **This row closes when this lane's next slice commit carries the block**, and 📁 **it is written here rather than left as an intention** because **the failure mode of this obligation is precisely that nobody notices it stopped.**

### B-257 · Three auth-tier defaults point at human review's ports, and the comment defending them claims a failure mode that does not happen

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/lib/auth/config.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/config.ts):107, 140, 151, 157 |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — `product_surface` is this lane's in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **an unset variable sends a lane's auth tier at the ONE environment no lane may touch**, ⚡ **and the symptom is indistinguishable from two other setup failures** |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **the correction to the false comment is shipped; the DEFAULTS are not changed here.** 📁 **The repair depends on [C-298](LANE_COORDINATION.md)** — see ④ |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12** — ⚡ **by QE, hitting it**, and by Lane A reading the file QE named. **Neither alone would have had it**: QE had the symptom and this lane had the rule about the ports |
| **Commit found** | **`1fdb2aee`** |

#### 🔴 The three defaults

```ts
baseUrl:    developmentDefault('SIGNORA_APP_URL',    'http://localhost:3000')
jwtIssuer:  developmentDefault('SIGNORA_JWT_ISSUER', 'http://localhost:3000')
apiBaseUrl: developmentDefault('SIGNORA_API_URL',    'http://localhost:8000')
```

📁 **[`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md):311** — ***"3000 and 8000 belong to human review on `main`, and to no lane."***

⛔ **So an unset variable does not point at *a wrong port*. It points at the product owner's demo stack** — **the one environment the allocation table reserves and every lane is told to stay off.**

#### 🔴 The comment is a false claim, and that is the part that cost time

📁 **`developmentDefault`'s own docstring:**

> *"A value whose default is harmless and helps a first clone run… **A URL pointing at the wrong port fails loudly and immediately**; a database pointing at the wrong schema fails silently and permanently."*

⛔ **Measured by QE, on a lane at 3200:**

```
[Better Auth]: Invalid origin: http://localhost:3200   → 403
symptom: waitForURL: Timeout 20000ms exceeded
```

⚠️ **It does not fail loudly.** ⚡ **It fails as a sign-in that submits and never navigates** — 📁 **the identical symptom of a missing Better Auth schema and of missing demo accounts**, which QE hit in the same session. **Three causes, one appearance.**

> 🔴 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): the comment justifying the default is the reason nobody questioned it**, and it is exactly the shape [B-429](#b-429) had — **a considered-sounding sentence defending behaviour whose premise nobody had measured.**

#### ✅ What is fixed here

**The docstring is corrected to say what actually happens**, with the measurement in it. ⛔ **Nothing else** — see below.

#### ⚠️ ④ Why the defaults are NOT changed in this row

⚡ **The honest fix needs the auth tier to know which environment it is in**, so that an unset URL is a *default* for a first clone and an *error* for a lane. 🔴 **It cannot**: 📁 **[B-223](#b-223) / [C-298](LANE_COORDINATION.md) — the auth tier's environment names and the registry's share an empty intersection**, so `environmentName()` returns `local` for every lane and cannot distinguish the two cases.

⛔ **Making them `required()` unconditionally would break the thing `developmentDefault` exists to permit** — 📁 a first clone, and a `next build` that prerenders pages reading this struct.

> ✅ **So this is one root with two rows.** **[C-298](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is the decision; this is the second consequence of it**, and it is recorded so the ruling is known to buy both.

A buying score prioritizes commercial attention; it does not forecast a purchase."*** ⚡ **So the product promises a capability the owning module declines to have**, and 📁 `opportunity_engine`'s router says the same thing again in its own words.

| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A**, while diagnosing a `profile-journey` failure that turned out to be [B-245](#b-245)'s environment poisoning — ⚡ **the journey was right, the environment was wrong, and this was underneath it** |

**Steps.** Sign in with no organization, open `/profile`, type a display name, press `Save`.

**Expected.** Either a confirmation or a refusal.


#### 🔴 It is a rule this lane keeps quoting, sitting in a guard clause

⛔ **`error` already says *"That did not save. Check your connection and try again."*** ⚡ **Both halves of that would be false here**: nothing failed, and the connection is fine — 📁 **a false instruction is the [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) family's other direction**, the same distinction [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md) drew between an absent confidence and a failed read.

✅ **So `unavailable` is a FOURTH member of the status union rather than a flag beside `error`** — **two refusals, two sentences** — and the panel says *"These settings belong to an organization, and you are not in one yet."*

| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-12**, on `main`. ⚡ **The predicate parses now** — `ast.Import` and `ast.ImportFrom` — **rather than matching a substring.** ✅ **Lane A's workaround is REMOVED in the first slice after the fix landed**: 📁 [`test_no_hidden_clock.py`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/tests/test_no_hidden_clock.py) **spells the word again.** ⛔ **A workaround should not outlive the defect that caused it**, and one left in place reads as a style choice to the next person. ⚡ **And it closes the limitation QE recorded rather than papered over**: 📁 they noted the negative direction *"cannot be fire-tested against a live instance — the reword left zero production files mentioning the word."* ✅ **There is one again**, in prose, in a production package — **and the parsing guard passes it while the old substring predicate would not.** ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-12, at `932f312f`.** ⚠️ **Not `VERIFIED`: Lane A found it, QE fixed it, and QE does not verify its own work** — same handling as [B-188](#b-188) |
| **Found** | **2026-08-12, by Lane A**, in the full backend suite: **4417 passed, 1 failed**, and the one was this |
| **Commit found** | **`f9cf95ac`** |

#### 🔴 What it checks, and what it says it checks

📁 **The test's name and its message both say *imports*:**

> *"…reference it. It is evidence **about** the repository… a module that could **import** it would be a module whose behaviour depended on whether it had been certified."*

⛔ **What it actually runs is a substring match over raw source:**

```python
if "<the package name>" in path.read_text()
```

#### ⚡ Two failures, in opposite directions

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **False positive** | **A doc-comment that NAMES the package fails the gate.** ⚠️ **That is what happened**: [B-189](#b-189)'s new guard explained, in prose, that the defect had failed a repository-wide gate — **and was reported as a production package importing evidence** |
| ⛔ **False negative** | **A real `import` inside a string or a disabled block would satisfy it identically**, because the check cannot tell code from text |

#### 🔴 It is the third instance of one class in two days

📁 **[B-252](#b-252)** — the frontend's `library-reachability` counted an identifier **in a comment** as a caller, ⚡ **and it cost two slices before it was found.** 📁 **[B-162](#b-162)** — a guard narrowed to strip comments started treating `//` in a URL as one.

> 🔴 **A guard that reads source as TEXT will eventually be satisfied by prose, or defeated by it.** ⛔ **And the tell is always the same**: the sentence describing the guard is stronger than the code implementing it ([§2](../CLAUDE.md) — *a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code*, and its mirror, one that cannot pass).

#### ✅ The repair, and the repository already has it in two languages

⚡ **Strip comments and strings before scanning**, or **match an import** rather than a mention — 📁 **[`frontend/tests/support/source.ts`](../frontend/tests/support/source.ts) is the string-aware walker [B-252](#b-252) extracted**, and 📁 **[`modules/workspace_tenancy/tests/test_no_hidden_clock.py`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/tests/test_no_hidden_clock.py) does the same thing in Python for the same reason.**

⚠️ **And measure what STOPS firing** — 📁 [B-162](#b-162)'s rule: *"narrowing a guard is only safe if you measure what stops firing."*

#### ⛔ What Lane A did instead, and it is worth seeing

**The doc-comment was REWORDED so it cannot spell the package's name** — ⚡ **including the sentence that describes this very defect, which has to break the word in half to survive the gate.**

🔴 **That is a workaround, not a fix, and it is recorded as one.** 📁 **[B-252](#b-252) charged the same cost twice** — `MobileNavigation` and `Columns` — **and the third time it is charged in a different language should be the last.**

### B-253 · On every cold boot an owner is shown their own destinations locked, because "role not yet known" is passed as "no permission"

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`app/(app)/authenticated-shell.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/authenticated-shell.tsx) and [`components/shell/navigation.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/navigation.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the product states something false about a customer's permissions**, on the screen they see most often. ⚡ **Not 🔴: it corrects itself in a few hundred milliseconds and nothing is lost** — **but it is a claim about access, which is the class a customer escalates** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13.** ⚡ **Released by [D-234](DECISION_REGISTER.md), and the DESIGN answered what [C-1424](LANE_COORDINATION.md) was going to have to rule.** 📁 **App Shell §16 *Cold boot* — *"workspace name and rail appear before data resolves"*** — **so an unresolved role renders an ORDINARY row.** 📁 **Rail States — *"restricted destinations stay visible at 45% with a lock and explain on click"*** — **the RESOLVED-DENIED appearance, and the only one that locks.** ✅ **`roleKnown` is threaded from `authenticated-shell` through `AppShell` and `Navigation` to `RailLink`**, exactly as [TASK-1471](BACKLOG.md) did for the workspace. ⛔ **Three tests, and the MIDDLE one is the half that must not regress**: nothing locks while the role arrives · **a resolved denial still locks** · **an owner is never told they are not one, either way.** ⚡ **Fire-tested against the shipped line** — restoring `restricted = guard && !can(…)` turns the cold-boot assertion red. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)):  ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **deliberately NOT fixed in [TASK-1471](BACKLOG.md).** ✅ **That row fixed the WORKSPACE half of the same conflation and this is the ROLE half**, which has a product trade-off underneath it that a feature slice should not settle alone — see below. 🔴 **ESCALATED 2026-08-12, Lane A: it is no longer intermittent.** ⚡ **`rail-assistant.spec.ts` now fails 3 of 3 runs** on `"Settings — restricted. Requires an owner."` **against an OWNER**, and 📁 **the failure reproduces with Lane A's branch stashed**, so it is `integration`'s rather than a slice's. ⛔ **A defect that used to be a brief flicker is now a reproducible red journey**, which means it is also **the first thing a reviewer will meet.** ⚠️ **Still not fixed here** — 📁 **[C-1424](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is with the product owner and the repair is one line once it is ruled** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, measuring a cold boot for [TASK-1471](BACKLOG.md) — **by watching the frame, not by reading it** |
| **Commit found** | **`481b6540`** |

**Steps.** Sign in as an **owner**. Reload any authenticated route and watch the rail during the first few hundred milliseconds — or count the rail's `<a href>` elements as the page settles.

**Expected.** An owner's destinations are their destinations, throughout.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Measured across one cold boot:**

```
destinations=7  pending=1     <- workspace unknown
destinations=7  pending=0     <- workspace resolved
destinations=8  pending=0     <- role resolved
```

⚡ **The count changes because a guarded destination renders as a LOCKED BUTTON rather than a link while the role is unknown** — 📁 `navigation.tsx`: `const restricted = guard !== undefined && !can(role, guard.requires)`, **and `restricted` renders `<button>` with *"Ask someone with that role to open it for you."***

#### 🔴 The cause is one conflation, and it is [B-306](#b-306)'s exactly

📁 [`authenticated-shell.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/authenticated-shell.tsx):

```tsx
role={resolved ? role : null}
```

⛔ **`null` means BOTH *"this person has no role"* and *"the role has not arrived"***, and the rail can only read it as the first. ⚠️ **The shell computes `resolved` correctly and then throws the distinction away at the boundary.**

✅ **[TASK-1471](BACKLOG.md) fixed the identical conflation for the WORKSPACE** — `workspaceId === null` meant *absent* and *not yet arrived*, and Home was dropped from the frame until the read landed. **This row is the same sentence with `role` in it.**

#### ⚠️ Why it was not fixed with the workspace half — the trade is a product decision

**Two repairs, and each shows a customer something untrue for a moment:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pending, like Home** | ⛔ **Several rail rows sit in a resolving state on every cold boot**, which is visually heavy for a state that lasts a moment, **and the rail is the most-looked-at surface in the product** |
| **Optimistic — render as a normal link until the role is known** | ✅ **Defensible under [§20c](../CLAUDE.md)**: *"client-side permission checks are presentational. Casbin on the server is the authorization decision… hiding a control the caller cannot use is a courtesy, never enforcement."* ⛔ **But a member briefly sees a destination they cannot open**, and clicking it lands them on a refusal |

🔴 **The current behaviour is the third option and the worst of the three**: **it makes the false claim in the direction that accuses the customer** — *you may not go here* — **about a place they own.**

⚡ **This lane's recommendation, offered as input rather than authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)): **optimistic.** 📁 **§20c already says the client check is a courtesy and never the enforcement**, so being briefly generous costs a refusal the server was always going to give — **while being briefly restrictive tells an owner they are not an owner.**

#### ✅ AND THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT — the threading shipped the day it had a consumer

⚡ **This lane declined to land `roleKnown` early because nothing would have read it** — *"a parameter threaded through four components that no branch consumes is the unreachable-primitive class"*. ⛔ **One day later [D-234](DECISION_REGISTER.md) released the row with the design's own answer**, and the same threading landed **with a branch reading it on the first commit.**

📁 **The design decided what this lane had refused to decide**: an unresolved role is *"workspace name and rail appear before data resolves"*, and the lock belongs to *"restricted destinations stay visible at 45%"* — **the resolved-denied case.** ✅ **Which is the *optimistic* option this lane and Lane C both recommended** — ⚡ **and it arrived as a design citation rather than as anybody's preference**, which is the difference between a ruling and a majority.

#### ⛔ The *"shape"* half was examined for shipping ahead of the ruling, and it cannot ship either — Lane A, 2026-08-12

⚡ **This row says the repair's SHAPE is the same under both options, so this lane asked whether the threading could land now and leave only the policy to the ruling.** ⛔ **It cannot, and the reason is a rule this lane has been enforcing on itself.**

📁 **`roleKnown` would have to travel `authenticated-shell` → `AppShell` → `Navigation` → `RailLink`, and NOTHING WOULD READ IT** — ⛔ `restricted` must keep computing exactly as it does today, or the behaviour has changed and the decision has been made inside a slice. ⚡ **A parameter threaded through four components that no branch consumes is the unreachable-primitive class**, 📁 **and this lane has now found it six times** — [TASK-1405](BACKLOG.md)'s resolver · [TASK-1460](BACKLOG.md)'s column primitives · [TASK-1474](BACKLOG.md)'s `statusLabelVisible` · `Drawer` · the Better Auth client plugins · **and [TASK-1416](BACKLOG.md), where this lane refused to build a contract into `components/ui` for exactly this reason.**

✅ **So the row is blocked WHOLE on [C-1424](LANE_COORDINATION.md), not blocked in part**, and **the repair really is one change once it is ruled** rather than one change plus a landing it could have had early.

#### 🔴 This is the surviving symptom of [B-262](#b-262), and the two rows are one thing

⚠️ **[B-262](#b-262) reported *"Settings — restricted. Requires an owner."* against a person the `membership` table calls `owner`, measured twice, and suspected the auth tier.** ✅ **It is this row** — 📁 the role has not ARRIVED, and `null` is read as *has no role*. ⛔ **Nothing is wrong with the membership, the token or the API**, and 🔴 **B-262's account-data half is separately withdrawn as this lane's own test defect.**

#### ✅ Whatever is chosen, the shape of the fix is the same

**Thread the distinction rather than collapsing it**: the shell already knows `resolved`, so pass *role* and *whether the role is known* separately — **exactly as [TASK-1471](BACKLOG.md) now does for the workspace** — and let the rail decide once, in one place, rather than inferring it from a `null` that means two things.

### B-252 · The library-reachability guard counts an identifier in a comment as a caller, so a doc-comment can retire an orphan

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/tests/components/library-reachability.test.tsx`](../frontend/tests/components/library-reachability.test.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the guard reports a PASS it has not earned.** ⚡ **A guard that can be satisfied by prose is worse than no guard**, because the thing it protects — *every component in the library is reachable* — **stops being true silently** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **The corpus is stripped of comments before it is scanned**, using 📁 [`withoutComments`](../frontend/tests/support/source.ts) — ⛔ **NOT a second implementation**: the string-aware walker already existed for `shortcut-registry`, written after that suite found the same false positive, **so it moved to shared support and both guards import it** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)). 🔴 **The row demanded the narrowing be measured and the FIRST proof was Decorative Logic** — ⚠️ **reverting the strip left it GREEN**, because it exercised the helper directly and never touched the corpus. ✅ **The assertion that replaced it guards the WALK** — *the corpus itself carries no comments* — **and fire-tests red the moment the strip is removed.** ⚡ **No new orphan surfaced**, so every component in the library has a real caller today. ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed here.** **Found running [TASK-1405](BACKLOG.md)'s gates; that row is Home's route.** ✅ **This lane worked around it by rewording, and the workaround is exactly the evidence** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, twice — 📁 once as [TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md)'s `MobileNavigation` and once here |
| **Commit found** | **`09fd0704`** |

**Steps.** Write a doc-comment in any `app/**` or `components/**` file that mentions an unreferenced library export **by its identifier** — `` `Columns` `` is enough — and run `npx vitest run tests/components/library-reachability.test.tsx`.

**Expected.** The component is still an orphan; the allowlist is still correct.

**Actual.** ⛔ **The guard reports it as reachable and fails the OPPOSITE assertion:**

```
these are reachable now and should leave the allowlist:
  expected [ 'Columns' ] to deeply equal []
```

⚡ **The only occurrence was this, inside a JSDoc block:**

```
 * shape [TASK-1460](…)'s `Columns` and [C-291](…)'s Saved View store have.
```

#### 🔴 Why this is the dangerous direction

⚠️ **The failure this lane hit is the loud one** — a false *reachable*, which fails a different assertion and gets noticed. ⛔ **The quiet one is the same defect pointing the other way**: **a component with no callers whose name appears in any comment anywhere is reported reachable**, so **it leaves the allowlist, nobody schedules it, and the library grows an orphan the guard says is fine.**

📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code.*** ⚡ **This one can fail — it just cannot fail for the right reason**, which is the same class one step along.

#### ⚠️ It has now cost two slices, which is the argument for fixing it

| | |
|---|---|
| **[TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md)** | `git grep MobileNavigation` had to return zero for the row's DoD, and **four prose mentions kept it non-zero.** ✅ **Resolved by rewriting them to name the thing** — *"the phone's bottom navigation bar"* |
| **[TASK-1405](BACKLOG.md)** | ⛔ **The same rewrite, for the same reason** — *"TASK-1460's column primitives"* rather than the identifier |

🔴 **Twice is the threshold [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) names**: *"one lane's inconvenience is not evidence; two lanes' is."* ⚡ **And the workaround is itself a cost** — **a lane cannot name a component in a comment**, which is a strange constraint to impose on documentation in a repository that values it this highly.

#### ✅ The repair, and it is the same one `B-162` already applied elsewhere

📁 **[B-162](#b-162) narrowed a guard to strip comments** and this lane fixed its own regression there — **so the repository already has string-aware source walking to borrow.** ⛔ **Strip comments before scanning for callers**, and ⚡ **an import statement is a stronger signal still**: a caller imports, prose does not.

⚠️ **And whatever the mechanism, the fix must be measured the way B-162's was** — 📁 *"narrowing a guard is only safe if you measure what STOPS firing."* **Add a fixture with a commented identifier and no import, and prove it reports an orphan.**

### B-250 · The Playground seeder ignores `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL` and silently seeds the shared demo database

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — [`backend/tests/playground/seed.py`](../backend/tests/playground/seed.py) via [`backend/tests/conftest.py:52`](../backend/tests/conftest.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — current assignee of `platform_foundation` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a lane can write to a database that is not its own and be told it succeeded.** ⚡ **Nothing is corrupted** — the seeder replaces only the Playground it owns — **but the write lands in the environment reserved for human review** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *ports 3000 and 8000 belong to human review and to no lane*) |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed here.** `backend/tests/` is Platform Foundation's and QE's, not this lane's |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, restoring its own environment during [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) — ⚠️ **by doing it twice before noticing** |
| **Commit found** | **`4b830a7b`** |

**Steps.**

```
cd backend && SIGNORA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TESTS=1 \
  SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://…@localhost:5432/signora_lane_a \
  uv run python -m tests.playground.seed
```

**Expected.** The Playground is seeded into `signora_lane_a`, the database the command names.

**Actual.** ⛔ **It is seeded into `signora`** — the shared demo database — **and the command reports success**, printing a workspace id that does not exist in the database the operator asked for:

```
workspace   e17a2216-6d51-4145-9217-da10f4e36c2b
$ psql -d signora_lane_a -c "select count(*) from workspace where id='e17a2216…'"
 0
$ psql -d signora      -c "select count(*) from workspace where id='e17a2216…'"
 1
```

#### 🔴 The mechanism

📁 **The seeder builds its engines from [`tests/conftest.py`](../backend/tests/conftest.py), which reads different variables entirely:**

```python
DEFAULT_APP_DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get(
    "SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL",
    "postgresql+asyncpg://signora_app:…@localhost:5432/signora",   # <- the default
)
```

⛔ **`SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL` is never consulted**, so setting it does nothing and **the fallback is the shared database.**

#### ⚠️ Why the silence is the defect rather than the variable name

⚡ **`conftest.py`'s own comment shows the hazard was already understood** — *"Two lanes running `pytest` at the same time would have truncated each other's rows mid-run, producing failures neither could reproduce."* ✅ **That is exactly right, and it is why the `SIGNORA_TEST_*` variables exist.**

🔴 **What is missing is that the command accepts the WRONG variable without complaint.** 📁 **[`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) line 344 records the same class for migrations** — *"`migrations/env.py` reads `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL` from `os.environ` directly and never sees `backend/.env`… **set it to a different database and the migration runner locks one and migrates the other**. That is [B-007](#b-007)"* — ⛔ **so this is B-007's shape in the seeder, and B-007 is still open.**

⚠️ **And `make demo-seed` passes nothing at all**, so the documented invocation is correct only because the default happens to be the demo database. **A lane copying that line for its own database gets no error and no effect where it looked.**

#### ✅ The suggested repair, and it is a refusal rather than a rename

⛔ **Do not simply teach the seeder to read `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL`** — 📁 **the two-variable split is deliberate and correct** (migration identity vs runtime identity, [§8](../CLAUDE.md)).

✅ **Make the mismatch impossible to miss**: **when `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL` is set and names a different database from `SIGNORA_TEST_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`, refuse and say so.** ⚡ **A destructive command that already demands `SIGNORA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TESTS=1` is exactly the place to demand that the operator and the tool agree about which database is disposable** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *prefer a violation that is unrepresentable over one that is merely discouraged.*

⚠️ **Printing the database name beside the workspace id would also have caught it in seconds**, and costs one line.
