|---|---|---|
| **`profile-journey` — *reachable from the shell*** | `getByRole('link', { name: /@/ })` on `/` | ⛔ **The address lives inside the account menu, and [`account-menu.tsx:148`](../frontend/components/shell/account-menu.tsx) gates its contents on `open`.** ⚡ **[TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md) moved it there** — *"the theme toggle and Sign out left this file for the account menu"* |
| **`organization-setup` — *no control the platform cannot answer*** | `page.getByRole('combobox')` has count `0` | ⛔ **[`AccountSearch`](../frontend/components/intelligence/account-search.tsx) carries `role="combobox"` and lives in the TOP BAR**, so a page-wide query catches the shell's own search on **every** screen |
| **[B-247](#b-247)** | *What has happened* on the brief | The utility panel took it at ≥1024 |
| **[B-248](#b-248)** | one `<dialog>` per page | The shell now mounts a second |

#### ⚡ The class, which is worth more than any of the four

> 🔴 **A journey that names a shell surface is coupled to the shell, and the App Shell rows do not run the journeys that name it.**

⚠️ **All four broke on App Shell work promoted within the last two days** — [TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) — **and every one of those rows passed its own gate.** ⛔ **The journey map in [`certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py) is not at fault either**: `frontend/components/shell/` selects `__all__`, **so these journeys WERE selected.** ⚡ **They were selected and they were not green, and the cycle promoted anyway.**

**⇒ The gap is not selection. It is that a red journey with an unexplained cause has been accumulating**, and 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s consequence is exact: **a guard nobody trusts is documentation pretending to be code.**

#### ✅ The repairs, each small and each a behaviour change rather than a locator swap

**`profile-journey`** — **open the account menu, then follow the link.** ⛔ **Not `getByRole('link', …).first()` somewhere else**: the journey's claim is *"reachable from the shell, which is how anybody finds it"*, **and the honest version of that now includes the menu.**

**`organization-setup`** — **scope the query to `main`.** ⚡ **The assertion means *this SCREEN offers no control the platform cannot answer*, and the shell's search is neither this screen's nor unanswerable.**

### B-248 · A focus-trap guard assumes the page holds exactly one `<dialog>`, and the shell now mounts a second

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/tests/e2e/interaction-boundaries.spec.ts:80`](../frontend/tests/e2e/interaction-boundaries.spec.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **the focus trap is intact and the product is not implicated.** ⚡ **The guard reports a leak that is not there** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **`active.closest('dialog')`**, which asks the question the test actually means — *is the focused element inside **a** dialog?* — ⛔ **rather than *is it inside the first one in the document?*** ⚡ **It cannot rot again the next time the shell mounts one**, which is the property worth having and the reason this was not a one-character edit. ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed here** ([TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) is three App Shell sections). ⚠️ **Reported by the lane that caused it**, which is the point of the row |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, in the full headed run [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) selected (`__all__`) |
| **Commit found** | **`5cdae81a`** — ⚠️ **the cause is [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md), promoted earlier today, and this lane's own** |

**Steps.** `npx playwright test tests/e2e/interaction-boundaries.spec.ts -g "cannot walk out of a dialog"`.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Ten reported escapes in twenty tabs, every one of them the dialog's OWN close control:**

```
after 2 tabs: BUTTON "✕"
after 4 tabs: BUTTON "✕"
…
```

#### 🔴 The mechanism, and it is one word in the helper

```ts
const dialog = document.querySelector('dialog');
if (dialog?.contains(active)) return null;
```

⛔ **`querySelector` returns the FIRST `<dialog>` in document order, not the one that is open.**

⚡ **[`Dialog`](../frontend/components/ui/dialog.tsx) always renders its `<dialog>` element** — `open` drives `showModal()`, it does not gate the markup — **so a mounted-but-closed dialog is in the DOM the whole time.** 🔴 **[TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) mounted [`ShortcutsReference`](../frontend/components/shell/shortcuts-reference.tsx) at the shell**, so **every authenticated page now carries one before any dialog a screen opens.**

**⇒ The helper measures containment against the wrong dialog, and every tab inside the right one reads as an escape.**

#### ✅ The product is fine, and that is checkable rather than asserted

⚡ **The trap is the platform's**: `showModal()` inerts everything outside the top layer, and 📁 [`drawer.tsx`](../frontend/components/ui/drawer.tsx) records the same fact — *"`Dialog` uses `<dialog>.showModal()` — the platform inerts the rest."* ⛔ **Focus never left the evidence dialog; only the guard thought so.**

#### ⚡ The repair is `closest`, not `querySelector`

```ts
if (active.closest('dialog')) return null;
```

✅ **It asks the question the test actually means** — *is the focused element inside **a** dialog?* — ⛔ **rather than *is it inside the first one that happens to be in the document?*** ⚠️ **And it cannot rot again the next time the shell mounts something**, which is the property worth having: **the current form would break again on the second shell-level dialog, and [C-286](LANE_COORDINATION.md) already contemplates one.**

#### 🔴 What this says about the guard, and it is the general lesson

📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code.** ⚠️ **This is the third variety found today** — [B-244](#b-244) a guard that cannot pass, [B-246](#b-246) a guard that fails somebody else's test, **and now a guard that fails for a reason unrelated to the property it protects.** ⛔ **All three are worse than no guard**, because each one trains a lane to read past a red gate.

### B-247 · The utility panel took the account's history and a journey still looks for it on the page

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/tests/e2e/daily-usage.spec.ts:143`](../frontend/tests/e2e/daily-usage.spec.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the product is right and the journey is stale**, but it is 🟠 rather than 🟡 because **it is fresh**: [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md) was promoted **today**, and this is the gate reporting a change that landed hours ago |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **The journey opens the Activity tab and asserts the history THERE**, which is where [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md) put it. ⛔ **The claim is unchanged** — *the account carries a history of what has happened* — ⚡ **only where to look for it changed**, so this is a behaviour change in the test rather than a locator swap. ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed here.** Found running [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md)'s journey gate; **that row is three App Shell sections and this is the account brief** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, in the full headed run the change selected (`__all__`) |
| **Commit found** | **`5cdae81a`** — ⚠️ **untouched by that branch**: `git diff origin/integration...HEAD -- daily-usage.spec.ts` is empty |

**Steps.** `npx playwright test tests/e2e/daily-usage.spec.ts -g "carries a history of what has happened"`, at any viewport ≥ 1024.

**Expected**, per the assertion: an `h2` reading *What has happened* on the account brief.

**Actual.** ⛔ **No such heading exists on the page.** ✅ **The score renders**, so the brief itself is healthy — `brief.waitForScore()` passes on the line before.

#### ✅ The product is right, and it says so in its own comment

📁 [`app/(app)/accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx):

```ts
// 📁 §13's Activity tab — ⛔ the panel takes it only where the panel
// exists; below 1024 `carrying` is false and the section above renders.
const history = useUtilityPanel('Activity', historyFeed);
```

⚡ **So the history is exactly where the design puts it** — 📁 §13's Activity tab — **and the page-level section survives only below 1024**, which is the band with no panel. ⛔ **The journey runs above that band and asserts the section.**

#### ⚠️ Why this one matters more than a stale locator

🔴 **The change that moved it was promoted TODAY**, and the journey that guards it was not moved with it. ⚡ **That is the [§12](../CLAUDE.md) rotation problem in executable form**: *"a lane that has never seen this module continues the work"* — **and what it inherits here is a red gate whose cause is three files away.**

⛔ **It is also the second stale journey assertion found in one run** — see [B-244](#b-244), where the assertion would have sent a customer to a screen that verifies nothing. **Neither was caught when the change shipped**, which is a fact about when journeys are run rather than about either row.

#### ✅ The repair, and it is a behaviour change in the test rather than a locator swap

**The journey must open the Activity tab and assert the history there**, because *"the account carries a history of what has happened"* is still exactly the right thing to prove — ⛔ **the surface moved, the guarantee did not.** ⚠️ **Asserting the below-1024 fallback instead would be testing the band the design treats as the exception.**

### B-246 · A journey races two outcomes and the loser rejects into the next test

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/tests/e2e/confidence.spec.ts:53`](../frontend/tests/e2e/confidence.spec.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **the product is not implicated.** ⚠️ **The test fails on its own plumbing**, and 📁 [§19](../CLAUDE.md) makes a lane run its journeys before pushing, so a permanently red scenario trains a lane to read past the gate |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **Both branches of the race now RESOLVE** — ⛔ **not a wider timeout**, which only moves the rejection into a later test **and that is the version of this bug that is genuinely hard to find.** ⚡ **A third assertion was added rather than only silencing the loser**: `never` is not an outcome the product may produce, **so the scenario still refuses the one thing it exists to refuse** — the dialog closing as though the work was saved. ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed here.** **Found running [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md)'s journey gate; that row is three App Shell sections and this is a session-expiry journey** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, in the full headed run the change selected (`__all__`) |
| **Commit found** | **`5cdae81a`** — ⚠️ **untouched by that branch**: `git diff origin/integration...HEAD -- confidence.spec.ts` is empty |

**Steps.** `npx playwright test tests/e2e/confidence.spec.ts -g "does not silently swallow"`.

**Actual.**

```
TimeoutError: page.waitForURL: Timeout 20000ms exceeded.
  > 53 |  const signedOut = page.waitForURL(/\/signin/, { timeout: 20_000 }).then(…)
```

#### 🔴 The test is right about the product and wrong about promises

✅ **The intent is good, and worth keeping**: *"Either outcome is defensible; disappearing is not."* **The product may refuse and say so, or bounce to sign-in** — so the scenario races the two:

```ts
const signedOut = page.waitForURL(/\/signin/, { timeout: 20_000 }).then(() => 'sign-in');
const stillHere = expect(business.dialog).toBeVisible({ timeout: 20_000 }).then(() => 'dialog');
const outcome = await Promise.race([signedOut, stillHere]);
```

⛔ **`Promise.race` settles on the FIRST outcome and abandons the other — it does not cancel it.** ⚡ **When the dialog wins, `waitForURL` goes on waiting and rejects twenty seconds later**, with nothing attached to catch it. **The assertion passed and the test fails anyway.**

#### ⚠️ This lane has met this exact class before, in a different disguise

📁 **[TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) shipped and then fixed the same shape**: *"a rejected query = an unhandled rejection failing tests whose assertions passed"* — **there it was react-query, here it is Playwright.** 🔴 **The general form is worth more than either instance:**

> ⛔ **A promise that nobody awaits still settles.** ⚡ **Any construction that abandons one branch — `race`, a fire-and-forget `then`, a mutation nobody reads — must attach a handler to the branch it abandons**, or the failure surfaces somewhere with no relationship to the code that caused it.

#### ✅ The suggested repair, and it keeps the scenario's intent intact

**Give the abandoned branch somewhere to land**, so the race still answers *which outcome happened* and neither branch can fail a test it has already stopped deciding:

```ts
const signedOut = page.waitForURL(/\/signin/, { timeout: 20_000 })
  .then(() => 'sign-in' as const)
  .catch(() => 'never' as const);
```

⛔ **Not by widening the timeout**, which only moves the rejection into a later test — **and that is the version of this bug that is genuinely hard to find**, because the failure is then reported against a scenario that did nothing wrong.

### B-245 · A journey cannot create an organization and leave the environment as it found it, because the default workspace is the newest one and nothing can delete it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`workspace_tenancy`** *(the newest-first default)* · **`product_surface`** *(the resolution in [`workspace-provider.tsx`](../frontend/lib/state/workspace-provider.tsx))*. ⛔ **Not the journey that hit it** |
| **Current assignee** | **The current assignee of `workspace_tenancy`** — joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), ⛔ **not named here** ([C-213](#c-213)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **wrong behaviour a customer would hit, and a suite-wide test hazard.** ⚡ **It is [B-229](#b-229) one generation on, and B-229's repair does not cover it** |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **not fixed: the repair is a product decision about which organization a person lands in**, and that is not a lane's to take inside a feature slice ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)) ⚠️ **ROUTED 2026-08-12 as [C-299](LANE_COORDINATION.md)** — ⛔ **filed 2026-08-11 and carried to nobody until now.** ⚡ **Third instance of the same class; see [C-298](LANE_COORDINATION.md) ⑤.** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, building [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) §18 — **by doing it, and then by measuring what it cost** |
| **Commit found** | **`5cdae81a`** |

**Steps.** Sign in as the owner. Create an organization through the shipped `New organization` control on Settings. Open the product in a **fresh browser profile**.

**Expected.** The reader lands where they last were, or in an organization that holds their work.

**Actual.** ⛔ **They land in the newly created, empty organization** — and **there is no way to leave it behind permanently**, because nothing in the product deletes an organization.

#### 🔴 The mechanism, measured

**① The list is newest-first.** 📁 [`repositories.py:81`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/repositories.py) — *"Apply **newest-first** keyset ordering"* — and `list_visible` uses it unmodified.

**② The default is `workspaces[0]`.** 📁 [`workspace-provider.tsx`](../frontend/lib/state/workspace-provider.tsx): with no stored id and no `/w/:workspace` segment, the resolution falls to `first.id`.

**③ Nothing deletes one.** ⚡ **`useDeleteWorkspace` does not exist**, no route offers it, and `WorkspaceStanding` publishes `'deleted'` with nothing in the product able to produce it.

**⇒ Every created organization becomes the default for every browser that has no stored choice, permanently.**

#### ⚠️ Why [B-229](#b-229)'s repair is not enough, and this is the point of a second row

📁 **B-229's finding**: *"one journey creates a workspace and never restores the previous one"* — ✅ **and the repair it implies is to restore the choice.** ⛔ **A fresh context has no choice to restore.** ⚡ **So a journey can be perfectly well-behaved — this lane's was, and switched back explicitly — and still leave every later context landing in the wrong place.**

**Measured cost, in one session:** ⛔ **six organizations accumulated, and the suite's account-backed journeys began failing two projects later on `main a[href^="/accounts/"]` not found** — the attention list of an empty organization. **The same shape B-229 recorded at 23 failures.**

#### ⚡ The customer question underneath it, which is the real one

⛔ **This is not only a test hazard.** **A salesperson who creates a second organization to try something out is put into it on every new device, ahead of the one holding their book of business.** ⚠️ **Whether the default should be *newest*, *most recently used*, *the one with data*, or *explicitly chosen at creation* is a product decision** — 📁 and the design's §19 ③ says only that switching *"keeps the equivalent route when it exists, and lands on Home when it does not"*, **which is about switching rather than about defaulting.**

#### 🔴 Observed live, in a run this lane did not cause

⚠️ **The full headed suite was re-run on a freshly seeded environment**, and 📁 **[B-229](#b-229)'s own spec reproduced the whole mechanism unaided:**

```
E2E Org 1786475006314 | 2026-08-11 19:03:28   <- organization-setup.spec.ts
Playground            | 2026-08-11 18:45:47   <- the seeded data
```

⛔ **`organization-setup.spec.ts` ran at [7/314] and created a workspace that became the newest.** ⚡ **Every spec alphabetically after it — `perception`, and everything past `p` — then resolved to an organization with no accounts**, and failed on `main a[href^="/accounts/"]` not found.

🔴 **This is the confirmation that the two rows are one defect at two depths.** **B-229 names the spec; this row names why fixing the spec is not enough** — ⛔ **the run that produced the trace above happened AFTER the environment was reseeded and with no organization left behind by this lane.**

⚠️ **And it means the suite cannot currently pass end to end in one run**, whatever a lane changes: **the poisoning is alphabetical and unconditional.**

#### ✅ What this lane did instead, so nothing waits on the ruling

⛔ **[TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md)'s journey no longer creates an organization.** ⚡ **§18 and §19's labelled side are asserted in component tests**, where an unactivated workspace and a multi-organization reader can both be constructed — **and the browser asserts §16, which needs computed CSS and cannot be faked.** ⚠️ **The absence is recorded in the spec rather than left for somebody to discover.**

### B-244 · A journey asserts a verification link that would send the customer to a screen which cannot verify anything

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/tests/e2e/auth-journey.spec.ts:470`](../frontend/tests/e2e/auth-journey.spec.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **the test is wrong and the product is right**, so nothing a customer touches is broken. ⚠️ **It is not 🟢 because it fails the journey gate on every run**, and 📁 [§19](../CLAUDE.md) requires a lane to run its journeys before pushing — **a gate that reports a defect that is not one teaches a lane to read past it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **The assertion now names the route Better Auth actually emits** — `/api/auth/verify-email?token=` — ⛔ **not `/verify?token=`, which is the *"we have sent you a link"* screen and consumes no token.** ⚡ **The product was right and stays untouched**: had the old assertion been satisfied, the email would have carried the customer to a screen that cannot verify them. ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **deliberately NOT fixed here.** **Found running [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md)'s journey gate, and it is not that slice's**: the row is three App Shell sections and this is the authentication tier. ✅ **Reported with the diagnosis complete so whoever takes it does not repeat it** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, running the full headed suite the change selected (`__all__`) |
| **Commit found** | **`5cdae81a`** — ⚠️ **untouched by that branch**: `git diff origin/integration...HEAD -- auth-journey.spec.ts` is empty, and the spec was last written by [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md) at `b565c19e` |

**Steps.** `SIGNORA_AUTH_EMAIL_TRANSPORT=mailbox`, then `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth-journey.spec.ts -g "lands a real, openable link"`.

**Expected**, per the assertion: the mailbox entry's link matches `/verify\?token=/`.

**Actual.**

```
Received: http://localhost:3300/api/auth/verify-email?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9…
```

#### ✅ Which side is wrong, established by reading both rather than by guessing

⚡ **The product is right.** 📁 **[`app/(auth)/verify/page.tsx`](../frontend/app/(auth)/verify/page.tsx) reads `searchParams: { email?: string }` and nothing else** — ⛔ **it is the *"we have sent you a link"* screen and it consumes no token.**

🔴 **So if the assertion were satisfied, the email would carry a customer to a screen that cannot verify them.** ⚡ **The shipped link is Better Auth's own route, which verifies the token and then lands them in the product** — 📁 exactly what [`lib/auth/server.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/server.ts) intends: *"Straight into the product after verifying. The alternative is asking somebody to type a password they set ninety seconds ago."*

⚠️ **The test's own comment already knew this** — *"the token is Better Auth's own"* — **and then asserted a shape Better Auth does not emit.** ⛔ **`/api/auth/verify-email?token=` does not contain `verify?token=`**, and the regex requires it literally.

#### ⚡ Why this is worth a row rather than a quiet edit

📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code.*** ⛔ **This is the opposite failure — a guard that cannot pass** — and it is the more expensive one, because **a red gate that is always red stops being read.**

⚠️ **And the correct repair is not obviously *"loosen the regex"*.** **The assertion the journey actually wants is *the link is real and openable*, which is the row's own stated ask** — ✅ **so the honest fix asserts that the link RESOLVES**, by following it, rather than pattern-matching a URL whose shape belongs to a dependency. ⛔ **A regex over a vendor's URL is a test of Better Auth's routing, not of Signora's.**

### B-243 · 🔴 `backend/.env.example` runs the API as the database owner, so Row-Level Security is bypassed on every request

> ## ⛔ SUPERSEDED BY [B-183](#b-183) — folded 2026-08-12 by QE, whose duplicate this was
>
> **This row and [B-183](#b-183) are one defect.** ⚡ **Lane A filed this one first**, from a journey failing for a reason that had nothing to do with its slice. **QE then verified the defect independently, found no `B-243` in the register it could see, concluded the id was unallocated, and filed [B-183](#b-183).** ⛔ **Lane A's row was on a branch QE had not yet integrated** — **QE checked the register it had, not the register that existed.**
>
> ⚠️ **The cost was not the second id. It was that one defect carried two close conditions**: this row `FIXED` on the fix, [B-183](#b-183) `OPEN` until promoted. **The register said one defect was simultaneously fixed and open**, which is §2's *duplicated truth becomes contradictory truth* in its two-day form.
>
> ✅ **[B-183](#b-183) survives, and not because it is better.** **This row is earlier.** ⛔ **But four source files now cite `B-183`** — `backend/.env.example`, `alembic.ini`, `Makefile`, `backend/tests/security_invariants/test_database.py` — **and renumbering them a second time buys tidiness with risk.** **Cost decided it; correctness was indifferent.**
>
> ⚡ **§20e's tiebreak does not govern and QE first applied it anyway, against itself.** That rule is *one id claimed twice*; **this is two ids for one defect, the inverse** — an [L-1](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md) reuse-audit failure, whose resolution is exactly this: keep one, supersede the other, lose nothing. **Lane C caught the misapplication.**
>
> 📁 **Nothing here is deleted.** **Found by Lane A, 2026-08-11**, implementing [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md); **fixed by Lane C at `ee4e34c3`**, wider than the repair first proposed — it also caught `alembic.ini` carrying a claim `env.py` corrected in July, and a third owner credential unread in the Makefile's E2E block. **That attribution and that scope are carried into [B-183](#b-183)**, which is the half that would otherwise have been lost.

> ⚠️ **The origin is Lane C's and they owned it**: `B-243` was written into four source files **from Lane A's 200-block by an office allocating in 400/1400**, and it collided with a real Lane A allocation **inside one day**. ⚡ **That is the block rule demonstrating precisely what it prevents.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — [`backend/.env.example`](../backend/.env.example) line 35. ⛔ **Not `workspace_tenancy`**: the RLS policies and the query are both correct, and the credential is what disarms them |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — current assignee of `platform_foundation` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🔴 — ⛔ **a cross-tenant read, reproduced.** ⚡ **The repository's own words for this exact condition** ([§8](../CLAUDE.md)): *"A service connected as the owner is exempt from Row-Level Security on every table it touches, **which silently voids the entire tenancy model no matter how correct the policies are**."* ⚠️ **And [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) line 388 already says the right thing** — *"Note the database user: `signora_app`, **never the owner**"* — **so the repository contradicts itself, and the copy a developer actually runs is the wrong one** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-11, at `ee4e34c3`**, on the poll this row was reported to them. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ⚡ **Their fix is WIDER than the repair suggested below, and the difference is worth reading**: they also found **`alembic.ini` carrying a claim `env.py` had already corrected in July**, and **a third owner credential sitting unread in the Makefile's E2E block**. 🔴 **They also declined to apply the suggested patch as written, correctly** — 📁 `migrations/env.py:57` reads the same `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL`, **so flipping it is safe only because `Makefile:172` passes `OWNER_DATABASE_URL` explicitly, which they verified before changing anything.** ⛔ **Was `OPEN`** — deliberately NOT fixed by this lane; `backend/.env.example` is Platform Foundation and not this lane's ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *finding a defect outside your assignment is an obligation to report it, never permission to fix it*). ✅ **This lane's OWN `backend/.env` is corrected**, which is its environment and its to hold |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, implementing [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) — ⚡ **by a journey failing for a reason that had nothing to do with the slice** |
| **Commit found** | **`ed36dd0c`** — ⚠️ **the defect is far older; `.env.example` has carried this line for as long as it has existed** |

**Steps.** Configure a lane from `backend/.env.example`, as its own comment intends. Start the API. Sign in as **any** persona. Read `GET /workspaces`.

**Expected.** The list holds only workspaces that caller is a member of. 📁 The endpoint's own docstring: *"Scoped by RLS to the caller's own memberships — **there is no way to ask about another user's workspaces**."*

**Actual.** ⛔ **It holds every workspace in the database.**

#### 🔴 The evidence, measured rather than argued

```
$ psql -c "select rolname, rolsuper, rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname like 'signora%'"
 signora        | t | t        <- what .env.example configures
 signora_app    | f | f        <- what RUNNING.md line 388 prescribes
 signora_auth   | f | f
 signora_relay  | f | f
```

**`rolbypassrls = t`.** ⚡ **Every RLS policy in the schema is inert for that connection**, and `list_visible` is the case that shows it, because 📁 its own comment states the dependency out loud:

> *"No user filter appears here by design: the workspace table's RLS policy already restricts rows to workspaces the session's `app.user_id` is a member of."*

⚡ **The query is right. The policy is right. The credential removes both.**

#### ⚠️ What a customer sees, and it is how this was found

**Signed in as `marcus.hale`, who is a member of exactly one workspace:**

```
404 GET /api/proxy/workspaces/4f0decdf-…/onboarding
404 GET /api/proxy/workspaces/4f0decdf-…/members
404 GET /api/proxy/workspaces/4f0decdf-…/accounts
404 GET /api/proxy/workspaces/4f0decdf-…/signal-catalog
```

**`4f0decdf` belongs to `dana.reyes`, and Marcus has no membership in it.** ⚡ **The list handed him another user's organization; every other endpoint then correctly refused it** — 📁 [§7](../CLAUDE.md), *a caller who is not a member of the workspace they name gets `404`, never `403`* — **and the shell settled on a workspace whose every read fails.**

⛔ **So the visible symptom is a broken screen, and the actual defect is that the name of another customer's organization was rendered in this customer's browser.**

#### ✅ Proved by removing the cause, not by reading the code

**One change — `signora` → `signora_app` in this lane's `backend/.env`** — and the two personas that could not sign in both do. **Nothing else was touched.**

#### 🔴 What this means for every journey run in this lane

⚠️ **Every Playwright journey this lane has ever run executed with RLS disabled.** ⛔ **No journey in this repository's lane environments has exercised tenancy at all** — a workspace-crossing defect could not have failed one of them. ⚡ **That is worth more than the fix**: it is a standing gap in what the journey suite is able to prove, and it belongs to QE's view of coverage rather than to this row.

#### ⛔ Why the severity is 🔴 and not 🟠

**It is configuration rather than code, and the effect is the one the Security Invariants exist to prevent.** 📁 §8 makes the separation of migration and runtime credentials *"a permanent engineering rule, not a deployment preference"*, and names this exact consequence. ⚠️ **The example file is the artifact every new lane and every new developer copies**, so the blast radius is *every* environment configured the documented way.

#### ✅ The suggested repair, and it is one line

**`backend/.env.example` line 35 becomes the runtime identity [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) already prescribes:**

```
SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://signora_app:signora_app_local_dev@localhost:5432/signora
```

⚠️ **Migrations are unaffected and must not be changed with it**: the `Makefile` already passes `OWNER_DATABASE_URL` explicitly for `alembic upgrade`, which is 📁 §8's *"schema migrations execute only under the migration identity"*. ⛔ **The two identities are meant to differ, and today they do not.**

⚡ **Worth considering with the fix, and not this lane's to decide**: a Security Invariant asserting that the configured runtime connection has `rolbypassrls = false`. **A guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)) — and today the rule lives only in prose, in the file that disagrees with it.

### B-242 · The entry engine has routed locked accounts to a route that does not exist, since it shipped

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts) rule 05, and the route it names |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — current assignee of `product_surface` in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **wrong behaviour a customer would hit, at the worst possible moment.** ⚠️ **Not 🔴: nothing is lost and the account still unlocks** — **what is lost is the person's ability to find that out** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-11**, in [TASK-1467](BACKLOG.md), **which is the row that went looking.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, doing [TASK-1467](BACKLOG.md)'s reuse audit — ⛔ **before writing a line, which is what the row instructed** |
| **Commit found** | **`beae7d86`** — ⚠️ **the defect is far older than the row that found it** |

**Steps.** Lock an account by failing sign-in enough times, then sign in.

**Expected.** 📁 The design's §11: *"This account is locked"*, and a route forward.

**Actual.** ⛔ **The 404 gate** — ***"That address does not lead anywhere."***

### 🔴 The mechanism, and it is one line meeting nothing

📁 **[`rules.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts) rule 05** — *"Account locked — failed attempts"* — **routes to `/auth/locked`.** ⛔ **No such route existed.** ⚡ **Next.js answers an unmatched path with `not-found.tsx`**, which is a correct 404 screen giving a completely wrong answer.

> ⚠️ **This is the worst screen in the product to lose to a 404**, and the reason is not severity but *sequence*. **Somebody who cannot sign in has already tried the one thing they know how to do.** ⛔ **Telling them the address does not exist says the PRODUCT is broken, not their account** — and **there is no second surface for them to check**, because every other surface is behind the sign-in they cannot complete.

### ⚡ Why it survived, which is the part worth keeping

⛔ **Every gate the repository has was watching a different thing.** 📁 `make reachability` asks *"does anything LINK here"* — ✅ **and it is right to have said nothing**: nobody links to their own lockout. **It never asked whether the destination exists.** ⚠️ **And `rules.ts` is thoroughly tested** — the rule fires correctly and returns the correct string. **The string was never resolved against the route table.**

> 🔴 **The general form: a router tested against its own output is tested against a claim, not a destination.** ⚡ **Every `route: () => '…'` in that file is a promise nothing checks**, and [C-290](LANE_COORDINATION.md) asks for the check rather than another screen.

### ✅ The fix

📁 **[`app/(auth)/auth/locked/page.tsx`](../frontend/app/(auth)/auth/locked/page.tsx)** — the design's heading, the lock stated as temporary, the reassurance a lock actually needs (*nobody has been signed in*), and **a password reset as the one route forward that works while signed out.**

⛔ **The design's numbers are NOT rendered** — *"five attempts… 09:02… unlocks at 09:17"* — **because none of the three is published**: `AccountStanding` is `'locked'` and nothing more. ⚠️ **A wrong unlock time is worse than none**, and that gap is [C-290](LANE_COORDINATION.md).

✅ **Regression test**: `account-locked.test.tsx` **reads the route out of `RULES` rather than restating it**, so re-pointing the rule turns it red instead of making the screen quietly unreachable again.

### B-241 · The rail's pinned utilities have always overflowed the viewport by 106px, and a `fixed` sheet is where it became reachability

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/components/shell/app-shell.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/app-shell.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **wrong behaviour a customer would hit**: **on a phone, three of the rail's entries could not be pressed.** ⚡ **Not 🔴: every one of them is reachable another way, and the destinations above them were fine** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-11**, in the row that exposed it. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, when [TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md)'s own new journey timed out clicking a button Playwright reported as **visible** — 📁 *"element is outside of the viewport"* |
| **Commit found** | **`071f6a5e`** — ⚠️ **the defect is older than the row that found it** |

**Steps.** At **390×844**, open the navigation, and try to press `Shortcuts`, `Docs & support` or `Settings` in the rail's pinned group.

**Expected.** They are at the foot of the rail, on screen.

**Actual.** ⛔ **`Shortcuts` renders at `y = 872` on an 844px viewport.** It is in the DOM, it is `visible` by every definition the accessibility tree uses, **and it cannot be clicked.**

### 🔴 The cause, measured rather than reasoned

📁 **The rail's `<nav>` is `h-full`** and the rail's container also holds **the wordmark row and the workspace switcher above it** — ⚡ **106px of them.** ⛔ **So the nav claimed the container's FULL height while starting 106px down**, and its `flex-1` spacer then pinned the utility group to a bottom edge that is 106px past the real one.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Container** | `top: 0`, `height: 844` |
| **Nav** | `top: 106`, `height: **844**` — ⛔ **should be 738** |
| **`Shortcuts`** | `top: **872**` — **28px below the fold** |

> ⚠️ **This is not a defect the sheet introduced.** ⚡ **The same 106px of overflow existed at every width and in every previous cycle** — 📁 **the rail's container was a scrollable child of `min-h-screen`, so the overflow simply extended the page and a customer could scroll to it.** ⛔ **A `fixed` sheet has nowhere to scroll to**, which is the only reason it stopped being invisible.
>
> 🔴 **The general form is worth more than the fix: a layout defect that a scrollbar absorbs is a layout defect nobody reports.** **It became a bug the moment one container stopped scrolling**, and every `h-full` child of a container with siblings above it is the same shape.

### ✅ The fix

**The rail's container becomes a flex column** and the navigation gets a wrapper that is `min-h-0 flex-1`, **so `h-full` resolves against the space that is actually left.** ⛔ **`RegionBoundary` takes no `className` and was not given one** — 🔴 it is `components/ui`, and widening a shared component for one caller is what [§20c](../CLAUDE.md) forbids.

**Re-measured after: nav `top: 106`, `height: 738`, `Shortcuts` at `766`.** ✅ **106 + 738 = 844 exactly.**

⚠️ **The assertion that caught it was geometric, and a role query never would have been.** 📁 `toBeVisible()` passes on an element outside the viewport — **`visibility` is not position** — which is the same class as [B-180](#b-180) and this register's third instance of it in one day.

### B-240 · The keyboard reference is unreachable below 1024px, and the first explanation for it was invented

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/components/shell/navigation.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/navigation.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟢 — ⚡ **cosmetic in effect**: the shortcuts it lists cannot be pressed on a touch device anyway. ⚠️ **Filed at 🟢 rather than not filed, because the REASONING defect is worth more than the gap** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-11**, in [TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md), **at the cause.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ⛔ **Was `OPEN`** — *not fixed here; the cause is structural and predates this row* — **and the row that fixed the structure is the one that fixed this** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by QE**, reviewing [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) — 📁 *"a capability that disappears because of a type filter is the kind of thing that reads as a bug six weeks later even when the reasoning was sound."* ✅ **QE was right to ask, and the reasoning was NOT sound** |
| **Commit found** | **`4f37beb9`** — [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) |

### 🔴 The reasoning defect, which is the actual finding

⛔ **`RAIL_DESTINATIONS` publishes links only**, because the command palette and the phone bar both render anchors and 📁 [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) added an entry that opens an overlay. ⚡ **That filter is correct.** ⚠️ **Its side effect was that `Shortcuts` vanished from the phone bar**, and **this lane wrote a justification for it**: *"a keyboard-shortcut reference on a device with no keyboard is a control that cannot help anybody."*

🔴 **The design does not say that.** 📁 **App Shell, the `< 1024px` band, verbatim**: ***"Rail becomes a sheet from a top-bar button."*** ⛔ **The whole rail, utilities included** — **and the design nowhere marks this entry desktop-only.**

⚠️ **Writing a plausible reason for an accident is how a side effect becomes a decision nobody took**, and it is worse than the gap: **the next lane reads the comment, believes the exclusion was considered, and does not re-open it.** 📁 **The same class as [TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)'s row claiming an assertion it did not have** — a register asserting a rigour it does not possess.

### ⚡ The real cause, and why it is not fixed here

📁 **The phone surface is a fixed bottom bar** — [B-203](#b-203--below-768px-the-product-has-no-navigation-at-all)'s remedy — **and the design specifies a SHEET.** ⛔ **A bottom bar renders anchors**, so an entry that opens an overlay has nowhere to live in it. ✅ **The filter is right for what that surface is; the surface is what disagrees with the design.**

⛔ **Adding a sixth control to the bottom bar would be this lane inventing a phone treatment the design replaced.** ⚠️ **Building the sheet is not this row's scope** and would change every screen below 1024px.

### ✅ What was actually changed

⛔ **Nothing behavioural.** 📁 **The comment now states the truth**: the entry is unreachable below 1024px, the design does not sanction that, and the cause is the bottom bar rather than a judgement about keyboards. ⚡ **The gap is now visible to whoever builds the sheet**, which is the only thing that closes it.

### ✅ Closed 2026-08-11 by [TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md), and closed at the cause

⚡ **This row predicted its own fix and the prediction held**: *"the gap is now visible to whoever builds the sheet, which is the only thing that closes it."*

📁 **The bottom bar is deleted and the `<1024` surface is the rail itself**, opened from the top-bar button the band names. ⛔ **So `Shortcuts` is not added back to anything** — **the surface that could not hold it no longer exists**, and the rail's pinned utility group arrives below 1024 with the rest of the rail.

✅ **Asserted rather than asserted-about**: 📁 [`navigation-bands.spec.ts`](../frontend/tests/e2e/navigation-bands.spec.ts) opens the sheet at 390×844, finds `Shortcuts`, presses it and reads the reference's own heading.

⚠️ **And that assertion found a second defect the same day, which is recorded as [B-241](#b-241) rather than folded in silently** — **the button was in the DOM, visible, and 28px below the fold.**

### B-239 · The keyboard map omitted a live shortcut, and its own guard cannot see the class

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/lib/shell/shortcuts.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/shortcuts.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **wrong but survivable**: a real shortcut goes unused because the screen that exists to teach it does not mention it. ⚡ **Nothing breaks and nobody complains, which is why it is the quieter half of the defect** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-11, on the poll that found it**, in the slice that introduced it. ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** 🔴 **One half is deliberately NOT fixed — see *the open half* below** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A**, reading `workspace-switcher.tsx` while claiming [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) — ⛔ **not by the suite, and not by the guard written to prevent exactly this** |
| **Commit found** | **`6e1bd4f8`** — [TASK-1445](BACKLOG.md), the commit that shipped the map |

### 🔴 The defect

📁 **[`components/shell/workspace-switcher.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/workspace-switcher.tsx):162** — *"1–9 selects by position."* ⚡ **A customer with several organizations can press `3` while the switcher is open and land in the third.** ⛔ **The keyboard reference did not list it.**

⚠️ **The map was built from the design's `shortcutGroups`, which publishes eighteen and does not publish this one.** 🔴 **So the reference was complete with respect to the DESIGN and incomplete with respect to the PRODUCT** — and a customer opens it to learn what the product does.

### ⛔ It is the same defect as listing a dead key, pointed the other way

📁 **[TASK-1445](BACKLOG.md)'s whole thesis**: *"a reference that lists a shortcut nothing implements is a promise the product breaks the moment somebody presses it."* ⚡ **The inverse costs less per customer and is far harder to notice**: **nothing fails, nobody presses anything, and the feature is simply never discovered.** ⛔ **Both are [§2](../CLAUDE.md) — the repository asserting something untrue of itself.**

### ✅ The fix

📁 **`Shortcut` gains `published`** — *does the DESIGN list it* — **which is a different question from *does the product bind it*.** ⚡ **`1`–`9` joins the map as `partial`**, with its scope stated in the customer's words: *"Works while the organization switcher is open, and not while you are typing in it."*

⛔ **The count stopped being a literal.** **`coverage()` and both suites said *"of these 18"*; the map now renders nineteen** — ⚠️ **a register miscounting itself in front of the customer is the defect this row is about, so the assertions derive the total.** ✅ **`publishedByTheDesign()` keeps the design's eighteen countable**, because a change to that list is a design change and a change to the product's bindings is not.

⚡ **A new assertion bounds the extension**: ⛔ **an unpublished entry must be `pressable`.** **The map is not a wishlist — nothing may be added outside the design unless the product genuinely binds it.**

### 🔴 The open half — the guard verifies FILES, not CHORDS

⛔ **[`shortcut-registry.test.ts`](../frontend/tests/unit/shortcut-registry.test.ts)'s direction 2 was written for exactly this class** — *"a file that binds a global key without appearing in the registry fails"* — **and it passed the whole time.**

📁 **Because `workspace-switcher.tsx` was already registered, for `⌘⇧W`.** ⚡ **The file appears in the registry, so the scan is satisfied; the SECOND binding inside it is invisible.** 🔴 **A file registered for one shortcut may bind five.**

⚠️ **Closing it needs a parser rather than a scan** — the chords are `event.key` comparisons spread across guards, and matching them textually would produce exactly the false positives [B-162](#b-162) warns about. ⛔ **Not fixed here**, and **the limit is now stated in the guard's own docstring rather than left for the next reader to discover the way this lane did.**

✅ **The lesson is the row's, not the regex's**: 📁 **a guard proven to fire is not a guard proven to be SUFFICIENT.** ⚡ **Direction 2 was fire-tested — adding an unregistered keydown file turned it red — and the fire test used a NEW file, which is the case it handles.** ⛔ **The case it misses is a second binding in a file that already passes**, and **fire-testing the case you thought of never finds it.**

### B-238 · A lane pushed an unvalidated implementation commit to `integration`, and the claim guard cannot see it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **repository process** — [`infra/certification-guard.py`](../infra/certification-guard.py) `--audit-claims` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — 📁 the guard is QE's ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *a defect in a gate that stops QE certifying is QE's to fix*) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **`integration` carries a commit QE has not validated**, and **QE's next Certification Snapshot would pin it** believing every commit there had been fast-forwarded after validation |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **reported by Lane A against itself, on the poll it happened.** 🔴 **NOT fixed and deliberately not force-corrected — see below** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-11, by Lane A, doing it.** ⚡ **Reported WITH the breach it caused, because the breach is the evidence** |
| **Commit found** | **`1f9731a5`** pushed to `integration`, **carrying `6e1bd4f8`** — [TASK-1445](BACKLOG.md)'s implementation |
| 🔴 **SECOND INSTANCE — 2026-08-12, ten commits, same lane** | ⛔ **`24ba4d22` … `ed1513cc` on `origin/integration`, carrying 1–5 executable paths each: [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md)'s section-state law, `AccountSectionShell`, the rail anchoring, the loading and error states.** ⚠️ **Reported by QE, not by this lane** — 📁 **and that is the part worth recording**: the first instance was self-caught on the poll it happened, **and this one ran for ten commits without this lane noticing, because the route had become habit.** ⛔ **`--audit-claims` reported *0 claims awaiting promotion* throughout and was not wrong** — it audits commits whose subject begins `Claim `, **so it never looked at any of them.** ✅ **This is the row's own predicted failure, happening.** ⚡ **The count is the row's value and it now reads 2.** ✅ **`--audit-main` is clean: nothing uncertified reached `main`, which is the promotion guard doing its job regardless of what `integration` carries.** ⛔ **Not force-corrected, for the reason this row already gives** — history on a shared ref is not a lane's to rewrite. **What changed instead is the route: this lane pushes its own branch and lets QE fast-forward, and only a claim commit goes to `integration` directly.** |

### 🔴 What happened, exactly

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 7** — *"`git checkout integration && git merge --ff-only <lane-branch> && git push origin integration`"*. ⚡ **This lane ran the modern equivalent, `git push origin HEAD:integration`**, with the claim commit at `HEAD`.

⛔ **The claim commit is clean.** It touches [`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) and [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) and nothing else, which is the bound §20e sets — **and `--audit-claims` passes it.**

🔴 **But a push moves a BRANCH, not a commit.** **`6e1bd4f8` was its parent**, so the implementation went with it. **`integration` moved from `dbe793a7` to `1f9731a5` and gained a slice QE has not seen.**

### ⛔ Why the guard did not catch it, and this is the whole finding

⚡ **`--audit-claims` inspects the PATHS INSIDE each claim commit.** ✅ **It correctly refuses a commit calling itself a claim while carrying code** — it refused two, live, in this run. ⛔ **It never asks what ELSE arrived in the same push.**

⚠️ **This blind spot is already recorded** — 📁 [B-220](#b-220) named it and [B-161](#b-161--the-task-claim-protocols-own-step-7-pushes-a-lanes-unpromoted-implementation-to-integration) is QE's better diagnosis of the same defect. 🔴 **Both are `OPEN`, and this row is the third instance** — **which is the argument for fixing the guard rather than restating the rule.**

### ✅ The check that would have caught it

⚡ **A claim push is legitimate only when the lane branch is EXACTLY `integration` plus the claim.** 📁 **`git rev-list origin/integration..HEAD` should return one commit, and that commit should be the claim.** ⛔ **This lane's returned three.**

⚠️ **That check belongs in the guard, where a machine runs it** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md): *"prefer a violation that is unrepresentable over one that is merely discouraged."* **A rule kept by remembering is the class of rule this repository has watched fail three times.**

### ⛔ Why this lane did NOT force-correct `integration`

🔴 **Resetting `integration` to `dbe793a7` and re-pushing the claim alone would fix it in one command**, and **this lane did not run it.**

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): `integration` is QE's**, and a lane may fast-forward it **only** with a claim-only commit. ⛔ **A force-push is not a fast-forward** — it rewrites a shared ref, and **any lane or QE session that has already fetched would diverge silently.** ⚠️ **Recovering from a mistake is not a licence to take an authority the mistake did not grant**, and *"I could just fix it"* is exactly how a lane's error becomes a second, larger one.

✅ **Nothing is hidden and the cost is bounded**: the carried commit is a real slice that was going to reach `integration` anyway, with tests green, `tsc` clean and its journey run headed. ⛔ **What it lacks is QE's validation, and that is what QE must be told rather than left to infer.**

**QE decides**: ⓐ **reset `integration` to `dbe793a7`** and let the slice arrive normally · ⓑ **accept it in place** and validate it where it stands · ⓒ **treat the push order as harmless** and close this as guard-only.

### B-237 · A failed workspace read tells the customer they have no organization

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`app/(app)/page.tsx`](../frontend/app/(app)/page.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **found and fixed on the run that found it** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a customer would hit, and the wrong answer is the confident one.** ⛔ **The screen does not say *something went wrong* — it says *you are not part of an organization yet*, which is a statement about the customer's account rather than about the platform** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-11. **QE verifies** |
| **Commit found** | ⛔ **Found by using the product with a broken API tier**, not by a test — the attention screen was read while `/api/proxy/workspaces` was returning `500` |

**Steps.** Break the workspace read — any `500` will do — and open the attention screen while signed in as a member of an organization.

**Expected.** 📁 **[P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md)**: ***a failed read must never render as an empty result.*** **The screen should say the read failed.**

**Actual.** ⚡ **It renders `NoWorkspace`** — *"You are not part of an organization yet. Your organization is your company on Signora — where its accounts, evidence and decisions live. Create one, or ask a colleague to add you to theirs."*

🔴 **The customer is told a fact about themselves that is false.** ⛔ **They are a member of an organization.** ⚠️ **And the copy invites them to act on it** — create one, or ask a colleague — **so the most likely outcome is a duplicate organization created because Signora said the first one did not exist.**

**The cause is one missing question.** 📁 `app/(app)/page.tsx:224` reads `!workspacesLoading && activeWorkspace === null`. ⛔ **A failed read satisfies both**: loading is over and nothing arrived. ⚡ **`WorkspaceProvider` has published `error` since it was written** — the screen simply never asked.

✅ **Fixed by asking.** **A failed read renders the failure; only a successful read that genuinely returned nothing renders `NoWorkspace`.**

⚠️ **This is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md)'s eighth instance and the first at WORKSPACE scope.** 📁 [C-226](LANE_COORDINATION.md) found six on one screen and [B-006](#b-006) another — **every previous one made a section look empty. This one makes the customer's own membership look absent**, which is a larger claim than any of them.

### B-236 · The Action Batch's two events cannot be published, and every test used a fake

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`action_batch`** — [`domain/events.py`](../backend/modules/action_batch/domain/events.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **found and fixed while building [TASK-465](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a customer would hit** — ⛔ **the first real publish raises**, so an application would appear to succeed and the timeline would never hear about it. ⚠️ **Not 🔴 only because nothing published them yet** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-10, in the slice that found it. **QE verifies** |
| **Commit found** | ⛔ **Found by the FIRST code path that publishes through the real outbox** — [TASK-465](BACKLOG.md)'s apply endpoint — **not by a test** |

**Steps.** Publish `ActionBatchApplied` or `ActionBatchReversed` through `PostgresOutboxEventPublisher`.

**Expected.** A row in `outbox_event`.

**Actual.** ⚡ `AttributeError: 'ActionBatchApplied' object has no attribute 'event_type'`. 📁 **`PublishableEvent` requires `event_type`, `event_version`, `causation_id` and `to_payload()`** — **the two events declare none of them.**

🔴 **Why it was invisible, and this is the useful half.** ⛔ **Every test of these events used a fake publisher** that records what it is handed and asks nothing of it. ⚠️ **`test_public_contract.py` asserted the events' SHAPE and `test_batches.py` executed the use cases through `FakePublisher`** — 📁 exactly the pattern [B-172](#b-172) already found in this module: *"an import is not an execution."* ✅ **This is the same lesson one level up: a fake that is more permissive than the real port proves the caller compiles, not that it works.**

⚡ **The `# type: ignore[list-item]` on `_publish` was the visible tell**, and its comment said the protocol *"declares settable members which frozen domain events cannot satisfy"* — ⛔ **a real constraint, but it hid a second, simpler problem: the fields were absent entirely.**

✅ **Fixed by declaring what the protocol asks for on all three events** — `event_type`, `event_version`, `causation_id` and `to_payload()` — **the shape `ai_research_engine`'s events already use.** ⚡ **And the regression is the API test that found it**: `test_api_action_batch.py` publishes through the real outbox and reads the row back, so a future event that cannot be published fails there rather than in production.

### B-235 · A lane's blanket conflict resolution duplicates board rows, and this is the second time

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository governance — [`docs/ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md), [`docs/BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — 🔴 **this lane caused it, twice** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a reader would act on.** 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"no lane may remain assigned to work that has reached `main`, and no stale assignment is left behind"* — ⛔ **a board carrying a row's `CLAIMED` state BESIDE its `IN VALIDATION` state answers *"who is doing what"* twice, differently** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-10. **8 duplicated board rows collapsed to one each, keeping the furthest state**, and **[TASK-452](BACKLOG.md)'s second `Status` cell removed.** ⚠️ **QE verifies** |
| **Commit found** | Found by **scanning for it**, not by reading — a script that counts `TASK-nnn` occurrences per board row and `Status` cells per backlog row |

**Steps.** Rebase a lane branch that is many commits ahead of `integration`, resolve the `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` and `BACKLOG.md` conflicts by taking the union of both sides, and read the board.

**Expected.** 📁 **One row per `TASK-nnn`, at one status.**

**Actual.** ⚡ **Up to THREE rows for one task** — `TASK-471`, `TASK-482`, `TASK-481`, `TASK-493` and `TASK-475` each appeared twice or three times, **one saying `CLAIMED` and another `IN VALIDATION`** — and `TASK-452` carried two `Status` cells in one row.

🔴 **The cause is a resolution strategy, not a slip.** ⚠️ **A union keeps both sides of every hunk**, which is right for two lanes appending different rows and **wrong for one row whose status a later commit changed** — **the older cell is not a competing row, it is the same row before the edit.**

⛔ **And it is the SECOND occurrence**: 📁 *"TASK-471 to `IN VALIDATION`, and five duplicate board rows removed"* (`3e07724f`) **repaired exactly this a cycle earlier, and the strategy that produced it was used again.** ⚡ **Related to [B-232](#b-232), which is the same resolution failing in the other direction** — there a blanket *"take my side"* reverted a QE cell.

✅ **What actually prevents it, and it is not care.** ⚡ **The union resolution stays** — it is the safe default against B-232 — ⛔ **but it is no longer the end of the process.** **A scan now runs after every rebase, beside the [B-168](#b-168) directional check that already runs there**: *no `TASK-nnn` appears in more than one board row, and no backlog row carries more than one `Status` cell.* 🔴 **Both defects are of one kind — a mechanical resolution needs a mechanical check, because the whole reason the resolution is mechanical is that reading every hunk does not scale.**

### B-234 · The rail was a second `complementary` landmark, and the utility panel made it a collision

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`components/shell/app-shell.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/app-shell.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **found and fixed while building [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 **Wrong but survivable** while the rail was the only one; ⚠️ **🟠 the moment the utility panel mounted**, because two unlabelled-and-labelled `complementary` regions is a landmark menu that answers nothing |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-10. **Runtime-verified**: `getByRole('complementary')` returns **2** before and **1** after, and the one that remains is the panel |
| **Commit found** | ⛔ **Found by Playwright refusing to click**, not by a test asserting landmarks — *"`<span>Settings</span>` … intercepts pointer events"* |

**Steps.** Sign in, open any authenticated screen, and enumerate the `complementary` landmarks.

**Expected.** 📁 **One, and it is the utility panel.** **The design's landmark table is explicit and assigns each region exactly one role**: *"`nav[navigation]` — the rail, labelled *Primary*"* and *"`aside[complementary]` — the utility panel, labelled with its active tab."*

**Actual.** ⚡ **The rail's wrapper was an `<aside>`**, which is a `complementary` landmark in its own right — **an unnamed one, wrapping a `<nav>` that already carried the correct role.** ⛔ **So the rail announced itself twice, as two different kinds of region.**

🔴 **Latent until [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md).** **While the rail was the only `<aside>` the extra landmark was merely noise**; **mounting the utility panel made the page carry two**, and 📁 **this is the same defect [TASK-1444](BACKLOG.md) already found with `banner`** — *"a screen-reader user choosing that landmark would get a menu of two."*

✅ **The fix is one element.** **The wrapper is a `<div>`; the `<nav aria-label="Primary">` inside it is unchanged and still carries the landmark the design asks for.** ⛔ **Nothing about the rail's width, collapse or contents moved.**

⚠️ **And the test that should have caught it did not exist, so it does now**: **the shell asserts exactly one `complementary` and that its accessible name is the panel's** — **which fails if either the rail regains an `<aside>` or a second panel is ever mounted.**

### B-233 · The navigation region failed on every authenticated screen, at every width

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`components/shell/navigation.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/navigation.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — ⚡ **found and fixed on the poll it was found** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a customer would hit.** ⛔ **Not 🔴** — the `RegionBoundary` contained it, so **the page's own content was always intact**; ⚠️ **but every authenticated screen showed a failure band, and the primary navigation was one of the things it contained** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-10. **Runtime-verified in a browser**: `region_failed` **0**, `Dynamic href` **0**, and the band is gone. 🔴 **And a JOURNEY was red because of it and is now green** — 📁 `accessibility.spec.ts` *"the first tab stop is reachable and visible"*: **7 accessibility journeys failed before this fix and 6 after**, ⚡ **measured by stashing the change and re-running rather than argued.** ⛔ **The remaining 6 are pre-existing and data-dependent** (the lane workspace had no accounts) **and are untouched by this fix** — ✅ **since PROVEN by seeding this lane's database through `tests.playground.seed` and re-running: 21 of 21 green.** ⛔ **Correctly NOT filed as a defect** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a workstation gap must never be recorded as a repository defect*) |
| **Commit found** | Found during [TASK-1417](BACKLOG.md)'s **headed review** ([D-134](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) — ⛔ **not by a test, and no test could have failed** |

**Steps.** Sign in. Open **any** authenticated screen, at **any** viewport width.

**Expected.** The navigation renders.

**Actual.** 📁 ***"Signora could not load the navigation. Everything else on this page is unaffected — reload to try again."*** — a full-width failure band, plus *"Retry — attempt 1 of 3"*, **on every screen.** ⚡ **The console names the cause exactly**: `Dynamic href '/w/[workspace]/home' found in <Link>`.

🔴 **The cause, and it is a two-renderer defect rather than a typo.** 📁 **`Navigation` resolves `[workspace]` from the active workspace and DROPS the entry when none is known** — its own comment says *"an entry whose segment cannot be filled is dropped, not linked half-built"*. ⛔ **`MobileNavigation` mapped `RAIL_DESTINATIONS` raw and never called that logic**, so the literal reached a `<Link>` — **and a dynamic href throws in the App Router.**

⚠️ **At EVERY width, which is the part worth recording.** **The phone bar is hidden with `smalllaptop:hidden` — CSS, not conditional rendering — so it is mounted, and it throws, on a 1280px desktop.**

⚡ **The file already claimed the right thing and meant only half of it**: ***"One source, two renderings. A second array would be a second answer to what can this person reach."*** ✅ **True of the LIST and false of the RESOLUTION.** **`resolved()` is now shared, which is what that sentence had to mean to be true.**

⛔ **Why no test caught it.** 📁 **`navigation-rail.test.tsx` asserts the substitution and the drop — for `Navigation` only.** **`mobile-navigation.test.tsx` did not even stub the workspace provider**, so **the renderer that was broken was the one nobody asked the question of.** ✅ **Three regression tests added there, and the third is the general form** — ⚡ ***no rendered href contains `[`*** — **because the defect was never about Home; it was about one renderer not applying a resolution the other did.** **Fire-tested: reintroducing the raw map turns all three red.**

### B-232 · A lane's rebase resolution reverted QE's `PROMOTED` cell, and the revert reached `main`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository governance — [`docs/BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — 🔴 **this lane caused it** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **Wrong behaviour a reader would act on.** ⛔ **Not 🔴 — no code was affected and no gate was weakened** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, at promoted `e3eeca2`. **Measured on `main` rather than accepted**: `TASK-1403` reads `PROMOTED — QE, in certified e71e74d` again. ⚡ **And the gate that let it past is repaired** — [B-176](#b-176) |
| **Commit found** | Found by a directional scan of every Lane A row across `origin/integration`'s history |

**Steps.** QE promoted [TASK-1403](BACKLOG.md) and wrote `PROMOTED — QE, in certified e71e74d`. This lane then rebased, hit a conflict in `BACKLOG.md`, and resolved it by taking its own side.

**Expected.** ⛔ **A lane never writes `VERIFIED`, `CERTIFIED`, `PROMOTED` or `DONE`** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)) — **and never un-writes one either.**

**Actual.** ⚡ **The cell reverted to `IN VALIDATION`**, and because it landed on `integration` before the next cycle, **QE promoted the revert to `main`.** 📁 **All three refs then said a promoted slice was still awaiting validation.**

**Cause, and it is a process defect rather than a slip.** ⛔ **This lane resolved several `BACKLOG.md` conflicts with a blanket rule — *take the incoming side* — applied by a script.** ⚡ **That rule is right for a lane's own execution state and WRONG for QE's judgement cells**, and it cannot tell the two apart because it never looks at what the cell says.

> 🔴 **This is [B-168](#b-168) exactly, one generation later.** 📁 B-168: *"a clean rebase can silently revert QE's `VERIFIED` cells."* ⚠️ **This lane knew the rule, ran the directional check earlier the same day, and caught a `CHANGES REQUESTED` cell with it** — ⛔ **then stopped running it once the rebases became routine.** ✅ **A check that is only run when somebody remembers is the class of guard [§2](../CLAUDE.md) calls documentation pretending to be code.**

**Scope, measured rather than assumed.** ✅ **Exactly ONE row was affected.** ⚡ **Every Lane A row was scanned across the last forty versions of `BACKLOG.md` on `integration`** — `TASK-1412`, `TASK-1438`, `TASK-464` and `TASK-1411` all retain their `PROMOTED` cells, and the rows still in flight were never stronger than `IN VALIDATION`.

**Fix.** ✅ **QE's cell restored VERBATIM**, recovered from `ee7f1523` rather than re-typed — ⛔ **a paraphrase of somebody else's judgement is a second defect wearing a repair's clothes.**

⚠️ **The durable fix is not this commit.** ⛔ **It is that a `BACKLOG.md` conflict must be resolved cell by cell**, keeping QE's word wherever the cell carries one — **and the scan that found this is the thing to run after every rebase**, which is what [B-168](#b-168) already asked for.


### B-231 · Registering Better Auth's `twoFactor()` plugin broke account registration outright

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `product_surface` — [`frontend/lib/auth/server.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/server.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — and 🔴 **this lane shipped it**, in [TASK-493](BACKLOG.md), hours earlier |
| **Severity** | 🔴 **Blocks a milestone.** ⛔ **Nobody could create an account** — the first journey in the product |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-10, in the slice that found it.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes** |
| **Commit found** | Found by [TASK-475](BACKLOG.md)'s journeys running against the real stack |

> ⚠️ **NOT `VERIFIED` — and the reason is the rule QE applied to sixteen backlog rows this morning.** ⛔ **QE has not measured that account registration works.** **The suite passes and Lane A's own journeys found and fixed it, which is why the row reads `FIXED` rather than `OPEN`** — ✅ **but `VERIFIED` means QE pointed at the behaviour, and the certification gates never create an account.** **It closes when a journey QE can run does.**

**Steps.** Register `twoFactor()` in `lib/auth/server.ts`, then complete `/register` with any valid details.

**Expected.** 📁 **TASK-493's own Definition of Done**: *"Four capabilities registered and reachable, **zero journeys changed**."*

**Actual.** ⛔ **Every `POST /api/auth/sign-up` failed**:

```
[Better Auth]: Failed to create user
  error: column "twoFactorEnabled" of relation "user" does not exist
```

**Cause.** ⚡ **The plugin needs schema and this repository has no route to create it.** 📁 `0005_auth_schema.py` is explicit — *"this migration creates the schema and nothing inside it"*, **Better Auth owns its tables** — and ⛔ **there is no `better-auth migrate` step in `package.json`**, so a plugin that adds columns has nothing to add them.

> 🔴 **Why the suite did not catch it, and this is the part worth keeping.** ⚡ **`vitest` passed throughout — 2607 green** — because [`auth-plugins.test.ts`](../frontend/tests/unit/auth-plugins.test.ts) asserts the plugin is **imported and registered** and **never touches Better Auth's database.** ⛔ **It was a test of the configuration, not of the capability.**
>
> ⚠️ **That is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s decorative class in its most expensive form**: **the test was green, the type checker was clean, the row's Definition of Done said *zero journeys changed*, and registration was dead.** ✅ **📁 [§19](../CLAUDE.md) is exactly right and this is the evidence**: *"The responsibility does not end with writing the tests. It includes executing them."*

**Fix.** ⛔ **`twoFactor()` removed until its schema exists**, with the reason recorded where the next reader will be — in the plugins array itself, not only here. ✅ **`multiSession()` stays and is proven safe by the same journeys**: registration, verification and reset all pass with it registered.

✅ **Verified by running the journeys**, not by reasoning: **7 of 7 green** against the lane's own stack afterwards, including `@journey somebody with no account can create one`.

⚡ **The condition for its return is stated rather than remembered**: **when this repository has a mechanism that creates Better Auth's plugin schema**, `twoFactor()` can be registered again — ⛔ **and [C-280](LANE_COORDINATION.md)'s ADR should cover that mechanism, because `passkey` and `sso` will need the same thing.**


### B-230 · An account-level refusal carries the workspace id the design says it must not see

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `product_surface` — [`frontend/lib/entry/index.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/index.ts) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — `product_surface` is this lane's in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 **Wrong but survivable** — ⛔ **nothing consumed the field, which is exactly why it was invisible.** ⚠️ **It would have become 🟠 the moment [TASK-1403](BACKLOG.md)'s support bundle shipped without this fix, because the bundle is a data-egress surface** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-10, in the same slice that found it.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes; this lane does not** (§20e) |
| **Commit found** | Found by [TASK-1403](BACKLOG.md) writing the first consumer of `EntryDecision.workspaceId` |

**Steps.** `resolveEntry({ ...session, account: 'suspended' })`, then read `.workspaceId`.

**Expected.** ⛔ **`null`.** 📁 **The design states this as the REASON gate 1 is first**: *"Can this identity use the product at all? **Evaluated before any workspace is loaded, because a suspended account must not see workspace names it no longer has rights to.**"*

**Actual.** ⛔ **The person's workspace id.** ⚡ **`resolveWorkspace` runs once before the rule walk and answers regardless of which gate then decides** — so every gate 1 and gate 2 decision carried a resolved workspace, **which is the exact disclosure the gate ordering exists to prevent, reintroduced by computing the answer eagerly.**

> ⚡ **How it stayed invisible, and it is the useful half.** 📁 **The engine ships with no caller** ([TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md) says so deliberately; [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md) is the wiring row), **so nothing read the field.** ⛔ **A leak nobody reads is still a leak — it is a leak waiting for its first reader**, and [TASK-1403](BACKLOG.md) is that reader: it hands the field to a **support diagnostics bundle**, which the row itself calls *"a data-egress surface… where tenancy is usually forgotten."*
>
> ✅ **The existing sweep did not catch it and was not wrong to miss it.** `entry-engine.test.ts` asserted *"never routes to a workspace the person is not a member of"* — **and a suspended member IS still a member**, so the id was legitimate by that test's rule. **The property that was missing is the design's own ordering**, which is now asserted over the whole sweep by gate number rather than by fixture.

**Fix.** ⚡ **One expression, and the gate number is the test because the design's is**: `rule.gate < GATES.WORKSPACE_RESOLUTION ? null : workspaceId`. ⛔ **Gates 1 and 2 precede workspace resolution by construction, so a decision from either cannot have resolved one.** ✅ **Regression test in `entry-engine.test.ts`, asserted across every session in the sweep**, so a future rule placed in gate 1 or 2 cannot reintroduce it.

| ✅ **Measured, not inferred** | 📁 **`organization-setup.spec.ts:21` — `` const unique = () => `E2E Org ${Date.now()}` ``**, which is exactly the row that appeared. ⛔ **The file contains no `afterAll`, no `afterEach` and nothing that restores the previous workspace** — grepped, zero matches. ⚡ **And the execution order matches exactly**: `organization-setup` runs at **[140/218]**, and **every account-backed failure is after it** — `perception` [146] · `resilience` [153] · `search-journey` [161] · `signal-center` [163] · `visual` [165] |
| ⚡ **Each one passes on its own** | 📁 **`signal-center` is 4/4 green standalone** against the same seeded environment, and **0/2 inside the suite** — ⛔ **the assertion that fails is the vacuity guard**, `sawASummary`, because **the queue renders no rows at all**: the screen is reading an empty workspace |

### B-228 · WITHDRAWN — the seeder was never broken; the lane's invocation split one database into two

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **None.** ⛔ **There is no defect here.** ⚠️ **Filed against the Product Playground, which is `platform_foundation`; that attribution was wrong along with the rest** |
| **Severity** | ⛔ **WITHDRAWN 2026-08-09 by the lane that raised it, on a green run** |
| **Status** | ⛔ **`WITHDRAWN`** — **kept rather than deleted**, because the reasoning failure is worth more than the row was |
| ✅ **The seeder works** | **`replacing 2 previous Playground(s)` · `seeding 12 accounts through the real pipeline…` · 12 qualified opportunities · 4 of 4 readings re-scored · 51 users enrolled · exit 0.** ⚡ **No repository change of any kind was required to get there** |

| ✅ **`make e2e` was correct the whole time** | 📁 **`E2E_ENV` sets all three** — `SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL`, `SIGNORA_TEST_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` and `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL`, **all at the same database.** ⛔ **The repository's own path had no defect** |
| 🔴 **What survives, and it is [B-224](#b-224)** | ⚡ **This is B-224's real cost, demonstrated rather than argued.** **`make e2e` was unusable because of the port divergence, so a lane hand-rolled a substitute — and E2E_ENV's three variables are exactly what a substitute drops.** ⛔ **The wasted hour is the evidence for B-224, not for a defect in the Playground** |
