### B-227 · The Task Claim Protocol's step 7 pushes the lane's whole branch, and under continuous execution that is never only the claim

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Repository governance** — [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §20e, *The Task Claim Protocol*, step 7 |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **wrong behaviour a lane would hit, and it defeats the one boundary §20e machine-checks.** ⚡ **Not 🔴: nothing is broken at rest, no gate fails, and QE's `--audit-claims` still detects the result** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **found by Lane A, 2026-08-09, by doing it.** ⚠️ **Reported WITH the breach it caused, because the breach is the evidence** |
| **Found on** | `78c83be5`, claiming [TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Steps** | **Follow §20e step 7 literally while holding earlier slices at `IN VALIDATION`** — which *Continuous execution* explicitly permits: *"a branch may carry more than one slice — but only when every earlier one is `IN VALIDATION`"*. **Commit the claim alone (step 6), then run step 7 as written:** `git checkout integration && git merge --ff-only <lane-branch> && git push origin integration` |
| **Expected** | ⚡ **`integration` advances by ONE commit touching exactly [`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) and [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md)** — §20e's own bound: 📁 *"a claim commit touches `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` and `BACKLOG.md` and nothing else"*, enforced by `infra/certification-guard.py --audit-claims` |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`integration` advanced by ELEVEN commits.** **`--ff-only` fast-forwards to the BRANCH HEAD, not to the claim** — so it carried `step-up-dialog.tsx`, `code-input.tsx`, `lib/auth/server.ts`, `search-journey.spec.ts` and four register edits onto the ref QE alone may write. ⚡ **Measured**: `git diff --name-only 78c83be5..fde09dc2` → **12 files**, of which **10 are production code and tests** |
| 🔴 **Why it is the protocol and not only the lane** | ⚠️ **Step 7's command is correct exactly once — when the claim is the branch's only unpushed commit.** ⛔ **That was true under the original model, where a lane held one slice and reset after promotion.** ⚡ **Continuous execution changed the premise and step 7 did not follow**: a lane is now *required* to keep working while QE holds earlier slices, so **the steady state is a branch whose head is not the claim.** **Two rules of the same section, and the later one makes the earlier one's command wrong** |
| ⛔ **What makes it worse than a typo** | 📁 **§20e calls this *"the one thing a feature lane may push to `integration`"* and says it is *"bounded so tightly that a machine checks it"*. ⚡ **The bound is real and the audit works — but it runs at certification, AFTER the push.** **The protocol has no step that would have stopped it**, and the lane following the instruction literally is the one who breaks it |
| ✅ **The fix, and it is one line** | **Step 7 pushes the CLAIM COMMIT, never the branch**: `git push origin <claim-sha>:integration`, or `git checkout integration && git cherry-pick <claim-sha> && git push origin integration`. ⚡ **Both make the pushed object the thing that was bounded.** ⛔ **Neither changes the protocol's meaning** — step 7's purpose is *"the moment the claim exists, where every other lane will look"*, and a cherry-pick satisfies that exactly |
| ⚠️ **Recorded because it is the honest half** | ⛔ **Lane A pushed the eleven commits and the repair needed a force-push to a shared ref, which is the product owner's call and was approved.** ⚡ **It became moot before it ran: QE pushed first, validated the same work on its merits and promoted it** ([cycle 163](../PROJECT_STATUS.md)), leaving `integration` at `main` + the claim — **the state the repair would have produced.** ⛔ **That is luck, not a mitigation, and the row exists so the next lane does not need the same luck.** ⚠️ **It cannot be ruled out that the erroneous push is what delivered those commits to QE's snapshot** — the SHAs were rewritten, so the two cannot be distinguished from here, and **stating that is worth more than a clean-sounding account** |
| **Not this lane's to fix** | 📁 **`CLAUDE.md` is the product owner's** (§20e, *Shared files have one owner*) — ⛔ **Lane A does not edit it**, and [B-222](#b-222) is already open in the same file for the same reason |

### 🔴 The cost, measured rather than imagined

⛔ **This lane skipped [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md) — position 5 in its own queue — recording the reason as *"measured rather than asserted: this lane's PostgreSQL (`:5732`) is not running."*** ⚠️ **The database was running the whole time.** **The skip was written into the board, the row and a claim commit pushed to `integration`**, and it was wrong in all three.

> ⚡ **The lane's error is the lane's, and it is recorded as such** — [`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) carries the correction. **Reaching for the model when the process has a configuration file is the mistake.** ⛔ **But a published number that nothing uses is what made it a plausible one**, and the next lane will reach for `--exports` too: it is the *documented* way to ask.

### ⚠️ Which of the two is authoritative is the actual question

📁 **[`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) § Running a lane lists a database NAME per lane and no port.** ⚡ **So neither source is contradicted by the runbook, and both are internally consistent** — 🔴 **which is why this survived**: there is no check that could have failed.

**Two candidate repairs, and this lane is not choosing between them:**

**①** ⚡ **The model is right and the environments are not provisioned to it** — then `backend/.env` is the drift and per-lane PostgreSQL instances are missing.
**②** ⛔ **The environments share one PostgreSQL and are separated by DATABASE rather than by port** — which is what is actually running, and which the `signora_lane_a` / `signora_lane_b` / `signora_demo` naming already implies. **Then `--exports` should publish `5432` and the slot should stop implying a port.**

⚡ **② matches the evidence**, but **choosing is `platform_foundation`'s** — the slot model also drives Redis indices and compose projects, and changing what a slot means is not a one-line edit a consuming lane may make.

### B-223 · The auth tier's "is this deployed?" denylist and the environment registry share no vocabulary, so a lane that names itself cannot start

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/lib/auth/config.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/config.ts), `isDeployed()` · measured against [`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py), which is `platform_foundation`'s |
| **Current assignee** | **Joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)** — ⛔ **not written here** ([C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⚡ **latent, not live.** ⛔ **Nothing sets `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` for the frontend today**, so `environmentName()` returns `local` and every clone works. ⚠️ **It fires the first time anybody configures the variable to the name their own registry gives them** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **found by Lane A, 2026-08-09, implementing [TASK-473](BACKLOG.md).** ⛔ **Deliberately not fixed — see below; the repair is a security decision, not a typo** ⚠️ **ROUTED 2026-08-12 as [C-298](LANE_COORDINATION.md)** — ⛔ **filed 2026-08-09 and carried to nobody for three days.** 🔴 **Second instance of the class [B-219](#b-219) records about itself**: *a defect whose fix a lane may not make, with no `C-` row, can sit indefinitely.* |
| **Found** | 2026-08-09 by Lane A, ⚡ **by having to compute the authentication mode and discovering the two sources disagree about what an environment is called** |

**Steps to reproduce.** On `origin/integration`:

```bash
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'infra'); import environments as e; print([x.name for x in e.ENVIRONMENTS])"
→ ['review', 'lane-qe', 'lane-a', 'lane-b', 'lane-c', 'lane-d', 'lane-e', 'demo']

grep -n "isDeployed" -A2 frontend/lib/auth/config.ts
→ return !['local', 'test', 'development'].includes(environmentName());
```

**Expected.** ⚡ **The two agree on what an environment is called.**

**Actual.** ⛔ **The intersection is EMPTY.** **Not one of the registry's eight names appears in the auth tier's three**, and **not one of the auth tier's three is a registry row.**

**The consequence, stated concretely.** ⚠️ **A lane that exports `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT=lane-a` — which is the name [`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) gives it, and what `--exports` emits — is classified `isDeployed() === true`.** ⛔ **`resolveEmailTransport()` then refuses the console and mailbox transports and the auth tier will not start**, with a diagnostic saying *"is a deployed environment"* about a developer's laptop.

### ⛔ Why this is reported rather than repaired, and the reason is §13

⚡ **The obvious fix is to widen the allowlist to include the registry's development names.** ⛔ **That is a weakened guard, however it is dressed.**

📁 **The guard exists because the console transport writes verification and password-reset links to stdout** — *"a credential sitting in a log file"* — **and the mailbox keeps a HISTORY of them.** ⚠️ **Every name added to that list is an environment in which a credential may be written to a log**, and `review` and `demo` are both registry rows that serve people who are not the person who started the process.

> 🔴 **So the question is not *which names are missing*. It is *which environments may write a credential to stdout*, and that is a security decision with a named owner** — ⛔ **not a list a lane extends while passing through.** **[TASK-473](BACKLOG.md)'s own Change Budget says *"no weakened guard"* by name.**

### ✅ What [TASK-473](BACKLOG.md) did instead

**`authMode()` reports the classification rather than correcting it**, and 🔴 **the disagreement is pinned as a passing assertion** in `tests/unit/auth-mode.test.ts`:

```ts
expect(withEnvironment('lane-a', authMode)).toBe('production');
```

⚡ **That test is written to FAIL on the day somebody repairs this**, which is the point of recording a known-wrong behaviour as an assertion rather than as a comment: **a comment is read once, and a comment describing a defect is indistinguishable from a comment describing a design.**

### ⚠️ Two candidate repairs, neither this lane's to choose

**① Make the registry authoritative for both.** ⚡ **`infra/environments.py` already knows which environments are development slots**; the auth tier could ask it rather than keep a parallel list — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *truth has exactly one authoritative representation*. ⛔ **Crosses a tier boundary: a Node process cannot import a Python registry**, so it needs a published form, and that is a design decision.

**② Invert the list.** ⚡ **Name the environments where a credential in a log is acceptable, rather than the ones where it is not** — ⛔ **so a NEW environment is deployed-by-default instead of development-by-default.** **That is the safe direction and it is a behaviour change to a security guard**, which is 🔴.

| **2026-08-03** | `MINIMUM_QUERY = 2` lands — `7fb2cf2d`, *"A1 — find an account by name"* |
| **2026-08-08** | The spec types `'a'` — `80c21b14`, [TASK-484](BACKLOG.md) |

⛔ **The minimum was five days old when the spec was written against it.** ⚡ **Not a regression — a journey that has never passed since it was authored**, and nothing said so.

### 🔴 Second instance in one day, and that is the point

📁 **[B-225](#b-225) was the first**, found the same way this morning: *"nothing runs the journeys."* ⚡ **This is the same gap producing a second casualty**, and QE independently hit the third face of it in cycle 159 — 📁 **it could not run the journeys at all off `main`** ([B-156](#b-156)).

> ⚠️ **Three lanes, three encounters, one gap.** ⛔ **A gate nothing executes does not fail; it rots**, and the rot is only visible to whoever next runs it by hand.

### ✅ The fix

**Type a real query.** ⚡ **The seeded accounts are known**, so the spec asks for something a seller would type rather than one letter:

```ts
await search.fill('north');
```

⛔ **Not `MINIMUM_QUERY` characters of anything** — a two-letter query that happens to clear the threshold would still be a test about the threshold. **A journey types a name.**

### B-225 · A shipped `@smoke` journey has been red since 2026-08-08, and nothing runs the journeys so nothing said so

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/tests/e2e/permissions.member.spec.ts`](../frontend/tests/e2e/permissions.member.spec.ts):23 · [`frontend/app/(app)/authenticated-shell.tsx`](../frontend/app/(app)/authenticated-shell.tsx):172 |
| **Current assignee** | **Joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)** — ⛔ **not written here** ([C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⚡ **the PRODUCT is fine; the journey that proves it is not.** ⛔ **A member genuinely sees their morning** — the page snapshot at failure shows the attention list rendering correctly. **What is broken is the assertion, and a broken assertion on a `@smoke` journey is a gate that cannot pass** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **on the poll that found it.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-09 by Lane A, ⚡ **running the journeys as a BASELINE before starting [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md)** — 📁 **that row's verification is *"four shipped customer journeys passing unchanged on new paths"*, and a baseline is the only way to tell a rename's breakage from breakage that was already there** |

**Steps to reproduce.** With a lane stack on 3300:

```bash
HEADLESS=1 make e2e-quick ARGS="--grep @smoke"
→ 1 failed, 7 passed
  [member] permissions.member.spec.ts:23 @smoke sees their morning like everybody else
```

**Expected.** ✅ **The member's own identity is visible in the shell.**

**Actual.** ⛔ **`strict mode violation: getByText('marcus.hale@northwind.example') resolved to 3 elements.`**

### ⚡ Why it resolves to three, and two of them are enough

**The shell renders the email TWICE, by design** — 📁 a desktop link to `/profile` (`sm:inline`) and a mobile span (`sm:hidden`):

```
app/(app)/authenticated-shell.tsx:168  <Link href="/profile" …>{email}</Link>
app/(app)/authenticated-shell.tsx:172  <span className="…sm:hidden">{email}</span>
```

⛔ **Playwright's strict mode counts matches in the DOM, not visible ones**, so `sm:hidden` does not save it. **Two matches already fail; the third — a `Password for …` label from [`session-lock.tsx`](../frontend/components/auth/session-lock.tsx):193 — only makes it louder.**

**Dated, not guessed:** `git log -S` puts the mobile span at `2fe98430`, **2026-08-08, TASK-470 milestone 1**. ⚡ **The slice that added the second render did not update the spec that asserted there was one.**

### 🔴 The finding that is worth more than the fix

⛔ **This has been red for a day and nothing reported it, because nothing runs the journeys.** ⚡ **QE's cycle measurements name `make smoke` — 24 stages — and never a Playwright count**; 📁 [§19](../CLAUDE.md) puts the browser journeys on the *implementing lane* before handover ([D-113](DECISION_REGISTER.md), [D-114](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), and a lane that does not run them ships a red gate nobody sees.

> ⚠️ **This is the exact class [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md) was written for, one level up.** **That row made the journeys *watchable* by default; it did not make them *run*.** ⛔ **A gate whose default is never to execute is not a gate**, and the repository has now paid a day for it.

⚡ **Not proposed as a new mechanism here** — 📁 [D-212](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §8 forbids adding governance that has not been shown to help, and [§20c-2](../CLAUDE.md) forbids the obvious reflex of putting it in CI. **Recorded so the next person deciding where journeys run has the evidence.**

### ✅ The fix

**Scope the assertion to the one element that carries meaning** — the profile link — rather than to any text on the page:

```ts
await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: MEMBER.email })).toBeVisible();
```

⚡ **Same repair this lane made in `app-shell-rail.test.tsx`** when the shell's second wordmark broke an unscoped query: ⛔ **the duplicate render is correct and the query was wrong.** ✅ **And it asserts something stronger than before** — not merely that the address appears somewhere, but that it is the link to their own profile.

### B-171 · a new test types the coordination module as `ModuleType` and then sets an attribute on it, so `mypy --strict` fails

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Platform Foundation — [`backend/tests/test_coordination_source.py`](../backend/tests/test_coordination_source.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — its own test, in its own module |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **`mypy --strict` is a required gate and a Definition-of-Done row**, so the slice cannot be certified |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, at `edd82116`. **Measured on the promoted commit, not accepted**: `mypy --strict` clean over **854 files**. ⚡ **Lane C used `setattr`, not the `monkeypatch` QE's row suggested, and it was right to**: `setattr(coordination, "datetime", Exploding)` sits forty lines above in the same file, and **§6 makes the local pattern authoritative** — *"match existing patterns in the module you're working in."* **QE's row named the sibling file's convention; the lane applied the better rule.** 🔴 **The lane's own diagnosis is the durable half, and it is not about typing**: *"I reverted my own fix twice to prove those tests were load-bearing, then ran `mypy --strict` on the two `infra/` files and never on the test file I had just written."* ✅ **Its correction is a habit rather than a rule** — ***type-check the directory you touched, not the file you were thinking about.*** ⚠️ **Cost: two cycles, nine commits held.** |
| 🔴 **What actually went wrong, and it is not the type error** | ⛔ **I ran `mypy --strict` on `infra/coordination.py` and `infra/state-check.py` and never on the test file I had just written.** ⚡ **I even verified the tests were load-bearing by reverting the fix and watching them fail — thorough about behaviour, and I skipped the gate my own Definition of Done names.** 📁 **QE found it with *the cheap gates before certification*, which is exactly where it should have been found second and my own run first.** ✅ **The correction is a habit, not a rule: type-check the whole directory I touched, not the file I was thinking about** — **`mypy --strict tests/` rather than a named path** |
| **Commit found** | `525a1b10`, found by QE running the cheap gates before certification |

**Steps.** `uv run --directory backend mypy --strict .`

```
tests/test_coordination_source.py:447: error: Module has no attribute "NOTICES"  [attr-defined]
tests/test_coordination_source.py:449: error: Returning Any from function declared to return "str"  [no-any-return]
tests/test_coordination_source.py:451: error: Module has no attribute "NOTICES"  [attr-defined]
tests/test_coordination_source.py:525: error: Module has no attribute "NOTICES"  [attr-defined]
tests/test_coordination_source.py:529: error: Module has no attribute "NOTICES"  [attr-defined]
Found 5 errors in 1 file (checked 854 source files)
```

**Expected.** The gate passes, as §19 requires **before** handover.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Five errors.** ⚡ **`NOTICES` is not missing** — QE checked, it is at `infra/coordination.py:865` and on `main` too. **The module is loaded through `importlib` and typed `ModuleType`, which declares no such attribute**, so `_notice_for` reading and reassigning `coordination.NOTICES` is unprovable to `mypy --strict`.

> ✅ **The test's intent is right and QE is not asking for it back.** *"Run `_notice` against a substituted notices file, not the real one"* is exactly the discipline this suite already uses elsewhere — **a monkeypatched path rather than the live projection.**
>
> ⚡ **The repair is the typing, not the test.** **The sibling loader in [`test_certification_state_reading.py`](../backend/tests/test_certification_state_reading.py) has the same shape and passes** — it registers the module in `sys.modules` and uses `monkeypatch.setattr(module, "MANIFEST", path)`, **which mypy accepts because `monkeypatch.setattr` takes `object`.** ⛔ **Direct attribute assignment on a `ModuleType` does not.**

**Why it was not caught earlier.** ⚠️ **§19 puts `mypy --strict` on the implementing lane before handover.** ⛔ **This is the first slice in this run of cycles to reach QE with a red required gate**, and it was caught by the cheap gates in under a minute — **which is the whole reason they run first.**

### B-170 · `state-check` skips backlog rows whose state it cannot parse, so the same defect can recur silently a fourth time

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository tooling — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — §20e names `state-check.py` in QE's own carve-out ([D-022](../docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⚡ **the instances are fixed; the mechanism that let them hide is not** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Commit found** | `bc4f0c1d`, split out of [B-169](#b-169) once its instances were verified fixed |

**Steps.** Author a backlog row whose state is not in a `| **Status** |` row — inside the Module cell, or as a token containing a markdown link. Run `python3 infra/state-check.py`.

**Expected.** ⚡ **A row whose state cannot be read is reported**, the way the duplicate-identifier check reports a duplicate.

**Actual.** ⛔ **It is counted out of every total and never mentioned.** **The row exists, a human reads its state fine, and every instrument is blind to it.**

> 🔴 **Three occurrences, none caught by an instrument:**
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | **`TASK-1404`** | Unreadable from **2026-08-08** until a lane rendered a table that happened to show it |
> | **`TASK-1441`–`1444`** | Introduced by the very push that fixed `TASK-1404`; **QE found them by counting, not by a check** |
> | **A fifth row** | Found by Lane C when it repaired the four — ⚡ **QE's count of four was already stale when it was written** |
>
> ⛔ **Each was found by a person looking, and the second was authored by the lane that had just written the diagnosis for the first.** **Knowing the class does not prevent the next instance.**

**Repair.** ⚡ **Report, do not fail.** **`state-check` is advisory by design and this belongs at that level** — a finding line naming every row whose state it could not determine, so the count and the gap are visible together. ⛔ **A total that silently excludes what it could not read is the [B-101](#b-101) class**: *a figure that is confidently wrong is worse than a figure that is missing.*

### B-169 · four new rows carry their state inside the Module cell, so no instrument can read it — the defect [TASK-1404](BACKLOG.md) fixed, reintroduced in the same commit

| | |
|---|---|

| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-09, at `bc4f0c1d`. **Measured on the promoted commit: 167 rows, `0` unparsed**, against 4 when the row was filed. ⚡ **Lane C fixed it on the poll it arrived and titled the commit *"D-217's five rows carried a state no instrument could read — again"*** — **five, not the four QE counted**, because one more was added after QE measured. ⚠️ **The check QE asked for is NOT built**: `state-check` still skips rows it cannot parse rather than reporting them, so **nothing stops the sixth.** ⛔ **That half stays open as [B-170](#b-170).** |
| **Commit found** | `700015f6` (`D-217`), found by QE during cycle 176 validation |

**Steps.** From the promoted commit, count rows whose state no reader can parse:

```
before D-217 landed:  1 unparsed   (TASK-1404, fixed by this same push)
after:                4 unparsed   (TASK-1441, 1442, 1443, 1444)
```

```

⚡ **Every state reader in this repository looks for a `Status` row and takes its leading backticked token.** **There is no `Status` row, so `state-check.py`, both dashboards and the coordination projection are blind to all four simultaneously** — **the same triple blindness [`TASK-1404`](BACKLOG.md) was corrected for, in the commit that corrected it.**

> ✅ **These four are `SEQUENCED`, so nothing is claimable that should not be** — **the cost is undercounting, not misdirection.** ⚠️ **But that is luck: the same shape on a `READY` row hides claimable work from every lane.**

**Repair — the check, not the four rows.** ⚡ **`state-check.py` already parses every row; it should report rows whose state it cannot find rather than skipping them silently.** ⛔ **It currently counts what it can read and says nothing about what it cannot** — **which is why one unparsed row survived from 2026-08-08 until a lane rendered a table that happened to show it.** ✅ **Fix the four rows too, but the check is what stops the fifth.**

### B-168 · a clean rebase silently reverted QE's own `VERIFIED` cells, and QE promoted the reversion

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository process — QE's candidate construction |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — QE's own defect, found when a lane's report disagreed with QE's belief |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the repository's record of what QE has verified is silently wrong**, and QE is the only author of that record |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, under [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⛔ **Root cause: the check was never implemented.** **It existed only as a shell command written in this row, so there was nothing to fail and nothing to honour** — which is also why it could be ignored. ✅ **`certification-guard.py::backlog_states()` now reads the authoritative `Status` cell and nothing else**, and `verified_regressions()` compares two revisions by state. ⚡ **Prose cannot reach the output**: a title, a note, an evidence line or a reference naming `VERIFIED` contributes nothing. 📁 **9 regression tests in [`backend/tests/test_promotion_gate.py`](../backend/tests/test_promotion_gate.py)**, including the exact cell that produced the false positive |
| **Commit found** | `0a60ae83` on `main`, found during cycle 172's poll |

**Steps.** A lane's branch carries its own copy of a row it set to `IN VALIDATION`. QE verifies the row and writes `VERIFIED` in a Closeout. The lane later rebases; **its original commit still contains the older cell.** QE rebases the branch, the rebase applies **cleanly**, and QE promotes.

```
4ea8269f  QE's cycle-158 Closeout           ADDED   `VERIFIED` — QE ... at `1874df08`
0a60ae83  Lane A's own TASK-1435 commit     REMOVED it  -> back to `IN VALIDATION`
```

**Expected.** A promotion does not undo QE's judgement.

**Actual.** ⛔ **`TASK-1435` and `TASK-1436` read `IN VALIDATION` on `main` today**, and the work behind them was certified and promoted at `1874df08`. **Measured**: the `VERIFIED` cells QE wrote survive **zero** times.

> 🔴 **QE had already caught this twice and excluded commits for it** — cycle 156 (*"e9160a05 would revert my CHANGES REQUESTED"*) and cycle 160 (*"both residue commits revert my VERIFIED cells"*). ⛔ **In cycle 163 the rebase applied cleanly, so there was no conflict to read, and QE did not re-check.** ⚡ **The two earlier catches were both prompted by a conflict; this one had none.**
>
> ⚠️ **It surfaced only because a lane's own status report said rows were *"with QE"* that QE believed it had verified.** **Neither instrument caught it**: `state-check` compares documents against git, not QE's past writes against its present ones.

> ⛔ **The check produced its first FALSE POSITIVE on 2026-08-10 at `da889fd7`, and QE promoted through it — twice-wrong, and both halves are recorded.**
>
> **① The pattern is too loose.** `grep '^-.*\`VERIFIED\`'` matches **any** removed line containing the word, including a `READY` cell whose *prose* cites a verified row: *"Released: `TASK-1408` is `VERIFIED` and promoted at `e72b6af0`."* ⚡ **Measured: `VERIFIED` status cells were 12 before and 12 after, and NO row lost a `VERIFIED` state.** ✅ **The repair is to anchor on the cell**: `^-\| \*\*Status\*\* \| ✅ \*\*\`VERIFIED\`` — **which returns 0 on this same diff.**
>
> **② QE promoted while the check was firing**, because the check and the promotion sat in one command block with no gate between them. ⛔ **That is [B-142](#b-142)'s class — an exit code not consulted — and it is the third time this session that pattern has cost something.** 🔴 **A check whose output nobody is forced to read is a log line, not a gate.** ✅ **The promotion happened to be safe; that was luck, and it is recorded as luck.**

**Repair — a check, not more care**, since care demonstrably failed on the third occurrence. ⚡ **Before promoting, diff the candidate's `docs/BACKLOG.md` against `main` for `VERIFIED` cells that disappear:**

```
git diff origin/main..HEAD -- docs/BACKLOG.md | grep '^-.*`VERIFIED`'
```

⛔ **Any output is a candidate that undoes QE's own judgement, and the correct response is to exclude those commits** — exactly as QE did in cycles 156 and 160 when a conflict happened to make it visible.

### B-167 · `tsc --noEmit` type-checks a generated Next.js artifact, so a stale `.next/` fails the gate for a build six days old

| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it produces a confident wrong answer**, and the answer names files the change never touched |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Commit found** | `b565c19e` (`TASK-499`), found by QE during cycle 160 validation |

**Steps.** Rename a route, then type-check without clearing the build directory:

```
$ npx tsc --noEmit
.next/types/validator.ts(116,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../app/(auth)/sign-in/page.js'
.next/types/validator.ts(125,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../app/(auth)/sign-up/page.js'
.next/types/validator.ts(134,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../app/(auth)/verify-email/page.js'
TSC=2
```

**Expected.** The gate reports on the source under test.

**Actual.** ⛔ **It reported on `.next/types/validator.ts`, a generated file dated `2026-08-03` — six days before the commit being checked.** ✅ **`rm -rf .next && npx tsc --noEmit` → clean, and `make certify`'s own `tsc` gate then agreed.**

> 🔴 **The failure names three routes the commit deliberately removed**, so it reads exactly like *"the rename broke the type check"* — **the most plausible wrong conclusion available.** ⚠️ **[B-156](#b-156)'s class precisely: a gate that answers confidently from something other than what it was asked about.**
>
> ⛔ **And it would have failed certification.** **QE happened to run `tsc` by hand first and cleared the artifact before starting the run**, which is luck rather than process — **the next route rename certified without that step fails on a six-day-old build and the failure is attributed to the slice.**

**Repair.** ⚡ **Exclude `.next/` from the type gate, or clear it as a precondition of running one.** ⛔ **Excluding is the better half**: `.next/types/` is generated *from* the routes, so type-checking it asks whether a build artifact agrees with the source that has since replaced it — **a question with no useful answer.**

| | |

| **Module** | Repository tooling — `infra/environment-lease.py`, and the `Makefile` targets that take it |

| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Commit found** | Observed live during cycle 160, in both directions |

**Steps.** ⚡ **Measured, not reasoned about.** **One lease serves every heavy operation:**

```
Makefile:410  certify   -> environment-lease.py run certify
Makefile:62   dr        -> environment-lease.py run dr
Makefile:49   smoke     -> ... run smoke
Makefile:90   up        -> ... run up
Makefile:458  e2e       -> ... run e2e
```

**Expected.** §19 and [D-114](../docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md) put the customer journey **on the implementing lane before handover**, so the lane must be able to run it.

**Actual, from one cycle:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lane A, in its own commit** | *"the four journeys **NOT RUN**. QE took the environment lease for a second certify at 11:44:51… I re-pathed the specs; I have not executed them."* |
| ⛔ **Consequence** | ***"The row therefore stays `CLAIMED`."*** **Lane A refused to declare around a gate it could not run** — **which is correct, and is the right behaviour costing throughput** |
| **Then the reverse** | **QE's `make up`/`make dr` were refused by `e2e pid 1815192` in Lane A's worktree** — **Lane A running those journeys the moment the lease cleared** |

> 🔴 **Both halves are correct behaviour and the outcome is still a gate nobody can run reliably.** ⛔ **The lane cannot run journeys while QE certifies, and QE cannot run them at all** ([B-156](#b-156)). **[B-225](#b-225) — a shipped `@smoke` journey red for a day — is what that produces.**
>
> ✅ **QE did not `release --force` in either direction, twice, and waited 510s and 15s respectively.** ⛔ **Forcing is never the repair**: the lease's own text records that cycle 25 wrote `pytest 134 passed` against a suite of 2589 because two runs shared a database.

**Repair — and it is a product-owner-shaped question rather than a lane's.** ⚡ **The journeys need a database and ports; certification needs a database and ports; today they are the same ones.** **Options: a second allocated environment for journeys · a journey profile that reuses a lane's own stack rather than the shared one · or accepting the serialization and scheduling around it explicitly.** ⛔ **What must not happen is the current implicit answer, where the gate is skipped by whoever loses the race.**

docs/architecture/04-modules.md:0

**Expected.** ⚡ **Two things, and both are Definition-of-Done rows rather than preferences.** **§19**: *"Documentation updated — the module's design doc, consistent with the code"*, and **§12**: *"a slice with two of the three is unfinished, not a finished one with paperwork outstanding."* **Plus the `Slice-Handoff` block §20e requires on the last commit of every slice**, where *"every field is required; `none` is a valid value and silence is not."*

**Actual.** ⛔ **A new tenant-owned table, a new domain type, a new repository port and a new `public/` contract, with zero architecture documentation and no handoff.**

> ⚠️ **The rule's stated reason is rotation, and it is the whole argument here.** §12: *"the lane that implements the next slice of a module is usually not the one that implemented the last. It inherits the module's design doc, its ADRs and the Slice Handoff — and nothing else."* ⛔ **`TASK-492`'s own row says its producers are `BLOCKED`, so the next slice of this table will very likely be written by somebody else** — **and `11-tenancy.md` is exactly where they would look for a table's tenancy shape.**

**What is NOT wrong, recorded so the repair stays small.** ✅ **QE audited the tenancy properties directly and they are exemplary**: `workspace_id` non-nullable · `ENABLE` **and** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` · separate `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`DELETE` policies · **no `UPDATE` grant *and* no `UPDATE` policy** — *"both withheld rather than one: a policy without a grant is decorative, and a grant without a policy is a tenancy hole"* — · classified in **both** `TENANT_OWNED_TABLES` and `IMMUTABLE_TENANT_TABLES` **in the same change** · migration `0046` reversible · **+32 tests, +3 Security Invariants.**

⛔ **The code is not what is being returned.** **The repair is the two paragraphs that let the next lane use it.**

> ⚡ **QE promoted the certified commit anyway, deliberately, and that is not an inconsistency.** **§20e forbids an intermediate manual decision between successful certification and promotion** — *"the gates are the decision"* — **and `doc-drift` states of itself that it *"reports and does not gate"*.** ✅ **So the deterministic half ran deterministically, and the judgement half — `VERIFIED` versus `CHANGES REQUESTED` — is where this finding belongs.**

**An observation, not a defect, recorded rather than filed.** ⚡ **`DELETE` is granted on an append-only security stream**, matching `action_batch`'s shape in `0042` **for the stated reason that two append-only tables with two tenancy shapes is how one ends up wrong.** ⚠️ **`CLAUDE.md`'s immutability rule names `UPDATE` specifically and does not forbid `DELETE`, and erasure obligations need it** — **so QE is not calling it a defect.** ⛔ **But a security stream a workspace can delete from is a different compliance story from one it cannot**, and **that is a product-owner question rather than a lane's.**

### B-164 · `--force-with-lease` did not protect a claim commit QE had already reasoned about, because the lease was satisfied

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository process — QE's synchronization step, [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) Closeout activity 10 |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — QE's own error, self-caught and self-repaired |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a claim commit was destroyed on `origin/integration` and restored about two minutes later.** ⚡ **Nothing was permanently lost and no lane observed the gap**, but the mechanism will recur |
| **Status** | **`OPEN` — and it RECURRED on 2026-08-09 at `ee8e8fac`, which is the row's whole point.** ⛔ **QE force-pushed `main:integration` without running this row's own check first and destroyed `Claim TASK-1405`.** ✅ **Restored within two minutes** — the object survived, it was cherry-picked onto `main` and pushed as a **fast-forward**, and re-verified by subject, file list and `TASK-1405` appearing in both registers. **No lane observed the gap.** ⚡ **Second occurrence, and the cause was the same both times**: the habitual three-command push block ran to completion because nothing in it stops. ⛔ **The check exists and is written in this row; QE did not run it.** 🔴 **A check that must be remembered is a check that will be forgotten** — **the repair is to put `git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/integration` inside the push path rather than in a bug row.** — the repair is procedural, and the row exists so the procedure changes rather than the intention |
| **Commit found** | `8fa6a12c`, cycle 153, found by QE immediately after its own push |

**Steps.** During the same Closeout, in this order:

1. **QE rebased `integration` onto `main`, deliberately preserving `TASK-476`'s claim** — and wrote, in the commit message, that *"the claim would have been destroyed by the force-push QE had been proposing for seven cycles."*
2. **QE then committed a documentation correction to `main`** and ran its habitual three-command push block, whose third line is:

```
git push --force-with-lease=integration:785d3c67 origin main:integration
```

**Expected.** The claim survives.

**Actual.** ⛔ **`integration` was forced to `main`, which does not contain the claim.** **The lease was SATISFIED** — `integration` really was still at `785d3c67`, because **QE itself had just put it there.**

> 🔴 **This is the finding, and it is worth more than the incident.** **`--force-with-lease` protects against a *concurrent* modification by somebody else. It does not protect against destroying a commit you already knew about.** ⚡ **The lease answers *"has anyone else moved this ref?"* — it never answers *"will this push lose work?"***, and QE had been treating a satisfied lease as though it answered the second.
>
> ⚠️ **The habitual command was correct for seven cycles and became wrong the moment `integration` carried something `main` did not.** ⛔ **QE reasoned about exactly this hazard, in writing, and then ran the command anyway two minutes later** — **which is why the repair cannot be *"be careful"*.**

**What made it recoverable.** ✅ **The commit object survived** (`git cat-file -t 785d3c67`), so it was cherry-picked onto the new `main` and pushed as a **fast-forward**, and the restored claim was re-verified by **subject, file list and `TASK-476` appearing in both registers.**

**Repair.** ⚡ **Make the synchronization push refuse rather than depend on care**, which is this repository's standing preference — *operations that refuse unsafe states over operations that silently recover.* **Before any `main:integration` push, assert that `origin/integration` contains nothing `main` lacks:**

```
git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/integration     # must be 0, or rebase instead of push
```

⛔ **If it is not zero, the correct operation is §20e Closeout step 10's rebase, never a force-push** — **which is precisely what QE had done correctly ten minutes earlier.** ✅ **The check is one command and it distinguishes the two cases the lease cannot.**

### B-163 · the B-221 guard and the two-ref merge ship with no test, and the merge misresolves the one backward transition

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Platform Foundation — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — its own module, and its own fix |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⚡ **the fix is right and QE is not asking for it back.** ⛔ **But it is a guard against a defect that recurred three times, and nothing proves it still works tomorrow** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, under [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **`CHANGES REQUESTED` now ranks ABOVE `IN VALIDATION`** — the one transition §20e places *after* it. Ranked below, it resolved a returned slice back to `IN VALIDATION`, **hiding from the lane that it had to act.** 📁 **6 regression tests**, including the reverse cases so a stale return cannot override a later `VERIFIED` |
| **Commit found** | `de88facd`, found by QE during cycle 153 validation |

**① The guard has no test.** ⚡ **Measured, not asserted**: `de88facd` changes **63 lines of `infra/coordination.py` and zero lines of any test file.**

```
$ git diff --stat origin/main..de88facd -- backend/tests/ infra/
 infra/coordination.py | 76 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-----
```

[`test_repository_generators.py`](../backend/tests/certification/test_repository_generators.py) holds **10 tests**, and **none references `_notice` or `_integration_states`.** ⛔ **§11 is a hard rule** — *"no change ships without tests"* — and §2 is more specific: ***a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code.***

⚡ **Lane C's evidence that it fires is real and is not the same thing**: *"it fires on the live notice… it then refused my own correction notice."* ✅ **That proves it worked once, on one input, on one day.** ⛔ **A regression test is what proves it works after the next refactor** — **and B-221 recurred three times, which is the argument for the test rather than against it.**

> ⚠️ **QE could not prove it either.** `_notice('a', reachable=frozenset())` returns **empty** — there is no live Lane A notice to withhold — so the probe says nothing in either direction. **That is the finding, not an aside.**

**② `_LIFECYCLE` cannot represent the one transition that goes backward.** The merge resolves two refs by *"later wins"*:

```python
_LIFECYCLE = {..., "CHANGES REQUESTED": 3, "IN VALIDATION": 4, ...}
```

⛔ **`CHANGES REQUESTED` ranks BELOW `IN VALIDATION`, and [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §20e makes it the one state that FOLLOWS it** — *"QE, during validation. Something did not hold. Returned to the implementing lane."* **Every other transition is monotonic; this one is a return.**

**Measured on the shipped table:**

```
IN VALIDATION = 4 | CHANGES REQUESTED = 3

QE returned a slice: main=CHANGES REQUESTED, stale integration=IN VALIDATION
  merged  -> IN VALIDATION
  correct -> CHANGES REQUESTED
  ==> MISREPORTED
```

⛔ **A slice QE has returned would be reported as still waiting on QE**, and **the lane that must act would not see that it must act.** ⚠️ **It is reachable precisely in the divergence this function was written for** — `integration` is **38 behind `main`**, so the two refs disagreeing is the normal condition today, not an edge case.

> ✅ **The default is fail-safe and that is worth recording**: `reachable` defaults to `frozenset()`, so a caller that forgets to pass it **withholds every notice** rather than publishing an unchecked one. **That is the right direction** — the repository prefers operations that refuse over operations that silently recover.

**Suggested repair.** ⚡ **Both halves are small.** Give `CHANGES REQUESTED` a rank **above** `IN VALIDATION` — it is a later event in the lifecycle even though it is a return in the workflow — **and add the two cases to [`test_repository_generators.py`](../backend/tests/certification/test_repository_generators.py)**: a notice naming an unreachable row is withheld, and a notice naming a reachable one is published. ⛔ **The second case is the one that stops the guard from being tightened into something that withholds everything.**

### B-222 · `CLAUDE.md` §19 describes the Playwright default it was written to change, and the change has landed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **repository governance** — [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §19, *The headed-execution policy* |
| **Current assignee** | ⛔ **The product owner, and nobody else.** 📁 **§20e's shared-files table: `CLAUDE.md` is written by the product owner** — ⚡ **and the two edits Lane C has ever made to it were *directed rather than drafted*** ([D-170](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2, [D-195](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §8) |
| **Severity** | 🟢 **cosmetic — one clause of one note.** ⛔ **The POLICY the section states is now TRUE and was the point**; what is stale is the paragraph explaining why it was not yet |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **reported by Lane A, 2026-08-09, in the same change that made it stale.** ⛔ **Deliberately not fixed: `CLAUDE.md` is 🔴 and not this lane's** (§20e) |
| **Found** | 2026-08-09 by Lane A, delivering [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md) — ⚡ **by re-reading the sentence the row exists to make true, rather than by a check** |

**Steps to reproduce.** On this lane's branch:

```bash
grep -n "HEADED !== '1'" CLAUDE.md
→ 342: **`playwright.config.ts` reads `headless: process.env.HEADED !== '1'` —
       headless is today's default and `HEADED=1` opts in**

grep -n "headless:" frontend/playwright.config.ts
→ headless: !RUN_MODE.headed          # headed unless HEADLESS=1 or HEADED=0
```

**Expected.** ⚡ **The file describes the repository.**

**Actual.** ⛔ **Line 342 describes the repository as it was before [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md).** **`HEADED=1` no longer *opts in*; it selects the demonstration's pace, and headless is now the opt-*out*.**

### ⚡ Why this is worth a row rather than a shrug

📁 **§2: *"a document must not misdescribe reality"*** — ⛔ **and this is the one file every cold session reads first.** ⚠️ **The clause is also the repository's own worked example of the defect**, which is what makes leaving it wrong expensive: **§19 uses it to teach that a rule stated before its mechanism exists is a defect**, and a teaching example that is itself now false teaches the lesson backwards.

### ✅ The correction, written out so it costs one paste

**Line 342 currently ends:** *"The text is corrected here and the behaviour is [TASK-476](docs/BACKLOG.md); a rule stated before the mechanism exists is the defect this file warns about, so the row exists rather than the claim."*

**What is now true:** **`playwright.config.ts` reads `headless: !RUN_MODE.headed` — headed is the default, `HEADLESS=1` (or `HEADED=0`) opts out, and `HEADED=1` additionally slows the run to the demonstration's pace.** ✅ **[TASK-476](BACKLOG.md) closed the gap this note was recording; the rule and the repository agree.**

> ⚠️ **The lane that made the sentence stale is the lane reporting it, in the same change.** ⛔ **The alternative — landing the config and letting somebody discover the stale note later — is exactly [B-217](#b-217)'s and [B-154](#b-154)'s shape**, and it is cheaper to say so now than to be found.

### B-162 · the failed-read guard strips `//` inside string literals, so rendered copy on a line with a URL evades it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Product Surface — [`frontend/tests/components/stated-absence.test.tsx`](../frontend/tests/components/stated-absence.test.tsx) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — its own guard, changed in its own slice |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⚡ **the guard still fires on the common case, and Lane A proved that it does.** ⛔ **But it now misses a class it used to catch**, and the class is *rendered copy* rather than prose |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-09, at `9f35ad2f`. **Fixed by Lane A on the poll it was reported, and verified by measurement rather than by reading the diff**: **the exact case QE filed is now asserted `true` in the suite** — `<a href="https://x.test">{"Pipeline could not load"}</a>` — **the guard file's 8 tests pass, 2022 frontend tests pass, and the commit is certified and promoted.** ⚡ **The four new cases are assertions inside existing blocks, which is why the repository total is unchanged at 2022** *(checked, not assumed)*. ⛔ **The strip is now string-aware**: it walks the source tracking single quotes, double quotes, template literals and escapes, so a `//` inside a string is text and a `//` outside one is a comment. ✅ **Four cases added and each was measured failing first** — a URL beside rendered copy in JSX, a template literal followed by a trailing `// https://…`, a `//` inside a single-quoted string, and an escaped quote that must not end the string early. ⚡ **The lesson is the row's, not the regex's: narrowing a guard is only safe if you measure what STOPS firing.** **I measured that it still caught the common case and did not measure what it had let go.** *(Previously* **`OPEN`**.*)* |
| **Commit found** | `a512642b` (`TASK-1428`), found by QE during cycle 152 validation |

**Steps.** The guard strips comments before scanning, which is **correct and is not what this row disputes**:

```js
const code = (src) => src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '').replace(/\/\/.*$/gm, '');
```

⚠️ **`//` is not only a comment introducer. It occurs inside every absolute URL**, and the second replacement is not string-aware — it deletes from the first `//` to the end of the line, whatever that `//` was part of.

**Expected.** A surface that renders the sentence fails the guard, wherever else on the line it sits.

**Actual.** Measured, on the guard's own expression:

```
true   real code (must be TRUE)                  const t = "Pipeline could not load";
false  line comment (must be FALSE)              // no longer says could not load
false  block comment (must be FALSE)             /** explains could not load */
false  URL then sentence, SAME line              const u="https://a.com"; const t="could not load";
false  JSX href then sentence same line          <a href="https://x">could not load</a>
true   sentence BEFORE url same line             const t="could not load"; const u="https://a";
```

⛔ **Rows four and five are rendered copy and the guard says nothing.** **Row six passing is what makes it an ordering artefact rather than a general failure** — the sentence is invisible only when a `//` precedes it on the same line.

> ⚡ **The direction of the change is right and QE is not asking for it to be reverted.** [B-318](#b-318)'s class is real, a comment does not render, and **rewording the comment would indeed have left the guard reading prose.** ✅ **Lane A also did the thing §2 demands and the thing that made this row findable: it added a test proving the guard can still fire.** **That test is why the remaining hole is one line wide rather than unknown.**
>
> ⛔ **What it costs is narrow but real: this guard is the only thing standing between nine callers and a tenth local implementation**, and a JSX line carrying both an `href` and the sentence is not an exotic shape.

**Suggested repair, and it is smaller than the regex it replaces.** ⚡ **Strip only lines that are comments**, rather than trying to find comments inside lines:

```js
.replace(/^\s*(\/\/|\*|\/\*).*$/gm, '')
```

**A JSDoc block's continuation lines begin with `*`, and a trailing `// comment` after real code cannot hide a sentence that is already on that line.** ⚠️ **Whatever the repair, it belongs beside the existing proof case** — **the two negative halves must keep passing, and a third case should assert the URL line.**

### B-161 · the Task Claim Protocol's own step 7 pushes a lane's unpromoted implementation to `integration`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository process — [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) §20e, *The Task Claim Protocol*, step 7 |
| **Current assignee** | **Product owner** — §20e is theirs, and this is a governance defect rather than a code one |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **six code files reached `integration` without passing through QE**, and no gate refused them |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN` — and it is the same defect as [B-220](#b-220), which Lane A filed against itself on the poll that found it.** ⛔ **Two ids for one defect is what the identifier rule exists to prevent, so they are cross-linked rather than renumbered** *(the precedent is [B-152](#b-152) and [B-413](#b-413))*. ⚡ **Read [B-220](#b-220) for the mechanism — it is more precise than this row was.** **This row's *Steps* said `git merge --ff-only <lane-branch> && git push`, which is §20e step 7's literal form and has the same property.** **The command actually used was `git push origin lane-a-product-surface:integration`** — ⚡ *"the same command was correct one poll earlier, when the branch happened to be exactly the claim."* ✅ **Both routes push a branch where the protocol means a commit**, so the governance half of this row stands: **§20e step 7 as written carries whatever else is on the branch.** *(was: `OPEN`, unqualified)* |
| **Commit found** | `554dd74c` on `origin/integration`, found during cycle 146's promotion |

**Steps.** Hold an unpromoted slice on your lane branch. Claim the next task exactly as step 7 instructs:

```
git checkout integration && git merge --ff-only <lane-branch> && git push origin integration
```

**Expected.** ⚡ **The claim reaches `integration` and nothing else does.** §20e is explicit: *"a claim commit touches [`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) and [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) and nothing else"*, and *"code reaches `integration` by QE fast-forwarding a validated lane branch."*

**Actual.** **The fast-forward carries the whole branch.** `554dd74c` — `TASK-1409`, **six code files** including two new `components/ui` components — arrived on `integration` underneath the claim, along with two documentation commits. **The claim commit `227a074f` is itself perfectly bounded, and sits on top of them.**

> ⚡ **Nobody did anything wrong, and that is the finding.** **Lane A followed step 7 literally.** ⛔ **The two instructions are only compatible when the lane branch holds nothing else unpromoted** — and §20e's *Continuous execution* rule **guarantees it usually does**: *"the moment a lane sets `IN VALIDATION`, it returns to the backlog and claims the next `READY` task."* **The protocol that requires the claim and the rule that keeps work on the branch are in direct conflict.**

**What it cost this cycle — measured, not assumed.** ✅ **Nothing.** **QE had already rebased and certified the same two patches independently**, and `git patch-id --stable` confirms they are byte-equivalent:

```
integration 554dd74c → cbbab267…     main 6636e6ce → cbbab267…
integration 03a81b5d → b9cbb641…     main f954477e → b9cbb641…
```

⚡ **`promoted == certified` held, `--audit-main` is clean, and no uncertified code reached `main`.** ⚠️ **The cost was a non-fast-forward on `integration`**, resolved by the rebase Closeout step 10 already prescribes.

**Why no gate caught it.** `--audit-claims` reads commits *whose subject begins* `Claim TASK-`, and `554dd74c`'s does not. ⛔ **The check inspects the claim and never the commits the claim's own push brings with it.**

**Two shapes of fix, and the choice is the product owner's.** **Push only the claim commit** — `git push origin <claim-sha>:integration` — which is what *"a standalone commit, pushed to `integration`"* already means and never carries a parent that is not already there. **Or widen `--audit-claims` to check every commit a claim push introduces**, so the breach is refused rather than described. ⚡ **The first makes it unrepresentable; the second makes it detectable** (§2).

### B-160 · the coordination check cannot pass, because two of the numbers it compares change whenever any lane moves

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `infra/coordination.py` — `--check`, and the metrics `render()` bakes into the file |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — Platform Foundation ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **it reports *stale* about an accurate file**, which is the failure mode the tool's own docstring names |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Commit found** | `97a13cee` — measured on the promoted commit |

**Steps.** Regenerate and publish `coordination.toml`. Let any lane push a slice. Run `python3 infra/coordination.py --check`.

**Expected.** `current` — the file's *content* has not changed.

**Actual.** Exit 1, *"the published source does not match what the generator emits today."* **The whole difference, measured by rendering in-process and diffing `_content`:**

```
-awaiting_qe_transition = 0        +awaiting_qe_transition = 6
-lane_utilization   = 1.2          +lane_utilization   = 0.0
```

⚡ **Twelve diff lines, and every one of them is a metric.** ✅ **Every task, every backlog entry, every claimable count is identical.**

**Why it cannot be fixed by republishing.** `awaiting_qe_transition` counts rows stranded at `IN VALIDATION`, and `lane_utilization` derives from what lanes are working. ⛔ **Both change when *another* lane pushes, and Product Office is not involved** — so **the file goes stale through nobody's inaction**, and the only interval in which `--check` passes is between a regeneration and the next lane's push.

> ⚡ **Strengthened 2026-08-09 at `a68134d6`, and QE's original measurement understated it.** **A second occurrence was 66 changed lines, and every single one is an ELAPSED-TIME counter:**
>
> ```
>   60  blocked_days
>    4  blocked_duration_days
>    2  dependency_wait_days
> ```
>
> ⛔ **Zero task-level lines. Zero backlog entries. Zero claimable counts.** ⚠️ **These do not need another lane to push — they change with the WALL CLOCK, so the file goes stale while the repository is idle and nobody has done anything at all.**
>
> ⚡ **The generator's own docstring already names this exact failure and believes it fixed:** *"[it] read the wall clock and baked the result into the file, so the file drifted stale against its own `--check` roughly every 2.4 hours."* ⛔ **That repair covered `[meta]`'s timestamp** ([B-134](#b-134)) **and left three day-counters inside `_content` with the identical property.**
>
> ✅ **This makes the fix narrower and more obvious than the row first suggested**: the volatile set is **`blocked_days` · `blocked_duration_days` · `dependency_wait_days` · `awaiting_qe_transition` · `lane_utilization`**, and excluding them from `_content` — as `[meta]` already is — leaves a comparison that only changes when the *projection* changes.

> ⚠️ **[B-134](#b-134) is the same defect one field over, and its fix was half of one.** **That row removed `[meta]` from the comparison** — *"a check that reports stale about an accurate file teaches a reader to ignore it"* — ⛔ **and left inside `_content` two numbers with exactly the same property as the timestamp it excluded.**

**Why QE cares rather than filing it as tidiness.** ⛔ **QE spent four cycles reporting *"the coordination source is stale"* from this check**, and for three of those it was true and material ([B-159](#b-159)). ⚠️ **On the fourth it was metric drift, and nothing in the output distinguishes the two** — **so a real `claimable_now = 0` and a harmless `lane_utilization` delta print the same sentence.** ⚡ **That is the cost: the signal that found B-159 can no longer be trusted to mean it.**

**Two shapes of fix, and the choice is Lane C's.** **Exclude the volatile metrics from `_content`, as `[meta]` already is** — they are observations about the repository, not the projection's content — **or report *what* differs** so a reader can tell a task-level divergence from a metric recompute. ⛔ **Not written by QE**: `infra/coordination.py` is Lane C's, and this blocks no gate.

```

**Regenerating against the promoted commit yields `claimable_now = 22` and a 22-entry `backlog`.** ⚡ **QE verified this by rendering in-process and diffing `_content` — zero difference once regenerated, so the generator is correct and only the *published* file is behind.**

> ⛔ **This is [B-216](#b-216)'s class with the halves swapped, and it is the more dangerous orientation.** **There, prose asserted `READY` and the counters were right, so the counters caught it.** **Here the prose says *Build* and the counters say zero** — ⚠️ **and `_notice()` now *refuses* state words in prose, so the half a reader is told to trust is the half that is wrong.**

**Why it is 🟠 rather than 🟡.** ⚡ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) makes synchronization the highest repository priority when a lane idles on work that exists but has not reached it** — *"the cost is paid twice, once in the idle lane and once in the preparation that ages while it waits."* ✅ **Lane A has not idled on it**, because it reads `BACKLOG.md` too. ⛔ **But the source exists precisely so a lane need not.**

**Not repaired by QE, deliberately.** ⚡ **The repair is `python3 infra/coordination.py` followed by `--publish`, and both are Product Office's** — a projection republished by the lane that does not own it is a second author for a file whose whole guarantee is that it has one.

### B-158 · `coordination.py --dry-run` writes the file it is named for not writing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `infra/coordination.py` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — Platform Foundation ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — **it mutates the repository under a flag that promises it will not** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Commit found** | `7bc4b531` |

**Steps.** `python3 infra/coordination.py --dry-run`, then `git status`.

**Expected.** Nothing written. That is what the word means, and it is the one flag a reader reaches for when they want to look without touching.

**Actual.** `docs/coordination/coordination.toml` is rewritten. `main()` handles `--self-test`, then `--check` *(which returns)*, then falls through to an **unconditional** `OUT.write_text(fresh)` — and only *afterwards* consults `--publish`. ⛔ **`--dry-run` is documented as *"with `--publish`: validate only"* and is simply ignored on its own**, so the default write happens.

> ⚠️ **QE ran it, on a clean tree, while `make certify` was in flight** — ⛔ **and that half is QE's defect, not the tool's.** **An unfamiliar flag is read before it is run, especially during a certification**, which is the lesson [cycle 115](../PROJECT_STATUS.md) already recorded when QE edited `BUGS.md` mid-run. ✅ **Caught by `git status` and restored before the run sampled `tree_clean`** — **the record reads `tree_clean: true` and is true.** ⚡ **That was timing, not discipline, and it is recorded as timing.**

**Why it is worth a row rather than a habit.** ⚡ **The repository's own standard is *prefer operations that refuse unsafe states over operations that silently recover from them*.** ⛔ **A flag whose name is a promise of safety and whose behaviour is a write is the opposite**, and the next person to reach for it will be doing exactly what QE was doing — **trying to inspect without disturbing.**

**The fix is one branch**: `--dry-run` without `--publish` either prints the rendered source to stdout or exits with a message saying it does nothing on its own. ⛔ **Not written by QE** — `infra/coordination.py` is Lane C's, and this is not a gate that blocks certification.

### B-157 · `state-check` reads seven-hex commits and `git rev-parse --short` now returns eight, so a correct dashboard reports as stale

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository tooling — `infra/state-check.py`, `_newest_named_commit()` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — `state-check` is QE's Closeout instrument |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — **advisory only, and it fails toward noise rather than toward silence.** ⚠️ **But a noisy advisory is one somebody learns to skip**, which is how [B-153](#b-153) happened |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Commit found** | `a540f5ee` — found at this cycle's Closeout |

**Steps.** Write the dashboard's commit exactly as `git rev-parse --short main` prints it, then run `python3 infra/state-check.py`.

**Expected.** *"PROJECT_STATUS.md names `a540f5e`, reachable from `main`."*

**Actual.** *"PROJECT_STATUS.md names `2bf7450`, which predates the latest certification (a540f5e). The dashboard describes a repository that has since been certified at a later commit."* ⛔ **The dashboard was correct and current** — it named `a540f5ee` in five places.

**The mechanism, proven:**

```
git rev-parse --short main            →  a540f5ee     (eight)
re.findall(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7}\b", ...)   →  []
```

⚡ **`\b[0-9a-f]{7}\b` matches *exactly* seven: the trailing `\b` fails against an eighth hex character.** So the check skipped the current commit entirely and found the newest thing it *could* see — **the previous cycle's release summary, which is a dated record and is correctly not rewritten** (`CLAUDE.md` §2).

> ⚠️ **This will recur on every cycle from here, not occasionally.** **Git lengthens the abbreviation as the object count grows**, and this repository has crossed the threshold — so the *natural* way to write the commit is now the one the check cannot read.

**Why it is worth a row rather than a habit.** ⛔ **The workaround QE applied this cycle is to hand-write seven characters**, which makes the dashboard's correctness depend on a lane remembering to truncate. ⚡ **That is the [B-131](#b-131) shape** — a rule kept by discipline where a machine could keep it.

**The fix is the bound**, `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`, and `_is_ancestor` already validates every token it yields — **so a longer match is checked, not trusted.** ⛔ **Not written this cycle**: `state-check` gates Closeout, and changing a gate is a slice rather than a Closeout ([B-014](#b-014)).

> ⛔ **`auth.user` did not exist in `signora_lane_qe`.** The `auth` schema was there and empty, so **every sign-in timed out with no diagnostic** and the whole suite reported as an authentication failure. **QE's database was also five migrations behind head** (`0043` → `0048`), which the seeder found second.

> ⚠️ **Two earlier diagnoses of this were wrong, and both were QE's.** [B-178](#b-178) blamed a missing system library — withdrawn the same day. Before that it was recorded as *"NOT MEASURED BY QE"* for many cycles with no cause at all. **The cause was never in the suite, the browser, or the config.**
>
> **The sequence that works**, and every step uses the repository's own mechanism:
>
> ```
> SIGNORA_AUTH_DATABASE_URL=…/signora_lane_qe  npm run auth:migrate
> SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL=…/signora_lane_qe       uv run alembic upgrade head
> SIGNORA_AUTH_DATABASE_URL=…/signora_lane_qe  npm run demo:users
> SIGNORA_*_DATABASE_URL=…/signora_lane_qe     uv run python -m tests.playground.seed

>
> ✅ **`auth:migrate` refuses to guess a database or a secret, by name, twice** — *"guessing one would connect this tier to somebody else's environment."* **That is why this was never a silent failure, only an undiagnosed one.**
>
> ⛔ **What remains OPEN is this row's actual subject**: a journey run with no port still passes both URL guards. **The environment is fixed; the guard is not.**
>
> **[B-225](#b-225) reports that a shipped `@smoke` journey was red for a day and *"nothing said so, because nothing runs the journeys"*, and it names QE**: *"QE's cycle measurements name `make smoke` — 24 stages — and never a Playwright count."* ✅ **True, and QE accepts it.**
>
> ⛔ **QE then tried to run them and could not, for exactly this reason. Measured on `main` at `2b76ca56`:**
>
> ```
> $ python3 infra/environments.py --exports | head -1
> # no environment derived (not on a lane branch)
>
> Makefile:141  SIGNORA_WEB := $(shell ... sed -n 's/^SIGNORA_WEB_PORT=//p')  -> empty
> E2E_URL       http://localhost:$(SIGNORA_WEB)                               -> http://localhost
>
> $ HEADLESS=1 make e2e-quick ARGS="--grep @smoke"
> 3 failed - net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at http://localhost/sign-in   (~300ms each)
> ```
>
> 🔴 **The two rows are one gap seen from two ends.** **A lane can run the journeys because a lane branch derives a port; QE cannot, because QE works on `main` and `main` is not a lane.** ⛔ **So the one lane whose job is repository-wide validation is the one that cannot execute the repository's journey gate** — **and every QE cycle report has therefore been silent about it, which is what [B-225](#b-225) observed from the other side.**
>
> ⚡ **The repair is small**: derive a review-port pair for a non-lane checkout, **or** have `e2e` **refuse loudly when `SIGNORA_WEB` is empty** instead of building a portless URL. ⛔ **The second half matters more** — **a portless URL produced three ~300ms failures that read exactly like a product regression**, and this row exists because 157 of them were once nearly reported as findings.

**Steps.** Run `make e2e` from a checkout that is **not on a lane branch** — `main`, a detached HEAD, a review worktree.

**Expected.** The suite refuses, the way it already refuses an unset URL and a Human Review port.

**Actual.** **157 journeys fail in ~300ms each with `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at http://localhost/sign-in`** — and a session reading that list sees eleven suites red across authentication, workflows and commercial profile. ⛔ **It looks exactly like [B-209](#b-209) did.**

**The mechanism, proven rather than reasoned.** `Makefile:450` builds `E2E_URL ?= http://localhost:$(SIGNORA_WEB)`, and `infra/environments.py` prints `# no environment derived (not on a lane branch)` — **`SIGNORA_WEB` is empty, so the URL is `http://localhost`, with no port.** `resolveAppUrl()` then passes it through **both** of its guards:

```
new URL("http://localhost").port  ===  ""
REVIEW_PORTS.has("")              ===  false
```

⚡ **The URL *is* set, so the first guard is satisfied. The port is not 3000 or 8000, so the second is — because there is no port at all.** The run proceeds against port 80, which belongs to nobody.

> ⚠️ **The two guards that exist were both written from real incidents** ([B-408](#b-408)) and both are correct. **This is the third case neither was asked about**, and it is the one that produces a *verdict* rather than a refusal.

**Why it is 🟠 and not 🟡.** ⛔ **An abort that reports itself as 157 failures is a false lead pointed at whichever lane last touched the frontend.** QE caught it here only because every test failed in 300ms and the URL in the error had no colon in it — **a slower machine or a partial failure would not have been so obvious.**

**The fix is one condition, and it belongs beside the two that are already there:** an empty port is refused with the same message that names `docs/RUNNING.md`. ⛔ **QE has not written it in this cycle** — the promotion was already complete and a gate change is a slice, not a Closeout ([B-014](#b-014)).

**What this cycle can and cannot claim.** ⛔ **The journey suite was not run at `a540f5ee`.** Two attempts, both **aborted on environment**: this one, then `ConnectionRefused` on `5632` because QE holds no lane dev stack. **Neither is a statement about the commit.** ⚡ **Playwright is inside the gate shortfall [B-131](#b-131) prints on every run**, so certification neither ran it nor claimed to. **Lane A reports the journey walked headed and passing — recorded as the lane's claim, which is what it is.**

| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-09.** **`on_integration` becomes a FILTER rather than a preference.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **Filed by QE. Re-reported by Lane A on 2026-08-09** — ⚡ **which had said the previous poll that it would report it *if it survived a republication*. It did.** ⛔ **This office republished twice in between and did not check** |
| **Steps** | **Release a row on `lane-c-sync`, let the owning lane set it `BLOCKED` on `integration`, regenerate** |
| **Expected** | **`current` names a row the lane can claim** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`current = "TASK-470"` with `claimable = 1`, while `origin/integration` carried TASK-470 as `BLOCKED` — Lane A had released the claim and this office's branch still read `READY`** |

## ⚡ A preference is not a constraint

📁 **The sort already knew**: `key=lambda r: (not r.on_integration, …)` — ⛔ **it merely PREFERRED an on-integration row, and with none available it named an off-integration one anyway.**

> ## 🔴 **That is [C-425](LANE_COORDINATION.md) exactly, and this office wrote the ruling: *"the ref does not get to be ahead; it gets to be fast."*** ⛔ **The `on_integration` field was added to prevent this and was wired as a tiebreak.**

✅ **Now a filter.** **`current` is empty when nothing is claimable on `integration`.** ⚡ **And the pairing is deliberately kept: an empty `current` beside `claimable = 1` says the true thing — *work exists and QE has not integrated it* — where a stale `current` said the false one.**

⚠️ **Lane A's own note is the finding worth keeping**: ***"the projection is half-right: `claimable_now = 0` does report the truth alongside the stale `current`."*** ⛔ **A source that contradicts itself is worse than one that is simply wrong, because a reader can believe either half.**

| **[TASK-1429](BACKLOG.md)** | ⛔ absent | ⛔ absent | ⛔ absent |
| **[TASK-1431](BACKLOG.md)** | ⛔ absent | ⛔ absent | ⛔ absent |

**All three exist on `lane-c-sync` and nowhere a lane may claim from.** ⚡ **The array is right every time and the prose is wrong every time**, which is what makes this a generator defect rather than three authoring slips: **`backlog` is computed from what is synchronized; `notice` is written from what the office has authored.**

🔴 **The cost is not confusion — it is a lane being told it has work when it does not.** 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) calls that condition the most expensive state the repository can be in** — *"the cost is paid twice, once in the idle lane and once in the preparation that ages while it waits"* — ⛔ **and a notice asserting the opposite is what stops it being visible.**
