### B-138 · One test annotation fails `mypy --strict`, and it is holding sixteen commits and Lane A's whole queue

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Platform Foundation — [`backend/tests/test_coordination_source.py`](../backend/tests/test_coordination_source.py) line 167 |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · ⛔ **Blocking Quality Defect class** — `mypy --strict` is a certification gate, so nothing on this branch can be certified |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07.** **`-> Any`, exactly as QE confirmed in its scratch copy.** ⚡ **`coordination` is loaded through `importlib`, so it is a `ModuleType`: attribute access on it is `Any` and fine, while an *annotation* is a name lookup and fails** — which is why one line of the file was red and none of the others. ✅ **Verified here, not assumed: `mypy --strict` over 811 source files, `Success: no issues found` — the same 811 QE counted.** ✅ **`lint-imports` 37 kept, 0 broken.** ⛔ **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| ⛔ **The lesson, and it cost two returns** | ⚠️ **This lane's stated constraint was *never run gates*, and the real constraint is narrower: `clean_database` is autouse and truncates every table, so the *backend suite* stays with QE.** ⚡ **`mypy --strict` and `lint-imports` need no database, no stack and no port — 40 seconds, and this one named the file, the line and the symbol.** ⛔ **Treating a specific prohibition as a general one is how a lane hands QE a branch it could have checked itself**, and QE said so plainly: *"that constraint does not apply to `mypy --strict`."* ✅ **Both now run before every push from this lane** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by QE, cycle 89, cheap gates before certification |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
cd backend && uv run mypy --strict .
→ tests/test_coordination_source.py:167: error: Name "coordination.Task" is not defined  [name-defined]
  Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 811 source files)
```

**Expected.** Clean, as it is on `integration`.

**Actual.** One error. **`coordination` is loaded at runtime by `importlib`, so mypy has no static symbol for it.** Every *other* use in the file is an attribute access on a `ModuleType` — `Any`, and fine. **Line 167 is the only place the module is used in an annotation:**

```python
def row(task_id: str, unblocks: list[str]) -> coordination.Task:
```

**The fix is one word.** QE confirmed it in a scratch copy and restored the file: annotating the helper `-> Any` gives *"Success: no issues found in 811 source files"*. **Any equivalent works** — the constraint is only that a dynamically-loaded module cannot name a type.

### ⚡ Everything else on the branch is genuinely fixed, and QE checked rather than assumed

| | |
|---|---|
| [B-136](#b-136--the-worker-crash-loops-in-every-non-local-environment-because-the-composition-root-now-calls-a-guard-nothing-satisfies) | ✅ `SIGNORA_PROVIDERS: ""` in `docker-compose.prod.yml` |
| [B-134](#b-134--coordinationpy---check-can-never-pass-because-it-compares-a-file-against-its-own-commit-stamp) | ✅ **`--check` returns `0` on a detached checkout of the branch tip** — the exact steady state where it failed every time before |
| [B-135](#b-135--285-lines-of-new-governance-tooling-ship-with-no-tests) | ✅ 180 lines of tests, **38 passing**, and `import-linter` 37 kept / 0 broken |

**Three findings closed, one gate left red.** ⛔ **This is the second consecutive return of the same branch, and both blockers were `mypy --strict`-class or `smoke`-class — neither needs the backend suite.**

### The pattern is worth more than the fix

**Lane C's stated constraint is that the backend suite truncates the demo stack's database on this workstation, so the suite stays with QE.** ⚡ **That constraint does not apply to `mypy --strict`.** It touches no database, no Docker stack and no port; it took **40 seconds** here and named the file, the line and the symbol.

> **Both returns of this branch would have been caught before the push by a gate the lane can already run.**

### ⚠️ What the return costs, stated rather than left implicit

**Lane A cannot claim anything.** `origin/coordination` names `TASK-478` as its `current` — and **`git show origin/integration:docs/BACKLOG.md | grep -c TASK-478` returns `0`.** The row exists only on `lane-c-sync`.

**That is `CLAUDE.md` §20e's own sentence arriving in practice** — *"a `TASK-nnn` existing only on a lane branch is invisible to every lane"* — and [`state-check`](../infra/state-check.py) says the same thing from the other side: *"`origin/coordination` is published and `CLAUDE.md` on `integration` does not yet carry the poll that makes it binding, so the ref is advisory and `integration` remains the authority."*

⛔ **QE did not weigh that against the gate.** A failing gate excludes the slice and no other lane is held for it (`CLAUDE.md` §20e); **making a lane's gate pass is the one thing *QE removes its own blockers* explicitly does not license.** The cost is recorded here because it is real, not because it changes the answer.

### B-137 · `state-check` read the last certification *attempt* and called it the last certification

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | QE tooling — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — *"a defect in a gate that stops QE certifying is QE's to fix"* (`CLAUDE.md` §20e) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — **the instrument reported the inverse of the truth**, on the one line a cold session reasons from |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED`** by QE, 2026-08-07, with five regression tests and a mutation check. **`VERIFIED` after promotion** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by QE, cycle 87, by reading `state-check`'s output after a certification that failed |

**Steps to reproduce.** Run `make certify` on a commit whose `smoke` gate fails, then:

```bash
python3 infra/state-check.py
→ · `4d37ede` is certified and is NOT on `main` (ace4460). The cycle stopped
    after certification: promotion, Closeout, synchronization and Repository
    Ready have not run.
  · PROJECT_STATUS.md names `9ba145f`, which predates the latest certification
    (4d37ede).
```

**Expected.** `4d37ede` did not certify — its `smoke` gate is recorded `passed: false`. The repository's certification state is still `9ba145f`, which **is** on `main`.

**Actual.** Both findings above, and both false. **The cycle stopped *at* certification, not after it** — which is the opposite diagnosis, and it points a session at the promotion step instead of at the failing gate.

### The cause is one line, and the reason it survived is the interesting part

```python
runs = json.loads(manifest.read_text()).get("runs") or []
return runs[-1] if runs else None          # ← the last *attempt*
```

⚡ **The manifest deliberately records failures.** *"A failure is a statement about the commit; an abort is a statement about the run"* — a failed attempt is evidence and is never deleted, because §2 forbids rewriting a record of what was true then. **So the last entry is routinely a run that did not certify**, and every finding derived from it inherits that.

**It had been correct for eighty-six cycles** for one reason: every previous cycle's last manifest entry happened to be a passing one. **The first cycle to end in a failed gate is the first cycle where the reading is wrong** — and it is exactly the cycle where somebody most needs the reading.

### ⛔ `certification-guard.py` was right throughout

```
$ python3 infra/certification-guard.py 4d37ede0…
REFUSED — 4d37ede has a certification record, and it did not pass.
  · gate 'smoke' failed
```

**The promotion path never wavered.** Only the advisory view inverted — ⚡ **and that is the more dangerous half to get wrong.** A refusal is read once, at the moment it fires. **An advisory is what a session reasons from**, and this one would have told a cold session that a failed commit was certified and merely unpromoted.

### The fix

`_latest_certification()` now walks backwards to the newest run that **satisfied** — and borrows the predicate from `certification-guard.py` rather than re-deriving it, because **a second copy of *"did this run certify?"* is a second answer, and only one of them gates a promotion** (§2).

**Five regression tests**, [`backend/tests/test_certification_state_reading.py`](../backend/tests/test_certification_state_reading.py), on constructed manifests — the live one would pass identically with the fix reverted. **Mutation-checked**: restoring `runs[-1]` fails three of them, including *no passing run is no certification, not the last failure*.

⚠️ **One trap on the way, worth recording** because it costs an hour if it is not: the guard declares `@dataclass(slots=True)`, which resolves its own annotations through `sys.modules[cls.__module__]` **while the class body runs**. Loading it by path without registering it in `sys.modules` **first** raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'` several frames from anything naming the cause.

### B-136 · The worker crash-loops in every non-local environment, because the composition root now calls a guard nothing satisfies

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Platform Foundation — [`backend/apps/worker/main.py`](../backend/apps/worker/main.py), [`infra/docker-compose.prod.yml`](../infra/docker-compose.prod.yml) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — it authored TASK-419, and `infra/**` is its remit ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · ⛔ **Blocking Quality Defect class** — `make smoke` fails at Startup, so **nothing can be certified while it stands** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07.** **One line, and the guard is untouched**: `SIGNORA_PROVIDERS: ""` beside `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` in the `x-backend-env` anchor, so it merges into `api`, `worker` and `relay` together — **verified by resolving the YAML and reading all three.** ⚡ **Placed there rather than on `worker` because the two lines are one statement**: declaring an environment production without declaring what it may serve is half of it, and the worker crash-looped on the other half. ✅ **Proven, not inferred** — with `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT=production-local` and `SIGNORA_PROVIDERS=""` the registry builds; **without it the guard still raises**, checked in the same run. ⛔ **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by QE, cycle 87, by `make certify` |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
make smoke
→ 2. Startup
    ✗ worker is 'restarting', expected running
  SMOKE FAILED at: 2. Startup    (3 stages in 26s)
```

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env.prod-local -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs worker
→ File "/app/apps/worker/main.py", line 155, in startup
      provider_registry=build_data_provider_registry(ProviderSettings()),
  ProviderRegistrationError: simulated provider adapters were selected in
  environment 'production-local'. … set SIGNORA_PROVIDERS to an empty value
  to run without ingestion.
```

**Expected.** The worker starts. `smoke` runs its 24 stages.

**Actual.** The worker crash-loops. `smoke` stops at stage 2 of 24.

### ⚡ The guard is right. The slice made it reachable without giving anything a way to satisfy it

**Nothing here is wrong except the arithmetic of two defaults**, and both are defensible on their own:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| `ProviderSettings.providers` | `tuple(ProviderName)` | **Every provider**, because *"a process that recognises a provider architecturally and cannot serve it is half-configured"* |
| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT: production-local` | Correct — it is the production-image stack |
| `build_provider_registry` | refuses `providers and environment != "local"` | ⚡ **Correct, and deliberately fail-fast**: *"a service running on them would fabricate every score and signal built on top"* |

**The guard has existed and been right for some time. `36cbcb7d` is the first commit that *calls* it from a deployed process** — ADR-0404 capability 3 — **and no non-local environment sets `SIGNORA_PROVIDERS`.** So the first environment to reach the new code is the one that cannot satisfy it.

**The fix is one line in the environment, not in the guard**, and the error message already names it: `SIGNORA_PROVIDERS: ""` in [`infra/docker-compose.prod.yml`](../infra/docker-compose.prod.yml). ⛔ **Do not relax the guard** — §2 and the guard's own docstring: *"it is the one guard here that may never fail open."*

### Three cycles, three defects `make validate` structurally cannot see

⚡ **This is the third consecutive cycle where the only gate that caught the defect was one certification runs and `validate` does not.**

| Cycle | Row | Caught by | Why `validate` was blind |
|---|---|---|---|
| 84 | [B-132](#b-132--task-439-widened-the-signalrepository-protocol-and-left-the-fake-behind) | `mypy --strict` | `pytest` is green — Python does not enforce `Protocol` at runtime |
| 82 | [B-133](#b-133--task-445-left-an-unused-import-and-the-production-image-build-is-what-refused-it) | `next build`'s ESLint, inside `smoke` | An unused import is valid TypeScript |
| **87** | **B-136** | **`smoke`'s Startup, on the production images** | ⚡ **`validate` never builds or starts the production stack.** A composition root that cannot start is invisible to a test suite that never composes it |

**All three are [B-131](#b-131--the-validation-planner-requires-sixteen-gates-the-certification-record-contains-six) in the concrete.** The Validation Planner named `smoke` and `runtime-composition` for this change; **`runtime-composition` still leaves no trace in the certification record**, and a lane running the planner's own list before handover catches this in four minutes rather than at certification.

### B-134 · `coordination.py --check` can never pass, because it compares a file against its own commit stamp

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Platform Foundation — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py), [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — Platform Foundation is Lane C's ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), and it authored both |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — **wrong behaviour, and it is a governance instrument reporting a condition that is not true.** ⛔ **Not a Blocking Quality Defect**: `state-check.py` reports rather than fails, so no gate is held |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07.** **Two changes, and the diagnosis was exactly right.** ⚡ **`generated_from` now stamps `origin/integration`, which is what [479](architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md) §2 specified all along** — *"the integration commit the projection was taken at"* — **and I implemented `HEAD`.** ✅ **`--check` compares content and not `[meta]`**, so provenance can never read as staleness. ⚡ **Demonstrated the way it failed**: regenerate, commit, re-run — **exit 0 after the commit**, the condition it could never survive. ⛔ **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by QE, cycle 87, validating Lane C's nine commits |

**Steps to reproduce.** On the branch that introduced the check — no rebase, no edit, nothing stale:

```bash
git switch --detach origin/lane-c-sync     # a042b66c, "Regenerate the coordination source…"
python3 infra/coordination.py --check
→ coordination: the published source does not match what the generator emits
  today — regenerate it.
  exit 1
```

**Expected.** Exit `0`. The file was regenerated in the tip commit; the commit is *titled* for having done it.

**Actual.** Exit `1`, and the whole difference is one line:

```diff
-generated_from = "c7f648f"
+generated_from = "6f816ab"
```

### The cause

`render()` stamps the **running** `HEAD` into the file:

```python
f'generated_from = "{_git("rev-parse", "--short=7", "HEAD") or "unknown"}"',
```

and `--check` compares the **whole file**, stamp included:

```python
if OUT.read_text() != fresh:
```

**A generated file can never contain the SHA of the commit that contains it** — the SHA is not known until after the file is written. So the stamp is always one commit behind by construction, and **any rebase changes it again**. The check therefore fails on the commit that generates the file, on every commit after it, and on every rebased copy of both.

**It has never returned `0`. Not once, on any branch, including its own.**

### Why it matters more than a nuisance

[479](architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md) makes this file the one thing every lane polls, and `state-check.py` now calls `--check` on **every run**:

```python
findings.extend(_coordination_findings())
```

So `state-check` acquires a permanent false finding. **That is the same family as a guard that cannot fail** (`CLAUDE.md` §2) **wearing the opposite coat: a guard that cannot pass.** Both end in the same place — a signal nobody reads. ⚠️ **QE wrote [§0a-2](QUALITY_ENGINEERING.md) this week precisely because it stopped reading `state-check`'s output past the first few lines**, and a check that fires every time is how that habit is taught.

### The fix, and it is one line

**Compare the content that is *generated*, not the provenance of the run that generated it** — the ordinary shape for any build stamp. Exclude the `generated_from` line from the equality test, or move it out of the compared body.

⚡ **[B-135](#b-135--285-lines-of-new-governance-tooling-ship-with-no-tests) is why nobody saw it.** One test — *generate, then `--check`, and expect `0`* — fails on the first run.

| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |

**Expected.** `CLAUDE.md` §11: *"No change ships without tests. This is a hard rule, not a judgment call left to convenience or time pressure."*

### The repository's own pattern was already there to copy

[`backend/tests/test_claim_agreement.py`](../backend/tests/test_claim_agreement.py) loads `infra/state-check.py` **by path**, because its filename is not a Python identifier, and unit-tests its finding functions directly:

```python
def _load_state_check() -> ModuleType:
    """Import `infra/state-check.py`, whose filename is not a Python identifier."""
```

**Nineteen of the twenty-three `infra/*.py` tools are referenced by a test. `coordination.py` is not**, and the two new `state-check.py` checks are the first additions to that file to arrive without one.

### ⚡ No coverage gate can see this

`pytest --cov` measures `backend/`. **`infra/` is tooling, so a gap there is invisible to the floor** — which is why the rule is §11 rather than a percentage, and why this row exists rather than a failing gate.

**Neither `_coordination_findings` nor `_duplicate_index_findings` is exercised.** The first is [B-134](#b-134--coordinationpy---check-can-never-pass-because-it-compares-a-file-against-its-own-commit-stamp).

### B-425 · Lane A's queue answered "may I claim this?" twice, and named four blockers no tool could see

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Platform Foundation** — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py), [`docs/coordination/queues/lane-a.toml`](coordination/queues/lane-a.toml) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** *(Platform Foundation, [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md))* |
| **Severity** | 🟠 **wrong behaviour a lane would hit** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10.** Awaiting QE verification |
| **Commit found** | `f38882e8` |
| 🔴 **Found by** | ⛔ **The product owner asking *"why did Lane A go idle?"*** — ✅ **it had not.** ⚡ **But the question sent this office into its own queue file, which is where the defects were** |

#### Three defects, one file, all in the half that is hand-written

📁 **[B-423](#b-423) made the `backlog` array DERIVED from `BACKLOG.md`. The `[[blocked]]` entries stay hand-written and that is correct — they carry reasoning no other file holds.** ⛔ **What was missing is anything comparing the two halves.**

| # | Defect | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | ⛔ **Four `[[blocked]]` entries lost their header and `task` key**, becoming **top-level TOML tables** — `["C-1413"]`, `["TASK-1442"]`, `["an ADR — signora_platform/ is frozen"]`, `["TASK-464"]` | ✅ **The file still PARSED**, which is why nothing caught it. **Anything reading `blocked` saw 12 entries where 16 existed** |
| **2** | ⛔ **`TASK-1432` appeared twice** with two generations of contradictory blocker text | ✅ Both parsed; the older one had been superseded and never removed |
| **3** | 🔴 **Five rows were `backlog` (claimable) and `[[blocked]]` at once** — `TASK-412` · `TASK-465` · `TASK-1430` · `TASK-1433` · `TASK-1445` | ⚡ **Every one of the five blockers was ALREADY DISCHARGED**: `TASK-464`, `TASK-1439`, `TASK-1442`, `TASK-1448` all `PROMOTED` 2026-08-10; `ADR-0408` accepted; `C-1413` closed |

#### ⚠️ The direction of the error is the part worth recording

⛔ **This office over-reported blockers, never under-reported them.** ⚡ **Not one of the five was real.** **A lane consulting the prose would have skipped work it was free to do** — and the stale answer is the convincing one, **because it carries a reason and the derived array does not.**

#### The fix

✅ **`_queue_contradictions()`** in [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py) compares the derived half against the written half at publish time and **prints, never repairs** — which of the two is wrong is a judgement about the work, [`state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py)'s rule for the same reason.

⚡ **Fire-tested live rather than afterwards**: it fired five times, and went silent one contradiction at a time as each was resolved. ✅ **Four orphans repaired, one duplicate and six stale entries removed; `lane-c.toml` audited and clean.**

#### ⛔ What it does NOT catch, stated rather than implied

⛔ **A `[[blocked]]` entry naming a blocker that is stale but NOT in the claimable array is still invisible.** ⚡ **The derived array is the only signal this check has**, and a genuinely-blocked row has no derived counterpart to disagree with. **Named as a limitation, not left to be discovered.**

The panel/rail contrast is real and is no longer evidence of a defect.**

##### The withdrawn argument, as written

📁 **The panel does exactly what the rail fails to do.** ⚡ **`PANEL_WIDTH[bandFor(width)]` is a four-band map read from the viewport; `RAIL_WIDTH` is a two-value pair read from a stored preference.** ⛔ **Two adjacent components in one shell, one band-driven and correct, one preference-driven and non-compliant** — and the second is the one every screen renders.

🔴 **The customer-visible consequence: on a 1024–1279 laptop a person who has never touched the collapse control sees a 232px rail where the design gives 56px of icons, taking 176px from a content region that band already constrains most.**

### B-434 · 🟡 `state-check` asks a coordination row to name a lane, which is the thing C-213 forbids it to name

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Repository tooling** — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py):1349 |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — 📁 [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s clarification: *a defect in a gate is QE's, unchanged* |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **wrong but survivable, and it is survivable only because nobody has acted on it.** 🔴 **The obvious remediation is the harmful one**: naming a lane in the `Owner` cell is exactly what [C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md) cost two days |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C**, 2026-08-13, on QE's advisory naming [C-289](LANE_COORDINATION.md) and [C-292](LANE_COORDINATION.md) |
| **Found** | **`06ac0d5d`**, checking two rows before "fixing" them |

**Steps.** Write a coordination row whose `Owner` names a **module** and leaves the assignee to be joined — the form [C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md) and [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) require. Run `python3 infra/state-check.py`.

**Expected.** The row passes: its owner is resolvable, by the join every other view uses.

**Actual.** ⛔ ***"`C-289`'s `Owner` names no lane, QE or the product owner. An owner a reader cannot route to is an absent owner."***

✅ **Both rows are correct as written, verified rather than assumed:** 📁 **[C-289](LANE_COORDINATION.md) — *"`knowledge_graph`'s current assignee — joined from `modules.toml`, ⛔ not named here (C-213)"*** · **[C-292](LANE_COORDINATION.md), the same form for `signal_engine`.** ✅ **`modules.toml` gives both `current_owner = "Lane A"`.** ⚡ **So the owner IS routable; the checker reads the wrong side of the join.**

🔴 **The predicate is `actor.search(owner)` at :1349** — a literal match for a lane, QE or the product owner **in the cell itself**. 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) requires the opposite: *"no document restates an assignee, and a coordination item names its MODULE; the assignee is joined at render time."***

⚠️ **Why 🟡 and not 🟢.** ⛔ **A false positive that names a specific row invites the fix that satisfies it**, and here that fix is **writing a lane name into the cell** — 📁 **which is how [C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md) made *"the lane that could act would not and the lane named could not"*, blocking TASK-205 for two days.** ⚡ **The check would go green and the repository would be one edit further from the rule it exists to protect.**

✅ **The fix is a join, not a wider regex:** resolve a `Module`-form owner through [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) and report only when *that* fails.

### B-433 · 🟠 A row naming two modules is counted claimable and then left out of the lane's queue, so it is executable and invisible at once

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — `platform_foundation` moved to Lane A at [D-230](DECISION_REGISTER.md) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the generator withholds executable work from the lane that owns it, while reporting the same row as available in its own summary.** ⚠️ **Not 🔴: `BACKLOG.md` still shows it and [`state-check`](../infra/state-check.py) reports it, so nothing is lost — but [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 3 sends a lane to its queue FIRST, and [D-234](DECISION_REGISTER.md) made that the constitution's wording** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C**, 2026-08-13, found on the sequenced-row sweep |
| **Found** | **`0c79753f`**, releasing [TASK-1419](BACKLOG.md) |

> 🔴 **CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-13 BY LANE A, AND THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS BELOW WAS WRONG.** ⛔ **This row said the `Module` cell naming two modules was the cause. It is a coincidence.** ✅ **Verified in the code before accepting the correction** — 📁 [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py): **`claimable = [r for r in mine if r.state == ASSIGNED]`** against **`claimable_now = [r for r in claimable if r.on_integration]`**.
>
> ⚡ **Two expressions, and only one carries the `on_integration` guard.** **[TASK-1419](BACKLOG.md) was `READY` in a working copy and `SEQUENCED` on `integration`, so the array withheld it CORRECTLY and the summary counted it anyway.** ⛔ **[TASK-1477](BACKLOG.md) is emitted because it is synchronized, not because it names one module.**
>
> 🔴 **And the obvious fix is the dangerous one.** **Making the array emit the row — which is how this row read — publishes unsynchronized work to every lane**, which is precisely what the guard prevents and is [C-422](LANE_COORDINATION.md) exactly. ✅ **Lane A moved the COUNT to the array, never the array to the count**, and extracted `supply_line` so the difference is publishable: *"9 claimable of 48 assigned, 1 authored and NOT on integration."* ⚡ **That difference is the Synchronization Queue [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already asks this office to publish every cycle.**
>
> ⛔ **The *"third distinct way a READY row is unreachable"* claim below is WITHDRAWN.** **The row was genuinely unclaimable from `integration` and the ref was right to withhold it.** ⚠️ **What was broken was the report, which made a correct withholding look like a drop** — **a different defect, and a smaller one.**
>
> 📁 **Left standing rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): the original is what this office measured and believed, and the correction is what the code says.

**Steps.** *(as originally written — the reproduction is real; the inference from it was not.)* Release a `SEQUENCED` row whose `Module` cell names **two** modules — [TASK-1419](BACKLOG.md) reads **`action_batch` + `product_surface`**. Run `python3 infra/coordination.py`.

**Expected.** The row appears in `queues/lane-a.toml`'s `backlog`, as a single-module row does.

**Actual.** ⛔ **The summary counts it — *"Lane A: 10 claimable"* — and the emitted array holds 9 and does not name it.** 📁 **`state-check` then reports *"TASK-1419 is READY and appears in no lane queue"*, correctly.**

⚠️ **ORIGINAL INFERENCE, WRONG, kept for the record:** *"Isolated by comparison: TASK-1477, single-module, IS emitted."* ⛔ **The comparison held and the variable was misidentified — TASK-1477 differed in synchronization, not in module count, and this office varied one thing and read another.**

⚡ **What survives from it, and is worth keeping:** **adding the id to the array by hand does not hold — the generator overwrites it**, which is right for a generated file and is why the defect was in the generator rather than in the queue.

### B-432 · 🟠 The coordination register has more resolution vocabulary than any reader knows, and a sweep that knows two words reports a queue twice its size

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Repository-wide** — [`LANE_COORDINATION.md`](LANE_COORDINATION.md) · [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) · any tool that counts open items |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — the register's triage is this office's |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **wrong behaviour a reader acts on**: it decides how large the product owner's queue appears |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C**, 2026-08-12, on correcting its own report |
| **Found** | **By a figure disagreeing with itself twice in one day** |

#### 🔴 The measurement, isolated one variable at a time

| Sweep | PO items reading live |
|---|---|
| `Status` cell only, terminal = `CLOSED` · `READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` | **63** |
| **+ also read the `State` cell** | ⛔ **63 — no change whatsoever** |
| **+ full terminal vocabulary instead** | ✅ **33** |
| Both | ✅ **29** |

⚡ **The dominant cause is the VOCABULARY, not the schema.** 📁 **The register resolves items with at least nine words — `CLOSED` · `RULED` · `READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` · `REVIEW LATER` · `DEFERRED` · `RESOLVED` · `ANSWERED` · `WITHDRAWN` · `SUPERSEDED` — and a reader knowing two of them reports 63 where 29 are live.**

⛔ **The `State`-versus-`Status` schema gap accounts for 4 items and, on its own, for NONE** — it only helps once the vocabulary is complete, because the items carrying a `State` cell hold `RULED` and `REVIEW LATER`, which the short list misses anyway.

#### ⚠️ This office reported the wrong cause, twice, before measuring it

🔴 **On 2026-08-11 it told the product owner and QE that *"81 PO-owned items carry their ruling in a `State` cell and I counted every one as unanswered."*** ⛔ **That is false.** ✅ **81 is the number RESOLVED by any means; the schema hid 4 of them.** ⚡ **QE was additionally told to re-check its own figures *"for the same reason"* — pointing a second lane at the wrong cause.**

📁 **The 29 was right both times. The explanation was not**, and an explanation is what another lane acts on.

#### ✅ What a fix looks like

⚡ **Publish the terminal vocabulary once, where a tool can read it** — ⛔ **not in prose, and not re-derived by each reader.** 📁 **`state-check.py` already names the five ownership/state SCHEMAS in its own warning text; the resolution VALUES have no such list.**

⚠️ **Adding a word to the register without adding it there makes every counter wrong silently** — 🔴 **which is what happened, and the register gains vocabulary naturally as the product owner rules in their own words.**

> **Measured across all 198 backlog rows:**
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | Rows with an `Epic` cell | **86 of 198** |
> | Rows carrying a derivable **`[workflow N]`** link | 🔴 **51** |
> | ⛔ **Rows from which no workflow can be derived** | 🔴 **147** |
>
> ⚡ **And the `Epic` label is free text with no controlled vocabulary.** 📁 **Workflow 13 is named *Application Shell*; the rows that belong to it say *"Common Platform Foundation — App Shell"*, *"App Shell — workflow 29"*, *"Common Platform Foundation"*.** ⛔ **A name match finds ONE row. The seven App Shell rows this bug was opened over are invisible to every mechanical link.**
>
> 🔴 **So `workflows.toml`'s `tasks` array is a hand-maintained copy of a relationship the repository does not otherwise express** — 📁 **[OPERATING-MODE §5h](coordination/lane-c/OPERATING-MODE.md), and QE's corollary applies exactly: the defence is DERIVATION, never detection.** ⛔ **Here derivation is impossible, because the source data does not exist in 147 rows.**
>
> ⚠️ **This reframes what the register can answer.** **The repeated question — *how many workflows are pending* — has been answered from this registry twice, and the answer rests on a list nothing can check.** ✅ **The four `planned`-but-spent workflows found on 2026-08-13 were found by resolving ids BY HAND, which is the only method that works and does not scale.**
>
> ### ⚖️ Two repairs, and neither is a sweep
>
> | | | |
> |---|---|---|
> | **A** | **Give every row a `Workflow` cell**, or require the `[workflow N]` link in `Epic` | ✅ **Makes the link derivable and the registry checkable.** ⛔ **147 rows to touch, and it is scope on the product owner's own register** |
> | **B** | ⛔ **TESTED AND IT FAILS. Derive workflow membership from the DESIGN each row names.** ✅ **It resolves 51 rows and finds real ones the link method misses** — workflow 13 gains `TASK-1458`, `1461`, `1462`, `1463`, `1470`. 🔴 **But design→workflow is MANY-to-one and it over-assigns**: `Fortune Signora Authentication.dc.html` serves **six workflows** — Login, Registration, Email Verification, Forgot Password, Password Reset and Invitation Acceptance — **so workflow 7 derived `TASK-485`, `486`, `487` and `488`, which are Registration and Email Verification.** ⛔ **It also leaves the same 147 rows unresolvable, because a row with no `Design authority` cell has nothing to derive from either** |
>
> 🔴 **So only A remains, and it is expensive.** ⛔ **B was this office's recommendation for the length of one measurement and is withdrawn before it reached the product owner — tested rather than proposed.** ⚡ **The reason it fails is worth more than the option: a design document is not a workflow, and six workflows share one.**

⚠️ **Which means the registry is not merely stale — the relationship it encodes exists NOWHERE ELSE in the repository.** ⛔ **A hand-maintained list is the only representation, so [§5h](coordination/lane-c/OPERATING-MODE.md)'s *derive it* has no source to derive from until a row carries the link.**

✅ **Recommendation, as input: A, and scoped to NEW rows only** — require the `[workflow N]` link in `Epic` going forward, and leave the 147 historic rows alone. ⚡ **The registry becomes trustworthy for everything written after the decision without touching the product owner's register**, and the existing gap stays visible rather than being papered over.
>
> ✅ **Recorded rather than actioned, per the product owner's standing instruction to document and proceed.** ⛔ **Until one is chosen, any workflow-level count carries this caveat, and this office will state it every time rather than quoting a number that reads as measured.**

> ### 🔴 SECOND MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-13 — four `planned` workflows have every row PROMOTED
>
> **Measured by resolving each `planned` workflow's task ids against `BACKLOG.md` rather than reading the registry's state:**
>
> | # | Workflow | Rows |
> |---|---|---|
> | **10** | **Team Management** | `TASK-471` — **PROMOTED** |
> | **12** | **CRM Integrations** | `TASK-402` — **PROMOTED** |
> | **14** | **Companies** | `TASK-440` — **PROMOTED** |
> | **16** | **Global Search** | `TASK-481` · `TASK-301` · `TASK-460` — **all PROMOTED** |
>
> ⛔ **The original finding was that a workflow reads COMPLETE because its remaining rows are not in it.** ⚡ **This is the inverse: a workflow reads PLANNED while every row it names is on `main`.** **One register, two opposite errors, and neither is visible without resolving the ids.**
>
> 🔴 **AND IT COST A PLANNING RECOMMENDATION.** ⛔ **Asked where Lane A's next supply should come from, this office recommended **Team Management** on the registry's `planned` state and its note — *"418 calls it the highest reuse in all 26 screens — 8 of 13 endpoints already ship."*** ✅ **`TASK-471` has been `PROMOTED` since 2026-08-10.** ⚠️ **The recommendation was withdrawn before any work started, and only because the duplicate-check ran first.**
>
> ⛔ **The states are NOT corrected here, deliberately.** **`on_main` would assert the workflow is complete, and *"every row it names is promoted"* is a weaker claim than *"the design is covered"*** — 📁 **which is the original B-431 defect, in the other direction.** ⚡ **Asserting completion from a row list that is known to be incomplete is how this row was opened.** ✅ **A truthful state needs the screen-level coverage measurement, and that is the repair rather than a relabel.**
| **Found** | **By cross-checking the registry's `tasks` arrays against `BACKLOG.md` rather than reading either alone** |

#### 🔴 The measurement

| | |
|---|---|
| **Rows in `BACKLOG.md`** | **189** |
| **Rows listed against any workflow** | **78** |
| ⛔ **Rows belonging to no workflow** | **111** |

⚠️ **Not all 111 are defects.** 📁 **13 are pre-workflow-model legacy rows (`<400`) and 7 more are `500`–`999`** — platform and infrastructure work that legitimately maps to no customer journey.

🔴 **21 in the `1400+` block are.** ⛔ **They are the entire App Shell audit output** — `TASK-1460`–`1472`, plus `TASK-1413`, `1430`, `1431`, `1454`, `1455`, `1457`, `1458`, `1459` — **and every one of them is remaining work inside a workflow the registry already names.**

#### ⛔ Why it misleads rather than merely lags

📁 **`[meta] updated = 2026-08-07`.** ⚡ **Four days, and the decomposition has moved substantially since.**

⛔ **The failure is directional and it always reads the same way: a workflow looks MORE finished than it is.** ⚡ **Worked example — workflow 13, Application Shell: the registry lists 21 tasks, 19 of them terminal. `TASK-1461` (two navigation generations mounted at once), `TASK-1470` (`Ask Signora` in the wrong position) and `TASK-1471` (the frame skeletonises itself) are three structural defects inside that workflow, and none of the three is in its list.**

⚠️ **The `state` field is separately stale in the other direction** — 📁 **eleven workflows declare `planned` or `decomposed` while every task the registry lists for them is terminal.** ⛔ **Neither measure is safe alone, which is the actual finding.**

#### ✅ What a fix looks like

⚡ **Assign the 21 `1400+` rows to the workflows they already belong to, restamp `[meta] updated`, and re-check the eleven `state` values against their rows.** ⛔ **Do not close the gap by relabelling states** ([D-187](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6).

⚠️ **The legacy 20 are a separate question** — 📁 **either they map to a workflow or the registry should say they are platform work, and guessing is what produced this row.**

#### 🔴 The sharpest measurement yet — 2026-08-14, asked *"how many workflows are completed and pending"*

**Every workflow's declared `state` compared against the backlog states of the tasks its own `tasks` array names:**

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **Declared `planned` while carrying PROMOTED work** | **9 of the 10** — **Team Management · CRM Integrations · Companies · Global Search · AI Copilot · Executive Dashboard · Opportunity Intelligence · Signal Center · Billing** |
| ⛔ **The only `planned` workflow that is genuinely unstarted** | **Notification Center (17)** |
| ⚠️ **Declared in-flight while every listed task is shipped** | **4** — **Password Reset (`in_validation`) · Workspace Creation (`in_progress`) · Initial Onboarding (`active`) · User Profile (`blocked`)** |
| ✅ **Workflows with no closed task at all** | **3** — **Invitation Acceptance (7) · Notification Center (17) · Workflow Automation (26)** |

🔴 **So the `state` field is demonstrably wrong for at least 13 of 29, and `planned` is wrong 9 times out of 10 — a field that is right once in ten is worse than an absent one**, because a reader takes it as a measurement.

⛔ **And the second half still bites: *"all listed tasks shipped"* is NOT *"the workflow is complete."*** 📁 **The `tasks` arrays resolve only 51 of 198 rows**, so a workflow can read finished on a partial list. ⚡ **Workflow 10 lists ONE task; workflow 13 lists twenty-one.**

> ⛔ **Neither field can answer *how many workflows are done*, and this office states that rather than quoting a number that reads as measured.** ✅ **What is safe to quote: 29 workflows exist, 3 have no shipped work, and the screen-level coverage audit is the only route to the rest.**

⚠️ **Method note, and it is [OPERATING-MODE.md](coordination/lane-c/OPERATING-MODE.md) §5f caught in the act.** **A first pass matched `name` and `state` as adjacent lines and returned 28 workflows, silently dropping workflow 13 — the largest one in the file.** ✅ **Counting a second way (`grep -c '^\s*name\s*='` → 29) is what exposed it.** ⛔ **The narrow predicate did not error; it under-reported.**

### B-430 · 🟡 `state-check` reports a correct row as defective, and the fix it invites is the one C-213 cost two days

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Repository-wide** — [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — 📁 `state-check.py` is a gate, and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) makes a gate QE's |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⛔ **wrong but survivable: the check is advisory and blocks nothing.** ⚠️ **Filed because of what it invites, not what it stops** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C**, 2026-08-11, on the routine poll |
| **Found** | **By acting on the check's own output** — ⚡ **the sweep it prompted found four real releases and two false reports** |

#### 🔴 The defect that matters

📁 **[C-289](LANE_COORDINATION.md#c-289)'s `Owner` cell reads:**

> ***"`knowledge_graph`'s current assignee — joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), ⛔ not named here ([C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md#c-213))"***

⛔ **`state-check` reports it as `C-289's Owner names no lane, QE or the product owner. An owner a reader cannot route to is an absent owner.`**

✅ **The owner IS routable. `modules.toml` gives `knowledge_graph` → `current_owner = "Lane A"`, and the join resolves today.**

🔴 **The row is not merely acceptable — it is the ratified practice.** 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *Ownership is determined by architecture, and recorded in one registry*: *"No document restates an assignee, and a coordination item, backlog row or defect names its module; the assignee is joined at render time."***

⚡ **So the check flags the one row in the register that follows the rule, and the obvious way to satisfy it is to hard-code `Lane A` into the cell** — ⛔ **which is exactly the stale-assignee defect [C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md#c-213) cost two days of blocked work to establish.** 🔴 **A check that is satisfied by reintroducing a known defect is worse than no check.**

#### ⚠️ A second false positive in the same gate, and it is milder

📁 **The `SEQUENCED`-row check fires when ANY predecessor has been handed over, not when ALL have.**

⚡ **Measured across two days on the same rows:**

| Date | Reported | Genuinely free | False |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2026-08-10** | **4** | **1** | **3** |
| **2026-08-11** | **5** | **4** | **1** |

⚠️ **This one is defensible and is NOT asked to change.** ⛔ **It is advisory and its job is to prompt a re-check, which is what it did — the 2026-08-11 sweep released four rows because of it.** ✅ **The cost is one verification pass; the alternative is a row that stays parked because nothing re-asks.** 📁 **It is recorded here only so the two are not confused: the first report is a defect, the second is a design choice, and [TASK-1414](BACKLOG.md#task-1414--workflow-23--security-center--a-persons-own-security) carries the dated evidence for both.**

#### ✅ What a fix looks like

⚡ **Resolve the `Owner` cell through [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) before judging it** — the same join every other consumer of that registry already performs. ⛔ **Do not ask the register to name lanes inline.**

⚠️ **`infra/coordination.py` already does this join correctly**, which is where the reference implementation is.

### B-429 · 🟠 The user menu drops the design's first fact, on a premise the registration form disproves

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `product_surface` — [`frontend/components/shell/account-menu.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/account-menu.tsx) · [`frontend/app/(app)/layout.tsx`](../frontend/app/(app)/layout.tsx):37 |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — `product_surface` is this lane's in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — **a stated design requirement is absent from a shipped screen** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-12.** ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes.** ✅ **`session.user.name` is threaded from [`layout.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/layout.tsx) through `AuthenticatedShell` → `AppShell` → `TopBar` → `AccountMenu`**, and the menu states all four facts. 🔴 **The false comment was REMOVED with the fix**, which the row asked for by name: ⛔ **it read as a considered design decision and that is how it survived review and promotion.** ✅ **The half of it that was RIGHT is kept and is now tested**: ⛔ **a name is never derived from the address**, and a session carrying none renders the email alone. ⚡ **`name: string | null` is REQUIRED on every prop in the chain, not optional** — 📁 **an optional prop is exactly how this happened**: a caller omitted it silently and nothing asked. **Six test call sites had to answer it, which is the type doing the work** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)). ✅ **The avatar now takes its initials from the name** — 📁 the design draws *"MR"* for *Marta Reinhardt*, **which an address cannot produce.** ✅ **Fire-tested both ways**: dropping the name turns one red, sourcing the initials from the address turns another. **3057 frontend / 168 files · 6 profile journeys watched headed.** ⚠️ **The prior state, kept rather than rewritten** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)): 🔵 **`OPEN` — Lane C**, 2026-08-10, from the global-UX reconciliation ⚠️ **UPDATED 2026-08-12 — the FIX was right and the PROOF was not** ([B-191](#b-191)). 🔴 **`name={null}` in [`layout.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/layout.tsx) — the exact line the original defect dropped — left the suite green.** ⛔ **The component test rendered `AccountMenu` with a name the TEST supplied**, so it proved the component displays what it is given, **and that was never the defect.** ✅ **Repaired with a JOURNEY**, because the seam is a server component reading a session and no component test can reach it: 📁 `profile-journey` signs in as a real person and reads the menu **through `layout.tsx`, the real session and the whole shell chain.** ⚡ **QE's exact revert now turns it red.** |
| **Commit found** | [TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md), `PROMOTED` |

#### 📁 The design requirement

**App Shell §11, `userSpecs` → `Content rules`:** ⚡ ***"Always states name, email, role and workspace."*** **Four facts. The mock renders all four** — *"MR · Marta Reinhardt · marta@northwind.com · Admin · Northwind Global"*.

#### ✅ Three of four ship, and the implementation is otherwise faithful

⛔ **This is NOT a legacy component and must not be rebuilt.** 📁 It quotes the design verbatim in its own docstring and delivers **280px right-aligned · email · role as a brand-tint chip (`bg-accent-subtle text-accent`) · workspace name · a three-way segmented theme control** rather than a toggle · **sign out below a hairline**. ✅ **[TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md) built this from the finalized design and got it right.**

#### 🔴 The defect is the reason given for the fourth

📁 **`account-menu.tsx`:155, in the code:**

> ***"Name is not stated, because the platform does not publish one — the session carries an email and nothing else. Inventing a display name from the local part would be the shell asserting a fact about a person it does not have."***

⛔ **The reasoning is sound and the premise is false.**

| Evidence | |
|---|---|
| 📁 `register-form.tsx`:63 | ⚡ **Registration REQUIRES it** — *"Enter your full name."* **No account exists without one** |
| 📁 `profile/page.tsx`:36 | ✅ **Another route in this application reads `user?.name` from the same session** |
| 📁 **`app/(app)/layout.tsx`:37** | 🔴 **The root cause, and it is one line**: `<AuthenticatedShell email={session.user.email}>` — **`session.user.name` is in scope on that line and is not passed** |

⚡ **So the shell's own composition drops the fact one line before the menu needs it**, and the comment then explains the absence as a platform limitation. ⛔ **The guard was honest; the measurement behind it was never taken.**

#### The fix

✅ **Thread `name` from `layout.tsx` through `AuthenticatedShell` to `AccountMenu`, and render it above the email as the design's identity block draws it.** ⛔ **Do not derive a name from the email local part** — that half of the comment is correct and stays.

#### ⚠️ Why this is worth a row rather than a silent patch

📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *a comment justifying absent behaviour is a false claim sitting in the codebase*.** ⚡ **The comment will outlive the fix unless it is removed with it** — and it currently reads as a considered design decision, which is how it survived review and promotion.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — [`docs/coordination/queues/`](coordination/queues/), read by [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — 📁 the coordination subsystem is this office's under [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md) |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — ⚠️ **survivable but recurring, and QE has now reported it three consecutive cycles** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`VERIFIED` — QE**, 2026-08-10, at promoted `e3eeca2`. **Measured**: the generator is idempotent on a second run, no queued id sits at `CLAIMED` or beyond in either lane, and `--check`/`--dry-run` write nothing |
| **Found** | **2026-08-10.** ⚡ **QE's diagnosis was right and is what made this findable**: *"the queues are regenerated, not maintained by hand — so I read this as the projection not being re-run after promotion rather than anything anybody wrote wrongly."* ⚠️ **Half right, and the other half is the bug** |
| 🔴 **The measurement that separates the two halves** | ✅ **The PUBLISHED projection is correct BY CONSTRUCTION** — [`coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py):1069 builds `backlog` from `state == ASSIGNED and r.on_integration`, **so a `PROMOTED` or `CLAIMED` row cannot appear in it.** **Verified this cycle: 0 stale rows in `coordination.toml` for either lane.** ⛔ **The stale ids are in the hand-maintained QUEUE FILES** — `lane-a.toml` still listed `TASK-464` after promotion |
| 🔴 **So the root cause is [§2](../CLAUDE.md), not scheduling** | ⛔ ***"Truth has exactly one authoritative representation; everything else derives from it."*** **Eligibility is DERIVED by the generator from `BACKLOG.md`. The queue file's `backlog` array RESTATES it.** ⚡ **Two representations of one fact, and the hand-maintained one drifts on every promotion — which is exactly the *"synchronisation is maintenance, derivation is architecture"* case** |
| ⚠️ **Why it can reach a lane, so it is not merely cosmetic** | 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 3 sends a lane to `queues/lane-<a\|b>.toml`.** 📁 **[D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) sends it to `origin/coordination`.** ⚡ **The ref is correct; the file is the one that drifts — so the two documented paths disagree, and only one of them is safe** |
| ✅ **Smallest fix, bounded and deliberately not done here** | **Derive the queue file's eligibility rather than storing it** — either drop the `backlog` array from the queue files entirely and let `[rationale]`/`blocked` remain, or have `--publish` regenerate it from the projection. ⛔ **NOT a redesign of the queue model, and not a change to what a lane reads** |
| ⛔ **What was done this cycle instead** | **`TASK-464` removed by hand and the projection republished.** ⚠️ **That is the fourth hand-fix of the same class, which is the argument for the fix above rather than a fifth** |

### B-420 · The Team page's history region crashes — the hook claims an array and the endpoint is cursor-paginated

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** — [`frontend/lib/query/hooks/team.ts`](../frontend/lib/query/hooks/team.ts):236 |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **a shipped screen a customer reaches.** ⚡ **Contained by `RegionBoundary`, so the page survives and the region fails** — which is that primitive working exactly as designed |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A, 2026-08-10, on the poll it arrived.** 📁 **`lib/query/hooks/team.ts` now declares `apiRequest<CursorPage<HistoryEntry>>`, the call site reads `history.data?.items ?? []`, and `components/team/history.tsx` guards with `Array.isArray`.** ✅ **Plus a static detector — [`tests/unit/envelope-contract.test.ts`](../frontend/tests/unit/envelope-contract.test.ts) — which cross-references every backend `response_model=CursorPage[...]` route against `apiRequest<Thing[]>` in the hook layer**, because ⛔ **a runtime check inside `apiRequest` cannot work: a generic has no presence at runtime.** ⚡ **Fire-tested by reintroducing the defect.** ⚠️ **The row read `OPEN` on `integration` until now while the fix was already PROMOTED there — a stale register entry, and this lane's own**: the BUGS.md edit was lost in a branch rebuild and the code was not. ⛔ **A fixed defect showing `OPEN` is the [§2](../CLAUDE.md) defect — the repository asserting something untrue of itself** — **corrected here rather than left for QE to chase.** ✅ **Lane C was right to report and right not to fix** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). ⚠️ **QE verifies and closes; this lane does not.** **Was: ⚠️ `OPEN` — reported by Lane C, 2026-08-10** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-10, by the product owner USING the product** — 📁 **`/settings/team` in a browser.** ⚡ **Not by any suite** |
| **Steps** | **Sign in as an owner · open `/settings/team`** |
| **Expected** | **The organization history renders, or says it could not load** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`TypeError: entries is not iterable` at `history.tsx:137`**, caught by `RegionBoundary` and logged as `signora.region_failed` |

### 🔴 Root cause — a type ASSERTION standing where a check was needed

| | |
|---|---|
| **The endpoint** | `GET /workspaces/{id}/history` → **`response_model=CursorPage[HistoryEntryResponse]`** — an envelope, `{items, next_cursor}` |
| **The hook** | `apiRequest<HistoryEntry[]>(...)` — ⛔ **declares a bare ARRAY** |
| **Why it reaches `groupByDay`** | ⚡ **`entries.length === 0` evaluates `undefined === 0` → `false`**, so the empty-state guard **passes the envelope straight through** to a `for…of` |

> ## ⛔ **`apiRequest<T>` is a CLAIM about the wire, not a check of it.** ⚡ **TypeScript believed it, so nothing typed failed** — and the component's own tests pass an array fixture directly, which never exercises the envelope.

### ✅ Measured scope — it is ONE hook, not a class

**Five hooks declare a bare array. Four are correct**: `/integrations`, `/invitations`, `/ownership` and `/account-search` are all genuinely `response_model=list[...]`. ⛔ **`/history` is the only `CursorPage` among them.**

📁 **Ten endpoints return `CursorPage` repository-wide** ([§7](../CLAUDE.md): *cursor-based pagination for all collections*), **and this is the only one a bare-array hook reads.**

⚠️ **So the fix is one hook — and the interesting question for Lane A is whether the guard belongs in `apiRequest` rather than in each caller**, because the next `CursorPage` endpoint a hook adopts will fail the same silent way.

### B-419 · A blind replace closed the wrong coordination item, and I reported it as closed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`docs/LANE_COORDINATION.md`** — Product Office's editing practice |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **an item was marked `CLOSED` with no analysis under it, and this office told the product owner it was closed.** ⚡ **A false `CLOSED` is worse than an `OPEN` nobody has reached: an open item is visibly waiting, a closed one is answered** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10.** **Both rows repaired by anchored edit, and [C-271](LANE_COORDINATION.md) then actually analysed.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-10, opening C-271 to work it and finding it already `CLOSED` by me** |
| **Steps** | **`t.replace("\| **Status** \| 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-10 \|", new, 1)`, intending C-272** |
| **Expected** | **C-272 closed** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`count=1` replaces the FIRST match IN THE FILE. C-271 appears above C-272 and had a byte-identical `Status` line, so C-271 was closed and C-272 stayed `OPEN`** — **with C-272's three answer cells sitting under an open row** |

> ## 🔴 **THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS, and the previous two are this office's too.**

📁 **[B-411](#b-411)** — a non-greedy regex under `re.S` swallowed the row below the one it edited. 📁 **[B-412](#b-412)** — a blind replace matched its own explanatory comment, *"and a `.replace()` with `count=1` looks maximally careful and still cannot tell data from prose."*

⛔ **B-412 named this exact mechanism and I used it anyway.** ⚡ **The rule already existed**: 📁 **[D-185](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §5 — *"continue preferring repository operations that target explicit rows, fields and structured data rather than broad pattern replacement."***

### ✅ The repair, and why the practice is the fix rather than a check

**Both rows were repaired by locating the section heading first and editing the `Status` line at a known offset from it** — the same anchored form B-412's repair adopted. **C-271 was then given the analysis it never had**, because reopening it and closing it again unanalysed would have been the worse error.

⛔ **No check is added.** ⚡ **A linter that verified every `CLOSED` had analysis beneath it would be a new mechanism for a practice failure** ([D-229](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §1), **and the practice is one line: anchor on the heading, never on the cell text.**

### ⚠️ And the reporting half, which is the part that matters most

🔴 **This office reported C-272 as closed in a status report to the product owner while the file said `OPEN`.** ✅ **The analysis was real and was under the right item** — **only the state was wrong** — **but the report asserted a state this office had not verified after writing it.** 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): the repository must always tell the truth, and a report about the repository is held to the same standard.**

### B-418 · A partial test-database configuration reports a migration error, and migrations are fine

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** — [`infra/workstation.py`](../infra/workstation.py) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it costs an hour rather than a minute, because the diagnostic names the wrong subsystem.** ⚡ **Measured twice: the first occurrence cost two lanes an hour, the second cost Lane A part of a slice on 2026-08-10** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, with four regression tests.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-10, in Lane A's TASK-464 report** — 📁 *"that's the second time that specific trap has cost me time — the first time it cost two lanes an hour"* |
| **Steps** | **Set `SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL` and not the other two, then run the integration suite** |
| **Expected** | **Something names the misconfiguration** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`relation "action_batch" does not exist` — against a schema already at head `0046`.** 🔴 **The suite read a DIFFERENT database from the one migrations ran against, and the error points at migrations, which are fine** |

> ## ⛔ **The cost is not the misconfiguration. It is that the error names the wrong subsystem, so the search starts in the wrong place.**

📁 **The first occurrence was filed as [B-228](#b-228) and WITHDRAWN** — *"the seeder was never broken, and my invocation split one database into two."* ⚡ **The withdrawal was correct and the trap survived it**, because a withdrawn row leaves nothing behind that would catch the next instance.

### ✅ The fix — in the check that already exists for exactly this shape

⚡ **`workstation.py --check` already prevents one silent-mismatch failure**: a mismatched RSA pair that *"mints tokens successfully and 401s every request, with nothing in either tier naming the cause."* ✅ **This is the same shape, so it goes in the same place rather than into a new tool** ([D-229](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §1).

**`test_database_findings()` is a pure function of an environment mapping**, so both shapes of the trap are reproducible in a test rather than described in a comment:

| Shape | Caught |
|---|---|
| **A subset set** | ✅ **Names which variables are missing and what the resulting error will falsely blame** |
| **All three set, naming different databases** | ✅ **The count check cannot see this one — only the database name is compared, so differing credentials, host and query string stay legal** |
| **All three naming one database** | ⛔ **Silent** |
| **None set** | ⛔ **Silent** — 📁 **Lane C holds no database at all** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)), **and this check runs most often on exactly that clone** |

⚠️ **That last row is the one the tests exist for.** 📁 **This file's own opening: *"A setup check that cries wolf is worse than no setup check"*** — its advice is `--force`, which would destroy a working configuration it failed to recognise. **Fire-tested: reverting the check turns the two detection tests red and leaves both silence tests green.**

### B-417 · I resolved a conflict in a lane's favour and then appended to its line, which breaks that lane's next commit

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`docs/BACKLOG.md`** — Product Office's editing practice |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it returns another lane's branch from QE and costs that lane a manual conflict resolution it did not cause.** ⚡ **Twice now, on two lanes' time** |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN` — Lane C, 2026-08-10.** ✅ **Practice corrected below; the rule is the fix and there is nothing to code** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-10, testing QE's diagnosis of why Lane A's branch would not rebase** — ⛔ **and the diagnosis was wrong, which is how this was found** |
| **Steps** | **① A lane claims a row this office has released, so both edit one `Status` cell. ② This office rebases, resolves in the lane's favour — correctly — and APPENDS its own `*(Was: …)*` rationale to the lane's line. ③ The resolution reaches `integration`. ④ The lane's next commit changes that cell again and finds context it never wrote** |
| **Expected** | **A resolution in a lane's favour leaves that lane's next commit applying cleanly** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`TASK-1441`'s cell on `integration` carries this office's appended text, and Lane A's delivery commit conflicts on it** |

> ## ⛔ **QE proposed changing [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 7 for this. It is not step 7, and the measurement says so.**

📁 **QE's reading: *"integration says `CLAIMED`, Lane A's commit says `IN VALIDATION`… it is B-227's mechanism again, and it will keep recurring until step 7 changes."*** ⚡ **Two candidate causes were tested and both are innocent:**

| Candidate | Measured |
|---|---|
| **QE's sync rebase rewrites claim shas** *(`08d11ce0` → `0da0b0b1`)* | ⛔ **Innocent.** ✅ **`git patch-id --stable` is IDENTICAL for both — `fec2f35aa3af`. Git skips it as previously-applied**, which is exactly what it did on this lane's own rebases all day |
| **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 7's push shape** | ⛔ **Innocent here.** **The conflict is not on the claim commit at all — it is on the DELIVERY commit, one cell, one line** |
| ✅ **This office appending to the winning line** | 🔴 **Exact correlation.** **Of the three conflicts resolved this way today, `TASK-1441` is the ONLY one whose `Status` cell carries this office's text on `integration` — and it is the only one Lane A cannot rebase past** |

### ✅ The correction, and it needs no rule change anywhere

> ## **When a conflict resolves in favour of another lane's execution-state cell, take that line VERBATIM. Put the rationale in a cell of its own.**

⚡ **Appending makes the line partly this office's, and the owning lane's next commit then finds context it never wrote.** ✅ **A separate cell carries the same reasoning and collides with nothing** — 📁 **which is what this office did on `TASK-1453`, adding three cells beside Lane A's untouched status line, and that row has caused nobody a conflict.**

⛔ **The rationale is worth keeping** — a release this office made and a lane then claimed is exactly the history [§2](../CLAUDE.md) says not to erase. **The defect is WHERE it was written, not that it was.**

### B-414 · A trigger steward became an executor, and the ref offered Lane C a module it may not build

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation` — [`infra/coordination.py`](../infra/coordination.py)** |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **the published ref advertised a row in a lane's `backlog`, which is the array [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 4 tells a lane to select from.** ⚠️ **Not 🔴: nobody claimed it, and Lane C would have hit its own Change Budget on the first file it opened** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, in the same change, with four regression tests.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-10, on the startup poll, by noticing [`queues/lane-a.toml`](coordination/queues/lane-a.toml) and `coordination.toml` naming different owners for `TASK-412`** |
| **Steps** | **Publish the projection with a `READY` row that has no `Module` cell and a `Trigger steward` cell** |
| **Expected** | **The steward names who watches the trigger. It does not name who implements** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **`_lane_for` fell through to the steward and returned `Lane C`, so `TASK-412` appeared in Product Office's `backlog`** — **a row whose own Change Budget is 🟢 `modules/ai_platform/**`, a module [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) settles on Lane A and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) forbids Lane C to implement** |

> ## ⛔ **[D-135](DECISION_REGISTER.md) introduced the steward in the words that describe the defect exactly: *"every task should have an owner even if it cannot yet have an executor."***

**The function read it as both.** On a parked row the difference is invisible and D-135's purpose is served — **`TASK-411` is `SEQUENCED`, no lane can claim it, and naming its steward assigns nobody any work.** ⚡ **On a *claimable* row the same line manufactures an executor**, and the projection is the one channel that reaches a lane without QE.

**Two documents, one row, opposite owners** — `queues/lane-a.toml` queued `TASK-412` to Lane A while the ref offered it to Lane C. ⛔ **That is the [C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md) class this ref was built to end**, reappearing inside the instrument rather than in a hand-maintained table.

### ✅ The fix withholds the steward from a startable row, and loses nothing

**`_classify` already renders a startable row with no lane as `WAITING ARCHITECTURE`** — which is what `TASK-412` truthfully is: [D-042](DECISION_REGISTER.md) deliberately deferred its module boundary and *"do not force a module boundary until implementation naturally reaches it"* is still the ruling. ⚡ **The row does not vanish; it stops being advertised as claimable by a lane that may not build it**, and it now appears in the generator's *resolves to no lane* report where a deferred boundary belongs.

⚠️ **The remaining contradiction is the row's, not the tool's, and it is [C-1413](LANE_COORDINATION.md)**: `TASK-412`'s Module cell is deliberately unnamed while its Change Budget names `modules/ai_platform/**`. ⛔ **Not settled here** — a module boundary is architecture, and this office prepares rather than decides.

| **Actual** | ⛔ **The words inserted into the middle of a comment sentence — *"It appears under `[[blocked]]` with its blocker named"* — producing `[[blocked]] with its blocker named.` as a line of TOML** |

> ## ⛔ **The commit doing this was the commit implementing [D-185](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §5**, which reads: ***"continue preferring repository operations that target explicit rows, fields and structured data rather than broad pattern replacement."***

⚡ **So this row is not a confession, it is evidence for the ruling.** **The instruction is correct precisely because the failure is this easy** — ⛔ **a `.replace()` with `count=1` looks maximally careful and still cannot tell data from prose.**

### ✅ What the repair did instead, and it is the general rule

| ⛔ Wrong | ✅ Right |
|---|---|
| **`t.replace('[[blocked]]', …, 1)`** | **split on lines, find the line whose `.strip()` *is* `[[blocked]]`, splice there** |
| **Matches prose, comments, examples** | ⚡ **A structural token matched as a whole line cannot be a mention** |

✅ **And the post-condition that caught it in seconds: `tomllib.loads()` on the file before anything reads it.** **The queue is parsed by four instruments; making the *author* parse it first is one line.**

⚠️ **This is the fifth instance today of one class — a pattern answering a question only the structure can answer** ([B-411](#b-411--a-non-greedy-regex-under-res-swallowed-the-row-below-the-one-it-edited) lists the first four). ⛔ **The pattern across all five is not carelessness; it is that text tools are being used on structured files, and the fix is not more care — it is parsing.**

### B-411 · A non-greedy regex under `re.S` swallowed the row below the one it edited

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`docs/` — Product Office's own editing practice.** ⛔ **Not a tool defect; a *method* defect, which is why it is filed rather than fixed in code** |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **it deleted a delivered slice's acceptance criteria and nothing caught it for four commits.** ⚡ **It surfaced only because QE hit the collision at integration and declined to adjudicate** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-08.** **Line restored from `origin/integration`; all 114 rows verified against integration for further loss (zero).** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-08, by QE at cycle 121**, ⚡ **reporting that Lane C's tip *"genuinely carries no such line — so the deletion is deliberate."*** ⛔ **The observation was exact and the inference was wrong** |
| **Steps** | **Edit one table cell with `re.search(r'\| \*\*Status\*\* \| .*? \|\n', text, re.S)` and splice by `.start()`/`.end()`** |
| **Expected** | **The Status cell replaced** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **The Status cell *and the row beneath it* replaced.** 📁 **[TASK-486](BACKLOG.md)'s `Features` line — *"Six single-character boxes · paste fills every box · resend with the doubling timer · a wrong code keeps the digits"* — the delivered slice's acceptance criteria, gone** |

## ⚡ The mechanism, and why it is invisible

**`re.S` makes `.` match newlines. A non-greedy `.*?` then stops at the first ` |\n` it can find — which is the *next* row's terminator whenever the target cell has no internal one.** ⛔ **The match still succeeds. The regex still looks correct. Nothing errors.**

> ## ⛔ **The commit that did it was the commit RESTORING a lane-owned state I had overwritten** — **`c53fbcf6`, fixing one D-123 violation while committing a silent deletion.** ⚡ **A careful correction is exactly where this lands, because the correction is written quickly and reviewed as *"just putting it back."***

## 🔴 The fourth instance today of one class

| | Where | What matched wrongly |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | **A scan for `READY` rows** | **The word inside [TASK-203](BACKLOG.md)'s prose. Reported a `DISPOSED` row as claimable** |
| **②** | **A scan for finished predecessors** | **Ids inside my own *(Was:* history. 16 false positives** |
| **③** | **`state-check`'s ten stale rows** | **Acted on the eight names it PRINTED. Missed two** |
| **④** | **This** | **A cell terminator one row too far. Deleted content** |

> ## ⚡ **All four are the [B-101](#b-101) class — a pattern answering a question only the data can answer — and ⛔ every one was caught by *re-measuring*, never by re-reading.**

## ✅ The practice that changes

⛔ **No more multi-line `re.S` surgery on a register.** ⚡ **Edit a table cell by locating its *line*, not by spanning to a terminator**: split on `\n`, find the line whose prefix is the cell label, replace that line. **A row cannot then be swallowed, because a row is never crossed.**

✅ **And a post-condition on any scripted register edit, which is what actually caught the blast radius here**: ⛔ **compare every row's line count against `origin/integration` and refuse a push where any row shrank unintentionally.** **Zero of 114 shrank after the repair.**

⚠️ **What QE did was right and is worth naming.** **It checked three things before deciding — no Lane A commit touched the line, neither earlier Lane C commit touched it, and Lane C's tip genuinely lacked it — then declined to adjudicate a content judgement between two lanes and excluded the commits.** ✅ **That is the correct call on the evidence available. The evidence was just incomplete in a way only the author could resolve.**

### B-410 · The entire repository tree was published onto `origin/coordination`, and every lane's poll broke

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`infra/`** — Platform Foundation, [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🔴 — ⛔ **shared infrastructure, and it broke the *one command* [D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) gives every lane.** ⚡ **`git show origin/coordination:coordination.toml` returned `fatal: path does not exist`. A lane polling during that window learns nothing and has no fallback that is not the 14,392 lines the ref exists to replace** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-08, [D-181](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Recovered to `5f7b7a24`; `--publish` and `--self-test` added; `_git_strict` added.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-08, by Lane C, one line after causing it** — ⚡ **on the *output* of the next command, not on the output of the failing one, which is the whole defect** |
| **Steps** | **Run `git push origin HEAD:coordination --force-with-lease 2>&1\|tail -2 \|\| echo "…republish separately"`** |
| **Expected** | **A refusal, or a two-file tree** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **A 1609-file, 257-directory repository tree on an orphan ref that is flat by contract** |

## ⚡ The root cause is not the push. It is that a push existed to hand-roll.

> ## ⛔ **The command was written to *tolerate* failure and therefore could not report *unexpected success*.**
>
> ## ⚡ **Commands intended to tolerate failure must never obscure unexpected success.** — [D-181](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2, the product owner's wording.

**`|| echo "coordination ref: separate orphan, republish separately"` was appended in the expectation that the push would be rejected.** ⛔ **It was not.** **The fallback text never printed — and its *absence* was the only signal, in a shell where absence of output is the normal case.** ⚠️ **The wrong action and the handled skip were typographically identical on screen.**

### 🔴 The same defect, one layer down, in code

📁 **`_git()` in `infra/coordination.py` returns `.stdout.strip()` and discards the return code.** ⚡ **That is correct for reading** — an absent ref is a legitimate answer to *"what does `integration` say about this row?"* — ⛔ **and wrong for anything that writes, where an empty string and a successful push are indistinguishable.**

> ⚠️ **A `--publish` built on it would have printed *published* over a rejected push**, which is this same bug re-committed in the fix for it.

✅ **`_git_strict()` raises. Reads keep the tolerant form deliberately, and the docstring says which is which and why.**

### ✅ What actually prevents recurrence

⛔ **Not a warning beside the old procedure — the old procedure is gone.** **`python3 infra/coordination.py --publish` regenerates, builds the two-file tree, validates it, and moves the ref only if every clause holds.** **Hand-rolling is no longer the convenient path.**

| Clause | Checked by |
|---|---|
| **Destination is exactly `coordination`** | **name comparison, not a prefix** |
| **No subtrees** | ⚡ **a directory on a flat ref *is* the repository-tree case** |
| **No unexpected file · no contract file absent** | **by *name*** — ⛔ **a count alone passes a two-file tree holding the wrong two files** |
| **`coordination.toml` parses and carries `[meta]`, `[lane]`, `[task]`** | **a file without `[lane]` answers nothing a lane asked** |

✅ **`--self-test` proves it fails**, rather than asserting it: 🔴 **REFUSES the repository tree** — *257 directories, 1609 unexpected files, `coordination.toml` absent* — 🔴 **REFUSES the correct tree aimed at `integration`**, ✅ **ACCEPTS the published tree.** ⚡ **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code*, and [B-409](#b-409--the-starvation-check-counted-work-the-lane-had-already-finished-so-it-never-fired) is this office's own worked example of what an unproved guard is worth.**

⚠️ **What this row does not claim.** **The recovery required the product owner's approval and did not happen without it** — the push was refused by the permission classifier, this office stopped, and [D-181](DECISION_REGISTER.md) is the grant. ✅ **That part of the sequence worked.**
