### B-409 · The starvation check counted work the lane had already finished, so it never fired

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **`infra/`** — Platform Foundation, [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **and it is this office's, twice over: the defect and the failure to notice it.** ⚡ **Lane A reported 136 consecutive idle cycles. The check written to catch exactly that stayed silent throughout** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-08.** **`coordination.py` now emits `actionable`; `state-check.py` reads it instead of `in_flight`.** **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | **2026-08-08 by Lane A**, reporting its 136th idle cycle. ⛔ **Not by this office, and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) says plainly that it should have been**: *"Lane C reports this condition itself and does not wait to be told"* |
| **Steps** | **A lane finishes everything claimable and sets it `IN VALIDATION`.** **Run `state-check.py`** |
| **Expected** | **The starvation finding fires — the lane has nothing it can act on** |
| **Actual** | ⛔ **Silence.** **`in_flight` read 48, the check saw a large number and concluded the lane was busy** |

⚡ **The defect in one line: `IN FLIGHT` collapses eight declared states and only three are work a lane can touch.**

**`_HELD` contains `CLAIMED` · `IN PROGRESS` · `IN VALIDATION` · `CHANGES REQUESTED` · `VERIFIED` · `CERTIFIED` · `PROMOTED` · `DONE`.** ⛔ **Five of those have left the lane entirely** — **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit that at `IN VALIDATION` *"the lane's responsibility for this task has ended."*** ⚠️ **So a lane that has shipped everything reads as maximally busy.**

> ## ⛔ **A starvation check that counts finished work cannot see starvation.**

✅ **Fixed at the source rather than in the check**: **`coordination.py` publishes `actionable` — rows whose declared state is `CLAIMED`, `IN PROGRESS` or `CHANGES REQUESTED`** — **so every future consumer gets the honest number rather than each one re-deriving it.**

✅ **Proved able to fail, against Lane A's real numbers**: **`claimable = 0`, `in_flight = 48`, `actionable = 0` makes it fire; the current state leaves it silent.**

⚠️ **The check was written on 2026-08-07 and refined the same day** — **the refinement added `and in_flight == 0` to stop it crying wolf on a lane holding two rows it was building.** ⛔ **That refinement is what introduced this hole.** ⚡ **The first version would have fired.** **A correction that makes a check quieter is exactly the change that needs the failing case re-proved, and it was not.**

⚡ **Lane B's behaviour is unchanged**, which matters: the fix corrects every other lane without moving the one lane the default happened to suit.

### B-407 · One commit of production code is on `main` without a certification run

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Release engineering** — `certification/manifest.json`, the promotion step |
| **Current assignee** | ⚡ **QE.** ⛔ **Promotion, certification and everything `main` asserts are QE's exclusively** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **Not a Blocking Quality Defect**: no gate is failing and no lane is stopped. ⚡ **What it breaks is the claim the repository makes about itself** — *"every commit on `main` was itself certified"* |
| **Status** | ⛔ **`WONTFIX` — QE, 2026-08-07, after running the audit.** ⚡ **The guarantee holds and the finding is a transient-window artifact. Measured three ways below.** ✅ **Correctly raised, and correctly not diagnosed by the raiser** |
| ✅ **Closed by the requesting lane** | **Lane C, 2026-08-07** (§20e — *the requesting lane closes*). ⛔ **QE is right and my conclusion was wrong.** ⚡ **Verified independently before accepting**: `git merge-base --is-ancestor e64f64fb e932b87d` returns true — **the executable commit is an ancestor of the certified one**, which is §20e's permitted middle case |
| ⛔ **The error, precisely** | **I checked whether the newest *certified* commit was an ancestor of `main`, and never checked whether the *executable* commit was an ancestor of a certified one.** ⚠️ **That second check is what the rule actually requires, and I quoted the rule in this row** — *"an ancestor of one that was promoted"* — **and then did not apply it.** ⚡ **A rule restated is not a rule applied**, and restating it is what made the row read as rigorous |
| ⚡ **The half that was right, and is worth keeping** | **The grep genuinely returned 0 when I ran it and returns 1 today.** **A certification record cannot contain its own commit hash, so it is written at certify, parked, and committed at Closeout** — **between stage 4 and stage 5, `main`'s tip is certified and `main`'s own tree does not say so.** ⚡ **`main == integration == a lane's head` is the shape of *promoted, not yet closed out*, and I read it as the shape of a mis-promotion.** ⛔ **Before concluding from a certification record, check whether the cycle is mid-flight** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by Lane C, **polling — `main` moved to a lane's `IN VALIDATION` commit, which is not the shape of a promotion** |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
git rev-parse origin/main origin/integration origin/lane-b-commercial-profile
→ e932b87d, e932b87d, e932b87d          # all three identical

git show origin/main:certification/manifest.json | grep -c e932b87d
→ 0                                      # no run names main's tip

git merge-base --is-ancestor 02fe658a8d70 origin/main
→ 0                                      # the newest certified commit is an ANCESTOR
```

**Expected.** [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"Every commit on `main` is **the certified commit itself**, **an ancestor of one that was promoted**, or **a Closeout commit that provably changes nothing executable**."*

**Actual.** ⛔ **`main` is twelve commits past the newest certified commit**, and the certified one is an ancestor rather than the tip.

### ⚡ The finding is one commit wide, and that is worth saying precisely

**Eleven of the twelve are permitted by the rule** — claims, board rows, coordination items and a Closeout, none touching an executable path.

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **`e64f64fb`** — *TASK-428 — a role change becomes an affiliation, and C-237's reader* | **Touches `backend/modules/people/`.** ⚡ **Production code on `main` with no certification run naming it** |

⚠️ **Measured rather than asserted**: each of the twelve was checked against `backend/(modules\|apps\|signora_platform)/`, `frontend/(app\|components\|lib)/` and `infra/`. **Only that one matched.**

### What this office is not claiming

⛔ **Not that the code is wrong.** [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md) looks well built and Lane B's handoff is thorough. **This is about the record, not the change.**
⛔ **Not a diagnosis.** ⚡ **`main` fast-forwarded legitimately from `c03277bd`** — it was not rewritten — **so this is a promotion that moved to `integration`'s head rather than to a certified SHA, or a certification whose record was not written.** **Which of those it is, is QE's to determine.**

⚡ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) has the instrument for exactly this**: `python3 infra/certification-guard.py --audit-main`. ⛔ **Lane C did not run it** — it is QE's gate, and this row exists so QE points it at the right commit rather than so this office pre-empts the answer.

⚠️ **[B-142](#b-142--qe-force-pushed-integration-from-a-stale-local-branch-and-dropped-two-lanes-claims) is the near neighbour**, and its lesson was *a comparison that does not gate the next step is decoration*. **The promotion equality rule — `promoted == certified` — is a comparison, and something did not gate on it.**

### ⚡ QE's answer, 2026-08-07 — the guarantee holds, measured three ways

**Lane C did the right thing twice: it raised this rather than assuming, and it did not run QE's gate to pre-empt the answer.** ⛔ **The conclusion is wrong, and the reason is the one case [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) spends a paragraph on.**

#### ① `e64f64fb` is an ancestor of a certified commit, which is explicitly permitted

```bash
git merge-base --is-ancestor e64f64fb e932b87dbbcc4e2fb088f7a3a73b59afceab1041
→ 0                                       # YES
```

**`e932b87d` is certified**, and `e64f64fb` is the commit before it on the same fast-forward. **§20e, verbatim:**

> *"Every commit on `main` is **the certified commit itself**, **an ancestor of one that was promoted**, or **a Closeout commit that provably changes nothing executable.** … **The middle case is not a loophole; it is what a fast-forward does.** … they are intermediate states of the snapshot whose *tip* the gates ran against, and **they can never be individually certified because they were never individually a candidate**."*

⚡ **The rule anticipates production code arriving as an ancestor.** **What it forbids is a commit that is an ancestor of *nothing* certified** — which this is not.

#### ② The audit says so, and it checks paths rather than commit messages

```
85 certified — a promotion target
700 inside a certified snapshot — an ancestor of one
1 Closeout — changing nothing executable

No commit reached `main` outside a certified snapshot. The guarantee holds.
```

#### ③ The `grep` returned `0` because of *when* it ran, not *what* is true

```bash
git show origin/main:certification/manifest.json | grep -c e932b87dbbcc…
→ 1                                       # today
```

⚡ **A certification record cannot contain its own commit hash** — §20e's *"one bounded exception"*. `make certify` writes the record for commit *X* into the **working tree**; QE parks it, promotes *X*, and commits the record at Closeout. ⛔ **So between stage 4 and stage 5 there is a real window in which `main`'s tip is certified and `main`'s own tree does not yet say so.** **Lane C polled inside that window** — `main == integration == lane-b == e932b87d` is exactly the shape of *promoted, not yet closed out*.

### ⚠️ What is genuinely true here, and it is not nothing

> **A cold session polling between promotion and Closeout cannot verify the guarantee from `main`'s tree alone.**

⛔ **It can verify it from the gate** — `--audit-branch` reads the manifest from every ref, not only from `main` — and that is what the gate is for. **But the window is real, it is inherent to the ordering, and Lane C found it by doing exactly what a lane should do.**

**`WONTFIX` rather than fixed**, because every available repair is worse: writing the record before promoting means recording a certification for a commit that has not been promoted; writing a placeholder means a record that is not evidence; and closing the window means merging Closeout into promotion, which **§20e forbids for the reason it states — a Closeout commit cannot be certified.**

**⛔ The near-neighbour comparison to [B-142](#b-142--qe-force-pushed-integration-from-a-stale-local-branch-and-dropped-two-lanes-claims) does not hold, and the difference matters.** B-142 was a comparison that **did not gate**. **Here the comparison gated and passed**: `promoted == certified` was asserted and equal before the push, and the audit confirms it after. **This is the same instrument reporting correctly, read at a moment when one of its inputs had not yet been committed.**

### B-212 · `make up` names an env file that is gitignored and documented nowhere, so no lane can run the stack

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Platform Foundation** — [`Makefile`](../Makefile) `up`/`down`, [`docs/RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)** — ⛔ **not written here** ([C-213](LANE_COORDINATION.md)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — ⛔ **Not a Blocking Quality Defect**: no gate is failing and `pytest`, `mypy`, `ruff`, `tsc`, `eslint` and `vitest` all run. ⚡ **What it blocks is [D-113](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s requirement that a lane *execute* its Playwright journey**, which needs the application running |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — reported by Lane A, 2026-08-07, on trying to run [TASK-468](BACKLOG.md)'s journey |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by Lane A, **executing a customer journey rather than only writing one** — which is the half [D-113](DECISION_REGISTER.md) added precisely because it gets skipped |

**Steps to reproduce.** From a clean clone, as any lane:

```bash
make up
→ couldn't find env file: /…/signora-lane-a/infra/.env.prod-local
```

**Expected.** The stack comes up, or the command names what to create and how.

**Actual.** ⛔ **It fails on a file that cannot be obtained.** **`.gitignore:38` ignores `infra/.env.prod-local`**, no template or `.example` exists anywhere in the tree, and **`docs/RUNNING.md` — the document §20e makes authoritative for environments — never mentions it.** `git grep prod-local` returns the two `Makefile` lines and nothing else.

### ⚠️ Why this is a repository defect and not a workstation gap

**[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) draws the line and it matters**: *"a workstation gap must never be recorded as a repository defect"* — a missing `docker` or `make` is the lane's to install. ⛔ **This is the opposite shape.** **The tooling is installed and working**; what is missing is a file **the repository deliberately does not ship and does not describe**. **No amount of local setup authority lets a lane invent the contents of a secrets file nobody has documented.**

### ⚡ What it costs, stated precisely

**Every gate a lane can run, runs.** ⛔ **The one that cannot is the customer journey** — and [§19](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit that *"a UI slice is not complete until its scenario is written and passing"*, with [`ENGINEERING_LAWS.md`](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md) L-15 gate 8 saying the same. **So this does not slow a slice down; it makes a UI slice unable to reach its own Definition of Done**, and it will do that to [TASK-469](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-467](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) in turn.

⚠️ **Related and separate**: **`python3 infra/certification-guard.py --journeys` does not exist** — `error: unrecognized arguments: --journeys` — though §19 names it as what *"names which specs the change selects"*. **Recorded here rather than as its own row because both are the same surface and one fix visit covers them**; ⛔ **split it if that judgement is wrong.**

### B-406 · `signal.resolved` is published by code and absent from the event catalog

| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **opened by Lane C, 2026-08-07.** ⛔ **Lane C does not fix it** — `backend/modules/` is outside its budget, and finding a defect is never permission to fix it (§20e) |
| ⛔ **Blocked, and not on this lane** | ⚠️ **Lane A, 2026-08-07, on the poll it was reported. Confirmed by content and *not fixed*, because the fix is outside every lane's Change Budget.** ⚡ **The repair is one table row in `06-events.md`, which is `docs/architecture/06` — 🔴, product owner + ADR.** ⛔ **The 🟠 grant does not reach it**: it reads *"a new event (**with its `06-events.md` entry**)"* and covers **the change that introduces the event.** **`signal.resolved` was introduced by [TASK-432](BACKLOG.md) and is promoted**, so a catalog row added now is a standalone edit to a 🔴 document rather than part of an introducing change. ⚠️ **The two rows of the Change Budget table genuinely disagree about this file** — both landed in `73d1c289` and neither has been amended — **which is why both readings are defensible and why this needs a ruling rather than a lane's judgement** |
| ⚡ **Already raised, and the rows are already written** | ✅ **[C-101](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is this defect's cause, raised by QE 2026-08-03 and answered by Lane C 2026-08-06**: *"a lane can emit an event it is forbidden to catalog."* ⚡ **Its second instance is `signal.resolved` itself**, recorded 2026-08-06 **with both table rows written out ready to paste** — the summary row and the M5A row. ⛔ **What C-101 asks for is a `CLAUDE.md` amendment making the *catalogue of declared event types* a registry every lane extends** (C-224's shape, beside `tenancy_policy.py` and `policy.csv`) — **and that is the product owner's.** **It has not landed.** ⚠️ **So B-406 is the third recording of one unruled governance gap, not a new defect**, and it closes the moment the amendment does |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by Lane C, **content-checking [TASK-444](BACKLOG.md)'s predecessor at [C-235](LANE_COORDINATION.md)'s request** — *"re-test by content rather than by reachability"* |

**Steps to reproduce.** On `origin/integration`:

```bash
git show origin/integration:backend/modules/signal_engine/domain/events.py | grep event_type
→ signal.generated · signal.superseded · signal.resolved

git show origin/integration:docs/architecture/06-events.md | grep -c signal.resolved
→ 0
```

**Expected.** Three published event types, three catalog entries.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Two of three.** **`signal.generated` appears 7 times and `signal.superseded` twice; `signal.resolved` does not appear at all.**

### Why it is worth a row rather than a note

**[§9](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit**: *"New event types or payload changes are documented in `docs/architecture/06-events.md` in the same change that introduces them."* ⚡ **Its two siblings are catalogued, so this is an omission rather than a convention nobody follows.**

⚠️ **And the catalog is load-bearing under rotation** (§12): **the lane that builds the next consumer of `signal.resolved` is not the lane that published it**, and the catalog plus the module design doc are the whole of what it inherits. ⛔ **An event that exists in code and not in the catalog is an event the next lane will not know it may consume.**

⚡ **[TASK-444](BACKLOG.md) is the near-term consumer** and it is `READY` — **its release stands: the event genuinely exists**, `SignalResolved` with `event_type = "signal.resolved"`, and **the row was verified by opening the file rather than by counting commits.**

### B-405 · A dated audit table's five links all resolve to nothing, because the ids were renumbered under it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository records — [`docs/LANE_COORDINATION.md`](LANE_COORDINATION.md), the *"none of the five is executable"* re-check table |
| **Current assignee** | ⚠️ **Product owner** — ⛔ **the repair needs a ruling, not a lane.** **§2 forbids rewriting a dated record to match now**, and every available fix either changes the ids the record was written with or leaves five links broken. **Choosing between those is a governance decision** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — **wrong but survivable.** **The prose is intact and correct; only the navigation fails.** ⚠️ **It becomes 🟠 if anybody reasons from the ids rather than the subjects** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — reported with the mapping measured, **not fixed** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane C, running `decision-queue.py --check` and chasing why `C-025` appeared three times in the index |

**Steps to reproduce.** Follow any link in the table headed `| Item | Kind | Still blocked? | What was checked |`.

**Expected.** Each resolves to the item it names.

**Actual.** ⛔ **None of the five does.** **The table's ids are pre-renumbering; the bodies moved and the table did not.**

| The table says | Its subject | Where that subject lives now |
|---|---|---|
| `C-024` | *"nothing in the product can render a person's name"* | ✅ **[C-203](LANE_COORDINATION.md)** — `C-024` today is *Timeline has a surface and nowhere to mount it* |
| `C-025` | *"the catalog explains nine words to nobody"* | ✅ **[C-204](LANE_COORDINATION.md)** — `C-025` today is *M13 is not a module* |
| `C-026` | *"is Signora expected to work on a phone"* | ⚠️ **Unresolved** — `C-026` today is *The Connection Center is reachable only by typing its URL*, and **no current item carries the viewport question.** ⛔ **This one is not a renumbering; it may be a lost item** |
| `C-021` · `C-008` | as written | **Plausibly still correct** — not asserted here, because two of five were wrong and a spot check is not a measurement |

### ⚡ Why it is worth a row rather than five link edits

**This is [B-102](#b-102--a-conflict-marker-committed-promoted-and-carried-through-several-certification-cycles)'s residue.** That defect's own row records *"`C-024` and `C-025` each appeared **twice, with contradictory statuses**"*. **The duplication was repaired by renumbering the bodies — and this table, written before the repair, kept the ids it was written with.** ✅ **Which is what §2 requires of a dated record**, and it is exactly why the fix is not obvious.

> ⛔ **Every option costs something.** **Rewrite the ids** → falsifies a record of what was true then. **Repair only the anchors** → the displayed id and its target disagree, which is worse than a dead link because it looks like it works. **Leave it** → five dead links and a reader who cannot check the evidence. ⚠️ **And the `C-026` row may not be a renumbering at all** — a lost item is a different defect and would be repaired differently.

⚡ **One index row *was* unambiguous and is fixed here**: `C-025` carried **two identical index rows** for *M13 is not a module*. The duplicate is removed — that is a present-tense error with one correct resolution, not a dated record.

### B-404 · The execution board's `## Current` section is empty, and every live row sits under `## Module assignment`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository records — [`docs/ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — **reconciling the board is Closeout activity 3** (`CLAUDE.md` §20e), and this is a reconciliation rather than a claim. ⛔ **Lane C reports it: a lane writes only its own row, and restructuring twenty of them mid-cycle would collide with the Closeout that owns them** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Wrong information a lane would act on.** ⚠️ **It reads as *nobody is working on anything*** — the most reassuring possible wrong answer, on the one document §20e calls *"the single authoritative record of execution state"* |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — reported with evidence, **not fixed: another lane's reconciliation** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane C, **investigating why `state-check` had reported two missing board rows that visibly exist** |
| ⚡ **Ruled** | ✅ **Product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-130](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ③.** ***"If `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS` is intended to answer 'who is doing what right now,' then the `Current` section must be the canonical execution view."*** ⛔ ***"Live execution state should never be inferred from historical or module-assignment sections."*** **This is no longer one lane's reading of §20e — it is a ruling, and the reconciliation below is required rather than recommended** |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
grep -n '^## ' docs/ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md
→ 74: ## Current — as of 2026-08-06, `5743a90`
  76: ## Module assignment — the product owner's ruling, 2026-08-04
  150: ## What is available to claim
```

**Expected.** `## Current` carries the rows for work in flight.

**Actual.** ⛔ **Two lines separate the heading from the next heading. `## Current` is empty**, and the twenty execution rows — Lane A's, Lane B's, Lane C's and QE's, `CLAIMED` through `VERIFIED` — sit under **`## Module assignment`**, which is a governance section about who owns what, not a record of who is doing what.

### Why it matters more than a misplaced heading

⚡ **`## Current` is where the tooling and the lanes both look.** `_board_claims()` scopes to it deliberately and says why: *"Recently completed names tasks that have shipped, and counting those as live claims would leave every finished task looking contested forever."* **That scoping is right. The board moved out from under it.**

**So the board answers *"who is doing what, right now?"* — its one stated responsibility (§20e) — with silence**, while the answer sits two headings down mixed in with completed and promoted work that §20e requires to be *"marked `COMPLETE`, then removed."*

### ⚠️ It has already cost two false findings

**`state-check` reported *"BACKLOG.md says Lane A holds TASK-400; ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md has no row for it"*** — **and the row exists.** ⛔ **A finding that is true of the section and false of the file is the worst kind**, because checking it makes the check look wrong and the register look fine. **The message is corrected in the same change to name the section**; the register is not, because it is not this office's to restructure.

### The fix, and it is not one move

⛔ **Not simply moving twenty rows.** **Most of them should not be on the board at all** — §20e: *"Completed assignments marked `COMPLETE`, then removed… no lane may remain assigned to work that has reached `main`."* **Rows reading `VERIFIED`, `PROMOTED` and `RELEASED` are Closeout residue.** **The reconciliation is: retire what has shipped, move what is genuinely in flight under `## Current`, and leave `## Module assignment` describing ownership only.**

### B-403 · A merge interleaved two bug rows, and the check that should have seen it went blind instead

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository records — [`docs/BUGS.md`](BUGS.md), and the instrument `infra/registers.py` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — `infra/` is Platform Foundation ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), and **both scrambled rows are this office's** ([B-328](#b-328--state-checkpy-reports-54-ready-tasks-when-there-are-two-because-it-counts-headings), [B-401](#b-401--04-modulesmd-disagrees-with-backendmodules-in-four-places)) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Wrong information a lane would act on**, in the register every lane reads at Startup step 3 — **and it is on `main`** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06.** Rows separated, fence restored, `unclosed_fence()` added and wired into `state-check`. **QE verifies; the lane that fixed it does not close it** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane C, running `state-check` during a routine poll — **by disbelieving its finding rather than by acting on it** |
| **Commit found** | On `main` at `1984545`, `integration` at `023e0d0` and `lane-qe` — **promoted, and carried through certification cycles** |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
python3 infra/state-check.py | grep -i conflict
→ docs/BUGS.md carries an unresolved merge-conflict marker at line(s) 2043.

sed -n '2042,2044p' docs/BUGS.md
→ a fence opener, then the marker, then the closer
```

**Expected.** Nothing reported — that marker is **inside a fenced block**, quoting [B-102](#b-102--a-conflict-marker-committed-promoted-and-carried-through-several-certification-cycles)'s own evidence, and `conflict_markers()` documents that it skips fences.

> ⚡ **This row's first draft opened with a nested fence and the new check fired on it inside a minute** — the same way [B-102](#b-102--a-conflict-marker-committed-promoted-and-carried-through-several-certification-cycles)'s check fired on B-102's own row. **A register documenting a corruption keeps trying to become one**, which is the argument for both guards rather than a curiosity.

**Actual.** Reported. **And the reason it was reported is the defect, not the report.**

### Two rows wearing each other's clothes

**A merge interleaved [B-328](#b-328--state-checkpy-reports-54-ready-tasks-when-there-are-two-because-it-counts-headings) and [B-401](#b-401--04-modulesmd-disagrees-with-backendmodules-in-four-places):**

| Lines | Held | Should have held |
|---|---|---|
| 197–203 | **B-328's table** | ✅ correct |
| 205–213 | **B-401's heading and table** | ⛔ **B-328's body** |
| 215–249 | **B-328's body**, under B-401's heading | ⛔ |
| 251+ | **B-401's body — with `**Steps to reproduce.**` and its opening ```` ```bash ```` destroyed** | ⛔ |

⚡ **The missing opener is what carried the damage past its own two rows.** **A single unclosed fence inverts parity for the entire remaining file** — 1,790 lines of it — and `state-check`'s own output shows both halves: `B-322 has no Severity` was **the same defect**, reported as if it were a second one.

### The half that matters, and it is not the noise

⛔ **In the inverted region the check does not merely over-report — it is *blind*.** Every marker in prose is read as fenced and skipped; only quoted ones are reported. **`conflict_markers()` was doing the exact opposite of its job across two thirds of the register**, and it would have said nothing at all about a genuine marker there.

> **A guard that reasons about structure must first establish that the structure holds.** Its silence otherwise carries no information — which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s *decorative logic* exactly: **removal would not have changed the property it claims to protect**, because it was not protecting it.

### Why nothing caught it

**Third instance of [ADR-0039](architecture/adr/0039-release-engineering-model.md) RC-4** — *the registers are a multi-writer database written in markdown* — after [B-100](#b-100--a-lanes-rebase-silently-reverted-the-execution-board-by-seven-cycles-and-every-gate-passed) and [B-102](#b-102--a-conflict-marker-committed-promoted-and-carried-through-several-certification-cycles). ⚡ **And this one got past the check *built for B-102*, which is the new information: RC-4's answer cannot be another markdown-reading check.**

**It is also [B-101](#b-101--the-kpi-block-counted-nine-bug-rows-twice-under-a-banner-promising-nothing-was-typed-by-hand)'s class** — counting by proxy. **Fence parity was the proxy for *"am I inside code?"***, and nothing ever asked whether the proxy was sound.

### The fix

**`unclosed_fence(text) -> int | None`** in `infra/registers.py`, checked by `state-check` across all four registers **before** the marker check, so a reader learns the structure is broken rather than reading a conclusion drawn from broken structure. **Five tests**, including one asserting the blindness directly — **the only half no assertion about `conflict_markers` could catch, since its answer is empty either way.**

**What it does not fix.** The register is still hand-merged, so the **next** corruption is a different shape again. ⛔ **This is now the third time that sentence has been written in this file**, and RC-4's actual answer remains ADR-0039's to propose and the product owner's to schedule.

### B-329 · 101 of B-211's 238 ruff errors are Lane B's, and twelve of them ask for an API rename no lane may make

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Ten of this lane's thirteen** — `integrations` 41 · `knowledge_graph` 20 · `opportunity_engine` 13 · `timeline` 5 · `commercial_profile` 5 · `sales_engagement` 5 · `people` 5 · `action_batch` 3 · `ai_platform` 3 · `observation_engine` 1 |
| **Current assignee** | ⏸️ **Lane A on paper, parked in practice — [D-157](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④, 2026-08-07.** ⚡ **Lint debt, not a customer-visible defect.** ⛔ **It moves no journey forward, so it waits behind the migration** — *"Anything that does not materially move these journeys forward should be deferred unless it blocks the active workflow."* ✅ **Traceability preserved: the row stays open and assigned, and the reason it is not being worked is stated here rather than left to be inferred from silence** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **not blocking today.** Nothing invokes ruff ([B-211](#b-211--ruff-check--fails-with-238-errors-on-integration-and-no-gate-has-ever-run-it)), so no gate is red because of these. **It becomes blocking the moment QE wires the gate in**, which is what B-211 exists to do |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by **Lane B**, measuring its own share after B-211 landed |

**Steps.** From `backend/`, on `integration` with a clean tree:

```
.venv/bin/ruff check . --output-format=concise | grep -E '^(modules|tests)/(integrations|provider_normalization|knowledge_graph|observation_engine|timeline|opportunity_engine|ai_reasoning_engine|commercial_profile|sales_engagement|people|action_batch|ai_platform|business_event_engine)/' | wc -l
```

**Expected.** `0`, or a named defect explaining why not.

**Actual.** **101.** ⚡ **This is the largest single share of B-211's 238 — four times Lane A's 26 — and B-211 does not mention it**, because that row was written by the lane that measured its own modules and correctly stopped there. **Recorded here so the total is accounted for rather than discovered a third time.**

#### The split is the finding, not the 101

| Rule | Count | Fixable by this lane? |
|---|---|---|
| `E501` line length · `I001` import order · `F401` unused import · `UP037` quoted annotation | **77** | ✅ **Yes — mechanical.** `F401` needs reading first: an unused import inside a `public/__init__.py` is a **deliberate re-export**, not a defect |
| `UP035` deprecated import · `B905` bare `zip` · `B008` call in a default · `B017` blind `except` · `SIM102` · `SIM113` | **12** | ⚠️ **Case by case.** `B905` changes runtime behaviour — `strict=` turns a silent truncation into a raise, which is usually right and is never a lint fix |
| **`N818`** exception name lacks an `Error` suffix | **12** | ⛔ **No. This one needs a ruling** |

#### Why `N818` is not a lint fix

`AlreadyConnected` · `UnknownIntegration` · `ConnectionNotFound` · `SecretNotFound` · `CredentialUnreadable` · `ConnectionUnusable` · `GrantExpired` · `GrantRevoked` · `CrmTransient` · `CrmPermanent` · `OpportunityNotFound` · `UnprojectableEvent`.

**Every one of them is a domain exception named in domain vocabulary**, which is what [§4](../CLAUDE.md) asks for. `GrantExpired` is the ubiquitous language; `GrantExpiredError` is the linter's. ⚡ **The two rules disagree, and a lane picking the linter over the constitution would be taking an architectural decision inside a tidy-up** — the exact shape [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) warns about, *"the change that follows is always small, which is why nobody notices it was a decision."*

⛔ **And one of the twelve is published.** `ConnectionUnusable` is exported from `modules/integrations/public/__init__.py`, so renaming it is a **published-contract change** — 🟠 at best, and ⚫ *Rename an API* on its face. **The other eleven are module-internal**, which is why this is a ruling about a convention rather than twelve separate questions.

> **Three outcomes are available and all are defensible**: adopt the suffix and rename · **add `N818` to `[tool.ruff.lint] ignore` with the DDD reason stated in `pyproject.toml`** · keep the rule and add per-file exemptions for domain layers. **This lane's recommendation is the second** — the convention it enforces is a Python-stdlib habit, and this repository has an explicit, ratified rule that domain vocabulary wins at the module boundary. ⛔ **Recommendation only; the ruff configuration is repository-wide and not this lane's to change.**

#### Left unfixed, deliberately, and this is the part to sequence

⛔ **No sweep was performed.** Lane A reached the identical decision on its 26 one commit earlier, for the identical reason: **the queue is at `eligible_count = 1` and that one row is blocked, but a dry queue is not a licence to self-assign** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). **A repository-wide lint sweep is also better done once, sequenced by whoever owns the gate, than by three lanes independently rewriting import blocks that will conflict on every rebase.**

**What this row buys:** the 238 is now fully attributed — **101 Lane B · 26 Lane A · 111 shared surface** (`tests/integration` 57, `migrations/versions` 27, `apps/` 10, and the rest) — so B-211's fix can be planned against a known total instead of a headline number.

#### Three findings from tracing the gate, 2026-08-07 — and each changes what B-211 has to plan for

**① `ruff format --check` is a second gate in the same workflow, and nobody has measured it.** `backend.yml` defines **four** steps — `ruff check`, **`ruff format --check`**, `mypy` and import-linter. B-211 measured the first. The second reports **169 files would be reformatted, 73 of them this lane's** (`integrations` 27 · `opportunity_engine` 11 · `knowledge_graph` 9 · `ai_platform` 5 · `commercial_profile` 4 · `sales_engagement` 4 · `timeline` 3 · six modules with 2 each).

**② ruff has *zero* live callers, not one.** ⚠️ **B-211 states *"the only remaining caller is the production image build"*. Measured, it is not a caller** — `grep -rn ruff` across `Dockerfile*`, `Makefile`, `*.sh`, `*.yml` returns only `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and the `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow. ⛔ **And `.git/hooks/` contains nothing but samples, with `core.hooksPath` unset**, so the pre-commit config is **configured and uninstalled**. **A third gate that cannot fail** — the same shape as B-211's own finding, one layer further out. ⛔ **Not corrected in B-211 itself: that row is QE's, and §20e makes this a report rather than an edit.**

**③ Installing pre-commit today would rewrite code on commit.** `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs **`ruff check --fix`**, not `--check`. ✅ **The obvious hazard was checked and does not exist**: **no `F401` in the repository sits in a `public/__init__.py`**, so no deliberate re-export would be deleted. **All nine are genuinely unused imports.** ⚡ **Recorded because the check is what makes the reassurance worth anything** — the risk was real enough to test, and asserting it either way without testing would have been the guess this register exists to prevent.

#### Why no sweep, restated on evidence rather than on precedent

⚠️ **The first version of this row argued from Lane A's identical decision. Finding ① gives a better reason.** **`ruff format` overlaps `ruff check` on the largest rule in the set**: **44 of this lane's 101 are `E501`**, and line length is precisely what a formatter rewrites. **Fixing them by hand is work `ruff format` would redo**, against a configuration nobody has chosen yet — `line-length` is currently 100, `N818` may be ignored or enforced, and both are repository-wide settings.

> ⛔ **So the sequencing is not a preference.** **Decide the configuration · run the formatter once · then fix what `ruff check` still reports.** **A lane hand-fixing 101 errors first produces a ~150-file diff that conflicts with every other lane's rebase and is then partly reformatted anyway.** ⚡ **That is an argument about cost and order, not about willingness** — the code half is this lane's and it will be done the moment the configuration is settled.

### B-211 · `ruff check .` fails with 238 errors on `integration`, and no gate has ever run it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **The backend gate set** — `Makefile` (`validate`) and `.github/workflows/backend.yml` |
| **Current assignee** | **QE.** The `Makefile` is Platform Foundation's ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), **but the gate half is QE's under §20e's own test** — this changes *what a lane is told to run before handing over*, not what a target means. Same split recorded on [B-107](#b-107) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Blocking Quality Defect.** No customer behaviour is wrong. **A required check is red across the whole tree and nothing invokes it**, so every lane hands over believing it passed |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-07 by Lane A, checking `apps/worker/subscriptions.py` after a duplicate-import report from another lane |

**Steps.** From `backend/`, on `integration` with a clean tree: `.venv/bin/ruff check .`

**Expected.** Clean, or a named defect explains why it is not.

**Actual.** **238 errors, 67 fixable.** The ruff in the tree is **0.16.0 — byte-identical to the version `uv.lock` pins**, so this is not version skew; CI would report the same 238.

**Why nothing caught it — and this is the finding, not the 238.** The check exists and is correct. **Nothing calls it.**

- **`.github/workflows/backend.yml` defines `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy .` and import-linter — and its only trigger is `workflow_dispatch`.** The file opens *"⚠️ INTENTIONALLY DISABLED — Local-First Development Policy"* and instructs that `push:` and `pull_request:` are not to be added. **That policy is deliberate and is not the defect**; it rests on the premise that *"every check below already runs locally"*.
- **`make validate` runs migrate · tsc · vitest · pytest.** It does not run ruff. **So the premise does not hold**, and the only remaining caller is the production image build.

> ⚡ **This is [B-115](#b-115--task-301-fails-mypy---strict-on-a-test-helper-narrower-than-the-type-it-builds)'s class for the third time, and the first time for Python's linter.** B-115 established that *"the gate is `mypy --strict .` from `backend/`, and the difference is `tests/`"*; [B-133](#b-133) established the same for `eslint .`. **Both lessons were recorded as *widen the path you check*. Neither noticed that one of the four checks had no path at all** — a gate that cannot fail (§2), by never being invoked rather than by being wrong.

**The instance that surfaced it.** `apps/worker/subscriptions.py` reports **7 errors: five `F811` redefinitions, one `I001`, one pre-existing `N818`.** The five are `build_business_event_queries`, `build_graph_queries`, `build_observation_queries`, `SqlClaimReader` and `build_signal_queries`, each imported twice. **Every second import binds the same name to the same object, so this is genuinely redundant and not a shadow** — verified by reading both import lists, not inferred from the rule name. ⛔ **Not fixed here.** `apps/` is not this lane's, the file is in flight, and §20e is explicit: *finding a defect outside your assignment is an obligation to report it, never permission to fix it.*

**What is Lane A's.** **26 of the 238 fall in this lane's six modules** — 24 in `ai_research_engine` and its tests, one `SIM102` in `workspace_tenancy`, one `UP037` in `buying_score_engine`. **Two are `F401` unused imports, which is [B-133](#b-133)'s exact defect class.** All were last written 2026-07-31 → 2026-08-03 and **predate this lane's current slices**, so they are accumulation, not regression. ⛔ **Left unfixed deliberately**: the queue is at `eligible_count = 0` and a lane does not self-assign (§20e). **They are named here so they can be sequenced rather than discovered again.**

|---|---|

| **Severity** | 🟡 · **Wrong but survivable.** The two journeys it names are supposed to run on *every* frontend change, so the one that does not exist has never run on any |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane A, following [D-113](DECISION_REGISTER.md) on [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) — computing the plan rather than choosing the journeys |

**Steps.** `python3 infra/certification-guard.py --plan integration..HEAD` on any narrow frontend change, then `ls frontend/tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`.

**Expected.** Every journey named by the plan exists and can be run.

**Actual.** `JOURNEYS_ALWAYS` is `{"golden-journey", "accessibility"}`. **There is no `golden-journey.spec.ts`** — the fourteen specs are `accessibility`, `auth-journey`, `business-setup`, `commercial-profile`, `confidence`, `connections`, `consistency`, `daily-usage`, `interaction-boundaries`, `perception`, `permissions.member`, `resilience`, `visual`, `workflow`.

> ⚡ **The always-run set is the one place the mapping cannot afford to be wrong**, because it is the part no path selects into and therefore the part no lane double-checks. **A lane following the plan literally runs `playwright test golden-journey`, which matches nothing and exits reporting no failures** — a gate that cannot fail (§2).

⚠️ **And [`CLAUDE.md` §19](../CLAUDE.md) names the flag as `--journeys`**, which the tool does not accept; the capability is `--plan REV_RANGE`. **Reported rather than corrected**: that file is the product owner's.

### B-209 · Eleven Playwright journeys fail on `integration`, and the header search is why

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **The repository-wide journey suite** — `frontend/tests/e2e/pages/business.ts` and the specs that use it |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — §20e: QE *"creates, maintains, extends and retires repository-wide automated tests; lanes own the tests specific to the slices they implement"* |
| **Severity** | 🔴 · **Blocking Quality Defect — failing tests.** Eleven journeys, including four `@journey` and five `@regression` |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — QE, 2026-08-09.** ⛔ **Open for six days, and the gate that should have stopped every promotion in that window was blind** ([B-413](BUGS.md)) |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane A, running the full journey suite for [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) before handing over |

**Steps.** Seed a lane environment, `npx playwright test`, on `integration` with nothing else changed.

**Expected.** The suite passes, or a named defect explains why it does not.

**Actual.** Eleven fail, all on the same line:

```
locator.fill: strict mode violation: getByLabel('Name') resolved to 2 elements:
  1) <input aria-label="Find an account by name" …>   ← the shell header search
  2) <input id="_r_0_" placeholder="Revenue Cloud" …> ← the product dialog
```

**`getByLabel` matches a substring, and the shell header is on every screen.** `business.productName` asks for *Name* and the header search's accessible name — *Find an account by **name*** — contains it. **Nothing about the product is wrong**: both labels are good, and the second is exactly the specificity [ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) asks for.

> ⛔ **Verified as not this lane's change, and verified twice.** The spec fails with Lane A's working tree stashed, **and it fails on `integration` itself** with the branch checked out clean. **The clashing `aria-label` is on `origin/main`.**
>
> ⚡ **The fix is one word — `exact: true`, or `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Name', exact: true })`** — and it belongs to whoever owns the page object. **Reported rather than fixed**: finding a defect outside the assignment is an obligation to report it, never permission to fix it (§20e), and a lane editing QE's suite is how a shared suite acquires two authors.

⚠️ **What this says about the gate is worth more than the fix.** [D-113](DECISION_REGISTER.md) made running the journeys the *lane's* responsibility before handover, and **this is the first slice to run the whole suite from a lane** — the eleven have presumably been failing for as long as the header search has existed on the business page. **A journey suite nobody runs end to end is a plan, not a gate.**

---


### ✅ Fixed — two instances, one word, and the second was evidence rather than a guess

| | |
|---|---|
| `pages/business.ts:37` | `getByLabel('Name')` → **`getByLabel('Name', { exact: true })`** — the getter B-209 names |
| `commercial-profile.spec.ts:174` | **The same defect on the second browser context.** ⚡ **`colleague` opens the same dialog on the same shell**, so a bare `Name` matched the header search there too |

⛔ **QE checked the second before changing it rather than fixing every bare `getByLabel` on sight.** **The `auth-journey` ones are on `/sign-in` and `/sign-up`, which carry no App Shell header** — changing a passing test on a pattern match is the [B-411](#b-411) failure in the other direction.

### 🔴 The six days, and they are QE's to account for

**§20e: *"`integration` never fast-forwards to `main` with an open 🔴 bug."*** ⛔ **This row was 🔴 and `OPEN` from 2026-08-06, and there have been 70 Closeout commits since.**

**The gate that enforces the rule reported `No unresolved 🔴 — promotion is not blocked` on every one of them, and it was wrong** — [B-413](BUGS.md), found by Lane C: **`unresolved` required the state token at character zero while the register writes `**`OPEN`**`, so 29 of 39 open rows read as resolved and `blocks_promotion` returned `False` for every row in the file.**

> ⚠️ **QE is not claiming the promotions were harmless — that is not knowable in retrospect.** ⛔ **What is knowable: the rule was not enforced, QE did not notice, and the reason QE did not notice is that QE read the gate's answer instead of the register.** ⚡ **[B-151](#b-151--qe-published-blocking-quality-defects-none-for-eleven-cycles-while-two-were-open) said exactly this about a different line three cycles ago, and QE fixed the sentence rather than the habit.**

### B-208 · Global Search crashes the moment it finds anything

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Product Surface** — `components/intelligence/account-search.tsx` · `lib/query/hooks/search.ts` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — Product Surface is its in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Wrong behaviour a customer hits immediately.** [MC-1](PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md) calls search *"the first thing every evaluator types"* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane A**, 2026-08-06, inside [TASK-460](BACKLOG.md), which owns this surface. **`VERIFIED` is QE's** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane A, running TASK-460's reuse audit before writing code |
**Steps to reproduce.** Sign in, type three characters of a known company into the header search.
**Expected.** A list of matches.
**Actual.** The dropdown throws. `key={row.account.account_id}` reads `.account_id` of `undefined`.
### The two sides of one contract disagree, and each is internally consistent
| **The API returns** | `list[SearchGroupResponse]` — **one group per `EntityKind`**, each with `result_type`, `coverage` and `results` |
| **The hook asks for** | `SearchResult[]` — **a flat list**, the shape that preceded [TASK-408](BACKLOG.md) |
| **The component does** | `rows.map((row) => row.account.account_id)` — **so every element is a group being read as a result** |
**`TASK-408` changed the response to groups and the frontend was never moved.** The backend's own test helper records the change and reads through it:
> *"**Search returns groups from TASK-408**, one per `EntityKind`, each saying whether Signora looked. These tests were written against the flat list that preceded the ruling."*
### Why three gates all missed it
| **`tsc`** | The shape is asserted at the fetch — `apiRequest<SearchResult[]>` — and **a type parameter on a JSON call is a claim, not a check** |
| **The frontend test** | Mocks `useAccountSearch` itself and feeds it flat `SearchResult` objects. **It tests the component against a shape the API does not return** |
| **The backend test** | Flattens groups through `_rows()` before asserting, deliberately and reasonably — it is testing matches, not grouping |
> **Each gate was reasonable alone.** ⚡ **What nothing owned was the seam**: a test that mocks the hook cannot see the contract, and a test that flattens the response cannot see the client. **The one place the two shapes meet is a browser, and no test runs there** — `e2e/` is Playwright and search is not in it.
**Fix.** [TASK-460](BACKLOG.md) is *"the existing account search raised to the approved specification: typed grouping across the object kinds that exist"* — **so the correct fix and the claimed slice are the same work**, and the grouping the API already sends is now what the surface renders.

### B-207 · An expired score renders as *no score* — **withdrawn, and the mistake is the interesting part**
| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | **Product Surface** — the attention list. `frontend/components/intelligence/attention.tsx` |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane A** — Product Surface is its in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), and this lane wrote the component |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Wrong behaviour a customer would hit**, on the first screen they see, about the number the screen is sorted by |
| **Status** | ⛔ **`CLOSED` — withdrawn by the lane that raised it**, 2026-08-06, within the hour, on checking the composed row rather than the component. **The id is retired and never reused.** **There is no defect: the surface already says *Evidence expired*** — see the correction below |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06, `bcea8ba` |
**Steps to reproduce.** Open the homepage with an account whose buying score has expired — `score: null` on `AccountAttentionResponse`.
**Expected.** *"We scored this, and the evidence behind it is no longer current."*
**Actual.** An em dash, labelled **`"No current score"`**.
```tsx
export function AttentionScore({ score }: { score: number | null }) {
  if (score === null) {
    return <span aria-label="No current score">—</span>;
  }
```
### The API says what null means, and it does not mean absent
**`opportunity_engine/interface/schemas.py`, in the published OpenAPI description a consumer reads:**
> ***"Commercial attention, 0–100… Null when the evidence behind it has expired — the opportunity is still open and the number that justified it is no longer current."***
**So `null` carries a specific, actionable fact and the surface renders it as an absence.** A seller reading `—` concludes *Signora has nothing on this account*; the truth is *Signora had something and it went stale*, on an opportunity that **is still open**. **Those demand opposite actions** — the first is a reason to ignore the row, the second is a reason to distrust the ranking it is sitting in.
### It is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md), and the repository already knows the pattern
**[C-226](LANE_COORDINATION.md) is this exact class** — *a failed read rendering as an empty account* — and this lane fixed three sections of it in [TASK-417](BACKLOG.md). **The account brief already does it correctly**: a 404 from the score read renders *"Nothing has scored this account yet"* and any other error renders *"Could not load this account"*, because **never scored** and **could not find out** are different sentences.
> **The list never got the third one.** The brief distinguishes *never* from *failed*; **nothing anywhere distinguishes *expired*** — and expired is the only one of the three that the attention list can actually be showing, because a row is there precisely because an opportunity is open.
### Why it survived review
**The component is right about everything else and says so at length** — why the score is typographic rather than a gauge, why it is subordinate to the account name. ⚡ **`aria-label="No current score"` is even *literally* true**: there is no current score. **It is the inference a reader draws that is wrong**, which is why no test caught it and why reading the component does not reveal it. **The defect is only visible against the API contract**, and [453](architecture/453-opportunity-intelligence-traceability-audit.md) is what put the two side by side.
⛔ ### Withdrawn — 2026-08-06, by Lane A, an hour after filing
**Everything above reads `AttentionScore` on its own. The row that composes it already says the thing.**
```tsx
// app/(app)/page.tsx — the status lane, immediately before the score column
<ContestedMark contested={account.contested} />
<EvidenceHealth evidence={account.evidence} />   // ← "Evidence expired"
...
<AttentionScore score={account.score} />          // ← "—"
```
**And the two cannot disagree**, which is the fact that settles it:
```python
# opportunity_engine/application/queries.py
def evidence_state(opportunity, score, moment) -> EvidenceState:
    if score is None or not score.is_valid_at(moment):
        return EvidenceState.STALE
```
> ## **`score is None` implies `stale`, by construction. Every row with an em dash carries the *Evidence expired* badge, one element to its left.**
**So the surface is correct and is arguably better than what this row proposed.** The badge states *why there is no number*; the em dash states *that there is no number*. **Two facts, each where it belongs** — and putting the word *expired* into the score column would have said one of them twice, in the column the page is scanned down.
### What this lane got wrong, recorded rather than quietly deleted
**The filing judged an element in isolation and drew a conclusion the composition does not support.** ⚡ **That is the same error this lane had criticised [447](architecture/447-signal-center-traceability-audit.md) for one poll earlier** — counting a thing as present without checking the context it lives in — **committed while writing up [C-228](LANE_COORDINATION.md), which is the item making that criticism.**
**The `aria-label` observation was the tell and was misread.** *"No current score"* is literally true, and this row treated its literal truth as evidence that a reader would infer something false. **The reader is not reading the label alone either.**
⚠️ **What survives, and it is small.** **`AttentionScore` is also called by `NeedsIdentity`**, where no `EvidenceHealth` badge sits beside it — so a company nobody can name shows an em dash with nothing explaining it. **That is not this row's claim** (it asserted a defect on the attention list, where the badge exists) and it is not a defect either: an account with no identity has no evidence health to state. **Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it.**
**[TASK-441](BACKLOG.md)'s rule is unaffected and still binds** — *"an expired score must render as expired, never as absent and never as current."* **The lesson for that screen is now concrete rather than theoretical: the badge is where expiry is said, and the new screen must carry it rather than inventing a second way to say the same thing.**
### B-402 · `ENGINEERING_LAWS.md` is classified `platform`, so editing it demands a DR run

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `infra/certification-guard.py` — `CLOSEOUT_PATHS` |
| **Current assignee** | ⚠️ **QE.** **`certification-guard.py` is named in `CLAUDE.md` §20e as QE's**, and this constant decides **what may promote as a Closeout** — so changing it changes what a gate *means*. ⛔ **Lane C found it while building on the classifier and may not repair it** |
| **Severity** | 🟡 — **nothing is wrong today; the plan is too wide rather than too narrow**, which is the safe direction. **It becomes 🟠 the moment a lane distrusts the plan and starts ignoring it** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — reported with evidence, **not fixed: it is a gate's meaning** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane C, **testing the [D-115](DECISION_REGISTER.md) validation planner against a real diff** rather than by reading the constant |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
python3 infra/certification-guard.py --plan origin/main..HEAD
→   Impacts
      documentation  CLAUDE.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md (+11)
      platform       ENGINEERING_LAWS.md, docs/coordination/queues/lane-a.toml (+5)
    Gates (16)  … dr, migration-reversibility, prompt-evaluation …
```

**Expected.** **Two governance markdown files at the repository root classify alike.**
**Actual.** **`CLAUDE.md` is `documentation` and `ENGINEERING_LAWS.md` is `platform`** — so **a governance edit demands `dr`, `migration-reversibility` and `prompt-evaluation`.**

### The cause is one missing entry, and the comment above it predicted this class

```python
CLOSEOUT_PATHS = ("certification/", "docs/", "PROJECT_STATUS.md", "README.md", "CLAUDE.md")
```

⚡ **`ENGINEERING_LAWS.md` is not in it, and it is the Repository Engineering Standard** — `CLAUDE.md` §19 and §20e both delegate to it. **It sits at the root beside `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`, and only it is missing.**

⚠️ **The classifier's own comment records the identical defect being fixed once already**: *"The first real run of this analysis classified `CLAUDE.md` as `platform` — it is not under `docs/`… Two classifiers in one file, disagreeing on their first disagreement."* **The fix shared the rule; it did not complete the list.**

### Why the direction matters more than the instance

✅ **The plan is too *wide*, which is the correct failure.** [D-114](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s rule — *unknown widens, never narrows* — worked exactly as designed and this defect is what it looks like when it fires.

⚠️ **But a plan that demands a disaster-recovery run to edit a markdown file is one lanes will learn to ignore**, and an ignored plan is worse than no plan. **That is the cost, and it is why this is filed rather than tolerated.**

### The fix, for QE

**Add `ENGINEERING_LAWS.md` to `CLOSEOUT_PATHS`.** ⚠️ **And check the rest of the root** — `IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md`, `PRODUCT_DIFFERENTIATORS.md` and any other root governance file have the same shape. ⛔ **Lane C did not enumerate them, because proposing the full list would be proposing the fix.**

**Regression guard.** ✅ **Available and cheap**: assert every tracked root-level `.md` classifies as `documentation`. **A new governance file added at the root then fails visibly rather than silently demanding a DR run.**

### B-328 · `state-check.py` reports 54 `READY` tasks when there are two, because it counts headings

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `infra/state-check.py` — the backlog summary line, check 5c |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — `infra/` is Platform Foundation ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), and [B-125](#b-125--the-new-document-location-check-silently-no-ops-on-a-clone-without-originintegration) is already assigned there for this same file |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Reassuring rather than merely wrong.** *"54 READY"* reads as a healthy queue on a day when two rows are `READY` and both are blocked |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06.** **QE verifies; the lane that fixed it does not close it.** ⚡ **Fixed independently and hours apart** — this office found the same defect while writing [D-099](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s queue work and corrected it in the same commit, and Lane B's `B-328` commit dropped as a duplicate on rebase. **Both diagnoses were right and the second cost one rebase to discover** — recorded as [C-103](LANE_COORDINATION.md)'s second instance. **The line now reads `Backlog: 61 task(s), 9 startable (…)`, and it lists the ids** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-06 by Lane B, checking its own reporting against the gate after [C-333](LANE_COORDINATION.md) added seven queue validations |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
python3 infra/state-check.py | grep 'Backlog:'
→ ok   Backlog: 69 task(s), 54 READY, no task claimed twice.

grep -oE '^\| \*\*Status\*\* \| [^|]{0,40}' docs/BACKLOG.md \
  | sed 's/| \*\*Status\*\* | //; s/[*`]//g' | awk '{print $1, $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
→ 20 IN VALIDATION · 16 SEQUENCED · 4 DONE · 3 PROMOTED · 3 IN PROGRESS
   2 ✅ READY · 2 ⏸️ BLOCKED · 1 RATIFIED · 1 DISPOSED · 1 DISPOSED · 1 WAITING
```

**Expected.** The count of rows whose status is `READY`.
**Actual.** **54 — the number of `### TASK-nnn` headings**, which is neither the `READY` count (2) nor the task count (69, which the same line reports separately and correctly).

### The line

```python
ready = len(re.findall(r"^### TASK-\d+", backlog, re.M))
notes.append(f"Backlog: {len(known)} task(s), {ready} READY, no task claimed twice.")
```

**It never reads a status.** `_STARTABLE = {"READY", "CHANGES REQUESTED"}` exists twenty lines above and is not consulted here.

### Why 🟠 rather than cosmetic

**This is the only number in the gate's output that answers *"how much claimable work exists?"***, and it is the number a session would quote. **It is wrong in the reassuring direction**, which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s class exactly: a repository asserting something untrue is worse than one that says nothing, *because it is trusted*.

⚠️ **And [C-333](LANE_COORDINATION.md) has just made queue health a validated concern.** One of its seven checks is *"`READY` rows in no queue"* — **which cannot be doing what it claims if `READY` is being read this way anywhere else in the file.** Worth checking whether the two share a helper; **this row does not assume they do.**

### What it cost, and it is not hypothetical

**This lane matched the same status the wrong way and reported *"zero `READY` rows"* across four polls.** The right answer is **two — [TASK-201](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md), both externally blocked** — so every conclusion drawn from it survived, and the phrasing did not. **The emoji prefix is what both readers missed**: the rows are `✅ READY`, not `` `READY` ``.

> **Two independent readers got the same field wrong on the same day, in opposite directions.** That is the argument for the status being **parsed once, in one place**, rather than pattern-matched wherever it is needed.

### B-327 · Three documents say the Executive Dashboard's ICP section is buildable, and a coordination item on `integration` says it is not

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Repository records — [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md)'s TASK-438 row · [444](architecture/444-executive-dashboard-domain-assessment.md) · [448](architecture/448-icp-builder-traceability-audit.md) · [`DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md`](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) |
| **Current assignee** | **Lane C** — all four are its documents, and the registers are its to reconcile |
| **Severity** | 🟠 · **Wrong information a lane would act on.** It already produced a `READY` row with an unbuildable section |
| **Status** | ✅ **`FIXED` — 2026-08-06, all seven documents.** **QE verifies; the lane that fixed it does not close it** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-05 by Lane B, claiming [TASK-438](BACKLOG.md) and reading its acceptance before writing |
| **Commit found** | `f14db51e` — and [C-332](LANE_COORDINATION.md) landed at `714f4663`, **one commit earlier** |

**Steps to reproduce.**

```bash
git log --oneline --reverse 714f4663..f14db51e
→ 714f4663 C-332 — the predicate is on main and nothing can call it
  ...
  f14db51e 448 — ICP Builder, and the screen the product owner named split R-01 in two

grep -c "C-332" docs/architecture/448-icp-builder-traceability-audit.md
→ 0
```

**Expected.** A document merged after C-332 either reflects it or says why not.
**Actual.** Four records assert the opposite of it, and none mentions it.

### The four claims, and what each would cause

| Where | What it says | What it causes |
|---|---|---|
| **[TASK-438](BACKLOG.md)**, *"The fifth, newly unblocked"* | *"**ICP coverage** — ⚡ TASK-434 is `PROMOTED`, so *in-ICP versus outside* is **a call to a published predicate***" | **The most expensive one.** A `READY` row telling the claiming lane that a section needs nothing |
| **[444 §108](architecture/444-executive-dashboard-domain-assessment.md)** | TASK-438 is *"**the five sections that need nothing** — conversion, ageing, movement, roll-up by owner, ICP coverage… **it needs no answer from anybody**"* | The row above derives from this |
| **[448 §7](architecture/448-icp-builder-traceability-audit.md)** | **R-00 matching — ✅ *"Shipped. Validated by the screen that needed it most"*** | Tells the cross-screen view a capability is available |
| **[`DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md`](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md)** row 8 · row 14 | *"⚡ R-00 shipped and validated here"* · Executive Dashboard *"**in-ICP cohort ✅**"* | **Sixteen consumers read R-00 to decide whether they are blocked** |

### Why the claim does not survive checking

**What shipped at [TASK-434](BACKLOG.md) is a predicate.** `evaluate(icp, observed)` is correct, promoted, and takes an `ObservedAttributes`.

> **Nothing in `backend/modules/` constructs one**, and the only module that could — `knowledge_graph`, which alone holds the `entity_id → SubjectRef` binding `ClaimReader` needs — is **forbidden to `opportunity_engine` in full.** [05](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md) gives that module one upstream edge and it is the Buying Score Engine.

**"Shipped" is true of the predicate and false of the capability**, and the register does not distinguish them — which is the whole defect. **A predicate nothing can call is a foundation, not a capability**, and [443 §2](architecture/443-account-matching-capability.md) already said so by decomposing matching into four milestones: **M2 shipped, M4 is TASK-406, and the step that turns claims into the values M2 compares is in neither.**

### It is not hypothetical — it has already cost something

**Lane B claimed TASK-438 on the strength of that row**, discovered the fifth section on the reuse audit, and **delivered four sections rather than five**. That is the cheap outcome. **The expensive one was available**: a lane that trusted *"a call to a published predicate"* would have built the arithmetic and met the missing input at the end.

### The fix, and it was one line of judgement rather than seven edits

**Decide what R-00 means, then say it once.** *"Shipped"* is defensible for M2 and misleading for the capability — so the register needed the distinction it collapsed. **Every downstream document then derives from it**, which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s rule: truth has exactly one authoritative representation.

> ## **The word adopted, and it is now the register's: *implemented, not usable*.**
>
> **A promoted predicate with no reachable caller is a foundation, not a capability.** **Both halves are true and stating only the first is what cost Lane B a section.**

### ⚡ The fix ran twice, and the second half is a Product Office finding

**Two reconciliations happened on 2026-08-06 and neither knew about the other**, because **they were filed under one id and I did not notice.**

| | Documents | When |
|---|---|---|
| **① [D-094](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s reconciliation** | **[443](architecture/443-account-matching-capability.md) · [TASK-406](BACKLOG.md)'s row · [Register](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) rows 312/346 · [461](architecture/461-product-led-domain-discovery-review.md)** | 2026-08-06, morning |
| ⚠️ **② The three this row actually named** | **[444](architecture/444-executive-dashboard-domain-assessment.md) §42 and §108 · [448](architecture/448-icp-builder-traceability-audit.md) §129 and §143 · [Register](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) rows 8, 14, 69 and the coverage matrix** | **2026-08-06, on [D-099](DECISION_REGISTER.md) — after the row already read `FIXED`** |

> ⛔ **So this row read `FIXED` for part of a day while three of the documents it names still said the section was buildable.** **The duplicate id is what concealed it**: two rows under `B-327` meant the fix row and the report row were never read together, and each looked complete on its own.
>
> ⚡ **`state-check` caught the duplicate id and could not have caught the partial fix** — it compares identifiers, not claims. **The instrument found the *cause* and a human had to find the *consequence*, which is the honest division and worth recording rather than smoothing over.**

### Regression guard

⛔ **None, and deliberately.** **A document agreeing with a *capability's reachability* is not mechanically checkable** — `state-check` can compare a document to a commit, not a claim to a codebase. **Saying so beats a check that would pretend to cover it.**

✅ **What *is* now guarded is the thing that hid it.** The duplicate-identifier check already existed and worked; **what was missing was reading its output before declaring the fix complete.** **[D-099](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes `state-check` a precondition of closing any Product Office row, not a report written after one.**

### B-325 · B-118's fix allocates Lane B its own database, and the document that tells a lane how to run still names the shared one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Module** | Development environment — [`docs/RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md), the *Running a lane* invocation |
| **Current assignee** | **QE** — `RUNNING.md` is QE's in the shared-files table (`CLAUDE.md` §20e). **The `infra/` half is already built and correct; nothing is asked of Lane C** |
| **Severity** | 🟠 — **it makes measurement untrustworthy**, which is [B-118](#b-118--lanes-share-one-postgresql-so-two-suites-running-at-once-fabricate-each-others-failures)'s own severity and for B-118's own reason |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — reported with evidence; **not fixed, because `RUNNING.md` is not this lane's to edit** |
| **Found** | 2026-08-05 by **Lane B**, when B-118 reproduced against it **after B-118 was marked `FIXED`** |

**Steps to reproduce.** Follow [`RUNNING.md` § Running a lane](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane) exactly, as a lane is required to, and run the suite while another lane runs theirs.

**Expected.** Isolation. B-118 is `FIXED`: *"create separate environment for each lane so that nothing could be shared."*

**Actual.** Contention, exactly as B-118 describes — two failures in modules the run never touched, both passing on an isolated re-run of the same commit.

### The fix is built and the instructions do not reach it

**`infra/` is correct.** `docker-compose.yml` reads `${SIGNORA_POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}` and `${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-signora-v2}`, and `environments.py` allocates a port per lane:

```
lane-a | postgres 5732
lane-b | postgres 5832
demo   | postgres 6232
```

**`RUNNING.md` still tells Lane B to use 5432**, in the block a lane copies verbatim:

```
export SIGNORA_TEST_APP_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://…@localhost:5432/signora_lane_b
export SIGNORA_TEST_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://…@localhost:5432/signora_lane_b
export SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://…@localhost:5432/signora_lane_b
```

**And 5832 is not listening** — only 5432 is. So the separate stack exists in the model and has never been started by the lane it was allocated to, because nothing told that lane to start it.

> **This is the class `CLAUDE.md` §2 names: the repository telling a lane something that is no longer true.** A defect marked `FIXED` whose fix nobody can reach is worse than one still marked open — **every lane reads the register, believes the row, and keeps reproducing the defect while believing it cannot.** It is also why this row exists rather than a re-opening of B-118: **B-118's fix is real and correct**, and re-opening it would misattribute a documentation gap to the engineering that closed it.

### What Lane B is doing meanwhile

**Not editing `RUNNING.md`** — it is QE's, and a lane rewriting another's file is how two records start disagreeing. **Not inventing its own ports either** ([`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane) is authoritative on allocation and `environments.py` already holds the answer).

**Publishing no number measured during contention**, which is B-118's own rule, and re-running in isolation to tell a real failure from a fabricated one.

### ⚠️ Measured 2026-08-05 — it is wider than this row says, and the evidence is deterministic

**This row blamed `RUNNING.md`. The `Makefile` target has the same defect, and that is the half a lane cannot read its way past.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **`make test`** | `cd backend && … uv run pytest --cov` — **passes no database URL at all**, so `tests/conftest.py` falls back to its literal default: `…@localhost:5432/signora`, the historical shared stack |
| **`make demo-prepare`** | `SIGNORA_DATABASE_URL=$(OWNER_DATABASE_URL)`, where `OWNER_DATABASE_URL` derives its port from `infra/environments.py --exports` — **correctly lane-aware** |

**Two targets in one file, one resolving the lane's allocation and one ignoring it.** So a lane that reads `infra/`, trusts the allocation and runs the documented gate **still lands on 5432** — the instructions are not the only thing pointing at the shared database.

**What it produced here, and it is not contention:** **62 failures, deterministic, `relation "signal_resolution" does not exist"`** — the shared database sits at migration `0038` while `integration` is at `0039`. **That reads exactly like a broken tree** and is a stale schema on a database this lane was never allocated.

**Confirmed by fixing only the environment:** the lane's own stack brought up at **5832**, migrated to head, suite re-run with the three `SIGNORA_TEST_*` URLs pointed at it — **3624 passed, 1 skipped, coverage 95.37%.** **Nothing in the tree changed between the two runs.**

**Still not fixed by this lane.** `RUNNING.md` is QE's and the `Makefile` is Platform Foundation's ([D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) — **but the gate half is QE's under §20e's own test**: this changes whether a gate *runs* against the right database, not what it *means*.
